alex.name: 站轻拳 (5LP)
alex.notes: Chains into stand LP / crouch LP / crouch LK; Alex's only 4F option; Incurs 20% damage scaling penalty if used as the first hit of a combo

alex.name: 站中拳 (5MP)
alex.notes: Core combo and frametrap tool with small pushback and lots of active frames for some oki potential as well (up to +7 on Hit / +3 on Block with meaty timing); Has a Target Combo follow-up (HP) that's hit confirmable (19F hit confirm window) which can lead into Prowler Stance oki on hit; +1 extra recovery frame (15F) on block and +2 extra recovery frames (17F) on whiff

alex.name: 站重拳 (5HP)
alex.notes: Good range poke and Drive Gauge bully tool; Can be held (see Hold version for more details); Interestingly this version has more active frames (5) than the fully held version (3); Super cancelable; Incurs 10% damage scaling penalty if used as the first hit of a combo

alex.name: Stand HP (hold)
alex.notes: Button must be held for 16 frames (results in uncharged version if released early); Hold version benefits from: Fully cancelable + Increased damage + Increased frame advantage + Increased range; Incredible pressure and bully tool due to its huge range and massive blockstun frames enabling true blockstring pressure into HP Flash Chop for 1.5 bars of drive gauge damage as still retain + frames on block; Puts airborne opponents into a limited juggle state; Alex has a slightly extended front leg hurtbox while holding the HP button during start-up on frames 8-19; Incurs 20% damage scaling penalty if used as the first hit of a combo

alex.name: 站轻脚 (5LK)
alex.notes: Very far range for a stand LK (albeit a bit slow); Incurs 20% damage scaling penalty if used as the first hit of a combo

alex.name: 站中脚 (5MK)
alex.notes: Long range poke with solid hitbox priority as well as lifting up the front leg hurtbox on frames 5-16 which helps with crushing low hitting attacks from the opponent; Combos into stand LK from a decent distance after successfully low crushing (and Punish Countering) the opponents low attack

alex.name: 站重脚 (5HK)
alex.notes: Very long range poke with decent hitbox priority; Can be held (see Hold version for more details); Puts airborne opponents into a limited juggle state (free juggle on Punish Counter); Punish Counter puts grounded opponents into a free juggle crumple state (+23 before opponent falls to the ground); The brief extended leg hurtbox on frame 15 of start-up (1F before active) is strike invincible; Incurs 15% damage scaling penalty if used as the first hit of a combo

alex.name: Stand HK (hold)
alex.notes: Button must be held for 16 frames (results in uncharged version if released early); Cancelable into Prowler Stance (d+PP) on hit or block; Hold version benefits from: Stance cancelable + Increased damage + Increased frame advantage + Increased range and hitbox priority; Small extended hurtbox on Alex's raised leg during start-up on frames 17-24; KDA listed on hit or on the Prowler Stance cancel refers to when hitting a grounded opponent (a lot variable against airborne opponents but generally higher KDA then); Incurs 15% damage scaling penalty if used as the first hit of a combo

alex.name: 蹲轻拳 (2LP)
alex.notes: Chains into stand LP / crouch LP / crouch LK; Consistent 5-frame punish option that links into crouch MP at max range; Incurs 20% damage scaling penalty if used as the first hit of a combo; Topmost hurtboxes on frames 1-7 are vulnerable only to airborne attacks (this is to discourage its use as an anti-air)

alex.name: 蹲中拳 (2MP)
alex.notes: Long range poke and combo tool; +4 extra recovery frames (20F) on whiff; Drive Rush cancel routes are more restrictive than Alex's other cancelable pokes (does not naturally combo into crouch HP for a HP Flash Chop ender); Topmost hurtboxes on frames 1-9 are vulnerable only to airborne attacks (this is to discourage its use as an anti-air)

alex.name: 蹲重拳 (2HP)
alex.notes: Cancelable into Prowler Stance (d+PP) on hit or block; Primary Anti-Air and Combo tool; Head and extended arm hurtbox are invincible to airborne strikes on frames 10-14 (until active frames end); Forces Stand a grounded hit (important for some of the combo routes from Stance such as enabling Lariat to hit from further away); Cannot hit cross-up (behind Alex); Punish Counter puts opponents into a limited juggle state (higher launch on airborne opponents); Only the first 2 active frames are cancelable and can hit grounded opponents (the remaining active frames can only hit airborne); Stand-size hurtboxes on frames 10-30 (but Alex is still considered in a Crouch status for the entire duration of the move); Has extremely short horizontal reach against a grounded opponent, making this awkward to combo into without the use of things like Drive Rush

alex.name: 蹲轻脚 (2LK)
alex.notes: Alex's longest range 5F option which can be invaluable for Modern Alex players since he loses neutral access to crouch LP in Modern; Has a situational Sweep Target Combo follow-up (HK) that doesn't combo naturally on hit, but can be useful as a 5F punish tool or potentially as a Drive Rush check; Chains into stand LP / crouch LP / crouch LK; Incurs 20% damage scaling penalty if used as the first hit of a combo

alex.name: 蹲中脚 (2MK)
alex.notes: Solid low poke with good frame advantage on hit (links into crouch LP on hit); Incurs 20% damage scaling penalty if used as the first hit of a combo

alex.name: 蹲重脚 (2HK)
alex.notes: Cancelable into Prowler Stance (d+PP) on hit only with a lenient hitconfirm window; Very long range sweep with good hitbox priority; Has some juggle potential naturally without Drive Rush

alex.name: 跳轻拳 (j.LP)
alex.notes: Fast option with good horizontal hitbox priority

alex.name: 跳中拳 (j.MP)
alex.notes: Puts airborne opponents into a limited juggle state; Decent air-to-air hitboxes; Cancelable into Flying Cross Chop (air d+HP) from forward jump only; Projectile invincible on lower body (legs) on frames 7-21

alex.name: 跳重拳 (j.HP)
alex.notes: Spikes down airborne opponents on hit; Pretty good vertical hitbox priority; Projectile invincible on lower body (legs) on frames 9-24

alex.name: 跳轻脚 (j.LK)
alex.notes: Cross-up; Can be used as a fuzzy instant Overhead on characters with a tall hurtbox

alex.name: 跳中脚 (j.MK)
alex.notes: Hitbox position requires frame perfect input timing to connect on normal sized Crouching opponents (more lenient on taller characters with larger hurtboxes); Has the most horizontal range of Alex's jump-ins (but harder to time properly compared to Jump HK); Projectile invincible on lower body (legs) on frames 8-25

alex.name: 跳重脚 (j.HK)
alex.notes: Good horizontal range jump-in and in some oki scenarios the only jump-in option Alex has; Projectile invincible on lower body (legs) on frames 10-21

alex.name: Flying Cross Chop
alex.notes: Can only be performed during a forward jump; Can be canceled into from forward Jump MP (similar to a Target Combo); Spikes down airborne opponents and normally leaves Alex up close for oki pressure (KDA on this is quite variable but usually between KD +6~14); Leg hurtbox is projectile invincible on frame 19 until landing; +15 extra landing recovery frames (35F) on whiff; Alex is in a crouching state during landing recovery with a Stand-size hurtbox for the first 3 recovery frames; Useful movement tool for escaping the corner (rolls far away from the opponent if not anti-aired)

alex.name: Chop
alex.notes: Overhead with high damage, good frame advantage on hit and minimal pushback to maintain pressure; Can combo into Stand MP at any range when used out of Drive Rush

alex.name: Oblique Stomp
alex.notes: Core combo and pressure tool with small pushback (similar to stand MP); +2 on block which lets do a strike / throw mix into either his regular throws or his HP/OD Power Bomb command grab (this requires Alex to be completely point-blank if not utilizing Drive Rush momentum, even holding back just 3 frames before inputting the MK will push Alex out of range for for his throws / command grab on block); When used mid-screen, the opponent can hold back on block to avoid Alex's throws or HP Power Bomb (OD Power Bomb still reaches), but this is obviously not an option for them when in the corner, and Alex can punish this with crouch LK combos or doing MP Power Bomb instead (the MP version can be interrupted by a 4F light if b+MK was blocked raw and not meaty or out of Drive Rush); Transitions into Collapsing Driver when hitting back turned opponents (this cinematic hit counts as a separate move for damage scaling)

alex.name: Palm Strikes
alex.notes: Cancelable into Prowler Stance (d+PP) on HIT only; Hit confirmable Target Combo (19F hit confirm window); 1F gap frametrap on block while also being safe on block for some reason (becomes +1 on block true blockstring in Burnout); Safe to Drive Impact between hits; Spikes down airborne opponents on hit

alex.name: Twisted Drop
alex.notes: Cancelable into Prowler Stance (d+PP) on HIT only; A sweeping target combo that cannot combo naturally (requires Counter-Hit / Punish / Drive Rush); Can be useful as a 5F punish tool or potentially as a Drive Rush check

alex.name: Prowler Stance
alex.notes: Cannot block while in stance; Counter-Hit state for entire duration; Standing state on frames 1-5 while initially entering stance with a Stand size hurtbox until frame 8 (and then maintains the Crouch state until stance is left via other means); Transitions into a Crouch size hurtbox on frames 9-15 while initially entering stance; Transitions into a low profile hurtbox on frame 16 but does not avoid standard-height projectiles (maintains this low profile until stance is left via other means); Cancelable into Stance moves on frame 18 of start-up and onward (frame 17 for Stance Exit) as long as Alex remains in Prowler Stance; Alex autocorrects to face the opponent immediately after a side switch

alex.name: Prowler Stance Exit
alex.notes: Manually exits Prowler Stance, maintaining the low profile and Crouch state on frames 1-9, and then normal Stand state on frames 10-25; Exiting Prowler Stance manually takes 25 frames total, during which time Alex is in a Counter-Hit state and cannot block; Fastest total Stance + Exit duration is 42 frames; Holding Up will buffer the Stance Exit at the earliest possible timing

alex.name: Low Rush
alex.notes: Stays in Prowler Stance; Maintains the same low profile and Crouch state from Prowler Stance for the entire duration; Distance traveled: 1.76; The dash has a total duration of 28 frames but can be canceled earlier into various Stance follow-ups; Can be kara canceled into the Slash Elbow follow-up (f+P) on frames 1-14; Can be kara canceled into the Tactical Hop (LK) and Air Stampede (MK) follow-ups on frame 18; Can be kara canceled into any other stance follow-upon on frame 20 except for another dash forward / dash backward; Holding forward does not buffer the dash (must be timed using the standard input buffer window)

alex.name: Low Retreat
alex.notes: Stays in Prowler Stance; Distance traveled: 1.00; Maintains the same low profile and Crouch state from Prowler Stance for the entire duration; Cannot be canceled into follow-ups until the end of 31 frame duration (except Stance Exit 1 frame earlier); Holding back does not buffer the dash (must be timed using the standard input buffer window)

alex.name: Slashing Elbow
alex.notes: Head and elbow hurtboxes are invincible to airborne strikes with a invincibility window depending on button strength used (LP: 8-15F | MP: 11-18F | HP: 14-21F); Maintains the low profile from the initial stance on start-up until 5F before active frames (LP: 1-7F | MP: 1-10F | HP: 1-13F); Maintains the Crouch state from the initial stance during start-up and active frames (despite the Stand sized hurtboxes after losing the low profile state), and then transitions into a Stand state during the entire recovery frames; Start-up and range varies depending on button strength used (all the move properties are otherwise the same); f+LP (Classic) / f+L (Modern): 12F start-up and 2.32 distance; f+MP (Classic) / f+M (Modern): 15F start-up and 2.60 distance; f+HP (Classic) / f+H (Modern): 18F start-up and 3.14 distance; Solid frame advantage with 4 active frames and relatively low pushback makes this a good tool for maintaining oki pressure even from far away; Screen shake effect occurs when Alex has frame advantage on block; Hitbox expands significantly on the 3rd active frame (easier to space for frame advantage); Launches the opponent into a limited juggle state on Counter-Hit / Punish Counter or on airborne opponents; Cannot be canceled into from Palm Jab (Prowler Stance LP); Incurs 20% damage scaling penalty if used as the first hit of a combo

alex.name: Palm Jab
alex.notes: Fast long range jab that maintains the low profile Crouch state from the initial stance for the entire duration; Stays in Prowler Stance (except on Perfect Parry); Special cancelable move (even into moves outside of the Prowler Stance) that can also be canceled into other Prowler Stance moves (except Slashing Elbow, Hyper Takedown, Stance Exit and Forward / Back Dash) and chain-canceled into itself; Because Alex cannot block during the Stance and uses chain cancels for all combo applications, the Hit / Block advantage primarily matters when tick throwing with Hyper Takedown or using Slashing Elbow afterward; Very strong frame advantage for a light button, but also very committal since Alex can't block while in Prowler Stance; Can chain 4 consecutive Palm Jabs on hit and 3 on block (true blockstring when chained); Incurs 20% damage scaling penalty if used as the first hit of a combo

alex.name: Shoulder Launcher
alex.notes: Upper / Mid body hurtbox is invincible to airborne strikes on frames 1-6; Entire body is invincible to airborne strikes on frames 7-13; Maintains the low profile from the initial stance on frames 1-7 (also retains Crouch state on frames 1-13 or until active frames are finished); Anti-Air / Combo tool that launches the opponent into a limited juggle state on hit; Cannot hit cross-up (behind Alex); Will autocorrect if Alex crosses under the opponent while dashing (can be used for sideswap routes); Can be canceled into from Palm Jab (Prowler Stance LP); Transitions into Falling Moon on Counter-Hit / Punish Counter: Significantly higher damage (800 -> 2680) / Hard Knockdown +22 (instead of a regular KD +51) / Improved Super Meter & Drive Gauge properties; Damage and Meter data listed in parentheses (X) refers to the Falling Moon version that plays out on Counter-Hit / Punish Counter

alex.name: Heavy Lariat
alex.notes: Maintains the low profile from the initial stance on frames 1-6 (up to frame 16 when button is held) and also retains Crouch state on frames 1-14 (up to frame 23 when button is held) or until the active frames are finished; Gains 1-hit of armor if button is held for at least 6 frames, and then gains 1 more hit of armor if button is continually held (up to frame 23 on the fully held version which covers all the active frames); HP button has to be held for at least 13F to get the fully charged version (releasing the button earlier results in an immediate loss of armor as the normal Lariat plays out); Better frame advantage on block (+5 instead of +3) when fully held; Puts grounded opponent into a standing back turn state on Counter-hit (+8) or Punish Counter (+10) which can link into Power Drop or Collapsing Driver (b+MK) if close enough; Launches airborne opponents into a limited juggle state; Deals significant Drive Gauge damage on block (80% of a bar) as well as giving frame advantage on block makes this an incredibly strong bully tool up close; The fully held version can be a very strong oki tool when timed properly, beating both wake-up jabs, throws and a lot of OD reversals due to the armor on it; Has less horizontal range vs Crouching opponents rather than Standing; Hitboxes move forward per active frame so if spaced out properly Alex can get improved frame advantage on hit / block allowing for more possibilities; Incurs 20% damage scaling penalty if used as the first hit of a combo; Can be canceled into from Palm Jab (Prowler Stance LP) but Punish Counter is required to combo into the fully held version

alex.name: Tactical Hop
alex.notes: Immediately loses low profile state and exits Prowler Stance; Prejump frames 1-2 are in a Crouching state followed by a Standing state on frames 3-6; Lower body is Projectile invincible on frames 6-8 with a smaller jumping hurtbox on frames 6-33; Airborne on frames 7-36 (Forced Knockdown state while airborne); Performs a short hop that can be followed by air normals or Flying Cross Chop on frames 22-32; Air attacks can be buffered as early as frame 8 (button presses on frame 33 onward are buffered as ground normals after landing); 3F Landing recovery frames just like a regular jump (but cannot block after empty jump); Counter-hit state for entire move duration (including landing recovery); Has a much smaller jump arc than a regular jump making this good for varying up your approach or as a mixup tool; Distance traveled: 1.157

alex.name: Air Stampede
alex.notes: Immediately loses low profile state and exits Prowler Stance (but retains Crouch status until airborne on frame 9); Standing size hurtboxes on frames 5-8 of start-up despite still being in Crouch status; Airborne on frames 9-30 (Forced Knockdown state) so Alex is still airborne on the first active frame (but not the second active); Overhead that's +2 on block and deals significant Drive Gauge damage on block (80% of a bar) makes this a strong (although reactable) approach tool; Can control trajectory by holding left or right (range: 1.309 ~ 3.054); Can hold back to bait anti-airs from a distance or hold forward to intentionally whiff and bait the opponent's parry; Cannot hit cross-up (behind Alex); Low hitstop (only 6 frames) making this require fast decision making from the opponent if blocked (Punish Counter results in much bigger 15F hitstop); Causes a Hard Knockdown OTG ground bounce on Punish Counter that puts the opponent into a limited juggle state; Can be canceled into from Palm Jab (Prowler Stance LP)

alex.name: Sweep Combination 1
alex.notes: Long range sweep that maintains the low profile Crouch state from stance for the entire duration; Stays in Prowler Stance except on Counter-Hit, Punish Counter or Perfect Parry; Can be canceled into from Palm Jab (Prowler Stance LP) for a consistent knockdown even at the jab's max range; Hit confirmable (22F window) into the HK Target Combo follow-up sweep; Puts airborne opponents into a limited juggle state (allowing for the HK Target Combo follow-up sweep); Has some juggle potential naturally without Drive Rush; Transitions into Flying Suplex on Counter-Hit or Punish Counter: Significantly higher damage (600 -> 2420) / Hard Knockdown +18 (instead of a regular KD +29) / Improved Super Meter & Drive Gauge properties; Damage and Meter data listed in parentheses (X) refers to the Flying Suplex version that plays out on Counter-Hit / Punish Counter

alex.name: Sweep Combination 2
alex.notes: Long range sweep that maintains the low profile Crouch state from stance for the entire duration; Stays in Prowler Stance except on Counter-Hit, Punish Counter or Perfect Parry; Can be canceled into from Palm Jab (Prowler Stance LP) for a consistent knockdown even at the jab's max range; 3F gap on block between hits that can frame trap if the opponent doesn't delay their punish; Can exit stance after knockdown for +1 oki in the corner; Second hit can whiff on hit if the first hit lands near max range; Has some juggle potential naturally without Drive Rush; Transitions into Flying Suplex on Counter-Hit or Punish Counter: Significantly higher damage (1200 -> 2420) / Hard Knockdown +18 (instead of a regular KD +25) / Improved Super Meter & Drive Gauge properties; Damage and Meter data listed in parentheses (X) refers to the Flying Suplex version that plays out on Counter-Hit / Punish Counter

alex.name: Hyper Takedown
alex.notes: Exits Prowler Stance immediately losing the Low profile but retains Crouch state on frames 1-7 (despite having Standing size hurtboxes) and then in Standing state on the remaining recovery frames; A normal throw with increased range (1.02) and stronger oki options than Alex's normal Throws outside of his Prowler Stance; Transitions into Death Valley on Punish Counter: +70% damage increase (1200 -> 2040) / Hard Knockdown +21 (instead of regular KD +31) / Improved Super Meter gain / 1 bar of Drive Gauge damage; Throw Escape builds 0.5 Drive bars for the defender (randomly assigned if throws are input simultaneously); Cannot be canceled into from Palm Jab (Prowler Stance LP) and is only in throw range after one jab on hit or block; Damage and Meter data listed in parentheses (X) refers to the Death Valley version that plays out on Punish Counter

alex.name: Dangerous Armbar
alex.notes: Exits Prowler Stance immediately losing the Low profile but maintains the Crouch state on frames 1-14 (but with Standing size hurtboxes on frames 9-14); Projectile invincible on frames 3-23 (can be used to punish various projectiles on reaction if already in stance); Airborne on frames 15-26 (Forced Knockdown state); A Command Grab that only hits Standing opponents (cannot grab Crouch or Airborne); Grants Alex Hard Knockdown (HKD) oki even when used mid-screen; Transitions into Spirtal DDT on Punish Counter: +15% damage increase (2000 -> 2300) / Hard Knockdown +20 (instead of HKD +21) / Improved Super Meter gain / 1 bar of Drive Gauge damage; Can be canceled into from Palm Jab (Prowler Stance LP) making it a more effective tick throw; Damage and Meter data listed in parentheses (X) refers to the Spiral DDT version that plays out on Punish Counter

alex.name: Arm Lock
alex.notes: Can throw loop with Drive Rush or pressure with forward dash into LP Power Bomb or spaced normals; Drive Rush + stand HK leaves Alex +7 on Hit / +2 on Block anywhere on the screen and in range for OD Power Bomb (midscreen) or HP Power Bomb (corner); Punish Counter gives +70% (2040) damage, Hard Knockdown (denies back-roll option on wake-up), depletes 1 bar of Drive gauge from the opponent, and builds twice as much Super gauge for the attacker; Throw Escape builds 0.5 Drive bars for the defender (randomly assigned if throws are input simultaneously)

alex.name: Guillotine Hammer
alex.notes: No real oki after a corner side switch but can pressure with spaced Drive Rush normals; Punish Counter gives +70% (2040) damage, Hard Knockdown (denies back-roll option on wake-up), depletes 1 bar of Drive gauge from the opponent, and builds twice as much Super gauge for the attacker; Throw Escape builds 0.5 Drive bars for the defender (randomly assigned if throws are input simultaneously)

alex.name: Illegal Knees
alex.notes: Slightly higher damage (+100 extra) than most standard throws; Can throw loop in the corner using Drive Rush (forward dash leaves Alex at neutral KD advantage); Midscreen oki is very weak compared to regular throw even with Drive Rush; Punish Counter gives +70% (2210) damage, Hard Knockdown (denies back-roll option on wake-up), depletes 1 bar of Drive gauge from the opponent, and builds twice as much Super gauge for the attacker; Throw Escape builds 0.5 Drive bars for the defender (randomly assigned if throws are input simultaneously)

alex.name: Drive Impact: Lariat Kick
alex.notes: 2 hits of armor on frames 1-27; Damages opponents Drive Gauge on Block (1/2 bar) | Hit (1 bar) | Counter-Hit (1.25 bar) | Punish Counter (1.5 bar); Knocks down on hit; Pushes the opponent far back on hit or block and causes a Wall Splat if they hit the wall (Parry prevents the backwards stumble and Wall Splat, greatly reducing the pushback); Regular KDA without Wall Splat +35 KD | Wall Splat on Hit +65 KD | Wall Splat on Block +72 HKD; KDA can vary greatly depending on how high the opponent wall splats (higher KDA the higher they wall splat); Advantage after Wall Splat can vary depending on distance from the corner (farther from corner gives higher advantage); Crumples the opponent on Punish Counter or after absorbing at least 1 attack during start-up (+21 frames before the crumple state goes airborne, followed by airborne state on frames 22-46 before they are grounded); Puts airborne opponents into a long spinning free juggle state when hit as a Punish Counter or after absorbing an attack; If the armor absorbs an attack it slows the overall start-up by 1F (27F total instead of 26F) and incurs 6F hitstop for each projectile hit absorbed (making it less likely to punish the opponent after absorbing projectiles); Absorbing an attack causes the player to take 1/2 the damage in recoverable health (but will KO if this would bring the player's health below zero); Stun/Dizzy occurs when a Wall Splat connects on an opponent in Burnout; Stun gives a free combo follow-up for the next 195F after hitting the wall, followed by a HKD if the player falls to the ground untouched (the last 7F before hitting the ground has a crouch-sized hurtbox but is considered standing, allowing for unique combo setups); Incurs 20% damage scaling penalty if used as the first hit of a combo (applies to wall splat on HIT, crumple, Burnout dizzy on hit/block, or any character-specific means of comboing after a regular Drive Impact); Incurs a 20% multiplier damage scaling penalty after a Wall Splat on BLOCK - Because the blocked Drive Impact is not considered a "hit" for the combo, the next attack can incur its own separate damage scaling as a combo starter; Wall Splat puts opponent into a special juggle state where the next move freely connects and continues the juggle even if it normally wouldn't (similar to a Forced Knockdown or Drive Rush juggle properties); Does not cause Wall Splat if the Drive Impact connects as a combo or a true blockstring with no gaps (LOCK icon appears on-screen); It is possible to "combo" into Stun if the opponent has under 1.5 Drive bars - a blocked DI Wall Splat from slightly outside the corner into a second DI on hit will cause Burnout and Stun (because the blocked DI is not technically considered a combo starter); Costs 1 bar of Drive Gauge; Cinematic slowdown occurs if both players activate Drive Impact within range of each other (granting a Punish Counter to the player who activates it later); Attempting to counter with DI vs. DI with under 400 HP will result in a KO, as the second player will not have enough health to absorb it; Clashes with other Drive Impacts and refunds the Drive gauge cost if they collide on the same active frame (start at exactly the same time, or 1F apart if the first Drive Impact absorbs a strike) - The meter refund does not prevent Burnout from occurring; The scrub killer

alex.name: Drive Reversal: Headbutt
alex.notes: Has two versions: one performed during blockstun or parry stun (20F start-up) and one performed as a wake-up reversal (18F start-up); Fully invincible on frames 1-22 (blockstun) / frames 1-20 (reversal); Armor Break (blows through all armor like Drive Impact, but not counters like JP's Amnesia); Trying to Drive Reversal after the blockstun ends results in a Drive Impact; Drive Reversal immediately removes the current blockstun you're in and starts the attack; Causes a 4F screen freeze after the 6th start-up frame, which allows the opponent to perform a simple OS (inputting their buttons during the buffer window) to prevent their next attack from coming out; Safe on block (-2) when used against an opponent in Burnout; Costs 2 bars of Drive Gauge; If the opponent tries to throw against a wake-up Drive Reversal, it causes a 12F screen freeze and refunds 1 bar of Drive gauge (but does not prevent Burnout); Guaranteed to interrupt any Drive Rush canceled normal if performed immediately out of blockstun (unless the opponent reacts with an invincible move or counter); Inflicts 4F less hitstop (16F) on block compared to most characters which affects the timing of the opponent's punish

alex.name: 斗气招架 (Drive Parry)
alex.notes: Parries all strikes and projectiles (high and low) from frame 1; 12F parry window (can hold the parry to extend the parry window); Perfect Parry occurs on the first 2 active frames (cannot achieve Perfect Parry if you buffer into parry by holding it during Reversal windows; Perfect Parries have to be timed properly); Can still hold charge directions during Parry (allowing characters with charge specials to stand block before performing their reversal); Can block during the recovery frames of a regular parry (can still get hit during the recovery frames if you don't block correctly); Getting thrown or hit at any point during the recovery frames of a whiffed parry attempt results in a Punish Counter; Successfully parrying a move puts you into the same amount of blockstun as that move would regularly do on block (but a Perfect Parry has only 1F of recovery); Throw invincible during the recovery of a successful parry (just like during blockstun); Perfect Parrying a strike has only 1F of recovery and disables the opponent from canceling their attack (basically a guaranteed punish opportunity except for safe jump setups); Perfect Parrying a strike requires holding the correct block direction (Down+Back for low strikes, Back for high/mid strikes); Attempting a Perfect Parry with the wrong block direction results in an "imperfect parry" that builds an extra 3000 Drive Gauge and plays a distinct audio/visual cue; After a successful Perfect Parry, you suffer a 50% penalty to your Damage, Drive Gauge Generation, and Drive Gauge Damage on any of your following attacks when punishing the opponent (in addition, both you and the opponent suffer a 20% penalty to your Super Meter gain during this period); Fully invincible for 6F after a successful Perfect Parry against a strike, which carries over to any attack you perform (ensuring a 5F or faster punish will always interrupt multi-hit attacks); Perfect Parrying projectiles puts you into fixed 10 frames of recovery and applies the same 50% scaling penalties (and 20% Super Meter penalty) on your following attacks when punishing the opponent; Parrying a Strike and Projectile on the same frame will result in a regular parry for the strike attack (effectively ignoring the projectile's hitstop / blockstun); Perfect Parrying a Strike and Projectile on the same frame will give a screen freeze like you Perfect Parried a Strike, but still give you 10F recovery as if you had Perfect Parried a Projectile; Can cancel into Drive Rush during active frames 3 and onward (fastest Drive Rush method is to buffer a forward input before doing parry + forward again); Can cancel into Drive Reversal from a successful parry (just like you normally can during blockstun); Costs 1/2 bar of Drive Gauge and continues to deplete 50 Drive Gauge per frame (0.3 Drive bars per second) as you hold the Parry; You lose the parry if you go into Burnout from the initial Drive Gauge cost (Perfect Parry requires frame-perfect timing when starting from under 1/2 of a Drive bar); Rewards 1 bar of Drive Gauge (1/2 bar total after factoring in the initial parry cost) for successfully parrying a strike; Rewards 1/2 bar of Drive Gauge (0 bar total after factoring in the initial parry cost) for successfully parrying a projectile (with a few exceptions); Rewards 2 bars of Drive Gauge (1.5 bars total after factoring in the initial parry cost) for successful parrying a Super Art or Drive Impact; Successfully parrying a strike attack splits the regular block pushback between both players (while Perfect Parrying a strike removes all of its pushback); Successfully parrying a projectile or Drive Impact reduces the pushback of it by half (while Perfect Parrying a projectile or Drive Impact removes all of its pushback); Your hurtbox and throw box expand slightly towards the opponent for the entire duration of the Parry (Throw box extension starts instantly on frame 1, while the Hurtbox extension starts on frame 3, after the initial 2F Perfect Parry window); Parrying while crouching maintains a regular crouch hurtbox for the first 2 frames of the parry (during the initial Perfect Parry window)

alex.name: 斗气冲刺 (Drive Rush)
alex.notes: Dashes forward and enhances the next normal or command normal used out of the Drive Rush with +4 extra hitstun / blockstun, as well as improved juggle properties (Juggle Limit increased by +3 / Juggle Start/Increase reduced to 0); The +4 bonus frame advantage gained from a Drive Rush enhanced move also stacks with any bonus frame advantage that move may have gained from Counter-Hit, Punish Counter, or Burnout; Grounded special-cancelable normals can also be canceled into Drive Rush on hit or block, as well as from light normals on whiff; Drive Rush maintains buffers (freezes the buffer window) during its start-up and freeze frames - This allows players to do things normally not possible within the normal buffer windows, such as Drive Rushing into a charge special; The initial 10F screen freeze eats the opponent's directional inputs (except Jumps) but does not prevent attacks from being buffered immediately afterward (this can cause inputs to be combined in unintended ways, such as crouch MK + Fireball performing a raw Fireball, or a vertical jump + walk forward turning into a forward jump); Framedata shown in parentheses refers to the Drive Rush version used from a Parry; Drive Rush recovery is only 24F total (23F if done from a Parry) - but the enhanced dash itself is 46F total (45F if done from Parry) and you can cancel it as early as frame 9 (frame 11 if done from a Parry); Inputting a direction (walk/crouch/block/jump) after the Drive Rush recovery plays out 2 additional recovery frames before the transition occurs (this allows the user to perform an enhanced crouching or command normal late in the dash by inputting the direction + button simultaneously); You stop building any form of Drive Gauge on your attacks after using a Drive Rush in the MIDDLE of a combo (but you still continue to build Drive gauge as normal if you did Drive Rush at the START of a combo); Applies an extra damage scaling penalty after using a Drive Rush in the MIDDLE of a combo (no damage scaling if you use Drive Rush at the START of a combo); Costs 3 bars of Drive Gauge if canceled into from a normal attack; Costs 1/2 bar of Drive Gauge if canceled into from Parry (for a total of 1 bar of Drive Gauge when you factor in the initial 1/2 bar cost of the Parry); Normals used out of Drive Rush carry additional forward momentum (but throws and specials immediately halt all momentum, which can be a useful strategy to punish opponents for trying to interrupt your Drive Rush); Parry Drive Rush can only be initiated after frame 3 of the Parry (but can be performed immediately after recovering from a successful parry); Parry Drive Rush cannot be initiated with less than 1/2 of a Drive bar (as the initial Parry cost will put the user into Burnout) - But whiff canceling a Light normal into Drive Rush can achieve a similar effect; Cannot cancel Drive Rush into a Parry (inputting MP+MK results in a MK normal coming out instead); Drive Rush puts the user into a counter-hit state for the entire duration (this makes it impossible to tech a throw that connects during the dash)

blanka.notes: Can hit cross-up; Medium trajectory; Can steer Blanka's air momentum forward or backwards (forward momentum is faster than backwards); Airborne on frames 8-12, 27-67 (Forced Knockdown state)

Can hit cross-up; Farthest trajectory; Can steer Blanka's air momentum forward or backwards (forward momentum is faster than backwards); Airborne on frames 8-12, 27-69 (Forced Knockdown state)

blanka.name: Aerial Rolling Attack (air)
blanka.notes: Takes 40 frames to charge (holds charge for 10F after leaving charge); Possible during any jump direction (even at the start of a forward jump) or after Coward Crouch > Raid Jump; Cancelable into from jump MP; Can hit cross-up (second hit whiffs unless near the corner); Powerful tool on both offense and defense, especially against Throws; Usually +1 on block if used instantly from a jump off the ground; Second hit is performed on HIT only; Forced Knockdown state while airborne

blanka.name: Wild Hunt
blanka.notes: Slow start-up command grab; Range: 3.41 (mid-range); Airborne on frames 14-33 (Forced Knockdown state)

Slow start-up command grab; Range: 3.41 (mid-range); Airborne on frames 14-33 (Forced Knockdown state)
Slow start-up command grab; Range: 4.25 (furthest); Airborne on frames 19-36 (Forced Knockdown state)

Slow start-up command grab; Range: 2.70~3.59; Can steer Blanka's air momentum forward or backwards (forward momentum is faster than backwards); Airborne on frames 9-28 (Forced Knockdown state); Jumps higher than the non-OD versions and can avoid many attacks; Can be combo'd into which sets up very high KDA (Knockdown Advantage) to setup for oki / Blanka-Chan

cviper.name: 站轻拳 (5LP)
cviper.notes: Chains into stand LP / crouch LP / crouch LK; Incurs 20% damage scaling penalty if used as the first hit of a combo

cviper.name: 站中拳 (5MP)
cviper.notes: Primary combo and frame trap starter; Great meaty tool with 4 active frames (up to +9 on Hit / +4 on Block); Leaves C. Viper in throw range on block, but all characters can walk back to make the throw whiff; Great approach tool out of Drive Rush for continued strike/throw pressure

cviper.name: 站重拳 (5HP)
cviper.notes: Long range poke that can be Super Jump canceled into Feint or Seismic Hammer for high damage combos; C. Viper's only Feint cancel that is plus on block

cviper.name: 站轻脚 (5LK)
cviper.notes: Primary 5F punish tool and link option after chained light normals (can link after Crouch LP in 4-hit light confirms); Higher hitstun than other light normals (combos naturally into MP Thunder Dash); Incurs 20% damage scaling penalty if used as the first hit of a combo

cviper.name: 站中脚 (5MK)
cviper.notes: Strong poke and whiff punish tool that can be Super Jump canceled for more damage; Combos into 2HP when SJC'd (Super Jump canceled) after a whiff punishing something (Punish Counter); Counter-hit allows a link to SA2 or a SJC into LP Seismic Hammer; +2F extra recovery frames (20F) on whiff

cviper.name: 站重脚 (5HK)
cviper.notes: Puts airborne opponents into an OTG juggle state on hit; Stagger state on Punish Counter (+19); Shorter range against crouching opponents; Can be juggled into after Seismo + SJC Air Burn Kick, then Super Jump canceled for further damage (SJC into grounded OD Burn Kick is a 2F timing window that's part of many optimal combo routes); Punish Counter advantage is big enough to allow for a Super Jump cancel into a full jump-in combo

cviper.name: 蹲轻拳 (2LP)
cviper.notes: Chains into stand LP / crouch LP / crouch LK; Incurs 20% damage scaling penalty if used as the first hit of a combo; Topmost hurtboxes on frames 1-6 are vulnerable only to airborne attacks (this is to discourage its use as an anti-air); 1F extra hitstun (and frame advantage) than stand LP but has less range; Can be used as the third hit of a chain that links into stand LK, but this will whiff if the opponent stand blocks (also whiffs under many reversal standing jabs at this range)

cviper.name: 蹲中拳 (2MP)
cviper.notes: Great hitstun for a 6F medium normal (combos into OD Seismic Hammer); Topmost hurtboxes on frames 1-8 are vulnerable only to airborne attacks (this is to discourage its use as an anti-air)

cviper.name: 蹲重拳 (2HP)
cviper.notes: Forces stand on hit; Viper's main special cancelable poke and combo tool (combos naturally into meterless Seismic Hammer); Viper's core tool for FFF (Fierce Feint Fierce) combo routes

cviper.name: 蹲轻脚 (2LK)
cviper.notes: Chains into stand LP / crouch LP / crouch LK; Incurs 20% damage scaling penalty if used as the first hit of a combo; Crazy good frame advantages for a crouch LK; Pseudo-special-cancelable due to Super Jump (this SJC has relaxed execution requirements and can be performed with a simple Up input from a crouching state)

cviper.name: 蹲中脚 (2MK)
cviper.notes: Long range low poke (furthest range crouch MK in the game that's still pseudo-special-cancelable) that can be Super Jump canceled for a combo extension (this SJC has relaxed execution requirements and can be performed with a simple Up input from a crouching state); Incurs 20% damage scaling penalty if used as the first hit of a combo; Has good advantage on block when used from Drive Rush (but the high pushback keeps C. Viper out of throw range)

cviper.name: 蹲重脚 (2HK)
cviper.notes: +4F extra recovery frames (29F) on block; Cannot be Super Jump canceled for safety; Punish Counter sets up a KD +45 safe jump using High Jump normals; Has some Juggle potential naturally without Drive Rush (like after OD Seismo for a meterless combo extension)

cviper.name: 跳轻拳 (j.LP)
cviper.notes: Good close range air-to-air for opponents slightly above C. Viper

cviper.name: 跳中拳 (j.MP)
cviper.notes: Puts airborne opponents into a limited juggle state; Cancelable into Air Burn Kick during a forward or neutral jump; Projectile invincible on lower body (legs) on frames 8-22

cviper.name: 跳重拳 (j.HP)
cviper.notes: Spikes down airborne opponents on hit; Strong hitbox priority for vertical approaches; Projectile invincible on lower body (legs) on frames 11-23

cviper.name: 跳轻脚 (j.LK)
cviper.notes: Can be used as a fuzzy instant Overhead; Combos naturally from any close-range Super Jump canceled normal against Standing tall characters (JP, Marisa, Sagat, Zangief); Very strong hitbox priority

cviper.name: 跳中脚 (j.MK)
cviper.notes: Cross-up; Great all-purpose jump-in (C. Viper's longest range forward jump normal) with exceptional hitbox priority; Projectile invincible on lower body (legs) on frames 7-20

cviper.name: 跳重脚 (j.HK)
cviper.notes: Cross-up; Cancelable into Air Burn Kick until the 37th airborne frame of jump or super jump (does not work in safe jump setups or on crouching opponents); Projectile invincible on lower body (legs) on frames 8-19

cviper.name: Neutral Jump HK
cviper.notes: Furthest horizontal range and strongest horizontal hitbox priority of all of C. Viper's jump normals (although the effective horizontal range is very limited due to only being accessible from a Neutral jump); Projectile invincible on lower body (legs) on frames 10-19

cviper.name: Viper Elbow
cviper.notes: Overhead; Crushes lows on frames 16-27 (not airborne or throw invincible)

cviper.name: Double Kick
cviper.notes: 2 hits; Carries over Counter-Hit / Punish Counter bonus frame advantage to both hits; Useful approach tool from Drive Rush that grants a strike/throw mixup on block or a Crouch MP link on hit; Minimal pushback gives this a lot of uses cases on hit or block; Incurs 20% damage scaling penalty if used as the first hit of a combo

cviper.name: High Impulse
cviper.notes: Grants a corner throw loop with forward dash (+7) or walking with manual timing; Can pressure with meaty Burning Kick + Double Burn (+2 oB): MK version makes the follow-up a true blockstring, while HK version leaves a small blockstring gap that can bait Drive Impact; Punish Counter gives +70% (2040) damage, Hard Knockdown (denies back-roll option on wake-up), depletes 1 bar of Drive gauge from the opponent, and builds twice as much Super gauge for the attacker; Throw Escape builds 0.5 Drive bars for the defender (randomly assigned if throws are input simultaneously)

cviper.name: Thunder Cradle
cviper.notes: No real oki after a corner side switch (but can pressure with Drive Rush normals); Can pressure with meaty LK Burning Kick into Double Burn (+2 oB) (punishable with wakeup Drive Impact, but opponent cannot DI punish the Double Burn); Punish Counter gives +70% (2040) damage, Hard Knockdown (denies back-roll option on wake-up), depletes 1 bar of Drive gauge from the opponent, and builds twice as much Super gauge for the attacker; Throw Escape builds 0.5 Drive bars for the defender (randomly assigned if throws are input simultaneously)

cviper.name: Drive Impact: Viper Cannon
cviper.notes: 2 hits of armor on frames 1-27; Damages opponents Drive Gauge on Block (1/2 bar) | Hit (1 bar) | Counter-Hit (1.25 bar) | Punish Counter (1.5 bar); Knocks down on hit; Pushes the opponent far back on hit or block and causes a Wall Splat if they hit the wall (Parry prevents the backwards stumble and Wall Splat, greatly reducing the pushback); Regular KDA without Wall Splat +35 KD | Wall Splat on Hit +65 KD | Wall Splat on Block +72 HKD; KDA can vary greatly depending on how high the opponent wall splats (higher KDA the higher they wall splat); Advantage after Wall Splat can vary depending on distance from the corner (farther from corner gives higher advantage); Crumples the opponent on Punish Counter or after absorbing at least 1 attack during start-up (+21 frames before the crumple state goes airborne, followed by airborne state on frames 22-46 before they are grounded); Puts airborne opponents into a long spinning free juggle state when hit as a Punish Counter or after absorbing an attack; If the armor absorbs an attack it slows the overall start-up by 1F (27F total instead of 26F) and incurs 6F hitstop for each projectile hit absorbed (making it less likely to punish the opponent after absorbing projectiles); Absorbing an attack causes the player to take 1/2 the damage in recoverable health (but will KO if this would bring the player's health below zero); Stun/Dizzy occurs when a Wall Splat connects on an opponent in Burnout; Stun gives a free combo follow-up for the next 195F after hitting the wall, followed by a HKD if the player falls to the ground untouched (the last 7F before hitting the ground has a crouch-sized hurtbox but is considered standing, allowing for unique combo setups); Incurs 20% damage scaling penalty if used as the first hit of a combo (applies to wall splat on HIT, crumple, Burnout dizzy on hit/block, or any character-specific means of comboing after a regular Drive Impact); Incurs a 20% multiplier damage scaling penalty after a Wall Splat on BLOCK - Because the blocked Drive Impact is not considered a "hit" for the combo, the next attack can incur its own separate damage scaling as a combo starter; Wall Splat puts opponent into a special juggle state where the next move freely connects and continues the juggle even if it normally wouldn't (similar to a Forced Knockdown or Drive Rush juggle properties); Does not cause Wall Splat if the Drive Impact connects as a combo or a true blockstring with no gaps (LOCK icon appears on-screen); It is possible to "combo" into Stun if the opponent has under 1.5 Drive bars - a blocked DI Wall Splat from slightly outside the corner into a second DI on hit will cause Burnout and Stun (because the blocked DI is not technically considered a combo starter); Costs 1 bar of Drive Gauge; Cinematic slowdown occurs if both players activate Drive Impact within range of each other (granting a Punish Counter to the player who activates it later); Attempting to counter with DI vs. DI with under 400 HP will result in a KO, as the second player will not have enough health to absorb it; Clashes with other Drive Impacts and refunds the Drive gauge cost if they collide on the same active frame (start at exactly the same time, or 1F apart if the first Drive Impact absorbs a strike) - The meter refund does not prevent Burnout from occurring; The scrub killer

cviper.name: Drive Reversal: Counter Spark
cviper.notes: Has two versions: one performed during blockstun or parry stun (20F start-up) and one performed as a wake-up reversal (18F start-up); Fully invincible on frames 1-22 (blockstun) / frames 1-20 (reversal); Armor Break (blows through all armor like Drive Impact, but not counters like JP's Amnesia); Trying to Drive Reversal after the blockstun ends results in a Drive Impact; Drive Reversal immediately removes the current blockstun you're in and starts the attack; Causes a 4F screen freeze after the 6th start-up frame, which allows the opponent to perform a simple OS (inputting their buttons during the buffer window) to prevent their next attack from coming out; Safe on block (-2) when used against an opponent in Burnout; Costs 2 bars of Drive Gauge; If the opponent tries to throw against a wake-up Drive Reversal, it causes a 12F screen freeze and refunds 1 bar of Drive gauge (but does not prevent Burnout); Guaranteed to interrupt any Drive Rush canceled normal if performed immediately out of blockstun (unless the opponent reacts with an invincible move or counter)

cviper.name: 斗气招架 (Drive Parry)
cviper.notes: Parries all strikes and projectiles (high and low) from frame 1; 12F parry window (can hold the parry to extend the parry window); Perfect Parry occurs on the first 2 active frames (cannot achieve Perfect Parry if you buffer into parry by holding it during Reversal windows; Perfect Parries have to be timed properly); Can still hold charge directions during Parry (allowing characters with charge specials to stand block before performing their reversal); Can block during the recovery frames of a regular parry (can still get hit during the recovery frames if you don't block correctly); Getting thrown or hit at any point during the recovery frames of a whiffed parry attempt results in a Punish Counter; Successfully parrying a move puts you into the same amount of blockstun as that move would regularly do on block (but a Perfect Parry has only 1F of recovery); Throw invincible during the recovery of a successful parry (just like during blockstun); Perfect Parrying a strike has only 1F of recovery and disables the opponent from canceling their attack (basically a guaranteed punish opportunity except for safe jump setups); Perfect Parrying a strike requires holding the correct block direction (Down+Back for low strikes, Back for high/mid strikes); Attempting a Perfect Parry with the wrong block direction results in an "imperfect parry" that builds an extra 3000 Drive Gauge and plays a distinct audio/visual cue; After a successful Perfect Parry, you suffer a 50% penalty to your Damage, Drive Gauge Generation, and Drive Gauge Damage on any of your following attacks when punishing the opponent (in addition, both you and the opponent suffer a 20% penalty to your Super Meter gain during this period); Fully invincible for 6F after a successful Perfect Parry against a strike, which carries over to any attack you perform (ensuring a 5F or faster punish will always interrupt multi-hit attacks); Perfect Parrying projectiles puts you into fixed 10 frames of recovery and applies the same 50% scaling penalties (and 20% Super Meter penalty) on your following attacks when punishing the opponent; Parrying a Strike and Projectile on the same frame will result in a regular parry for the strike attack (effectively ignoring the projectile's hitstop / blockstun); Perfect Parrying a Strike and Projectile on the same frame will give a screen freeze like you Perfect Parried a Strike, but still give you 10F recovery as if you had Perfect Parried a Projectile; Can cancel into Drive Rush during active frames 3 and onward (fastest Drive Rush method is to buffer a forward input before doing parry + forward again); Can cancel into Drive Reversal from a successful parry (just like you normally can during blockstun); Costs 1/2 bar of Drive Gauge and continues to deplete 50 Drive Gauge per frame (0.3 Drive bars per second) as you hold the Parry; You lose the parry if you go into Burnout from the initial Drive Gauge cost (Perfect Parry requires frame-perfect timing when starting from under 1/2 of a Drive bar); Rewards 1 bar of Drive Gauge (1/2 bar total after factoring in the initial parry cost) for successfully parrying a strike; Rewards 1/2 bar of Drive Gauge (0 bar total after factoring in the initial parry cost) for successfully parrying a projectile (with a few exceptions); Rewards 2 bars of Drive Gauge (1.5 bars total after factoring in the initial parry cost) for successful parrying a Super Art or Drive Impact; Successfully parrying a strike attack splits the regular block pushback between both players (while Perfect Parrying a strike removes all of its pushback); Successfully parrying a projectile or Drive Impact reduces the pushback of it by half (while Perfect Parrying a projectile or Drive Impact removes all of its pushback); Your hurtbox and throw box expand slightly towards the opponent for the entire duration of the Parry (Throw box extension starts instantly on frame 1, while the Hurtbox extension starts on frame 3, after the initial 2F Perfect Parry window); Parrying while crouching maintains a regular crouch hurtbox for the first 2 frames of the parry (during the initial Perfect Parry window)

cviper.name: 斗气冲刺 (Drive Rush)
cviper.notes: Dashes forward and enhances the next normal or command normal used out of the Drive Rush with +4 extra hitstun / blockstun, as well as improved juggle properties (Juggle Limit increased by +3 / Juggle Start/Increase reduced to 0); The +4 bonus frame advantage gained from a Drive Rush enhanced move also stacks with any bonus frame advantage that move may have gained from Counter-Hit, Punish Counter, or Burnout; Grounded special-cancelable normals can also be canceled into Drive Rush on hit or block, as well as from light normals on whiff; Drive Rush maintains buffers (freezes the buffer window) during its start-up and freeze frames - This allows players to do things normally not possible within the normal buffer windows, such as Drive Rushing into a charge special; The initial 10F screen freeze eats the opponent's directional inputs (except Jumps) but does not prevent attacks from being buffered immediately afterward (this can cause inputs to be combined in unintended ways, such as crouch MK + Fireball performing a raw Fireball, or a vertical jump + walk forward turning into a forward jump); Framedata shown in parentheses refers to the Drive Rush version used from a Parry; Drive Rush recovery is only 24F total (23F if done from a Parry) - but the enhanced dash itself is 46F total (45F if done from Parry) and you can cancel it as early as frame 9 (frame 11 if done from a Parry); Inputting a direction (walk/crouch/block/jump) after the Drive Rush recovery plays out 2 additional recovery frames before the transition occurs (this allows the user to perform an enhanced crouching or command normal late in the dash by inputting the direction + button simultaneously); You stop building any form of Drive Gauge on your attacks after using a Drive Rush in the MIDDLE of a combo (but you still continue to build Drive gauge as normal if you did Drive Rush at the START of a combo); Applies an extra damage scaling penalty after using a Drive Rush in the MIDDLE of a combo (no damage scaling if you use Drive Rush at the START of a combo); Costs 3 bars of Drive Gauge if canceled into from a normal attack; Costs 1/2 bar of Drive Gauge if canceled into from Parry (for a total of 1 bar of Drive Gauge when you factor in the initial 1/2 bar cost of the Parry); Normals used out of Drive Rush carry additional forward momentum (but throws and specials immediately halt all momentum, which can be a useful strategy to punish opponents for trying to interrupt your Drive Rush); Parry Drive Rush can only be initiated after frame 3 of the Parry (but can be performed immediately after recovering from a successful parry); Parry Drive Rush cannot be initiated with less than 1/2 of a Drive bar (as the initial Parry cost will put the user into Burnout) - But whiff canceling a Light normal into Drive Rush can achieve a similar effect; Cannot cancel Drive Rush into a Parry (inputting MP+MK results in a MK normal coming out instead); Drive Rush puts the user into a counter-hit state for the entire duration (this makes it impossible to tech a throw that connects during the dash)

cviper.name: Knuckled Pursuit
cviper.notes: Combos naturally on hit; No Drive gauge cost during SA1 install and gains 0.3 Drive bars on hit or block; Higher KD Advantage if Burning Kick hits airborne opponent or lands as a Punish Counter (+1 extra KD Advantage on Punish Counter); Grants +9 KD Advantage when connecting on a grounded opponent after Burning Kick is absorbed by armor

cviper.name: Double Burn
cviper.notes: Leaves C. Viper with advantage on block but does not combo on hit without a Punish Counter (KD +13 if follow-up whiffs); Leaves a 3F gap that can be interrupted with anti-air invincible moves or Drive Impact (true blockstring if opponent is in Burnout); If Burning Kick is blocked on a later active frame, the opponent can no longer punish with Drive Impact (forms a true blockstring on the final 2 active frames); No Drive gauge cost during SA1 install and gains 0.3 Drive bars on hit or block; An especially strong pressure & bully tool when the opponent is in Burnout; Knockdown Advantage varies greatly depending on opponents height from the ground (higher advantage the higher up in the air the opponent is) as well as how how late into the active frames the move connects; Grants +40 KD Advantage if this follow-up kick connects on a grounded opponent (like if the opponent doesn't block this follow-up kick)

cviper.name: Seismic Hammer
cviper.notes: 1-hit projectile; Distance varies based on button strength: LP close | MP ~50% screen | HP ~80% screen (all versions stop at the corner); Puts opponents into a limited juggle state; Can be feint canceled by pressing or holding K after 11F (total feint duration of 27F) allowing it to bait jumps or anti-projectile Supers; Super Jump cancelable on hit/block only; Combos from Crouch HP (meterless) or Stand HP / Stand HK (Super Jump cancel); Great tool for Burnout pressure especially during SA1 install (can repeatedly chain into itself with Super Jump cancels); Chained HP Seismo can connect 9 times consecutively on a cornered opponent before being pushed out of range (only 7-8 if canceled into from a heavy normal); Incurs 20% damage scaling penalty if used as the first hit of a combo; Hitbox is low to the ground, allowing opponent to block when landing from an empty jump

cviper.name: Focus Force (lvl 1)
cviper.notes: Has 1 hit of armor on frames 6-13 or until release; Absorbing a strike results in an automatic 10F counter-attack that comes out on frame 14 at the earliest (may be blocked if a light normal is absorbed early in the armor frames); Cancelable into forward dash on frames 12-14 or until button is released (cannot dash after absorbing a strike); C. Viper is in a Punish Counter state for the entire duration (including a forward dash cancel); Slightly increased oki on Punish Counter; Button can be held to extend the armor and dash cancel frames (up to frame 59) and changing various properties of the move (see the lvl 2 / lvl 3 versions of this move for more details); Only the first hit gains extra damage on Punish Counter; Only the second hit causes a Knockdown (can sometimes trade on the first hit, which can result in a follow-up combo for C. Viper); Focus + Dash cancel can be a useful way to deal with projectiles at some ranges when the Drive gauge is too low to parry; Useful tool against Drive Impact while in Burnout (though the armor starts too late to work in most DI cancel blockstrings); -17 on Punish Counter if only the first hit reaches the opponent (e.g. absorbing a ranged Dhalsim poke); This move cannot be performed if input while still holding down any Punch button on Classic Controls (this is to help prevent accidentally getting this move instead of a SJC feint)

cviper.name: Focus Force (lvl 2)
cviper.notes: Has 1 hit of armor on frame 6 until release; Absorbing a strike results in an automatic 10F counter-attack that comes out on frame 14 at the earliest; Cancelable into forward dash on frame 12 until button is released (cannot dash after absorbing a strike); C. Viper is in a Punish Counter state for the entire duration (including a forward dash cancel); The button must be held for at least 20 frames (up to 58 frames) to execute this partially held (lvl 2) version; Crumples the opponent on Punish Counter (airborne state, +8 before opponent falls to the ground); Only the first hit gains extra damage on Punish Counter; Only the second hit causes a Knockdown (can sometimes trade on the first hit, which can result in a follow-up combo for C. Viper); -17 on Punish Counter if only the first hit reaches the opponent (e.g. absorbing a ranged Dhalsim poke); This move cannot be performed if input while still holding down any Punch button on Classic Controls (this is to help prevent accidentally getting this move instead of a SJC feint)

cviper.name: Focus Force (lvl 3)
cviper.notes: Has 1 hit of armor on frames 6-59; Absorbing a strike results in an automatic 10F counter-attack that comes out on frame 14 at the earliest; Cancelable into forward dash on frames 12-60 (cannot dash after absorbing a strike); C. Viper is in a Punish Counter state for the entire duration (including a forward dash cancel); The button must be held for at least 59 frames to execute this fully held (lvl 3) version; Crumples the opponent on hit (airborne state, +25 before opponent falls to the ground); Only the first hit gains extra damage on Punish Counter; Only the second hit causes a Knockdown (can sometimes trade on the first hit, which can result in a follow-up combo for C. Viper); -17 on Punish Counter if only the first hit reaches the opponent (e.g. absorbing a ranged Dhalsim poke); This move cannot be performed if input while still holding down any Punch button on Classic Controls (this is to help prevent accidentally getting this move instead of a SJC feint)

cviper.name: Feint
cviper.notes: This feint can be canceled into during the start-up of Thunder Dash (214P) or Seismic Hammer (623P); The feint itself has a duration of 12F (Thunder Dash) or 16F (Seismic Hammer), but the Feint cancel window on each aforementioned Special is slightly different, resulting in different total duration for the Feint; Total feint duration: LP Thunder Dash 24F (12+12) / MP Thunder Dash 20F (8+12) / HP Thunder Dash 18F (6+12) / Seismic Hammer 27F (11+16); C. Viper is in a counter-hit state for the entire feint duration; The K button can be held to automatically feint at the earliest possible timing (can result in accidental Focus Force activation when performed from a Super Jump cancel even without negative edge enabled)

cviper.name: High Jump
cviper.notes: Cancelable into from any grounded normals (except Sweep, Overhead, and f+HK) and Seismic Hammer (623P) on Hit / Block (this cancel is notated by 'sj' (Super Jump) in the cancel data section of other moves); Jumps slightly higher and ~50% farther than normal jump; The start-up of the jump itself is cancelable into any Special or Super during pre-jump frames 2-6 (2F pre-jump > follow-ups); Airborne on frames 7-46 (Forced Knockdown state); Counter-hit state for entire duration including prejump and landing recovery; Has 3 landing recovery frames like a standard jump; Can only be performed as a Forward or Neutral jump (canceling into Super Jump with an Up+Back input results in a vertical Super Jump); Costs 1 bar of Drive Gauge to perform (but is free of cost during the Limit Decoupler (SA1) install); This High Jump functions like OD Specials, momentarily freezing the Drive Gauge's passive build-up, but still allowing C. Viper to build back some of the Drive Gauge she just spent on the follow-up hits; Because the pre-jump frames 2-6 are Special cancelable, it means C. Viper can effectively make all her normals (except Sweep, Overhead, and f+HK) Special cancelable (even when they're not Special cancelable normals); The upwards direction has to be input no later than 8F after any downwards direction in order to execute this Super Jump; Execution requirements are relaxed when canceled from a normal that is not otherwise special-cancelable (most notably crouch MK / crouch LK which can perform a SJC by tapping Up from a crouching state); Can perform safe jump setups with High Jump (requires KD Advantage of +45); BUG?: Burn Kicks (grounded or airborne) cannot be easily buffered into like all the other Specials performed from a Super Jump Cancel, but rather the Kick input has to be delayed until after the Super Jump script starts, and the Grounded Burn Kick versions can only be executed if the Kick is input on frames 2-3 of the pre-jump frames (this is a 2F window that's required for many of C. Viper's optimal damage conversions - For some reason, there is no button buffer accepted on frame 1 of the Super Jump script)

cviper.name: Limit Decoupler
cviper.notes: Strike and Throw invincible on frames 1-11 and further invincible to airborne strikes on frames 12-20; Armor Break; Depletes 0.5 Drive Bar on hit for the opponent; Temporarily grants C. Viper the ability to use any of her 1-bar moves (High Jump, Tracer Combination, Knuckled Pursuit, or Double Burn) at no cost to the Drive Gauge (doing this while in Burnout allows C. Viper only a single free move usage, which then ends the install timer); These 1-bar attack follow-ups also build 0.3 Drive bars on hit or block while the install is active; Install has a timed duration of 700 frames (~11.7 seconds) which freezes during any hitstop or cinematics; The install becomes active on frame 21 (after active frames) on hit, block, or whiff; C. Viper does not build any Super meter while this install is active (it might even be smart to save up to two levels of Super before activating this install, in order to be able to do another SA1 before the install timer ends to extend the overall install duration); If the first hit trades with a projectile at close range, it's possible for C. Viper to pick up a limited juggle like HP Thunder Dash, or Level 1/2 Super (depends on spacing / pushback / projectile hitstun)

cviper.name: Mission Complete
