cammy.name: Lift Uppercut
cammy.notes: Forces stand; Extended arm hurtbox is invincible to airborne strikes on frame 7-9 (active frames 3-5); Good anti-air against vertical approaches; Combos into naturally from jabs; Plus on block and can frame trap into stand / crouch LP with much better strike/throw pressure when used out of Drive Rush; Although this move has strong frame advantage against grounded opponents, active frames 4-5 whiff on Crouching opponents as Cammy punches above her head (if you want to meaty with it, keep in mind active frame 3 is the last frame that can connect on a crouching opponent, resulting in +6 on Hit / +3 on Block); Leads into the HK target combo launcher (17F hit confirm window)

cammy.name: Assault Blade
cammy.notes: Jump cancelable on HIT only; Launches the opponent into a limited juggle state on hit (free juggle state when used from Drive Rush); Cannot hit crouching; Good anti-air; Counts as 2 hits of damage scaling when used as the start of a combo

cammy.name: Delayed Ripper
cammy.notes: Cammy pulls back her hurtboxes far back on frames 5-14 as she leans back before the kick; Good auto-shimmy tool that launches opponents into a limited juggle state and is fully cancelable; +5F extra recovery frames (25F) on whiff or block; Incurs 20% damage scaling penalty if used as the first hit of a combo

cammy.name: Lift Combination
cammy.notes: Jump cancelable on HIT only; Launches the opponent into a limited juggle state on hit; Cannot hit crouching (-17 on crouch block when the HK follow-up whiffs)

cammy.name: Swing Combination
cammy.notes: First hit of the HK follow-up is cancelable into Cannon Strike (Divekick) and Level 2 Super; Second hit of the HK follow-up is fully cancelable; Leaves a large gap on block before a Divekick cancel or second hit of HK (opponent can always interrupt this); Last hit incurs 10% immediate scaling onto itself and 10% extra damage scaling on the follow-up hit if used in the middle of a combo; Both hits of the HK effectively count as separate hits in terms of damage scaling; Puts the opponent into a limited juggle state on hit

cammy.name: Rough Landing
cammy.notes: Throw Loop (Corner only): Walk forward into manually timed strike/throw mixup; Punish Counter gives +70% (2040) damage, Hard Knockdown (denies back-roll option on wake-up), depletes 1 bar of Drive gauge from the opponent, and builds twice as much Super gauge for the attacker; Throw Escape builds 0.5 Drive bars for the defender (randomly assigned if throws are input simultaneously)

cammy.name: Delta Throw
cammy.notes: Throw Oki (Corner only): Drive Rush into meaty strikes but no real throw oki; Punish Counter gives +70% (2040) damage, Hard Knockdown (denies back-roll option on wake-up), depletes 1 bar of Drive gauge from the opponent, and builds twice as much Super gauge for the attacker; Throw Escape builds 0.5 Drive bars for the defender (randomly assigned if throws are input simultaneously)

cammy.name: Leg Scissors Choke
cammy.notes: Throw Oki (Corner only): Manually timed strike / throw mix; Punish Counter gives +70% (2040) damage, Hard Knockdown (denies back-roll option on wake-up), depletes 1 bar of Drive gauge from the opponent, and builds twice as much Super gauge for both players

cammy.name: Drive Impact: Spin Raider
cammy.notes: 2 hits of armor on frames 1-27; Damages opponents Drive Gauge on Block (1/2 bar) | Hit (1 bar) | Counter-Hit (1.25 bar) | Punish Counter (1.5 bar); Knocks down on hit; Pushes the opponent far back on hit or block and causes a Wall Splat if they hit the wall (Parry prevents the backwards stumble and Wall Splat, greatly reducing the pushback); Regular KDA without Wall Splat +35 KD | Wall Splat on Hit +65 KD | Wall Splat on Block +72 HKD; KDA can vary greatly depending on how high the opponent wall splats (higher KDA the higher they wall splat); Advantage after Wall Splat can vary depending on distance from the corner (farther from corner gives higher advantage); Crumples the opponent on Punish Counter or after absorbing at least 1 attack during start-up (+21 frames before the crumple state goes airborne, followed by airborne state on frames 22-46 before they are grounded); Puts airborne opponents into a long spinning free juggle state when hit as a Punish Counter or after absorbing an attack; If the armor absorbs an attack it slows the overall start-up by 1F (27F total instead of 26F) and incurs 6F hitstop for each projectile hit absorbed (making it less likely to punish the opponent after absorbing projectiles); Absorbing an attack causes the player to take 1/2 the damage in recoverable health (but will KO if this would bring the player's health below zero); Stun/Dizzy occurs when a Wall Splat connects on an opponent in Burnout; Stun gives a free combo follow-up for the next 195F after hitting the wall, followed by a HKD if the player falls to the ground untouched (the last 7F before hitting the ground has a crouch-sized hurtbox but is considered standing, allowing for unique combo setups); Incurs 20% damage scaling penalty if used as the first hit of a combo (applies to wall splat on HIT, crumple, Burnout dizzy on hit/block, or any character-specific means of comboing after a regular Drive Impact); Incurs a 20% multiplier damage scaling penalty after a Wall Splat on BLOCK - Because the blocked Drive Impact is not considered a "hit" for the combo, the next attack can incur its own separate damage scaling as a combo starter; Wall Splat puts opponent into a special juggle state where the next move freely connects and continues the juggle even if it normally wouldn't (similar to a Forced Knockdown or Drive Rush juggle properties); Does not cause Wall Splat if the Drive Impact connects as a combo or a true blockstring with no gaps (LOCK icon appears on-screen); It is possible to "combo" into Stun if the opponent has under 1.5 Drive bars - a blocked DI Wall Splat from slightly outside the corner into a second DI on hit will cause Burnout and Stun (because the blocked DI is not technically considered a combo starter); Costs 1 bar of Drive Gauge; Cinematic slowdown occurs if both players activate Drive Impact within range of each other (granting a Punish Counter to the player who activates it later); Attempting to counter with DI vs. DI with under 400 HP will result in a KO, as the second player will not have enough health to absorb it; Clashes with other Drive Impacts and refunds the Drive gauge cost if they collide on the same active frame (start at exactly the same time, or 1F apart if the first Drive Impact absorbs a strike) - The meter refund does not prevent Burnout from occurring; The scrub killer

cammy.name: Drive Reversal: Countersnipe
cammy.notes: Has two versions: one performed during blockstun or parry stun (20F start-up) and one performed as a wake-up reversal (18F start-up); Fully invincible on frames 1-22 (blockstun) / frames 1-20 (reversal); Armor Break (blows through all armor like Drive Impact, but not counters like JP's Amnesia); Trying to Drive Reversal after the blockstun ends results in a Drive Impact; Drive Reversal immediately removes the current blockstun you're in and starts the attack; Causes a 4F screen freeze after the 6th start-up frame, which allows the opponent to perform a simple OS (inputting their buttons during the buffer window) to prevent their next attack from coming out; Safe on block (-2) when used against an opponent in Burnout; Costs 2 bars of Drive Gauge; If the opponent tries to throw against a wake-up Drive Reversal, it causes a 12F screen freeze and refunds 1 bar of Drive gauge (but does not prevent Burnout); Guaranteed to interrupt any Drive Rush canceled normal if performed immediately out of blockstun (unless the opponent reacts with an invincible move or counter)

cammy.name: 斗气招架 (Drive Parry)
cammy.notes: Parries all strikes and projectiles (high and low) from frame 1; 12F parry window (can hold the parry to extend the parry window); Perfect Parry occurs on the first 2 active frames (cannot achieve Perfect Parry if you buffer into parry by holding it during Reversal windows; Perfect Parries have to be timed properly); Can still hold charge directions during Parry (allowing characters with charge specials to stand block before performing their reversal); Can block during the recovery frames of a regular parry (can still get hit during the recovery frames if you don't block correctly); Getting thrown or hit at any point during the recovery frames of a whiffed parry attempt results in a Punish Counter; Successfully parrying a move puts you into the same amount of blockstun as that move would regularly do on block (but a Perfect Parry has only 1F of recovery); Throw invincible during the recovery of a successful parry (just like during blockstun); Perfect Parrying a strike has only 1F of recovery and disables the opponent from canceling their attack (basically a guaranteed punish opportunity except for safe jump setups); Perfect Parrying a strike requires holding the correct block direction (Down+Back for low strikes, Back for high/mid strikes); Attempting a Perfect Parry with the wrong block direction results in an "imperfect parry" that builds an extra 3000 Drive Gauge and plays a distinct audio/visual cue; After a successful Perfect Parry, you suffer a 50% penalty to your Damage, Drive Gauge Generation, and Drive Gauge Damage on any of your following attacks when punishing the opponent (in addition, both you and the opponent suffer a 20% penalty to your Super Meter gain during this period); Fully invincible for 6F after a successful Perfect Parry against a strike, which carries over to any attack you perform (ensuring a 5F or faster punish will always interrupt multi-hit attacks); Perfect Parrying projectiles puts you into fixed 10 frames of recovery and applies the same 50% scaling penalties (and 20% Super Meter penalty) on your following attacks when punishing the opponent; Parrying a Strike and Projectile on the same frame will result in a regular parry for the strike attack (effectively ignoring the projectile's hitstop / blockstun); Perfect Parrying a Strike and Projectile on the same frame will give a screen freeze like you Perfect Parried a Strike, but still give you 10F recovery as if you had Perfect Parried a Projectile; Can cancel into Drive Rush during active frames 3 and onward (fastest Drive Rush method is to buffer a forward input before doing parry + forward again); Can cancel into Drive Reversal from a successful parry (just like you normally can during blockstun); Costs 1/2 bar of Drive Gauge and continues to deplete 50 Drive Gauge per frame (0.3 Drive bars per second) as you hold the Parry; You lose the parry if you go into Burnout from the initial Drive Gauge cost (Perfect Parry requires frame-perfect timing when starting from under 1/2 of a Drive bar); Rewards 1 bar of Drive Gauge (1/2 bar total after factoring in the initial parry cost) for successfully parrying a strike; Rewards 1/2 bar of Drive Gauge (0 bar total after factoring in the initial parry cost) for successfully parrying a projectile (with a few exceptions); Rewards 2 bars of Drive Gauge (1.5 bars total after factoring in the initial parry cost) for successful parrying a Super Art or Drive Impact; Successfully parrying a strike attack splits the regular block pushback between both players (while Perfect Parrying a strike removes all of its pushback); Successfully parrying a projectile or Drive Impact reduces the pushback of it by half (while Perfect Parrying a projectile or Drive Impact removes all of its pushback); Your hurtbox and throw box expand slightly towards the opponent for the entire duration of the Parry (Throw box extension starts instantly on frame 1, while the Hurtbox extension starts on frame 3, after the initial 2F Perfect Parry window); Parrying while crouching maintains a regular crouch hurtbox for the first 2 frames of the parry (during the initial Perfect Parry window)

cammy.name: 斗气冲刺 (Drive Rush)
cammy.notes: Dashes forward and enhances the next normal or command normal used out of the Drive Rush with +4 extra hitstun / blockstun, as well as improved juggle properties (Juggle Limit increased by +3 / Juggle Start/Increase reduced to 0); The +4 bonus frame advantage gained from a Drive Rush enhanced move also stacks with any bonus frame advantage that move may have gained from Counter-Hit, Punish Counter, or Burnout; Grounded special-cancelable normals can also be canceled into Drive Rush on hit or block, as well as from light normals on whiff; Drive Rush maintains buffers (freezes the buffer window) during its start-up and freeze frames - This allows players to do things normally not possible within the normal buffer windows, such as Drive Rushing into a charge special; The initial 10F screen freeze eats the opponent's directional inputs (except Jumps) but does not prevent attacks from being buffered immediately afterward (this can cause inputs to be combined in unintended ways, such as crouch MK + Fireball performing a raw Fireball, or a vertical jump + walk forward turning into a forward jump); Framedata shown in parentheses refers to the Drive Rush version used from a Parry; Drive Rush recovery is only 24F total (23F if done from a Parry) - but the enhanced dash itself is 46F total (45F if done from Parry) and you can cancel it as early as frame 9 (frame 11 if done from a Parry); Inputting a direction (walk/crouch/block/jump) after the Drive Rush recovery plays out 2 additional recovery frames before the transition occurs (this allows the user to perform an enhanced crouching or command normal late in the dash by inputting the direction + button simultaneously); You stop building any form of Drive Gauge on your attacks after using a Drive Rush in the MIDDLE of a combo (but you still continue to build Drive gauge as normal if you did Drive Rush at the START of a combo); Applies an extra damage scaling penalty after using a Drive Rush in the MIDDLE of a combo (no damage scaling if you use Drive Rush at the START of a combo); Costs 3 bars of Drive Gauge if canceled into from a normal attack; Costs 1/2 bar of Drive Gauge if canceled into from Parry (for a total of 1 bar of Drive Gauge when you factor in the initial 1/2 bar cost of the Parry); Normals used out of Drive Rush carry additional forward momentum (but throws and specials immediately halt all momentum, which can be a useful strategy to punish opponents for trying to interrupt your Drive Rush); Parry Drive Rush can only be initiated after frame 3 of the Parry (but can be performed immediately after recovering from a successful parry); Parry Drive Rush cannot be initiated with less than 1/2 of a Drive bar (as the initial Parry cost will put the user into Burnout) - But whiff canceling a Light normal into Drive Rush can achieve a similar effect; Cannot cancel Drive Rush into a Parry (inputting MP+MK results in a MK normal coming out instead); Drive Rush puts the user into a counter-hit state for the entire duration (this makes it impossible to tech a throw that connects during the dash)

chunli.name: 站中脚 (5MK)
chunli.notes: Cannot hit crouching; Solid anti-air; Cannot hit cross-up (behind Chun-Li)

chunli.name: 站重脚 (5HK)
chunli.notes: Cannot hit crouching; Mid range horizontal anti-air; Extended leg and head hurtbox are invincible to airborne strikes on frames 14-16; Cannot hit cross-up (behind Chun-Li); Puts airborne opponents into a limited juggle state on hit (free juggle state on Punish Counter); Incurs a 20% damage scaling penalty if used as the first hit of a combo; Cancelable into Serenity Stream (Crouch Stance) with 12F start-up (much worse frame advantage noted in parantheses if you don't immediately do a follow-up from the stance)

chunli.name: 蹲轻拳 (2LP)
chunli.notes: Chains into stand LP / crouch LP / crouch LK; Incurs 20% damage scaling penalty if used as the first hit of a combo

chunli.name: 蹲中拳 (2MP)
chunli.notes: Decent range and disjointed for a poke; +1F extra recovery frame (14F) on whiff; Topmost hurtboxes on frames 1-9 are vulnerable only to airborne attacks (this is to discourage its use as an anti-air)

chunli.name: 蹲重拳 (2HP)
chunli.notes: Forces stand; Only cancelable on the second hit; Solid anti-air on frames 12-13 and again on frames 21-23; Cannot hit cross-up (behind Chun-Li); Carries over Counter-Hit / Punish Counter bonus frame advantage to both hits; First hit puts airborne opponents into a limited juggle state (second hit air resets them, but can whiff in certain scenarios); Cancelable into Serenity Stream (Crouch Stance) with 11F start-up (much worse frame advantage noted in parantheses if you don't immediately do a follow-up from the stance)

chunli.name: 蹲轻脚 (2LK)
chunli.notes: Special cancelable (unlike most other crouch LKs); Chains into stand LP / crouch LP / crouch LK; Incurs 20% damage scaling penalty if used as the first hit of a combo

chunli.name: 蹲中脚 (2MK)
chunli.notes: Good start-up and range low poke and combo tool; Incurs a 20% damage scaling penalty if used as the first hit of a combo

chunli.name: 蹲重脚 (2HK)
chunli.notes: +2F extra recovery frames (21F) on block; Cancelable into Serenity Stream (Crouch Stance) with 23F start-up (much worse frame advantage noted in parantheses if you don't immediately do a follow-up from the stance); Knockdown advantage when canceling into Serenity Stream (Crouch Stance) depends on what Chun-Li does afterwards: Remain in Crouch Stance: +36 KD | Exiting stance manually early (inputting QCB+P again): +13 KD (+17 KD if you cancel the stance exit early into other moves) | -8 KD (punishable) if Chun-Li doesn't remain in Crouch Stance or exit it manually early (inputting QCB+P again); Has more active frames than most sweeps (can be as safe as -4 with meaty timing)

chunli.name: 跳轻拳 (j.LP)
chunli.notes: Can be used as a fuzzy instant Overhead against tall characters (DJ / JP / Marisa / Sagat / Zangief) after a deep jump-in Medium / Heavy

chunli.name: 跳中拳 (j.MP)
chunli.notes: Both hits put airborne opponents into a juggle state; Cancelable into Air Legs or Level 1 air Super; Shifts the normal jumping hurtbox upward during start-up (helps with avoiding some attacks)

chunli.name: 跳重拳 (j.HP)
chunli.notes: Puts airborne opponents into a juggle state; Deals 300 less damage (500) against airborne opponents)

chunli.name: 跳中脚 (j.MK)
chunli.notes: Cross-up; Decent air-to-air

chunli.name: 跳重脚 (j.HK)
chunli.notes: Shifts the normal jumping hurtbox upward during start-up (helps with avoiding some attacks)

chunli.name: Neutral Jump HK
chunli.notes: Hits on both sides of Chun-Li; Decent air-to-air; Shifts the normal jumping hurtbox upward during start-up (helps with avoiding some attacks)

chunli.name: Wall Jump
chunli.notes: Forced Knockdown and Counter-Hit state for the entire duration of the jump; Can be performed after any jump direction as long as the wall is in range

chunli.name: Yoso Kick
chunli.notes: Not an Overhead; All 3 hits can cross-up; Puts airborne opponents into a juggle state; Cancelable into airborne Lighting Kicks and Level 1 Super; Can be canceled into other air normals as well; Forced Knockdown state after the bounce on Hit / Block; First stomp incurs a 15% damage scaling when hit as the start of a combo

chunli.name: Soaring Eagle Punches
chunli.notes: Puts airborne opponents into a juggle state; Target combo can be performed on whiff; Huge hitstun/blockstun against grounded opponents on the 2nd hit, allowing for unique follow-up combos / blockstring pressure that is normally impossible after a jump-in normal

chunli.name: Swift Thrust
chunli.notes: Fantastic poke / combo / buffer tool

chunli.name: Hakkei
chunli.notes: Short range combo / frametrap tool; Cancelable into Serenity Stream (Crouch Stance) with 11F start-up (much worse frame advantage noted in parantheses if you don't immediately do a follow-up from the stance)

chunli.name: Water Lotus Fist
chunli.notes: Overhead; Cancelable into Serenity Stream (Crouch Stance) with 16F start-up (much worse frame advantage noted in parantheses if you don't immediately do a follow-up from the stance)

chunli.name: Yokusen Kick
chunli.notes: Airborne on frames 8-28 (Forced Knockdown state); Crushes low attacks on frames 6-28; Causes a Crumple state on Punish Counter, which can lead to a grounded follow-up if canceled into Serenity Stream (Crouch Stance); Causes a spinning free juggle state on Punish Counter against airborne opponents; Huge hitbox priority; Cancelable into Serenity Stream (Crouch Stance) with 20F start-up (much worse frame advantage noted in parantheses if you don't immediately do a follow-up from the stance); There is a minor brief extended lower hurtbox on frame 15 of start-up (1F before active) that is strike invincible (less likely to counter-poke projectiles)

chunli.name: Falling Crane
chunli.notes: Overhead; Airborne on frames 7-39 (Forced Knockdown state); Can only hit cross-up (Chun-Li has to jump over the the opponent); Puts airborne opponents into a limited juggle state on hit; 1F better frame advantage listed in the parentheses refers to when hitting most crouching opponents (with the exception of taller characters like: DJ, JP, Marisa, Sagat, Zangief)

chunli.name: Serenity Stream
chunli.notes: Stance moves do not require charge for specials when canceling; Remains in stance for as long as you hold any down direction; Can block while in stance (but not while exiting the stance!) which causes Chun-Li to exit stance automatically (Chun-Li can immediately Drive Reversal after blocking while in stance); If Chun extends her Stance time by holding down it becomes impossible for her to block Overheads (since standing forces her to exit Stance first); Low profiles and projectile invincible on head hurtbox on frames 23-71 (this can be extended by holding down to maintain stance, but the low profile and projectile invincibility is lost immediately upon exiting stance); Chun-Li is in a Counter-Hit state while in stance (and also while entering / exiting stance); Crouching state while in stance (crouching state starts at frame 14 of start-up and remains crouching until the last 14F recovery when exiting stance); The 14F start-up listed refers to how long it takes for Chun-Li to enter Crouch Stance when performed raw or when canceled into from Light / Medium normals (however Chun-Li can start blocking 1F earlier after just 13F of start-up); How long it takes to enter Crouch Stance also further varies depending on which Heavy normal was canceled from (see notes on said Heavy normals); Heavy normals canceled into Crouch Stance have much more negative frame advantage if they are not immediately followed up with a stance normal (this is shown in the stance cancel framedata of each respective Heavy normal); How long it takes to exit Crouch Stance depends on which move Chun-Li used from the stance (see notes on the follow-up moves); Can also manually cancel the Crouch Stance early by inputting Up or doing the QCB+P input again (before inputting any follow-up): 23F recovery (but this recovery can be canceled into other moves after only 18F); Letting go of any down direction and exiting stance: 18F recovery; The most convoluted move Hatson has ever had to do framedata and notes for

chunli.name: Orchid Palm
chunli.notes: Low profiles slightly on frames 1-25 (the entire duration of the move); Remains in Crouch Stance if you continue holding down; Framedata listed in parentheses (X) is if you exit stance (stop holding down) after performing the move (it is recommended that you either remain in Crouch Stance (hold any down direction) or cancel this move into something (your cancels require no charge while in Crouch Stance); Stance moves do not require charge for specials when canceling; Takes 20F to exit stance directly after using this move (Chun-Li can block for the first 2F before entering the 18F exit animation); Perfect Parry forces Chun-Li to exit the stance and puts her in a Punish Counter state for the entire stance exit animation (2F less total recovery)

chunli.name: Snake Strike
chunli.notes: Low hitting slide; Projectile invincible on upper body / Low Profile on frames 1-36 (the entire duration of the move) - but only frames 1-31 if you exit stance afterwards; Low profiles on frames 8-21; Remains in Crouch Stance if you continue holding down; Framedata and KDA listed in parentheses (X) is if you exit stance (stop holding down) after performing the move (it is recommended that you remain in Crouch Stance by holding any down direction); Takes 18F to exit stance after using this move; 1F worse advantage on Perfect Parry if Chun-Li continues to hold crouch; Chun-Li does not move forward on the final active frame (maximum frame advantage can only occur with meaty timing on the opponent's wakeup; Combos naturally from stand HP

chunli.name: Lotus Fist
chunli.notes: Overhead on first hit only, unless the first hit whiffs, then the second hit is an Overhead as well (but if the first hit connects, then the second hit can be blocked high or low); Low profiles on frames 1-2 (can be used to frame perfect dodge Drive Impacts); No head hurtbox on frames 29-42; Crouch state on first 5F of start-up; Exits Crouch Stance; Fully cancelable (rare property for an Overhead); Plus on block and leaves Chun-Li inside throw range (becomes much more powerful against burned out opponents); Stance moves do not require charge for specials when canceling

chunli.name: Forward Strike
chunli.notes: Remains in Crouch Stance if you continue holding down; Framedata listed in parentheses (X) is if you exit stance (stop holding down) after performing the move (it is recommended that you either remain in Crouch Stance (hold any down direction) or cancel this move into something (your cancels require no charge while in Crouch Stance); Stance moves do not require charge for specials when canceling; Takes 23F to exit stance directly after using this move (Chun-Li can block for the first 5F before entering the 18F exit animation); Perfect Parry forces Chun-Li to exit the stance and puts her in a Punish Counter state for the entire stance exit animation (5F less total recovery)

chunli.name: Senpu Kick
chunli.notes: Remains in Crouch Stance if you continue holding down; Framedata listed in parentheses (X) is if you exit stance (stop holding down) after performing the move (it is recommended that you either remain in Crouch Stance (hold any down direction) or cancel this move into something (your cancels require no charge while in Crouch Stance); Puts airborne opponents into a limited juggle state; Stance moves do not require charge for specials when canceling; Takes 24F to exit stance directly after using this move (Chun-Li can block for the first 6F before entering the 18F exit animation); Perfect Parry forces Chun-Li to exit the stance and puts her in a Punish Counter state for the entire stance exit animation (6F less total recovery)

chunli.name: Tenku Kick
chunli.notes: Jump cancelable on HIT only; Exits Crouch Stance; Crouching state during first 6F of start-up; Launches the opponent high into the air on hit

chunli.name: Koshuto
chunli.notes: Pseudo-Throw Loop: Frame-perfect walk forward throw beats 6F attacks on wake-up (corner only) - Beats 4F attacks (real throw loop) against wider characters like Alex / Blanka / Honda / Marisa / Sagat / Zangief; Punish Counter gives +70% (2040) damage, Hard Knockdown (denies back-roll option on wake-up), depletes 1 bar of Drive gauge from the opponent, and builds twice as much Super gauge for the attacker; Throw Escape builds 0.5 Drive bars for the defender (randomly assigned if throws are input simultaneously)

chunli.name: Taiji Fan
chunli.notes: Back Throw oki when cornered: Can walk up for a pseudo strike/throw loop or just Drive Rush in for a real strike/throw mix; Punish Counter gives +70% (2040) damage, Hard Knockdown (denies back-roll option on wake-up), depletes 1 bar of Drive gauge from the opponent, and builds twice as much Super gauge for the attacker; Throw Escape builds 0.5 Drive bars for the defender (randomly assigned if throws are input simultaneously)

chunli.name: Ryuseiraku
chunli.notes: Can Drive Rush into meaty strike after throwing opponent into the corner; Punish Counter gives +70% (2040) damage, Hard Knockdown (denies back-roll option on wake-up), depletes 1 bar of Drive gauge from the opponent, and builds twice as much Super gauge for both players; The return of SFV Cammy air throw animation

chunli.name: Drive Impact: Hosen Kick
chunli.notes: 2 hits of armor on frames 1-27; Damages opponents Drive Gauge on Block (1/2 bar) | Hit (1 bar) | Counter-Hit (1.25 bar) | Punish Counter (1.5 bar); Knocks down on hit; Pushes the opponent far back on hit or block and causes a Wall Splat if they hit the wall (Parry prevents the backwards stumble and Wall Splat, greatly reducing the pushback); Regular KDA without Wall Splat +35 KD | Wall Splat on Hit +65 KD | Wall Splat on Block +72 HKD; KDA can vary greatly depending on how high the opponent wall splats (higher KDA the higher they wall splat); Advantage after Wall Splat can vary depending on distance from the corner (farther from corner gives higher advantage); Crumples the opponent on Punish Counter or after absorbing at least 1 attack during start-up (+21 frames before the crumple state goes airborne, followed by airborne state on frames 22-46 before they are grounded); Puts airborne opponents into a long spinning free juggle state when hit as a Punish Counter or after absorbing an attack; If the armor absorbs an attack it slows the overall start-up by 1F (27F total instead of 26F) and incurs 6F hitstop for each projectile hit absorbed (making it less likely to punish the opponent after absorbing projectiles); Absorbing an attack causes the player to take 1/2 the damage in recoverable health (but will KO if this would bring the player's health below zero); Stun/Dizzy occurs when a Wall Splat connects on an opponent in Burnout; Stun gives a free combo follow-up for the next 195F after hitting the wall, followed by a HKD if the player falls to the ground untouched (the last 7F before hitting the ground has a crouch-sized hurtbox but is considered standing, allowing for unique combo setups); Incurs 20% damage scaling penalty if used as the first hit of a combo (applies to wall splat on HIT, crumple, Burnout dizzy on hit/block, or any character-specific means of comboing after a regular Drive Impact); Incurs a 20% multiplier damage scaling penalty after a Wall Splat on BLOCK - Because the blocked Drive Impact is not considered a "hit" for the combo, the next attack can incur its own separate damage scaling as a combo starter; Wall Splat puts opponent into a special juggle state where the next move freely connects and continues the juggle even if it normally wouldn't (similar to a Forced Knockdown or Drive Rush juggle properties); Does not cause Wall Splat if the Drive Impact connects as a combo or a true blockstring with no gaps (LOCK icon appears on-screen); It is possible to "combo" into Stun if the opponent has under 1.5 Drive bars - a blocked DI Wall Splat from slightly outside the corner into a second DI on hit will cause Burnout and Stun (because the blocked DI is not technically considered a combo starter); Costs 1 bar of Drive Gauge; Cinematic slowdown occurs if both players activate Drive Impact within range of each other (granting a Punish Counter to the player who activates it later); Attempting to counter with DI vs. DI with under 400 HP will result in a KO, as the second player will not have enough health to absorb it; Clashes with other Drive Impacts and refunds the Drive gauge cost if they collide on the same active frame (start at exactly the same time, or 1F apart if the first Drive Impact absorbs a strike) - The meter refund does not prevent Burnout from occurring; The scrub killer

chunli.name: Drive Reversal: Hoyoku Kick
chunli.notes: Has two versions: one performed during blockstun or parry stun (20F start-up) and one performed as a wake-up reversal (18F start-up); Fully invincible on frames 1-22 (blockstun) / frames 1-20 (reversal); Armor Break (blows through all armor like Drive Impact, but not counters like JP's Amnesia); Trying to Drive Reversal after the blockstun ends results in a Drive Impact; Drive Reversal immediately removes the current blockstun you're in and starts the attack; Causes a 4F screen freeze after the 6th start-up frame, which allows the opponent to perform a simple OS (inputting their buttons during the buffer window) to prevent their next attack from coming out; Safe on block (-2) when used against an opponent in Burnout; Costs 2 bars of Drive Gauge; If the opponent tries to throw against a wake-up Drive Reversal, it causes a 12F screen freeze and refunds 1 bar of Drive gauge (but does not prevent Burnout); Guaranteed to interrupt any Drive Rush canceled normal if performed immediately out of blockstun (unless the opponent reacts with an invincible move or counter)

chunli.name: 斗气招架 (Drive Parry)
chunli.notes: Parries all strikes and projectiles (high and low) from frame 1; 12F parry window (can hold the parry to extend the parry window); Perfect Parry occurs on the first 2 active frames (cannot achieve Perfect Parry if you buffer into parry by holding it during Reversal windows; Perfect Parries have to be timed properly); Can still hold charge directions during Parry (allowing characters with charge specials to stand block before performing their reversal); Can block during the recovery frames of a regular parry (can still get hit during the recovery frames if you don't block correctly); Getting thrown or hit at any point during the recovery frames of a whiffed parry attempt results in a Punish Counter; Successfully parrying a move puts you into the same amount of blockstun as that move would regularly do on block (but a Perfect Parry has only 1F of recovery); Throw invincible during the recovery of a successful parry (just like during blockstun); Perfect Parrying a strike has only 1F of recovery and disables the opponent from canceling their attack (basically a guaranteed punish opportunity except for safe jump setups); Perfect Parrying a strike requires holding the correct block direction (Down+Back for low strikes, Back for high/mid strikes); Attempting a Perfect Parry with the wrong block direction results in an "imperfect parry" that builds an extra 3000 Drive Gauge and plays a distinct audio/visual cue; After a successful Perfect Parry, you suffer a 50% penalty to your Damage, Drive Gauge Generation, and Drive Gauge Damage on any of your following attacks when punishing the opponent (in addition, both you and the opponent suffer a 20% penalty to your Super Meter gain during this period); Fully invincible for 6F after a successful Perfect Parry against a strike, which carries over to any attack you perform (ensuring a 5F or faster punish will always interrupt multi-hit attacks); Perfect Parrying projectiles puts you into fixed 10 frames of recovery and applies the same 50% scaling penalties (and 20% Super Meter penalty) on your following attacks when punishing the opponent; Parrying a Strike and Projectile on the same frame will result in a regular parry for the strike attack (effectively ignoring the projectile's hitstop / blockstun); Perfect Parrying a Strike and Projectile on the same frame will give a screen freeze like you Perfect Parried a Strike, but still give you 10F recovery as if you had Perfect Parried a Projectile; Can cancel into Drive Rush during active frames 3 and onward (fastest Drive Rush method is to buffer a forward input before doing parry + forward again); Can cancel into Drive Reversal from a successful parry (just like you normally can during blockstun); Costs 1/2 bar of Drive Gauge and continues to deplete 50 Drive Gauge per frame (0.3 Drive bars per second) as you hold the Parry; You lose the parry if you go into Burnout from the initial Drive Gauge cost (Perfect Parry requires frame-perfect timing when starting from under 1/2 of a Drive bar); Rewards 1 bar of Drive Gauge (1/2 bar total after factoring in the initial parry cost) for successfully parrying a strike; Rewards 1/2 bar of Drive Gauge (0 bar total after factoring in the initial parry cost) for successfully parrying a projectile (with a few exceptions); Rewards 2 bars of Drive Gauge (1.5 bars total after factoring in the initial parry cost) for successful parrying a Super Art or Drive Impact; Successfully parrying a strike attack splits the regular block pushback between both players (while Perfect Parrying a strike removes all of its pushback); Successfully parrying a projectile or Drive Impact reduces the pushback of it by half (while Perfect Parrying a projectile or Drive Impact removes all of its pushback); Your hurtbox and throw box expand slightly towards the opponent for the entire duration of the Parry (Throw box extension starts instantly on frame 1, while the Hurtbox extension starts on frame 3, after the initial 2F Perfect Parry window); Parrying while crouching maintains a regular crouch hurtbox for the first 2 frames of the parry (during the initial Perfect Parry window)

chunli.name: 斗气冲刺 (Drive Rush)
chunli.notes: Dashes forward and enhances the next normal or command normal used out of the Drive Rush with +4 extra hitstun / blockstun, as well as improved juggle properties (Juggle Limit increased by +3 / Juggle Start/Increase reduced to 0); The +4 bonus frame advantage gained from a Drive Rush enhanced move also stacks with any bonus frame advantage that move may have gained from Counter-Hit, Punish Counter, or Burnout; Grounded special-cancelable normals can also be canceled into Drive Rush on hit or block, as well as from light normals on whiff; Drive Rush maintains buffers (freezes the buffer window) during its start-up and freeze frames - This allows players to do things normally not possible within the normal buffer windows, such as Drive Rushing into a charge special; The initial 10F screen freeze eats the opponent's directional inputs (except Jumps) but does not prevent attacks from being buffered immediately afterward (this can cause inputs to be combined in unintended ways, such as crouch MK + Fireball performing a raw Fireball, or a vertical jump + walk forward turning into a forward jump); Framedata shown in parentheses refers to the Drive Rush version used from a Parry; Drive Rush recovery is only 24F total (23F if done from a Parry) - but the enhanced dash itself is 46F total (45F if done from Parry) and you can cancel it as early as frame 9 (frame 11 if done from a Parry); Inputting a direction (walk/crouch/block/jump) after the Drive Rush recovery plays out 2 additional recovery frames before the transition occurs (this allows the user to perform an enhanced crouching or command normal late in the dash by inputting the direction + button simultaneously); You stop building any form of Drive Gauge on your attacks after using a Drive Rush in the MIDDLE of a combo (but you still continue to build Drive gauge as normal if you did Drive Rush at the START of a combo); Applies an extra damage scaling penalty after using a Drive Rush in the MIDDLE of a combo (no damage scaling if you use Drive Rush at the START of a combo); Costs 3 bars of Drive Gauge if canceled into from a normal attack; Costs 1/2 bar of Drive Gauge if canceled into from Parry (for a total of 1 bar of Drive Gauge when you factor in the initial 1/2 bar cost of the Parry); Normals used out of Drive Rush carry additional forward momentum (but throws and specials immediately halt all momentum, which can be a useful strategy to punish opponents for trying to interrupt your Drive Rush); Parry Drive Rush can only be initiated after frame 3 of the Parry (but can be performed immediately after recovering from a successful parry); Parry Drive Rush cannot be initiated with less than 1/2 of a Drive bar (as the initial Parry cost will put the user into Burnout) - But whiff canceling a Light normal into Drive Rush can achieve a similar effect; Cannot cancel Drive Rush into a Parry (inputting MP+MK results in a MK normal coming out instead); Drive Rush puts the user into a counter-hit state for the entire duration (this makes it impossible to tech a throw that connects during the dash)

chunli.name: Taunt
chunli.notes: Neutral Taunt actually has a hit attached to it that does 300 damage and is -58 / -65 on Hit / Block; Causes a crumple-like state on Punish Counter

chunli.name: Lightning Kick Barrage
chunli.notes: 10 hits total; Follow-up is only possible on hit / block; Maintains the same damage scaling percentage as the initial OD Lightning Legs

chunli.name: Kikosho
chunli.notes: Strike and Throw invincible on frames 1-7; 5-hit Super projectile; Armor Break; Depletes 0.5 Drive Bar on hit for the opponent; Can hit cross-up (behind Chun-Li); Minimum damage scaling of 30%

chunli.name: Aerial Kikosho
chunli.notes: Strike and Throw invincible on frame 1 only (during screen freeze); 5-hit Super projectile; 16F landing recovery frames (total recovery frames vary depending on how high from the ground the Super was performed); Armor Break; Depletes 0.5 Drive Bar on hit for the opponent; Can hit cross-up (behind Chun-Li); Minimum damage scaling of 30%

chunli.name: Hoyoku-sen
chunli.notes: Fully invincible frames 1-12; Last hit is jump cancelable by holding up (Chun-Li always jumps forward); Armor Break; Depletes 1 Drive Bar on hit for the opponent; Minimum damage scaling of 40%; Launches the opponent into a free juggle state on hit (or maintains the current juggle state); Incurs a 40% damage scaling penalty if used as the first hit of a combo; Counts as 3 hits of damage scaling when combo'd into; 30% penalty to Super meter gain on any of the follow-up hits she combos into after this move

chunli.name: Soten Ranka
chunli.notes: Fully invincible frames 1-9; No cinematic if the first hit whiffs (the following 2 hits on whiff do 1000 damage together); Armor Break; Depletes 1.5 Drive Bars on hit for the opponent; Super cinematic time regenerates ~1.8 Drive Bars for Chun-Li; Minimum damage scaling of 50%; Incurs 10% damage scaling when canceled into from specials

chunli.name: Soten Ranka (Critical Art)
chunli.notes: Fully invincible frames 1-9; Critical Art does +500 damage over regular version; No cinematic if the first hit whiffs (the following 2 hits on whiff do 1000 damage together); Armor Break; Depletes 2 Drive Bars on hit for the opponent; Super cinematic time regenerates ~2 Drive Bars for Chun-Li; Minimum damage scaling of 50%; Incurs 10% damage scaling when canceled into from specials

chunli.name: 气功拳
chunli.notes: 1-hit projectile; Projectile Speed: 0.05; Travels around 80% screen length; Projectile lasts 55f; Takes 50 frames to charge (holds charge for 10F after leaving charge); Does not require charge if canceled into from Stance moves

variations.notes: 1-hit projectile; Projectile Speed: 0.037; Travels around 90% screen length; Projectile lasts 90f; Takes 50 frames to charge (holds charge for 10F after leaving charge); Does not require charge if canceled into from Stance moves

1-hit projectile; Projectile Speed: 0.05; Travels around 80% screen length; Projectile lasts 55f; Takes 50 frames to charge (holds charge for 10F after leaving charge); Does not require charge if canceled into from Stance moves

1-hit projectile; Projectile Speed: 0.07; Travels around 60% screen length; Projectile lasts 25f; Takes 50 frames to charge (holds charge for 10F after leaving charge); Does not require charge if canceled into from Stance moves

2-hit OD projectile; Projectile Speed: 0.095; Travels full screen; Projectile lasts 29f; Takes 45 frames to charge (holds charge for 10F after leaving charge); Does not require charge if canceled into from Stance moves; Incurs a 20% damage scaling penalty if used as the first hit of a combo

chunli.name: Hundred Lightning Kicks
chunli.notes: 4 hits; Carries over Counter-Hit / Punish Counter bonus frame advantage to all hits; Puts airborne opponents into a limited juggle state on hit

variations.notes: 3 hits; Carries over Counter-Hit bonus frame advantage to all hits; Puts airborne opponents into a limited juggle state on hit; Puts grounded opponents into a free juggle state knockdown on Punish Counter (can follow-up with a jab air reset pressure in the corner); Very fast start-up and good range makes this a great punish tool for things otherwise not in range of Chun-Li's light attacks
4 hits; Carries over Counter-Hit / Punish Counter bonus frame advantage to all hits; Puts airborne opponents into a limited juggle state on hit
5 hits; Puts the opponent into a limited juggle state on hit

5 hits; Carries over Counter-Hit bonus frame advantage to all hits; Can be followed up on hit / block with an extension by pressing 2 kick buttons (KK) again; Puts the opponent into a Crumple state on a grounded Punish Counter that leads to all sorts of combo extensions (+11 before opponent becomes airborne, followed by airborne juggle frames); Puts airborne opponents into a limited juggle state (free juggle state on airborne Punish Counter); Long range makes it a useful midscreen juggle option after HK Lightning Kicks

chunli.name: Aerial Hundred Lightning Kicks
chunli.notes: 4 hits; Only possible during neutral or forward jump; Whiffs on crouching; Crouching state during the entire landing recovery frames; Recovery frames listed refers to the landing recovery frames (not including the variable air time); +3F extra landing recovery frames (18F) on whiff; Puts airborne opponents into a limited juggle state on hit; Forced Knockdown state while airborne; Incurs a 20% damage scaling penalty if used as the first hit of a combo

deejay.name: 站轻拳 (5LP)
deejay.notes: Chains into stand LP / crouch LP / crouch LK; Fastest jab check in the game with barely any recovery frames makes this the safest meaty jab oki there is; Incurs 20% damage scaling penalty if used as the first hit of a combo

deejay.name: 站中拳 (5MP)
deejay.notes: Good combo and frametrap tool that can also go into two different target combos

deejay.name: 站重拳 (5HP)
deejay.notes: Forces stand on active frames 1-2 (vital for his Jackknife Maximum combo routes); Strong combo / whiff punish tool with great range and lots of active frames (can easily convert into combos if spaced properly); Situational anti-air when used at range; Active frames 3-6 whiff on crouching opponents (don't try to use this against crouching opponents from further away); Only cancelable on the first 2 active frames and deals 100 less damage (700) on active frames 3-6; Incurs 20% damage scaling penalty if used as the first hit of a combo

deejay.name: 站轻脚 (5LK)
deejay.notes: DJs only light button that combos into HK Sobat on hit and into OD Sobat in Punish situations, making this a good buffer tool; Incurs 20% damage scaling penalty if used as the first hit of a combo

deejay.name: 站中脚 (5MK)
deejay.notes: Combo starter as well as a decent poke tool

deejay.name: 站重脚 (5HK)
deejay.notes: Good range poke and whiff punish tool that leads to Drive Rush combos on Punish Counter; Puts airborne opponents into a limited juggle state on Punish Counter; The brief extended leg hurtbox on frame 11 of start-up (1F before active) is strike invincible (cannot counter-poke projectiles); +4F extra recovery frames (26F) on whiff; Incurs 20% damage scaling penalty if used as the first hit of a combo

deejay.name: 蹲轻拳 (2LP)
deejay.notes: Chains into stand LP / crouch LP / crouch LK; Incurs 20% damage scaling penalty if used as the first hit of a combo; Topmost hurtboxes on frames 1-7 are vulnerable only to airborne attacks (this is to discourage its use as an anti-air)

deejay.name: 蹲中拳 (2MP)
deejay.notes: Core buffer / combo tool and also applicable in a lot of oki / meaty situations; Has very good hitbox priority against low attacks; +1F extra recovery frame (15F) on whiff; Fully cancelable and hit confirmable (19F hit confirm window) makes this Dee Jay's best buffer tool in neutral; Hitconfirm window is shorter when canceled into MP Machine Gun Upper (13F) or OD Sobat Kick (18F) due to their slower startup

deejay.name: 蹲重拳 (2HP)
deejay.notes: Combo tool and a decent counterpoke with good hitbox priority; Forces stand (vital for his Jackknife Maximum combo routes); Puts airborne opponents into a limited juggle state on Punish Counter (and results in a +71~74 Hard Knockdown)

deejay.name: 蹲轻脚 (2LK)
deejay.notes: Chains into stand LP / crouch LP / crouch LK; Incurs 20% damage scaling penalty if used as the first hit of a combo

deejay.name: 蹲中脚 (2MK)
deejay.notes: Unorthodox sweep that only causes Hard Knockdown on Punish Counter; Good hitbox priority for a low attack; Can be very hard to punish on block for some characters even when used up close

deejay.name: 蹲重脚 (2HK)
deejay.notes: Upper body and legs are invincible to airborne strikes on frames 12-23; Solid anti-air (but slow start-up); Puts airborne opponents into a limited juggle state (better juggle scenarios on Counter Hit and Punish)

deejay.name: 跳轻拳 (j.LP)
deejay.notes: Can be used as an instant Overhead

deejay.name: 跳中拳 (j.MP)
deejay.notes: Puts airborne opponents into a limited juggle state; Very lenient cancel window (25F) for the follow-up HP air target combo; Shifts the normal jumping hurtbox upward during start-up (helps with avoiding some attacks)

deejay.name: 跳重拳 (j.HP)
deejay.notes: Spikes down airborne opponents on hit

deejay.name: 跳轻脚 (j.LK)
deejay.notes: Situational air-to-air

deejay.name: 跳中脚 (j.MK)
deejay.notes: Cross-up

deejay.name: 跳重脚 (j.HK)
deejay.notes: Decent jump-in that hits in front of Dee Jay before swinging his leg downward

deejay.name: Knee Shot
deejay.notes: Alters DJ's trajectory causing him to fall slightly faster towards the ground, allowing DJ to manipulate his jump arcs and his pressure or setup options from a jump (up to 5F shorter airborne frames overall compared to a regular jump); Only possible during a forward jump; Active frames last until landing; Has a much larger hurtbox than regular jump-ins making this move easily get hit out of the air; Punish Counter state from active frame 2 and onward

deejay.name: Party in the Air
deejay.notes: First hit (MP) puts airborne opponents into a limited juggle state and the second hit (HP) spikes down airborne opponents on hit

deejay.name: Sunrise Heel
deejay.notes: Not an Overhead (despite looking like one); Plus on block normal with good range that combos naturally even from further away (even better combos when spaced out slightly); First 2 active frames cannot hit grounded opponents (only hits airborne); Doesn't hit crouching opponents until active frame 4 which grants Dee Jay +1 extra frame advantage (+6 oH / +2 oB); Framedata listed in parentheses (X) refers to when used against crouching opponents; Strong oki / meaty tool; Cancelable into all Supers; Puts airborne opponents into a limited juggle OTG bounce (can be followed up with any Super cancel, or OD Jackknife / OD Jus Cool on a high connect anti-air); First 3 active frames have very strong anti-air hitboxes (although extremely slow start-up for an anti-air)

deejay.name: Face Breaker
deejay.notes: Head hurtbox is invincible to airborne strikes on frames 4-12; Forces stand (vital for his Jackknife Maximum combo routes); Good anti-air and combo tool that's also fully cancelable; Cannot hit cross-up (behind Dee Jay); First hit puts airborne opponents into a juggle state on hit (second hit air resets them); Both hits put airborne opponents into a limited juggle state on Punish Counter; Carries over Counter-Hit / Punish Counter bonus frame advantage to both hits; Second hit still does 800 damage by itself it the first hit whiffs

deejay.name: Threebeat Combo 1
deejay.notes: Solid poking tool from jab that's easily hit confirmed into the third hit for the extra damage and +3 strike / throw mixup; Second hit (MK) can whiff on crouching from further away resulting in much worse frame advantage (-17 oH / -22 oB) listed in the parentheses; MK does not whiff if LP lands as a Punish Counter; 1-2F gap on block between hits; Incurs 20% damage scaling penalty if the prior LP was blocked

deejay.name: Threebeat Combo 2
deejay.notes: Good target combo to convert into damage and pressure from DJ's stand LP; Leaves DJ with +3 on hit and in range for a strike / throw mixup

deejay.name: Funky Dance 1
deejay.notes: The second hit can be delayed quite a bit which creates a frametrap on block for the opponent (cancel window is on frames 9-15 of MP); 2F extra recovery on BLOCK only; Puts airborne opponents into a free juggle state (and maintains current juggle state); Useful tool in Drive Rush juggles to carry opponent toward the corner

deejay.name: Funky Dance 2
deejay.notes: Last hit (HP) only combos if the second MP counter-hits (which can happen when the prior hits are delayed to create a frametrap scenario); Puts the opponent into a limited juggle state on hit; 3F gap on block between this HP hit and the prior MP for yet another frametrap setup

deejay.name: Funky Dance Feint
deejay.notes: A feint option to keep the opponent guessing on if they want to try to challenge DJ's MP Target Combo; Counter-Hit state for the entire feint duration

deejay.name: Dee Jay Special 1
deejay.notes: Can be spaced so the HP hits in later active frames for + frames on hit/block; Second hit (HP) can whiff on crouching from further away resulting in much worse frame advantage (-22 oH / -27 oB); Both hits always form a true blockstring; Puts airborne opponents into a free juggle state (and maintains current juggle state)

deejay.name: Dee Jay Special 2
deejay.notes: Super cancelable; Puts opponent into a limited juggle state

deejay.name: Speedy Maracas
deejay.notes: Hold one punch button to continue dancing longer; Gains 1/5th of a bar of Super meter on frame 88 (frame 68 if starting with 2+ bars); Gains more Super meter (49 per frame; 10,000 is 1 bar) the longer Dee Jay dances; Takes 272 frames to build 1 bar of Super meter if Dee Jay continues dancing; Can be canceled into from any Air Slasher even on whiff; Dee Jay is in a Counter-Hit state for the entire duration (Punish Counter state if canceled into this from Air Slasher)

deejay.name: Diss Track
deejay.notes: Throw Loop: Dash up > whiff 5LP for +3 mixup between strike / throw (not possible on mid-screen back roll); Punish Counter gives +70% (2040) damage, Hard Knockdown (denies back-roll option on wake-up), depletes 1 bar of Drive gauge from the opponent, and builds twice as much Super gauge for the attacker; Throw Escape builds 0.5 Drive bars for the defender (randomly assigned if throws are input simultaneously)

deejay.name: Flip Throw
deejay.notes: Back Throw oki when cornered: Can Drive Rush in for a strike/throw mix; Punish Counter gives +70% (2040) damage, Hard Knockdown (denies back-roll option on wake-up), depletes 1 bar of Drive gauge from the opponent, and builds twice as much Super gauge for the attacker; Throw Escape builds 0.5 Drive bars for the defender (randomly assigned if throws are input simultaneously)

deejay.name: Drive Impact: Wild Beat
deejay.notes: 2 hits of armor on frames 1-27; Damages opponents Drive Gauge on Block (1/2 bar) | Hit (1 bar) | Counter-Hit (1.25 bar) | Punish Counter (1.5 bar); Knocks down on hit; Pushes the opponent far back on hit or block and causes a Wall Splat if they hit the wall (Parry prevents the backwards stumble and Wall Splat, greatly reducing the pushback); Regular KDA without Wall Splat +35 KD | Wall Splat on Hit +65 KD | Wall Splat on Block +72 HKD; KDA can vary greatly depending on how high the opponent wall splats (higher KDA the higher they wall splat); Advantage after Wall Splat can vary depending on distance from the corner (farther from corner gives higher advantage); Crumples the opponent on Punish Counter or after absorbing at least 1 attack during start-up (+21 frames before the crumple state goes airborne, followed by airborne state on frames 22-46 before they are grounded); Puts airborne opponents into a long spinning free juggle state when hit as a Punish Counter or after absorbing an attack; If the armor absorbs an attack it slows the overall start-up by 1F (27F total instead of 26F) and incurs 6F hitstop for each projectile hit absorbed (making it less likely to punish the opponent after absorbing projectiles); Absorbing an attack causes the player to take 1/2 the damage in recoverable health (but will KO if this would bring the player's health below zero); Stun/Dizzy occurs when a Wall Splat connects on an opponent in Burnout; Stun gives a free combo follow-up for the next 195F after hitting the wall, followed by a HKD if the player falls to the ground untouched (the last 7F before hitting the ground has a crouch-sized hurtbox but is considered standing, allowing for unique combo setups); Incurs 20% damage scaling penalty if used as the first hit of a combo (applies to wall splat on HIT, crumple, Burnout dizzy on hit/block, or any character-specific means of comboing after a regular Drive Impact); Incurs a 20% multiplier damage scaling penalty after a Wall Splat on BLOCK - Because the blocked Drive Impact is not considered a "hit" for the combo, the next attack can incur its own separate damage scaling as a combo starter; Wall Splat puts opponent into a special juggle state where the next move freely connects and continues the juggle even if it normally wouldn't (similar to a Forced Knockdown or Drive Rush juggle properties); Does not cause Wall Splat if the Drive Impact connects as a combo or a true blockstring with no gaps (LOCK icon appears on-screen); It is possible to "combo" into Stun if the opponent has under 1.5 Drive bars - a blocked DI Wall Splat from slightly outside the corner into a second DI on hit will cause Burnout and Stun (because the blocked DI is not technically considered a combo starter); Costs 1 bar of Drive Gauge; Cinematic slowdown occurs if both players activate Drive Impact within range of each other (granting a Punish Counter to the player who activates it later); Attempting to counter with DI vs. DI with under 400 HP will result in a KO, as the second player will not have enough health to absorb it; Clashes with other Drive Impacts and refunds the Drive gauge cost if they collide on the same active frame (start at exactly the same time, or 1F apart if the first Drive Impact absorbs a strike) - The meter refund does not prevent Burnout from occurring; The scrub killer

deejay.name: Drive Reversal: Leg Scratch
deejay.notes: Has two versions: one performed during blockstun or parry stun (20F start-up) and one performed as a wake-up reversal (18F start-up); Fully invincible on frames 1-22 (blockstun) / frames 1-20 (reversal); Armor Break (blows through all armor like Drive Impact, but not counters like JP's Amnesia); Trying to Drive Reversal after the blockstun ends results in a Drive Impact; Drive Reversal immediately removes the current blockstun you're in and starts the attack; Causes a 4F screen freeze after the 6th start-up frame, which allows the opponent to perform a simple OS (inputting their buttons during the buffer window) to prevent their next attack from coming out; Safe on block (-2) when used against an opponent in Burnout; Costs 2 bars of Drive Gauge; If the opponent tries to throw against a wake-up Drive Reversal, it causes a 12F screen freeze and refunds 1 bar of Drive gauge (but does not prevent Burnout); Guaranteed to interrupt any Drive Rush canceled normal if performed immediately out of blockstun (unless the opponent reacts with an invincible move or counter)

deejay.name: 斗气招架 (Drive Parry)
deejay.notes: Parries all strikes and projectiles (high and low) from frame 1; 12F parry window (can hold the parry to extend the parry window); Perfect Parry occurs on the first 2 active frames (cannot achieve Perfect Parry if you buffer into parry by holding it during Reversal windows; Perfect Parries have to be timed properly); Can still hold charge directions during Parry (allowing characters with charge specials to stand block before performing their reversal); Can block during the recovery frames of a regular parry (can still get hit during the recovery frames if you don't block correctly); Getting thrown or hit at any point during the recovery frames of a whiffed parry attempt results in a Punish Counter; Successfully parrying a move puts you into the same amount of blockstun as that move would regularly do on block (but a Perfect Parry has only 1F of recovery); Throw invincible during the recovery of a successful parry (just like during blockstun); Perfect Parrying a strike has only 1F of recovery and disables the opponent from canceling their attack (basically a guaranteed punish opportunity except for safe jump setups); Perfect Parrying a strike requires holding the correct block direction (Down+Back for low strikes, Back for high/mid strikes); Attempting a Perfect Parry with the wrong block direction results in an "imperfect parry" that builds an extra 3000 Drive Gauge and plays a distinct audio/visual cue; After a successful Perfect Parry, you suffer a 50% penalty to your Damage, Drive Gauge Generation, and Drive Gauge Damage on any of your following attacks when punishing the opponent (in addition, both you and the opponent suffer a 20% penalty to your Super Meter gain during this period); Fully invincible for 6F after a successful Perfect Parry against a strike, which carries over to any attack you perform (ensuring a 5F or faster punish will always interrupt multi-hit attacks); Perfect Parrying projectiles puts you into fixed 10 frames of recovery and applies the same 50% scaling penalties (and 20% Super Meter penalty) on your following attacks when punishing the opponent; Parrying a Strike and Projectile on the same frame will result in a regular parry for the strike attack (effectively ignoring the projectile's hitstop / blockstun); Perfect Parrying a Strike and Projectile on the same frame will give a screen freeze like you Perfect Parried a Strike, but still give you 10F recovery as if you had Perfect Parried a Projectile; Can cancel into Drive Rush during active frames 3 and onward (fastest Drive Rush method is to buffer a forward input before doing parry + forward again); Can cancel into Drive Reversal from a successful parry (just like you normally can during blockstun); Costs 1/2 bar of Drive Gauge and continues to deplete 50 Drive Gauge per frame (0.3 Drive bars per second) as you hold the Parry; You lose the parry if you go into Burnout from the initial Drive Gauge cost (Perfect Parry requires frame-perfect timing when starting from under 1/2 of a Drive bar); Rewards 1 bar of Drive Gauge (1/2 bar total after factoring in the initial parry cost) for successfully parrying a strike; Rewards 1/2 bar of Drive Gauge (0 bar total after factoring in the initial parry cost) for successfully parrying a projectile (with a few exceptions); Rewards 2 bars of Drive Gauge (1.5 bars total after factoring in the initial parry cost) for successful parrying a Super Art or Drive Impact; Successfully parrying a strike attack splits the regular block pushback between both players (while Perfect Parrying a strike removes all of its pushback); Successfully parrying a projectile or Drive Impact reduces the pushback of it by half (while Perfect Parrying a projectile or Drive Impact removes all of its pushback); Your hurtbox and throw box expand slightly towards the opponent for the entire duration of the Parry (Throw box extension starts instantly on frame 1, while the Hurtbox extension starts on frame 3, after the initial 2F Perfect Parry window); Parrying while crouching maintains a regular crouch hurtbox for the first 2 frames of the parry (during the initial Perfect Parry window)

deejay.name: 斗气冲刺 (Drive Rush)
deejay.notes: Dashes forward and enhances the next normal or command normal used out of the Drive Rush with +4 extra hitstun / blockstun, as well as improved juggle properties (Juggle Limit increased by +3 / Juggle Start/Increase reduced to 0); The +4 bonus frame advantage gained from a Drive Rush enhanced move also stacks with any bonus frame advantage that move may have gained from Counter-Hit, Punish Counter, or Burnout; Grounded special-cancelable normals can also be canceled into Drive Rush on hit or block, as well as from light normals on whiff; Drive Rush maintains buffers (freezes the buffer window) during its start-up and freeze frames - This allows players to do things normally not possible within the normal buffer windows, such as Drive Rushing into a charge special; The initial 10F screen freeze eats the opponent's directional inputs (except Jumps) but does not prevent attacks from being buffered immediately afterward (this can cause inputs to be combined in unintended ways, such as crouch MK + Fireball performing a raw Fireball, or a vertical jump + walk forward turning into a forward jump); Framedata shown in parentheses refers to the Drive Rush version used from a Parry; Drive Rush recovery is only 24F total (23F if done from a Parry) - but the enhanced dash itself is 46F total (45F if done from Parry) and you can cancel it as early as frame 9 (frame 11 if done from a Parry); Inputting a direction (walk/crouch/block/jump) after the Drive Rush recovery plays out 2 additional recovery frames before the transition occurs (this allows the user to perform an enhanced crouching or command normal late in the dash by inputting the direction + button simultaneously); You stop building any form of Drive Gauge on your attacks after using a Drive Rush in the MIDDLE of a combo (but you still continue to build Drive gauge as normal if you did Drive Rush at the START of a combo); Applies an extra damage scaling penalty after using a Drive Rush in the MIDDLE of a combo (no damage scaling if you use Drive Rush at the START of a combo); Costs 3 bars of Drive Gauge if canceled into from a normal attack; Costs 1/2 bar of Drive Gauge if canceled into from Parry (for a total of 1 bar of Drive Gauge when you factor in the initial 1/2 bar cost of the Parry); Normals used out of Drive Rush carry additional forward momentum (but throws and specials immediately halt all momentum, which can be a useful strategy to punish opponents for trying to interrupt your Drive Rush); Parry Drive Rush can only be initiated after frame 3 of the Parry (but can be performed immediately after recovering from a successful parry); Parry Drive Rush cannot be initiated with less than 1/2 of a Drive bar (as the initial Parry cost will put the user into Burnout) - But whiff canceling a Light normal into Drive Rush can achieve a similar effect; Cannot cancel Drive Rush into a Parry (inputting MP+MK results in a MK normal coming out instead); Drive Rush puts the user into a counter-hit state for the entire duration (this makes it impossible to tech a throw that connects during the dash)

deejay.name: Jus Cool
deejay.notes: Follow-ups possible on frames 13-25; Follow-ups can be delayed quite a bit which gives DJ the time to react to the opponents actions as well as mix-up his own timings; Great shimmy tool with built-in mixups and whiff punishers to keep the opponent guessing on DJ's approach; Because the attacking player suffers all the shared pushback of a move against a cornered opponent, it effectively makes DJ sway further back when canceled into normals against a cornered opponent

deejay.name: Jus Cool > Funky Slicer
deejay.notes: Low attack; Great whiff punish tool after baiting the opponent; Great pressure tool against opponents in Burnout (+1 on block and becomes a frametrap when canceled into from stand HP); 2F less recovery (20F) on block; +3F extra recovery frames (25F) on whiff; Incurs 20% damage scaling penalty if used as the first hit of a combo

deejay.name: Jus Cool > Waning Moon
deejay.notes: Overhead; Throw invincible on frames 12-26; Low crushes on start-up frames 12-22 of the Overhead follow-up; Causes a HKD on hit for follow-up mixups, while also being +1 on block allowing for continued pressure; Causes a limited OTG juggle state on Punish Counter; +1 extra KDA (+28 HKD) on crouching opponents; Causes a spiked Hard Knockdown on airborne opponents (slightly lower KD advantage than normal)

deejay.name: Jus Cool > Maximum Strike
deejay.notes: Upper body invincible on start-up frames 6-14 and again on frames 20-44 (entire recovery frames) of the follow-up kick; Upper body and the extended kicking leg are invincible to airborne strikes on frames 15-19 (during active frames); Has shorter range against crouching opponents; Launches the opponent into a limited juggle state; Can hit cross-up (behind Dee Jay)

deejay.name: Jus Cool > Juggling Dash
deejay.notes: Projectile invincible on frames 1-20 of the follow-up crouch dash (frames 14-33 overall); DJ dashes forward to quickly close the gap, ducking under any projectiles or high hitting attacks; This dash can further be canceled into another follow-up back dash on frames 18-23 (frames 31-36 overall)

deejay.name: Jus Cool > Juggling Dash > Juggling Sway
deejay.notes: DJ hops back again to bait the opponent (no projectile invincibility or crouch sized hurtboxes like the prior forward dash); DJ shrinks his standing hurtbox width by roughly 50% on frames 5-17 of the back dash; Only 1F faster and slightly further distance covered than if DJ had just backdashed instead after the prior forwards dash; Cancelable into Funky Slicer (LK) / Waning Moon (MK) / Maximum Strike (HK) follow-ups (but not into another Juggling Dash)

deejay.name: The Greatest Sobat
deejay.notes: No invincibility whatsoever; Armor Break; Low crushes on frames 4-14; No hurtbox extension whatsoever (can force a trade against some projectiles for a follow-up combo); Very safe on block compared to other Supers (can be spaced out to be relatively safe even on block); Puts the opponent into a free juggle Crumple state on Counter Hit and Punish Counter allowing for follow-up juggles (grounded combo follow-ups can be possible if close enough; +4 before airborne on Counter Hit / +6 on Punish Counter); Cause a sliding Hard Knockdown on airborne opponents; Punish Counter vs. airborne opponents causes a wall bounce and free juggle state (opponent can fly over Dee Jay's head if near the corner); Counter Hit crumple has less KDA (HKD +66) and fewer follow-up combo options; Depletes 0.5 Drive Bar on hit for the opponent

deejay.name: Lowkey Sunrise Festival
deejay.command: 236236LP > LP > MP > HP > LK > MK > HK (bad)
deejay.notes: Fully invincible on frames 1-16 (follow-ups are also projectile invincible); Armor Break; First hit forces stand (relevant for combo follow-ups); This LP version of the Level 2 Super is the easiest one to do the rhythm for but it also deals the least amount of damage and limited to a lesser HK finisher; Dee Jay is +6 on hit for the first 5 hits of this super, allowing for follow-up combos (last HK hit knocks down); Damage shown in parentheses (2600) refers to the full version if Dee Jay does the HK knockdown finisher; Depletes 0.5 Drive Bar on hit for the opponent; Can hit cross-up (behind Dee Jay); 30% penalty to Super meter gain on any of the follow-up hits Dee Jay combos into after this move

deejay.name: Marvelous Sunrise Festival
deejay.command: 236236MP > LP > MP > HP > LK > MK > HK (good)
deejay.notes: Fully invincible on frames 1-16 (follow-ups are also projectile invincible); Armor Break; First hit forces stand (relevant for combo follow-ups); This MP version of the Level 2 Super is easier to do the rhythm for than the HP version, but it also deals 100 less damage (200 less damage overall if you do the HP / HK finishers); Each button pressed at the right beat deals an extra 100 damage; Dee Jay is +6 on hit after the first 5 hits (up to MK) allowing for follow-up combos; The final HK hit puts the opponent into a Crumple state which can only combo'd from with the HP / HK finishers; Depletes 0.5 Drive Bar on hit for the opponent; Can hit cross-up (behind Dee Jay); 30% penalty to Super meter gain on any of the follow-up hits Dee Jay combos into after this move

deejay.name: Jus Cool
deejay.notes: Launches the opponent into a limited juggle state; Follow-ups possible on frames 13-25 of the follow-up sway after the initial punch (frames 25-37 overall); Dash follow-up (6P) can be executed 6F earlier than the other follow-ups; +1F extra recovery frame (37F) on block; The attack follow-ups can be executed 3F earlier on block (allows for better frametrap / Burnout pressure opportunities); Follow-ups can be delayed quite a bit which gives DJ the time to react to the opponents actions as well as mix-up his own timings; Follow-ups can be executed 3F earlier on BLOCK only (this turns the LK follow-up into a true blockstring or frametrap tool depending on input timing); Great shimmy tool with built-in mixups and whiff punishers to keep the opponent guessing on DJ's approach; Because the attacking player suffers all the shared pushback of a move against a cornered opponent, it effectively makes DJ sway further back when canceled into normals against a cornered opponent
