Regular KDA without Wall Splat +35 KD | Wall Splat on Hit +65 KD | Wall Splat on Block +72 HKD; KDA can vary greatly depending on how high the opponent wall splats (higher KDA the higher they wall splat); Advantage after Wall Splat can vary depending on distance from the corner (farther from corner gives higher advantage); Crumples the opponent on Punish Counter or after absorbing at least 1 attack during start-up (+21 frames before the crumple state goes airborne, followed by airborne state on frames 22-46 before they are grounded); Puts airborne opponents into a long spinning free juggle state when hit as a Punish Counter or after absorbing an attack; If the armor absorbs an attack it slows the overall start-up by 1F (27F total instead of 26F) and incurs 6F hitstop for each projectile hit absorbed (making it less likely to punish the opponent after absorbing projectiles); Absorbing an attack causes the player to take 1/2 the damage in recoverable health (but will KO if this would bring the player's health below zero); Stun/Dizzy occurs when a Wall Splat connects on an opponent in Burnout; Stun gives a free combo follow-up for the next 195F after hitting the wall, followed by a HKD if the player falls to the ground untouched (the last 7F before hitting the ground has a crouch-sized hurtbox but is considered standing, allowing for unique combo setups); Incurs 20% damage scaling penalty if used as the first hit of a combo (applies to wall splat on HIT, crumple, Burnout dizzy on hit/block, or any character-specific means of comboing after a regular Drive Impact); Incurs a 20% multiplier damage scaling penalty after a Wall Splat on BLOCK - Because the blocked Drive Impact is not considered a "hit" for the combo, the next attack can incur its own separate damage scaling as a combo starter; Wall Splat puts opponent into a special juggle state where the next move freely connects and continues the juggle even if it normally wouldn't (similar to a Forced Knockdown or Drive Rush juggle properties); Does not cause Wall Splat if the Drive Impact connects as a combo or a true blockstring with no gaps (LOCK icon appears on-screen); It is possible to "combo" into Stun if the opponent has under 1.5 Drive bars - a blocked DI Wall Splat from slightly outside the corner into a second DI on hit will cause Burnout and Stun (because the blocked DI is not technically considered a combo starter); Costs 1 bar of Drive Gauge; Cinematic slowdown occurs if both players activate Drive Impact within range of each other (granting a Punish Counter to the player who activates it later); Attempting to counter with DI vs. DI with under 400 HP will result in a KO, as the second player will not have enough health to absorb it; Clashes with other Drive Impacts and refunds the Drive gauge cost if they collide on the same active frame (start at exactly the same time, or 1F apart if the first Drive Impact absorbs a strike) - The meter refund does not prevent Burnout from occurring; The scrub killer

dhalsim.name: Drive Reversal: Yoga Illusion
dhalsim.notes: Has two versions: one performed during blockstun or parry stun (20F start-up) and one performed as a wake-up reversal (18F start-up); Fully invincible on frames 1-22 (blockstun) / frames 1-20 (reversal); Armor Break (blows through all armor like Drive Impact, but not counters like JP's Amnesia); Trying to Drive Reversal after the blockstun ends results in a Drive Impact; Drive Reversal immediately removes the current blockstun you're in and starts the attack; Causes a 4F screen freeze after the 6th start-up frame, which allows the opponent to perform a simple OS (inputting their buttons during the buffer window) to prevent their next attack from coming out; Safe on block (-2) when used against an opponent in Burnout; Costs 2 bars of Drive Gauge; If the opponent tries to throw against a wake-up Drive Reversal, it causes a 12F screen freeze and refunds 1 bar of Drive gauge (but does not prevent Burnout); Guaranteed to interrupt any Drive Rush canceled normal if performed immediately out of blockstun (unless the opponent reacts with an invincible move or counter)

dhalsim.name: 斗气招架 (Drive Parry)
dhalsim.notes: Parries all strikes and projectiles (high and low) from frame 1; 12F parry window (can hold the parry to extend the parry window); Perfect Parry occurs on the first 2 active frames (cannot achieve Perfect Parry if you buffer into parry by holding it during Reversal windows; Perfect Parries have to be timed properly); Can still hold charge directions during Parry (allowing characters with charge specials to stand block before performing their reversal); Can block during the recovery frames of a regular parry (can still get hit during the recovery frames if you don't block correctly); Getting thrown or hit at any point during the recovery frames of a whiffed parry attempt results in a Punish Counter; Successfully parrying a move puts you into the same amount of blockstun as that move would regularly do on block (but a Perfect Parry has only 1F of recovery); Throw invincible during the recovery of a successful parry (just like during blockstun); Perfect Parrying a strike has only 1F of recovery and disables the opponent from canceling their attack (basically a guaranteed punish opportunity except for safe jump setups); Perfect Parrying a strike requires holding the correct block direction (Down+Back for low strikes, Back for high/mid strikes); Attempting a Perfect Parry with the wrong block direction results in an "imperfect parry" that builds an extra 3000 Drive Gauge and plays a distinct audio/visual cue; After a successful Perfect Parry, you suffer a 50% penalty to your Damage, Drive Gauge Generation, and Drive Gauge Damage on any of your following attacks when punishing the opponent (in addition, both you and the opponent suffer a 20% penalty to your Super Meter gain during this period); Fully invincible for 6F after a successful Perfect Parry against a strike, which carries over to any attack you perform (ensuring a 5F or faster punish will always interrupt multi-hit attacks); Perfect Parrying projectiles puts you into fixed 10 frames of recovery and applies the same 50% scaling penalties (and 20% Super Meter penalty) on your following attacks when punishing the opponent; Parrying a Strike and Projectile on the same frame will result in a regular parry for the strike attack (effectively ignoring the projectile's hitstop / blockstun); Perfect Parrying a Strike and Projectile on the same frame will give a screen freeze like you Perfect Parried a Strike, but still give you 10F recovery as if you had Perfect Parried a Projectile; Can cancel into Drive Rush during active frames 3 and onward (fastest Drive Rush method is to buffer a forward input before doing parry + forward again); Can cancel into Drive Reversal from a successful parry (just like you normally can during blockstun); Costs 1/2 bar of Drive Gauge and continues to deplete 50 Drive Gauge per frame (0.3 Drive bars per second) as you hold the Parry; You lose the parry if you go into Burnout from the initial Drive Gauge cost (Perfect Parry requires frame-perfect timing when starting from under 1/2 of a Drive bar); Rewards 1 bar of Drive Gauge (1/2 bar total after factoring in the initial parry cost) for successfully parrying a strike; Rewards 1/2 bar of Drive Gauge (0 bar total after factoring in the initial parry cost) for successfully parrying a projectile (with a few exceptions); Rewards 2 bars of Drive Gauge (1.5 bars total after factoring in the initial parry cost) for successful parrying a Super Art or Drive Impact; Successfully parrying a strike attack splits the regular block pushback between both players (while Perfect Parrying a strike removes all of its pushback); Successfully parrying a projectile or Drive Impact reduces the pushback of it by half (while Perfect Parrying a projectile or Drive Impact removes all of its pushback); Your hurtbox and throw box expand slightly towards the opponent for the entire duration of the Parry (Throw box extension starts instantly on frame 1, while the Hurtbox extension starts on frame 3, after the initial 2F Perfect Parry window); Parrying while crouching maintains a regular crouch hurtbox for the first 2 frames of the parry (during the initial Perfect Parry window)

dhalsim.name: 斗气冲刺 (Drive Rush)
dhalsim.notes: Dashes forward and enhances the next normal or command normal used out of the Drive Rush with +4 extra hitstun / blockstun, as well as improved juggle properties (Juggle Limit increased by +3 / Juggle Start/Increase reduced to 0); The +4 bonus frame advantage gained from a Drive Rush enhanced move also stacks with any bonus frame advantage that move may have gained from Counter-Hit, Punish Counter, or Burnout; Grounded special-cancelable normals can also be canceled into Drive Rush on hit or block, as well as from light normals on whiff; Drive Rush maintains buffers (freezes the buffer window) during its start-up and freeze frames - This allows players to do things normally not possible within the normal buffer windows, such as Drive Rushing into a charge special; The initial 10F screen freeze eats the opponent's directional inputs (except Jumps) but does not prevent attacks from being buffered immediately afterward (this can cause inputs to be combined in unintended ways, such as crouch MK + Fireball performing a raw Fireball, or a vertical jump + walk forward turning into a forward jump); Framedata shown in parentheses refers to the Drive Rush version used from a Parry; Drive Rush recovery is only 24F total (23F if done from a Parry) - but the enhanced dash itself is 46F total (45F if done from Parry) and you can cancel it as early as frame 9 (frame 11 if done from a Parry); Inputting a direction (walk/crouch/block/jump) after the Drive Rush recovery plays out 2 additional recovery frames before the transition occurs (this allows the user to perform an enhanced crouching or command normal late in the dash by inputting the direction + button simultaneously); You stop building any form of Drive Gauge on your attacks after using a Drive Rush in the MIDDLE of a combo (but you still continue to build Drive gauge as normal if you did Drive Rush at the START of a combo); Applies an extra damage scaling penalty after using a Drive Rush in the MIDDLE of a combo (no damage scaling if you use Drive Rush at the START of a combo); Costs 3 bars of Drive Gauge if canceled into from a normal attack; Costs 1/2 bar of Drive Gauge if canceled into from Parry (for a total of 1 bar of Drive Gauge when you factor in the initial 1/2 bar cost of the Parry); Normals used out of Drive Rush carry additional forward momentum (but throws and specials immediately halt all momentum, which can be a useful strategy to punish opponents for trying to interrupt your Drive Rush); Parry Drive Rush can only be initiated after frame 3 of the Parry (but can be performed immediately after recovering from a successful parry); Parry Drive Rush cannot be initiated with less than 1/2 of a Drive bar (as the initial Parry cost will put the user into Burnout) - But whiff canceling a Light normal into Drive Rush can achieve a similar effect; Cannot cancel Drive Rush into a Parry (inputting MP+MK results in a MK normal coming out instead); Drive Rush puts the user into a counter-hit state for the entire duration (this makes it impossible to tech a throw that connects during the dash)

dhalsim.name: Yoga Float
dhalsim.notes: Can perform air normals and specials or move left/right after 30F animation of Dhalsim rising up into the air; The 3KK (down-forward + KK) input moves Dhalsim forward as he rises into the air; Counter-hit state from frame 1 until landing; Airborne on frame 13 and until landing (Forced Knockdown state); Projectile invincible on lower legs frame 17 onwards; Active frames listed refers to the airborne period in which Dhalsim can move and perform airborne attacks (can also input airborne attacks during his 20F descent down; 1F crouching state on the final landing recovery frame; Dhalsim moves a lot faster while in the air than walking on the ground (Forward: 0.04 Speed | Backward: 0.03 Speed)

dhalsim.name: Aerial Yoga Float (air)
dhalsim.notes: Can be initiated after at least 8F into his jumps; Can perform air normals and specials or move left/right 15F after the Yoga Float has been initiated (see start-up frames); Counter-hit state from frame 1 until landing; Forced Knockdown state while airborne; Projectile invincible on lower legs frame 1 onwards; Active frames listed refers to the airborne period in which Dhalsim can move and perform airborne attacks (can also input airborne attacks during his descent down, which depends on float height; 18F at minimum); 1F crouching state on the final landing recovery frame; This airborne Yoga Float can only be used once per jump even after using OD Yoga Comet to regain air control; Movement Speed in both directions while floating: 0.03 (faster than walking)

dhalsim.name: Yoga Teleport
dhalsim.notes: No form of invincibility during teleport startup; Fully invincible on frames 5-15; Dhalsim's hurtboxes reappear on frame 16; After reappearing, there are 24 recovery frames (31 if teleporting backward); Values in parenthesis refer to teleporting backward; Forward teleport with Kick stays in front, Punch goes behind the opponent (if opponent is not cornered); Backward teleport travels 1.5 units regardless of whether PPP or KKK is input (except when limited by the corner or edge of the screen); Modern Controls: Forward teleport always appears behind the opponent (cannot perform the f+KKK version)

dhalsim.name: Aerial Yoga Teleport (air)
dhalsim.notes: No form of invincibility during teleport startup; Fully invincible on frames 10-15; Dhalsim's hurtboxes reappear on frame 16; Can follow-up with moves on frame 29 (frame 35 if teleporting backward); Punish Counter and Forced Knockdown state while airborne; 3 frames of landing recovery; Forward teleport with Kick stays in front, Punch goes behind the opponent (if opponent is not cornered); Backward Teleport with Kick goes further (2.5 units) than with Punch (1.5 units); Modern Controls: unlike grounded teleport, Dhalsim can perform all versions of the aerial teleport: f+SP (f+KKK) | f+LMH (f+PPP) | b+SP (b+PPP) | b+LMH (b+KKK)

dhalsim.name: Yoga Fire
dhalsim.notes: 1-hit projectile; Projectile speed varies depending on button strength; LP (Classic) / L (Modern): 0.033 speed; MP (Classic) / M (Modern): 0.044 speed; HP (Classic) / H (Modern): 0.06 speed; Hold down the button to get the improved version (releasing the button before frame 27 results in a regular fireball with 9F start-up after release); Extended head hurtbox on frames 15-39 is Projectile invincible; Can be performed while OD Yoga Arch is on the screen (otherwise cannot be used while another Yoga Fire or Yoga Arch is active)

dhalsim.name: Yoga Fire (hold)
dhalsim.notes: 2-hit projectile; Button must be held 27F for fully charged version; Projectile speed varies depending on button strength; LP (Classic) / L (Modern): 0.033 speed; MP (Classic) / M (Modern): 0.044 speed; HP (Classic) / H (Modern): 0.06 speed; Extended head hurtbox on frames 43-73 is Projectile invincible; Can be performed while OD Yoga Arch is on the screen (otherwise cannot be used while another Yoga Fire or Yoga Arch is active)

dhalsim.name: Yoga Arch
dhalsim.notes: 1-hit projectile; Projectile speed and trajectory varies depending on button strength (Classic) or held direction (Modern), with LK having the shortest horizontal range and HK having the furthest; LK (Classic) / hold Back (Modern): 0.0195 speed; MK (Classic) / hold Neutral (Modern): 0.0385 speed; HK (Classic) / hold Forward (Modern): 0.07 speed; Upon hitting the floor, the projectile leaves a stationary hitbox on the ground for 10 frames; Frame advantage listed refers to point blank upward hit; Puts airborne opponents into a free juggle state and does not increase the current juggle state; Can be performed while OD Yoga Fire is on the screen (otherwise cannot be used while another Yoga Fire or Yoga Arch is active)

dhalsim.name: Yoga Comet (air)
dhalsim.notes: 1-hit projectile; Projectile speed varies depending on button strength; LP (Classic) / L (Modern): 0.03 speed; MP (Classic) / M (Modern): 0.045 speed; HP (Classic) / H (Modern): 0.055 speed; Projectile hitbox dissipates after 55F if no contact is made; If the projectile lands on the floor it creates a stationary projectile hitbox that lasts for 10 frames; Frame advantage listed refers to the closest range minimum height verison (this move can be performed on the 2nd airborne jumping frame at the earliest); Can be performed from any jump; The last 5F of the landing recovery frames are in a crouching state

dhalsim.name: Yoga Inferno
dhalsim.notes: Throw invincible on frames 1-11; Armor Break; Button strength changes how this super functions; LP (Classic) / hold Back (Modern): Flame carpet with half screen range - 1920 damage; MP (Classic) / hold Neutral (Modern): hits ~1/3 screen range and ends with an anti-air finisher - 2100 damage; HP (Classic) / hold Forward (Modern): Anti-air version that whiffs on crouchers - 2040 damage; Values in parenthesis refer to HP version; Depletes 0.5 Drive Bar on hit AND block from the opponent; All versions deal 792 recoverable health damage (grey health) on block; LP and MP versions are only -10 on block and can be made entirely safe on block if spaced out, especially the LP version

dhalsim.name: Yoga Sunburst
dhalsim.notes: Fully invincible on frames 1-9; 5-hit Super projectile hitbox; Armor Break; Projectile speed and trajectory varies depending on button strength (LK having the shortest horizontal range and HK having the furthest); In Modern, hold back for shortest distance / neutral for medium distance / forward for furthest distance; LK (Classic) / L (Modern): 0.014 speed; MK (Classic) / M (Modern): 0.021 speed; HK (Classic) / H (Modern): 0.04 speed; Upon hitting the floor, the projectile leaves a large stationary hitbox on the ground for 20 frames; Cannot hit crouching up close; Can be held to deal much higher damage (3100 or 4000) and have a larger hitbox (can do some sick optimal stun combos with the held version)

dhalsim.name: Yoga Sunburst (hold)
dhalsim.notes: Fully invincible on frames 1-9; 7-9 hit Super projectile hitbox (7 hits of partial charge, 9 hits of full charge); Armor Break; Projectile speed and trajectory varies depending on button strength (LK (Classic) / L (Modern) having the shortest horizontal range and HK (Classic) / H (Modern) having the furthest); In Modern, hold back for shortest distance / neutral for medium distance / forward for furthest distance; LK (Classic) / L (Modern): 0.014 speed; MK (Classic) / M (Modern): 0.021 speed; HK (Classic) / H (Modern): 0.04 speed; Sunburst starts as active projectile building power above Dhalsim and is thrown when button is released; Hold button at least 23f to produce lvl 2 Yoga Sunburst; Hold button at least 71f to produce lvl 3 Yoga Sunburst; Automatically releases if the Yoga Sunburst above Dhalsim's head hits the opponent; Values in parenthesis refer to lvl 3 Yoga Sunburst

dhalsim.name: Merciless Yoga
dhalsim.notes: Fully invincible on frames 1-14; Armor Break; Depletes 1.5 Drive Bars on hit for the opponent; Super cinematic time regenerates ~2 Drive Bars for Dhalsim; 2F start-up when canceled into from Yoga Flame (hcb+P) special (this is to help it connect in combos)

dhalsim.name: Merciless Yoga (Critical Art)
dhalsim.notes: Fully invincible on frames 1-14; Armor Break; Critical Art does +500 extra damage over regular version; Depletes 2 Drive Bars on hit for the opponent; Super cinematic time regenerates ~2.4 Drive Bars for Dhalsim; 2F start-up when canceled into from Yoga Flame (hcb+P) special (this is to help it connect in combos)

dhalsim.name: Yoga Fire
dhalsim.notes: 2-hit OD projectile; Projectile speed varies depending on button strength; LPMP (Classic) / LM (Modern): 0.033 speed; LPHP (Classic) / LH (Modern): 0.044 speed; MPHP (Classic) / MH (Modern): 0.06 speed; Extended head hurtbox on frames 13-41 is Projectile invincible; Cannot be performed while another Yoga Fire or Yoga Arch is active on-screen (but can be followed up immediately with a meterless Yoga Arch)

ehonda.name: 站轻拳 (5LP)
ehonda.notes: Incurs 20% damage scaling penalty if used as the first hit of a combo; Hit confirmable into the MP target combo follow-up (18F hit confirm window); Talk to the hand

ehonda.name: 站中拳 (5MP)
ehonda.notes: Core combo / pressure tool as well as an excellent poke / bully tool due to the forward travel during startup; +4F extra recovery frames (17F) on whiff

ehonda.name: 站重拳 (5HP)
ehonda.notes: First active frame only hits airborne targets (so technically a 9-frame startup vs grounded opponents); Only the first 3 active frames are cancelable; Upper body is invincible to airborne strikes on frames 8-10; Solid anti-air on the first 3 active frames but cannot hit cross-up (behind E. Honda); Causes a Crumple state on grounded Punish Counter; Causes a spiked OTG knockdown state in airborne Punish Counters that Honda can juggle from; Decent poke on the last 4 active frames; The brief extended hurtbox on frame 10 is strike invincible (cannot counter-poke projectiles); Can cancel all active frames into Hundred Hand Slap if the Sumo Spirit buff is active; Honda's strongest meterless route into Taiho Cannon Lift (very important combo tool)

ehonda.name: 站轻脚 (5LK)
ehonda.notes: Incurs 20% damage scaling penalty if used as the first hit of a combo

ehonda.name: 站中脚 (5MK)
ehonda.notes: Lifts up most of his leg hurtboxes on frames 7-13 making this an extremely strong tool against low attacks; Can cancel into Hundred Hand Slap if the Sumo Spirit buff is active

ehonda.name: 站重脚 (5HK)
ehonda.notes: Forces stand on hit; Both hits are fully cancelable; Carries over Counter-Hit / Punish Counter bonus frame advantage to both hits; Values in parentheses refer to second hit only; First hits put airborne opponents into a free juggle state; Second hit puts airborne opponents into a limited juggle state; Second hit can be used as a situational anti-air (not the best though); Second hit whiffs on crouch from further away (crouch hitbox only hits up close) resulting in -9 on block (usually -5 on block if the second hit is blocked standing); Can frame trap into Teppo Double Slap on block when canceled on the 1st hit

ehonda.name: 蹲轻拳 (2LP)

ehonda.name: 蹲中拳 (2MP)
ehonda.notes: Great buffer and poke tool with very strong hitbox priority; Topmost hurtboxes on frames 1-11 are vulnerable only to airborne attacks (this is to discourage its use as an anti-air)

ehonda.name: 蹲重拳 (2HP)
ehonda.notes: Far range poke (not a low attack) that can be canceled into Supers; Becomes cancelable into Hundred Hand Slap if the Sumo Spirit buff is active; +2F extra recovery frames (19F) on whiff or when absorbed by armor; Can be spaced for extra frame advantage on hit/block

ehonda.name: 蹲轻脚 (2LK)
ehonda.notes: Chains into crouch LP / crouch LK; Can cancel into Hundred Hand Slap if the Sumo Spirit buff is active; Incurs 20% damage scaling penalty if used as the first hit of a combo

ehonda.name: 蹲中脚 (2MK)

ehonda.name: Saba Ori

ehonda.name: Tawara Throw
ehonda.notes: Throw Loop when used while cornered: Dash forward for a meaty strike or LK/OD Oicho Throw (command grab) - Can also Drive Rush for a meaty strike/throw mix (DR 2HP is +10/+4 and sets up pressure on block); Punish Counter gives +70% (2040) damage, Hard Knockdown (denies back-roll option on wake-up), depletes 1 bar of Drive gauge from the opponent, and builds twice as much Super gauge for the attacker; Throw Escape builds 0.5 Drive bars for the defender (randomly assigned if throws are input simultaneously)

ehonda.name: Drive Impact: Sumo Crunch
ehonda.notes: 2 hits of armor on frames 1-27; Damages opponents Drive Gauge on Block (1/2 bar) | Hit (1 bar) | Counter-Hit (1.25 bar) | Punish Counter (1.5 bar); Knocks down on hit; Pushes the opponent far back on hit or block and causes a Wall Splat if they hit the wall (Parry prevents the backwards stumble and Wall Splat, greatly reducing the pushback); Regular KDA without Wall Splat +35 KD | Wall Splat on Hit +65 KD | Wall Splat on Block +72 HKD; KDA can vary greatly depending on how high the opponent wall splats (higher KDA the higher they wall splat); Advantage after Wall Splat can vary depending on distance from the corner (farther from corner gives higher advantage); Crumples the opponent on Punish Counter or after absorbing at least 1 attack during start-up (+21 frames before the crumple state goes airborne, followed by airborne state on frames 22-46 before they are grounded); Puts airborne opponents into a long spinning free juggle state when hit as a Punish Counter or after absorbing an attack; If the armor absorbs an attack it slows the overall start-up by 1F (27F total instead of 26F) and incurs 6F hitstop for each projectile hit absorbed (making it less likely to punish the opponent after absorbing projectiles); Absorbing an attack causes the player to take 1/2 the damage in recoverable health (but will KO if this would bring the player's health below zero); Stun/Dizzy occurs when a Wall Splat connects on an opponent in Burnout; Stun gives a free combo follow-up for the next 195F after hitting the wall, followed by a HKD if the player falls to the ground untouched (the last 7F before hitting the ground has a crouch-sized hurtbox but is considered standing, allowing for unique combo setups); Incurs 20% damage scaling penalty if used as the first hit of a combo (applies to wall splat on HIT, crumple, Burnout dizzy on hit/block, or any character-specific means of comboing after a regular Drive Impact); Incurs a 20% multiplier damage scaling penalty after a Wall Splat on BLOCK - Because the blocked Drive Impact is not considered a "hit" for the combo, the next attack can incur its own separate damage scaling as a combo starter; Wall Splat puts opponent into a special juggle state where the next move freely connects and continues the juggle even if it normally wouldn't (similar to a Forced Knockdown or Drive Rush juggle properties); Does not cause Wall Splat if the Drive Impact connects as a combo or a true blockstring with no gaps (LOCK icon appears on-screen); It is possible to "combo" into Stun if the opponent has under 1.5 Drive bars - a blocked DI Wall Splat from slightly outside the corner into a second DI on hit will cause Burnout and Stun (because the blocked DI is not technically considered a combo starter); Costs 1 bar of Drive Gauge; Cinematic slowdown occurs if both players activate Drive Impact within range of each other (granting a Punish Counter to the player who activates it later); Attempting to counter with DI vs. DI with under 400 HP will result in a KO, as the second player will not have enough health to absorb it; Clashes with other Drive Impacts and refunds the Drive gauge cost if they collide on the same active frame (start at exactly the same time, or 1F apart if the first Drive Impact absorbs a strike) - The meter refund does not prevent Burnout from occurring; The scrub killer

ehonda.name: Drive Reversal: Raiden-ho
ehonda.notes: Has two versions: one performed during blockstun or parry stun (20F start-up) and one performed as a wake-up reversal (18F start-up); Fully invincible on frames 1-22 (blockstun) / frames 1-20 (reversal); Armor Break (blows through all armor like Drive Impact, but not counters like JP's Amnesia); Trying to Drive Reversal after the blockstun ends results in a Drive Impact; Drive Reversal immediately removes the current blockstun you're in and starts the attack; Causes a 4F screen freeze after the 6th start-up frame, which allows the opponent to perform a simple OS (inputting their buttons during the buffer window) to prevent their next attack from coming out; Safe on block (-2) when used against an opponent in Burnout; Costs 2 bars of Drive Gauge; If the opponent tries to throw against a wake-up Drive Reversal, it causes a 12F screen freeze and refunds 1 bar of Drive gauge (but does not prevent Burnout); Guaranteed to interrupt any Drive Rush canceled normal if performed immediately out of blockstun (unless the opponent reacts with an invincible move or counter)

ehonda.name: 斗气招架 (Drive Parry)
ehonda.notes: Parries all strikes and projectiles (high and low) from frame 1; 12F parry window (can hold the parry to extend the parry window); Perfect Parry occurs on the first 2 active frames (cannot achieve Perfect Parry if you buffer into parry by holding it during Reversal windows; Perfect Parries have to be timed properly); Can still hold charge directions during Parry (allowing characters with charge specials to stand block before performing their reversal); Can block during the recovery frames of a regular parry (can still get hit during the recovery frames if you don't block correctly); Getting thrown or hit at any point during the recovery frames of a whiffed parry attempt results in a Punish Counter; Successfully parrying a move puts you into the same amount of blockstun as that move would regularly do on block (but a Perfect Parry has only 1F of recovery); Throw invincible during the recovery of a successful parry (just like during blockstun); Perfect Parrying a strike has only 1F of recovery and disables the opponent from canceling their attack (basically a guaranteed punish opportunity except for safe jump setups); Perfect Parrying a strike requires holding the correct block direction (Down+Back for low strikes, Back for high/mid strikes); Attempting a Perfect Parry with the wrong block direction results in an "imperfect parry" that builds an extra 3000 Drive Gauge and plays a distinct audio/visual cue; After a successful Perfect Parry, you suffer a 50% penalty to your Damage, Drive Gauge Generation, and Drive Gauge Damage on any of your following attacks when punishing the opponent (in addition, both you and the opponent suffer a 20% penalty to your Super Meter gain during this period); Fully invincible for 6F after a successful Perfect Parry against a strike, which carries over to any attack you perform (ensuring a 5F or faster punish will always interrupt multi-hit attacks); Perfect Parrying projectiles puts you into fixed 10 frames of recovery and applies the same 50% scaling penalties (and 20% Super Meter penalty) on your following attacks when punishing the opponent; Parrying a Strike and Projectile on the same frame will result in a regular parry for the strike attack (effectively ignoring the projectile's hitstop / blockstun); Perfect Parrying a Strike and Projectile on the same frame will give a screen freeze like you Perfect Parried a Strike, but still give you 10F recovery as if you had Perfect Parried a Projectile; Can cancel into Drive Rush during active frames 3 and onward (fastest Drive Rush method is to buffer a forward input before doing parry + forward again); Can cancel into Drive Reversal from a successful parry (just like you normally can during blockstun); Costs 1/2 bar of Drive Gauge and continues to deplete 50 Drive Gauge per frame (0.3 Drive bars per second) as you hold the Parry; You lose the parry if you go into Burnout from the initial Drive Gauge cost (Perfect Parry requires frame-perfect timing when starting from under 1/2 of a Drive bar); Rewards 1 bar of Drive Gauge (1/2 bar total after factoring in the initial parry cost) for successfully parrying a strike; Rewards 1/2 bar of Drive Gauge (0 bar total after factoring in the initial parry cost) for successfully parrying a projectile (with a few exceptions); Rewards 2 bars of Drive Gauge (1.5 bars total after factoring in the initial parry cost) for successful parrying a Super Art or Drive Impact; Successfully parrying a strike attack splits the regular block pushback between both players (while Perfect Parrying a strike removes all of its pushback); Successfully parrying a projectile or Drive Impact reduces the pushback of it by half (while Perfect Parrying a projectile or Drive Impact removes all of its pushback); Your hurtbox and throw box expand slightly towards the opponent for the entire duration of the Parry (Throw box extension starts instantly on frame 1, while the Hurtbox extension starts on frame 3, after the initial 2F Perfect Parry window); Parrying while crouching maintains a regular crouch hurtbox for the first 2 frames of the parry (during the initial Perfect Parry window)

ehonda.name: 斗气冲刺 (Drive Rush)
ehonda.notes: Dashes forward and enhances the next normal or command normal used out of the Drive Rush with +4 extra hitstun / blockstun, as well as improved juggle properties (Juggle Limit increased by +3 / Juggle Start/Increase reduced to 0); The +4 bonus frame advantage gained from a Drive Rush enhanced move also stacks with any bonus frame advantage that move may have gained from Counter-Hit, Punish Counter, or Burnout; Grounded special-cancelable normals can also be canceled into Drive Rush on hit or block, as well as from light normals on whiff; Drive Rush maintains buffers (freezes the buffer window) during its start-up and freeze frames - This allows players to do things normally not possible within the normal buffer windows, such as Drive Rushing into a charge special; The initial 10F screen freeze eats the opponent's directional inputs (except Jumps) but does not prevent attacks from being buffered immediately afterward (this can cause inputs to be combined in unintended ways, such as crouch MK + Fireball performing a raw Fireball, or a vertical jump + walk forward turning into a forward jump); Framedata shown in parentheses refers to the Drive Rush version used from a Parry; Drive Rush recovery is only 24F total (23F if done from a Parry) - but the enhanced dash itself is 46F total (45F if done from Parry) and you can cancel it as early as frame 9 (frame 11 if done from a Parry); Inputting a direction (walk/crouch/block/jump) after the Drive Rush recovery plays out 2 additional recovery frames before the transition occurs (this allows the user to perform an enhanced crouching or command normal late in the dash by inputting the direction + button simultaneously); You stop building any form of Drive Gauge on your attacks after using a Drive Rush in the MIDDLE of a combo (but you still continue to build Drive gauge as normal if you did Drive Rush at the START of a combo); Applies an extra damage scaling penalty after using a Drive Rush in the MIDDLE of a combo (no damage scaling if you use Drive Rush at the START of a combo); Costs 3 bars of Drive Gauge if canceled into from a normal attack; Costs 1/2 bar of Drive Gauge if canceled into from Parry (for a total of 1 bar of Drive Gauge when you factor in the initial 1/2 bar cost of the Parry); Normals used out of Drive Rush carry additional forward momentum (but throws and specials immediately halt all momentum, which can be a useful strategy to punish opponents for trying to interrupt your Drive Rush); Parry Drive Rush can only be initiated after frame 3 of the Parry (but can be performed immediately after recovering from a successful parry); Parry Drive Rush cannot be initiated with less than 1/2 of a Drive bar (as the initial Parry cost will put the user into Burnout) - But whiff canceling a Light normal into Drive Rush can achieve a similar effect; Cannot cancel Drive Rush into a Parry (inputting MP+MK results in a MK normal coming out instead); Drive Rush puts the user into a counter-hit state for the entire duration (this makes it impossible to tech a throw that connects during the dash)

ed.notes: Forces stand; Good combo / punish / buffer tool that's hit confirmable with decent active frames; Combos into crouch MK on Punish Counter even from max range; HP can be held to initiate the Psycho Knuckle or release it early for a normal Stand HP instead; Goes into two different levels of Psycho Knuckle (30F hold for level 1 | 60F hold for level 2); The start-up when the HP button is released ranges from 4-8F depending on how late/early it is released

ed.name: 站轻脚 (5LK)
ed.notes: "One!"; Fantastic range for a light normal that also has a hit confirmable Target Combo extension makes this a solid poke tool in close/mid range; Ed extends his hurtboxes forward A LOT for 3F before active frames begin, making this button very susceptible to counterpokes; Hurtbox extensions on frames 3-5 are projectile invincible; Incurs 20% damage scaling penalty if used as the first hit of a combo

ed.name: 站中脚 (5MK)
ed.notes: Good poke tool with great range and an optional Target Combo follow-up; Hurtbox extensions on frames 4-9 are projectile invincible (more susceptible to strike counter-pokes); +4 extra recovery frames (20F) on whiff; Extends a wide hurtbox on whiff until the end of recovery

ed.name: 站重脚 (5HK)
ed.notes: Whiffs on crouch; Close range combo / frametrap tool as well as an optional anti-air; Recovers very fast for a Heavy normal

ed.name: 蹲轻拳 (2LP)
ed.notes: Chains into stand LP / crouch LP; Hits low but has stubby range (functions like other characters' crouch LK); Incurs 20% damage scaling penalty if used as the first hit of a combo

ed.name: 蹲中拳 (2MP)
ed.notes: Hits low (functions like other characters' crouch MK); A little bit stubby compared to most crouch MK; Incurs a 20% damage scaling penalty if used as the first hit of a combo

ed.name: 蹲重拳 (2HP)
ed.notes: Ed's sweep button (crouch HK is a hit confirmable target combo tool)

ed.name: 蹲轻脚 (2LK)
ed.notes: Great range for a light normal (functions similar to other characters stand LK); Hurtbox extensions on frames 3-4 are projectile invincible; Incurs 20% damage scaling penalty if used as the first hit of a combo; Topmost hurtboxes on frames 1-6 are vulnerable only to airborne attacks (this is to discourage its use as an anti-air)

ed.name: 蹲中脚 (2MK)
ed.notes: Forces stand; Great range and fully cancelable combo / poke tool as well as being a situational anti-air; Whiffs on crouchers from further away; +3F extra recovery frame (19F) on whiff; Extends a wide hurtbox on whiff until the end of recovery

ed.name: 蹲重脚 (2HK)
ed.notes: Fully cancelable combo / poke tool with fantastic range that as a hit confirmable Target Combo extension; +2F extra recovery frame (21F) on whiff

ed.name: 跳轻拳 (j.LP)
ed.notes: Basically just a smaller but faster version of jump HP

ed.name: 跳中拳 (j.MP)
ed.notes: Cross-up; Projectile invincible on lower body on frames 1-22 (good option to avoid projectiles)

ed.name: 跳重拳 (j.HP)
ed.notes: Spikes down airborne opponents on Counter-Hit / Punish Counter; Solid jump-in hitboxes; Projectile invincible on lower body (legs) on frames 9-23

ed.name: 跳轻脚 (j.LK)
ed.notes: Solid vertical jump-in range; Instant Overhead that cannot be crouched if used meaty on opponents wake-up from a properly spaced distance; Can also be used as a fuzzy instant Overhead on opponents in Burnout

ed.name: 跳中脚 (j.MK)
ed.notes: Very far horizontal reach (furthest of Ed's air normals); Huge hurtbox extension 3F before active makes this move susceptible to being counterpoked out of the air; Projectile invincible on the lower body (legs) on frames 10-20 as well as on the punching hurtbox extension during start-up on frames 7-9

ed.name: 跳重脚 (j.HK)
ed.notes: Puts airborne opponents into a juggle state; Projectile invincible on lower body on frames 8-17; Can only hit standing opponents up close one frame before landing

ed.name: Psycho Knuckle (level 1)
ed.notes: Requires Ed to hold HP for at least 30 frames before being released; Puts opponent into a crumple state on hit (+12 frames before the crumple state goes airborne); Grants +4 extra KDA (and +4 more frames of a grounded crumple state) on Punish Counter; Switches side with the opponent on hit / block unless they're close enough to the corner; Becomes +2 on block when it doesn't cross up on an opponent close to the corner; Can be canceled during start-up into Kill Rush command dash (Forward only) on frames 9-30; Has an extended foot hurtbox on frames 7 and onward; Recovery frames vary greatly - 25F: When a cornered opponent blocks this attack resulting in the +4 extra frame advantage on block | 29F: When the move is blocked and Ed goes behind the opponent | 32F: When the move whiffs and Ed goes behind the opponent | 35F: When all the active frames play out without connecting (like if the opponent jumps to avoid this while cornered); BUG?: If this move somehow connects on active frames 10-15 (only really possible in meaty oki scenarios), it doesn't sideswitch and deals less knockdown advantage and blockstun, even being punishable on block (ranging from -8 to -13 on block)

ed.name: Psycho Knuckle (level 2)
ed.notes: Strike hitbox that also has 1 hit of projectile durability (can pierce through 1-hit non-OD projectiles); Requires Ed to hold HP for at least 60 frames before being released; Puts opponent into a crumple state on hit (+12 frames before the crumple state goes airborne); Grants +4 extra KDA (and +4 more frames of a grounded crumple state) on Punish Counter; Can be canceled during start-up into Kill Rush command dash (Forward only) on frames 9-60; Has an extended foot hurtbox on frames 7 and onward; Recovery frames vary greatly - 29F: When the move is blocked and Ed goes behind the opponent | 32F: When the move whiffs and Ed goes behind the opponent | 35F: When all the active frames play out without connecting (like if the opponent jumps to avoid this while cornered)

ed.name: Cobra Punch
ed.notes: Low crush on frames 7-19 (not actually airborne); Puts airborne opponents into a limited OTG state (Secret Dribble Combos Only™); Can be used to corpse hop over a grounded opponent

ed.name: Flicker Combination 1
ed.notes: "One, Two!"; +3 on Hit and safe on block (-3) makes this a great poke / bully tool especially against opponents in Burnout; Third hit (LK) is hit confirmable after seeing if the first hits were blocked or not

ed.name: Flicker Combination 2
ed.notes: "One, Two, Three!"; Leaves Ed up close on hit with +1 frame advantage for pressure; Being hit confirmable makes this a great poke / bully tool

ed.name: Body Blow Combination
ed.notes: Combo tool that's fully cancelable; Puts opponents into a limited juggle state on hit; Second hit (HP) can whiff on block if used from max range resulting in -23 on whiff; Cannot be canceled into Kill Rush (backward); Counts as 2 hits of damage scaling

ed.name: Hitman Combination 1
ed.notes: Relatively safe on block if used from a good distance; Second hit can whiff if the first hit connects from max range resulting in -15 on hit / -20 on block

ed.name: Hitman Combination 2
ed.notes: Third hit (HP) is not an Overhead (despite looking like one)

ed.name: Low Smash Combination
ed.notes: Cancelable into all Supers on hit / block as well as Kill Rush (f+KK / b+KK) on hit only; Puts opponent into a limited juggle state on hit; Both hits are always a true blockstring (cannot frame trap the opponent's attempted punish on crouch HK); Counts as 3 hits of damage scaling

ed.name: Face Buster
ed.notes: Throw Loop (corner only): Drive Rush with 4F timing to throw the opponent (can block reversals out of this Drive Rush) | Dash forward and walk 3F for manually timed throw loop against Zangief only | LK Psycho Flicker (hold) with a manual 2F timing window pulls them in for +4 pressure on block (and it's safe from most Reversals and Drive Reversal); Punish Counter gives +70% (2040) damage, Hard Knockdown (denies back-roll option on wake-up), depletes 1 bar of Drive gauge from the opponent, and builds twice as much Super gauge for the attacker; Throw Escape builds 0.5 Drive bars for the defender (randomly assigned if throws are input simultaneously)

ed.name: Rib Crusher
ed.notes: Back Throw oki: basic meaties like f+HP or MK Flicker, and can Drive Rush with crouch MK / stand MP / stand HP for pressure or with stand LK for an auto-timed tick throw; Drive Rush oki does not give a true strike/throw mixup, and Ed cannot block reversals with 7F startup or faster even when whiffing stand LP (this whiff also leaves Ed point blank at -7 if the opponent does nothing); Punish Counter gives +70% (2040) damage, Hard Knockdown (denies back-roll option on wake-up), depletes 1 bar of Drive gauge from the opponent, and builds twice as much Super gauge for the attacker; Throw Escape builds 0.5 Drive bars for the defender (randomly assigned if throws are input simultaneously)

ed.name: Drive Impact: Turn Punch
ed.notes: 2 hits of armor on frames 1-27; Damages opponents Drive Gauge on Block (1/2 bar) | Hit (1 bar) | Counter-Hit (1.25 bar) | Punish Counter (1.5 bar); Knocks down on hit; Pushes the opponent far back on hit or block and causes a Wall Splat if they hit the wall (Parry prevents the backwards stumble and Wall Splat, greatly reducing the pushback); Regular KDA without Wall Splat +35 KD | Wall Splat on Hit +65 KD | Wall Splat on Block +72 HKD; KDA can vary greatly depending on how high the opponent wall splats (higher KDA the higher they wall splat); Advantage after Wall Splat can vary depending on distance from the corner (farther from corner gives higher advantage); Crumples the opponent on Punish Counter or after absorbing at least 1 attack during start-up (+21 frames before the crumple state goes airborne, followed by airborne state on frames 22-46 before they are grounded); Puts airborne opponents into a long spinning free juggle state when hit as a Punish Counter or after absorbing an attack; If the armor absorbs an attack it slows the overall start-up by 1F (27F total instead of 26F) and incurs 6F hitstop for each projectile hit absorbed (making it less likely to punish the opponent after absorbing projectiles); Absorbing an attack causes the player to take 1/2 the damage in recoverable health (but will KO if this would bring the player's health below zero); Stun/Dizzy occurs when a Wall Splat connects on an opponent in Burnout; Stun gives a free combo follow-up for the next 195F after hitting the wall, followed by a HKD if the player falls to the ground untouched (the last 7F before hitting the ground has a crouch-sized hurtbox but is considered standing, allowing for unique combo setups); Incurs 20% damage scaling penalty if used as the first hit of a combo (applies to wall splat on HIT, crumple, Burnout dizzy on hit/block, or any character-specific means of comboing after a regular Drive Impact); Incurs a 20% multiplier damage scaling penalty after a Wall Splat on BLOCK - Because the blocked Drive Impact is not considered a "hit" for the combo, the next attack can incur its own separate damage scaling as a combo starter; Wall Splat puts opponent into a special juggle state where the next move freely connects and continues the juggle even if it normally wouldn't (similar to a Forced Knockdown or Drive Rush juggle properties); Does not cause Wall Splat if the Drive Impact connects as a combo or a true blockstring with no gaps (LOCK icon appears on-screen); It is possible to "combo" into Stun if the opponent has under 1.5 Drive bars - a blocked DI Wall Splat from slightly outside the corner into a second DI on hit will cause Burnout and Stun (because the blocked DI is not technically considered a combo starter); Costs 1 bar of Drive Gauge; Cinematic slowdown occurs if both players activate Drive Impact within range of each other (granting a Punish Counter to the player who activates it later); Attempting to counter with DI vs. DI with under 400 HP will result in a KO, as the second player will not have enough health to absorb it; Clashes with other Drive Impacts and refunds the Drive gauge cost if they collide on the same active frame (start at exactly the same time, or 1F apart if the first Drive Impact absorbs a strike) - The meter refund does not prevent Burnout from occurring; The scrub killer

ed.name: Drive Reversal: Hammer Blow
ed.notes: Has two versions: one performed during blockstun or parry stun (20F start-up) and one performed as a wake-up reversal (18F start-up); Fully invincible on frames 1-22 (blockstun) / frames 1-20 (reversal); Armor Break (blows through all armor like Drive Impact, but not counters like JP's Amnesia); Trying to Drive Reversal after the blockstun ends results in a Drive Impact; Drive Reversal immediately removes the current blockstun you're in and starts the attack; Causes a 4F screen freeze after the 6th start-up frame, which allows the opponent to perform a simple OS (inputting their buttons during the buffer window) to prevent their next attack from coming out; Safe on block (-2) when used against an opponent in Burnout; Costs 2 bars of Drive Gauge; If the opponent tries to throw against a wake-up Drive Reversal, it causes a 12F screen freeze and refunds 1 bar of Drive gauge (but does not prevent Burnout); Guaranteed to interrupt any Drive Rush canceled normal if performed immediately out of blockstun (unless the opponent reacts with an invincible move or counter)

ed.name: 斗气招架 (Drive Parry)
ed.notes: Parries all strikes and projectiles (high and low) from frame 1; 12F parry window (can hold the parry to extend the parry window); Perfect Parry occurs on the first 2 active frames (cannot achieve Perfect Parry if you buffer into parry by holding it during Reversal windows; Perfect Parries have to be timed properly); Can still hold charge directions during Parry (allowing characters with charge specials to stand block before performing their reversal); Can block during the recovery frames of a regular parry (can still get hit during the recovery frames if you don't block correctly); Getting thrown or hit at any point during the recovery frames of a whiffed parry attempt results in a Punish Counter; Successfully parrying a move puts you into the same amount of blockstun as that move would regularly do on block (but a Perfect Parry has only 1F of recovery); Throw invincible during the recovery of a successful parry (just like during blockstun); Perfect Parrying a strike has only 1F of recovery and disables the opponent from canceling their attack (basically a guaranteed punish opportunity except for safe jump setups); Perfect Parrying a strike requires holding the correct block direction (Down+Back for low strikes, Back for high/mid strikes); Attempting a Perfect Parry with the wrong block direction results in an "imperfect parry" that builds an extra 3000 Drive Gauge and plays a distinct audio/visual cue; After a successful Perfect Parry, you suffer a 50% penalty to your Damage, Drive Gauge Generation, and Drive Gauge Damage on any of your following attacks when punishing the opponent (in addition, both you and the opponent suffer a 20% penalty to your Super Meter gain during this period); Fully invincible for 6F after a successful Perfect Parry against a strike, which carries over to any attack you perform (ensuring a 5F or faster punish will always interrupt multi-hit attacks); Perfect Parrying projectiles puts you into fixed 10 frames of recovery and applies the same 50% scaling penalties (and 20% Super Meter penalty) on your following attacks when punishing the opponent; Parrying a Strike and Projectile on the same frame will result in a regular parry for the strike attack (effectively ignoring the projectile's hitstop / blockstun); Perfect Parrying a Strike and Projectile on the same frame will give a screen freeze like you Perfect Parried a Strike, but still give you 10F recovery as if you had Perfect Parried a Projectile; Can cancel into Drive Rush during active frames 3 and onward (fastest Drive Rush method is to buffer a forward input before doing parry + forward again); Can cancel into Drive Reversal from a successful parry (just like you normally can during blockstun); Costs 1/2 bar of Drive Gauge and continues to deplete 50 Drive Gauge per frame (0.3 Drive bars per second) as you hold the Parry; You lose the parry if you go into Burnout from the initial Drive Gauge cost (Perfect Parry requires frame-perfect timing when starting from under 1/2 of a Drive bar); Rewards 1 bar of Drive Gauge (1/2 bar total after factoring in the initial parry cost) for successfully parrying a strike; Rewards 1/2 bar of Drive Gauge (0 bar total after factoring in the initial parry cost) for successfully parrying a projectile (with a few exceptions); Rewards 2 bars of Drive Gauge (1.5 bars total after factoring in the initial parry cost) for successful parrying a Super Art or Drive Impact; Successfully parrying a strike attack splits the regular block pushback between both players (while Perfect Parrying a strike removes all of its pushback); Successfully parrying a projectile or Drive Impact reduces the pushback of it by half (while Perfect Parrying a projectile or Drive Impact removes all of its pushback); Your hurtbox and throw box expand slightly towards the opponent for the entire duration of the Parry (Throw box extension starts instantly on frame 1, while the Hurtbox extension starts on frame 3, after the initial 2F Perfect Parry window); Parrying while crouching maintains a regular crouch hurtbox for the first 2 frames of the parry (during the initial Perfect Parry window)

ed.name: 斗气冲刺 (Drive Rush)
ed.notes: Dashes forward and enhances the next normal or command normal used out of the Drive Rush with +4 extra hitstun / blockstun, as well as improved juggle properties (Juggle Limit increased by +3 / Juggle Start/Increase reduced to 0); The +4 bonus frame advantage gained from a Drive Rush enhanced move also stacks with any bonus frame advantage that move may have gained from Counter-Hit, Punish Counter, or Burnout; Grounded special-cancelable normals can also be canceled into Drive Rush on hit or block, as well as from light normals on whiff; Drive Rush maintains buffers (freezes the buffer window) during its start-up and freeze frames - This allows players to do things normally not possible within the normal buffer windows, such as Drive Rushing into a charge special; The initial 10F screen freeze eats the opponent's directional inputs (except Jumps) but does not prevent attacks from being buffered immediately afterward (this can cause inputs to be combined in unintended ways, such as crouch MK + Fireball performing a raw Fireball, or a vertical jump + walk forward turning into a forward jump); Framedata shown in parentheses refers to the Drive Rush version used from a Parry; Drive Rush recovery is only 24F total (23F if done from a Parry) - but the enhanced dash itself is 46F total (45F if done from Parry) and you can cancel it as early as frame 9 (frame 11 if done from a Parry); Inputting a direction (walk/crouch/block/jump) after the Drive Rush recovery plays out 2 additional recovery frames before the transition occurs (this allows the user to perform an enhanced crouching or command normal late in the dash by inputting the direction + button simultaneously); You stop building any form of Drive Gauge on your attacks after using a Drive Rush in the MIDDLE of a combo (but you still continue to build Drive gauge as normal if you did Drive Rush at the START of a combo); Applies an extra damage scaling penalty after using a Drive Rush in the MIDDLE of a combo (no damage scaling if you use Drive Rush at the START of a combo); Costs 3 bars of Drive Gauge if canceled into from a normal attack; Costs 1/2 bar of Drive Gauge if canceled into from Parry (for a total of 1 bar of Drive Gauge when you factor in the initial 1/2 bar cost of the Parry); Normals used out of Drive Rush carry additional forward momentum (but throws and specials immediately halt all momentum, which can be a useful strategy to punish opponents for trying to interrupt your Drive Rush); Parry Drive Rush can only be initiated after frame 3 of the Parry (but can be performed immediately after recovering from a successful parry); Parry Drive Rush cannot be initiated with less than 1/2 of a Drive bar (as the initial Parry cost will put the user into Burnout) - But whiff canceling a Light normal into Drive Rush can achieve a similar effect; Cannot cancel Drive Rush into a Parry (inputting MP+MK results in a MK normal coming out instead); Drive Rush puts the user into a counter-hit state for the entire duration (this makes it impossible to tech a throw that connects during the dash)

ed.name: Psycho Spark
ed.notes: 1-hit Projectile hitbox; Can transition into Psycho Shoot (1-hit projectile) on frames 22-28; Tons of active frames and low recovery makes this an ideal oki tool; BUG?: Perfect Parrying this projectile results in only 1F recovery on the Perfect Parry as if it was a strike (despite also missing the screen freeze that comes with Perfect Parrying strike attacks)

ed.name: Psycho Shoot
ed.notes: 1-hit Projectile hitbox; Projectile speed varies depending on button strength; LP (Classic) / L (Modern): 0.05 speed; MP (Classic) / M (Modern): 0.1 speed; HP (Classic) / H (Modern): 0.15 speed

ed.name: Kill Rush (Forward)
ed.notes: No head hurtbox on frames 3-26; Cancelable into Kill Switch Break (f+P early) on frames 11-12; Cancelable into Kill Switch Chaser (f+P later) on frames 13-24; Cancelable into during start-up of Psycho Knuckle (hold HP) and Psycho Flicker (hold QCF+K); Counter-hit state for the entire duration; Distance: 2.24 (up to 2.69 if nothing is input during the first 17 post-recovery frames); Useful oki tool to chase Back Rise after some midscreen knockdowns (leave the stick in neutral for point blank oki, or hold crouch block to stop short to bait the opponent's throw)

ed.name: Kill Rush > Kill Switch Break
ed.notes: f+P must be input early (frames 1-11 of Kill Rush dash); Cannot hit cross-up (behind Ed); Launches the opponent into a limited juggle state on hit; Incurs 20% damage scaling penalty if used as the first hit of a combo; Counts as 2 hits of damage scaling when used during a combo

ed.name: Kill Rush > Kill Switch Chaser
ed.notes: f+P must be input late (frames 13-24 of Kill Rush dash); Cannot hit cross-up (behind Ed); Launches the opponent into a limited juggle state on hit (sometimes results in better juggle opportunities than Kill Switch Break); Doesn't have any additional damage scaling when used during a combo like the faster Kill Switch Break follow-up; Incurs 20% damage scaling penalty if used as the first hit of a combo

ed.name: Kill Rush (Backward)
ed.notes: No head hurtbox on frames 1-10; Cancelable into during start-up of Psycho Flicker (hold QCF+K); Steps back much further than Ed's regular backdash, albeit with 8F longer total recovery (31F instead of 23F); Counter-hit state for the entire duration; Ed extends a wide forward hurtbox during recovery, making him much more vulnerable to counterattacks (Drive Impact is a guaranteed punish at most ranges when Flicker is canceled from a normal); Distance: 0.999

ed.name: Psycho Storm
ed.notes: Strike and Throw invincible on frames 1-14; Armor Break; Depletes 0.5 Drive Bar on hit for the opponent; KDA varies when hitting airborne opponents (slightly higher KDA)

ed.name: Psycho Cannon
ed.notes: No invincibility whatsoever; 7-hit Super Projectile; Projectile speed varies depending on button strength (Classic) / direction held (Modern); LP (Classic) / Hold Back (Modern): 0.03 speed; MP (Classic) / Neutral (Modern): 0.045 speed; HP (Classic) / Hold Forward (Modern): 0.09 speed; Last hit launches opponent into a limited juggle state on hit (all the prior hits do not increase the juggle state); If another attack hits the opponent on the same frame as the last hit of this Super, the opponent stays grounded for combo extensions; Depletes 1 Drive Bar on hit for the opponent; The LP version depletes all Drive Bar on the last hit only (allows the opponent to resume Drive gauge regeneration during Ed's long juggle sequences); Fantastic tool for combos / pressure / setups; Doesn't deal a lot of damage by itself but when combined with all of Ed's other tools this a very powerful Super; 50% penalty to Super meter gain on any of the follow-up hits Ed combos into after this move; KDA varies greatly depending on a lot of factors (the higher in the air this hits the higher the KDA)

ed.name: Psycho Chamber
ed.notes: Fully invincible on frames 1-14; Armor Break; Depletes 1.5 Drive Bars on hit for the opponent; Super cinematic time regenerates ~2.2 Drive Bars for Ed; Can trade on active frames 15-19 (runs out of invincibility) dealing only 500 damage since it doesn't transition into the cinematic version; Incurs 10% damage scaling when canceled into from specials (20% when canceled from LP Psycho Uppercut / 30% when canceled into from LK/MK Flickers)

ed.name: Psycho Chamber (Critical Art)
ed.notes: Fully invincible on frames 1-14; Armor Break; Critical Art does +500 extra damage over regular version; Depletes 2 Drive Bars on hit for the opponent; Super cinematic time regenerates ~2.2 Drive Bars for Ed; Can trade on active frames 15-19 (runs out of invincibility) dealing only 500 damage since it doesn't transition into the cinematic version; Incurs 10% damage scaling when canceled into from specials (20% when canceled from LP Psycho Uppercut / 30% when canceled into from LK/MK Flickers)

ed.name: Psycho Spark
ed.notes: 2-hit OD Projectile hitbox; Can transition into OD Psycho Shoot (2-hit OD Projectile) on frames 18-28; With perfect meaty timing on the last active frame this only hits once and doesn't knock down the opponent, resulting in +16 on hit / +10 on block (although the non-OD version offers similar meaty advantage without requiring a frame perfect setup); BUG?: Perfect Parrying this projectile results in only 1F recovery on the Perfect Parry as if it was a strike (despite also missing the screen freeze that comes with Perfect Parrying strike attacks)

variations.notes: 2-hit OD Projectile hitbox; Can transition into OD Psycho Shoot (2-hit OD Projectile) on frames 18-28; With perfect meaty timing on the last active frame this only hits once and doesn't knock down the opponent, resulting in +16 on hit / +10 on block (although the non-OD version offers similar meaty advantage without requiring a frame perfect setup); BUG?: Perfect Parrying this projectile results in only 1F recovery on the Perfect Parry as if it was a strike (despite also missing the screen freeze that comes with Perfect Parrying strike attacks)

ed.name: Psycho Shoot
ed.notes: 2-hit OD Projectile hitbox; Projectile speed varies depending on button strength; LP (Classic) / L (Modern): 0.04 speed; MP (Classic) / M (Modern): 0.1 speed; HP (Classic) / H (Modern): 0.175 speed; Gains +4 extra KD (+50 KD) if used point-blank after an OD Psycho Spark hit

variations.notes: 2-hit OD Projectile hitbox; Projectile speed varies depending on button strength; LP (Classic) / L (Modern): 0.04 speed; MP (Classic) / M (Modern): 0.1 speed; HP (Classic) / H (Modern): 0.175 speed; Gains +4 extra KD (+50 KD) if used point-blank after an OD Psycho Spark hit

ed.name: Psycho Uppercut
ed.notes: Invincible to airborne strikes on frames 1-19; Cannot hit cross-up (behind Ed); Launches opponent into a limited juggle state; Cannot juggle into SA3 with the cancel, even if delayed (use LP Psycho Uppercut instead for that purpose)

variations.invincible: Invincible to airborne strikes on frames 1-15
variations.notes: Invincible to airborne strikes on frames 1-15; Great anti-air despite being slow start-up, which can actually make it more consistent againt delayed airborne approaches like Divekicks; Cannot hit cross-up (behind Ed); Launches opponent into a limited juggle state; The cancel into SA3 must be delayed a little bit in order to juggle properly; Has -5F less recovery frames (23F) on hit and block; Incurs 30% damage scaling penalty if used as the first hit of a combo; Counts as 2 hits of damage scaling when used during a combo

variations.invincible: Invincible to airborne strikes on frames 1-19
variations.notes: Invincible to airborne strikes on frames 1-19; Cannot hit cross-up (behind Ed); Launches opponent into a limited juggle state; Cannot juggle into SA3 with the cancel, even if delayed (use LP Psycho Uppercut instead for that purpose)

variations.invincible: Invincible to airborne strikes on frames 1-19
variations.notes: Invincible to airborne strikes on frames 1-19; Cannot hit cross-up (behind Ed); Launches opponent into a limited juggle state; Cannot juggle into SA3 with the cancel, even if delayed (use LP Psycho Uppercut instead for that purpose)

variations.invincible: Fully invincible on frames 1-16 (gains extended invincibility on HIT for the follow-up swing
variations.notes: Fully invincible on frames 1-16 (gains extended invincibility on HIT for the follow-up swing; Cannot hit cross-up (behind Ed); Has +5F extra recovery frames (41F) on hit or block; Framedata listed refers to the version that plays out on whiff (performs an extra attack on hit or block); Slow start-up makes this a poor reversal on wake-up but can be used to blow through the opponents buttons / delayed tech / Reversals

ed.name: Psycho Blitz
ed.notes: 3 hits; Puts the opponent into a limited juggle state on hit; +8 recovery frames (24F) on block only

variations.notes: 3 hits; Carries over Counter-Hit / Punish Counter bonus frame advantage to all hits; Puts airborne opponents into a limited juggle state on hit; Incurs 30% damage scaling penalty if used as the first hit of a combo
3 hits; Puts the opponent into a limited juggle state on hit; +8 recovery frames (24F) on block only
3 hits; Puts the opponent into a limited juggle state on hit; +3 recovery frames (26F) on block only

9 hits (7 hits on block/whiff); Puts the opponent into a limited juggle state on the final 9th hit (the first 8 hits keep the opponent grounded and maintain the current juggle state on airborne opponents; Can be canceled into SA2/SA3 on the last 2 hits (Ed gets different SA2 combo routes depending on which hit is canceled from); All 4-frame normals can punish this move on block, and can interrupt its startup when canceled from Ed's light normals; Incurs 30% damage scaling penalty if used as the first hit of a combo; Counts as 2 hits of damage scaling when used during a combo

ed.name: Psycho Flicker
