elena.name: 站轻拳 (5LP)
elena.notes: Fantastic range for a jab; Incurs 20% damage scaling penalty if used as the first hit of a combo

elena.name: 站中拳 (5MP)
elena.notes: Great poke / buffer / footsies tool in neutral with a hit confirmable Target Combo follow-up; Active frames 1-2 have shorter range; Active frames 3-5 gain an extended foot hitbox resulting in 2F better advantage on hit or block; Foot hitbox on active frames 3-5 cannot hit crouching opponents or cross-up (behind Elena); The initial leg hitbox that can hit crouching opponents is only active during the first 3 active frames (disappears on active frame 4-5), making it less useful as a meaty; Forces stand on Punish Counter (this enables the MP Target Combo follow-up to combo even on initially crouching opponents); Combos into a variety of follow-ups (5MP / 2MP / 2MK) when used to Punish moves in the midrange; Hit confirmable into Super or the Target Combo extension (too delayed Target Combo cancels only combo with a Counter-hit, Punish Counter, or Drive Rush starter); Hatson's 2nd favorite move in the game

elena.name: 站重拳 (5HP)
elena.notes: Forces stand on hit; Further range foot hitbox cannot hit crouching opponents (shorter overall range against crouching opponents); Strong horizontal anti-air; Cannot hit cross-up (behind Elena); Hit confirmable (19F) into the HP target combo; Launches the opponent into a limited juggle state on Punish Counter; The brief extended leg hurtbox on frame 11 of start-up (1F before active) is strike invincible (cannot counter-poke projectiles)

elena.name: 站轻脚 (5LK)
elena.notes: Amazing range for a light normal (furthest of Elena's light normals) but doesn't combo into LK Spin Scythe like her jabs do; Incurs 20% damage scaling penalty if used as the first hit of a combo

elena.name: 站中脚 (5MK)
elena.notes: Core combo and frametrap tool; +2F extra recovery frames (15F) on whiff

elena.name: 站重脚 (5HK)
elena.notes: Crushes low attacks on frames 9-17; Launches the opponent into a limited juggle state on Punish Counter; The brief extended leg hurtbox on frame 11 of start-up (1F before active) is strike invincible (cannot counter-poke projectiles)

elena.name: 蹲轻拳 (2LP)
elena.notes: Chains into crouch LP / crouch LK; Incurs 20% damage scaling penalty if used as the first hit of a combo; Topmost hurtboxes on frames 1-6 are vulnerable only to airborne attacks (this is to discourage its use as an anti-air)

elena.name: 蹲中拳 (2MP)
elena.notes: Combo / Poke / Buffer tool with good range; Not an ideal anti-air despite looking like one

elena.name: 蹲重拳 (2HP)
elena.notes: Upper body (legs) are invincible to airborne strikes on frames 8-19; Core combo and anti-air tool; Forces stand on hit (important for Rhino Horn combo routes); Cannot hit cross-up (behind Elena); Second hit puts airborne opponents into a limited juggle state (this won't connect when the first hit causes an air reset) giving Elena some combo potential when anti-airing early with crouch HP so only the 2nd hit connects; Both hits connect after a Drive Impact crumple or wall splat for improved juggle damage; Carries over Counter-Hit / Punish Counter bonus frame advantage to both hits; Special / Drive Rush cancel occurs on the second hit (even if this hit whiffs); Incurs 20% damage scaling penalty if used as the first hit of a combo

elena.name: 蹲轻脚 (2LK)
elena.notes: Chains into crouch LP / crouch LK; Incurs 20% damage scaling penalty if used as the first hit of a combo

elena.name: 蹲中脚 (2MK)
elena.notes: +2F extra recovery frames (18F) on whiff or block; Incurs 20% damage scaling penalty if used as the first hit of a combo; Moves forward on startup for a more consistent link into crouch LP; Decent pressure tool with Drive Rush that leaves Elena +1 on block slightly out of throw range

elena.name: 蹲重脚 (2HK)
elena.notes: Has some Juggle potential naturally without Drive Rush; Great range for a sweep but punishable by most other sweeps at max range

elena.name: 跳轻拳 (j.LP)
elena.notes: Cross-up that can gain extra frame advantage with a Target Combo extension; Can be used as a fuzzy instant Overhead (except against Blanka) after a deep jump-in Heavy (or jump-in Mediums in Burnout as well)

elena.name: 跳中拳 (j.MP)
elena.notes: Puts airborne opponents into a limited juggle state; Can follow up with a Target Combo extension for an even stronger juggle; Whiffs completely on normal-sized crouching opponents; Shifts the normal jumping hurtbox upward during start-up (helps with avoiding some attacks)

elena.name: 跳重拳 (j.HP)
elena.notes: Elena's strongest general purpose jump-in (reaches grounded opponents faster and deals all its damage in one hit unlike jump HK

elena.name: 跳轻脚 (j.LK)
elena.notes: Strong hitbox priority (especially vertically downwards) that can beat or trade with many anti-air normals; Can be used as a fuzzy instant Overhead after a deep jump-in Heavy (or jump-in Mediums in Burnout as well)

elena.name: 跳中脚 (j.MK)
elena.notes: Cross-up; Has a wide hitbox in both directions

elena.name: 跳重脚 (j.HK)
elena.notes: First hit puts airborne opponents into a limited juggle state; Second hit causes a spiked knockdown on airborne opponents; Second hit has the furthest horizontal range on Elena's jump-ins; Overall weaker as a jump-in since only one hit will connect at most jump timings

elena.name: Trunk Slap 1
elena.notes: Mid-range poke tool with high pushback that's mostly at safe on block (except at close range against exceptionally far-reaching 4F normals) and deals a good amount of drive gauge damage on block; Easily hit confirmable into the Target Combo follow-up (21F hit confirm window)

elena.name: Handstand Whip 1
elena.notes: Overhead with fast start-up and decent range; Can be hit confirmed into the Target Combo follow-up (17F hit confirm window)

elena.name: Round Arch
elena.notes: Crushes low attacks on frames 9-17 and shifts Elena's throw hurtbox backward starting on frame 5; Not actually airborne despite the animation; Puts the opponent into a limited juggle state on Punish Counter that can only juggle into LK / MK / OD Scratch Wheel in the corner; +2F extra recovery frames (19F) on whiff; Incurs 20% damage scaling penalty if used as the first hit of a combo

elena.name: Slide
elena.notes: Crouching state for the entire duration of the move (can slide under attacks that don't hit Crouch) but does not low profile under fireballs; Half-screen slide that hits low; +4F extra recovery frames (22F) on whiff

elena.name: Starling Beak
elena.notes: Second hit is fully cancelable while the first hit is only Super cancelable; Second hit cannot hit crouching opponents; Frame advantage shown in parenthesis refers to when the second hit whiffs on a crouching opponent; Interruptible 6F gap on block between hits

elena.name: Turning Tail
elena.notes: Both the follow-up hits on HP cannot hit crouching opponents; How unsafe the move is on block varies depending on if the opponent stand or crouch blocks the initial stand HP; Stand block: -3 | Crouch Block after blocking the initial HP standing: -10 | Crouch blocking the initial HP and the follow-up hits: -23; Puts the opponent into a limited juggle state on hit with a much stronger juggle after Punish Counter stand HP; Follow-up hits incur 20% damage scaling penatly if used as the first hit of a combo (only occurs if you crouch block the initial HP and then get hit standing)

elena.name: Hind Kick
elena.notes: Elena's core target combo conversion on crouching opponents (stand HP and crouch MK target combos both can't hit crouching opponents); Launches the opponent into a limited juggle state on hit

elena.name: Fluttering Lark
elena.notes: Second hit is fully cancelable; Second hit cannot hit crouching opponents and will always whiff after blocked crouch MK (block data is only applicable if parried); Frame advantage shown in parenthesis refers to when the second hit whiffs on a crouching opponent; +4 extra recovery frames (24F) on whiff

elena.name: Trunk Slap 2
elena.notes: Hit confirmable extension from Elena's long range f+HP that leads to a knockdown ender on hit; Has no juggle potential on its own (does not juggle after a wall splat)

elena.name: Trunk Slap Final
elena.notes: Target Combo ender with good corner carry and knockdown advantage; Can lead to auto-timed Lynx Whirl pressure on the opponent's wakeup

elena.name: Handstand Whip 2
elena.notes: Hit confirmable Target Combo that grants a meterless knockdown from Elena's long range overhead

elena.name: Soaring Raid
elena.notes: Both hits cross-up and grant Elena +12 frame advantage combo follow-ups on hit; If the opponent is crouching, Elena lands before the MK follow-up active frames come out; The MK follow-up does not connect as an air-to-air even in Forced Knockdown scenarios

elena.name: Raptor Range
elena.notes: Both hits put airborne opponents into a limited juggle state; Cannot hit a grounded opponent

elena.name: Leg Tackle
elena.notes: Has a frame perfect corner throw loop against Zangief (dash + walk 2F); Can Drive Rush with frame perfect timing for a 1-bar corner throw loop against standard characters (slightly more lenient against Alex / Blanka / E. Honda / Marisa / Sagat / Zangief); Punish Counter gives +70% (2040) damage, Hard Knockdown (denies back-roll option on wake-up), depletes 1 bar of Drive gauge from the opponent, and builds twice as much Super gauge for the attacker; Throw Escape builds 0.5 Drive bars for the defender (randomly assigned if throws are input simultaneously)

elena.name: Leg Lift Throw
elena.notes: Cannot get throw oki after a corner side switch (except for a frame perfect Drive Rush + Throw against Zangief); Sets up an auto-timed Drive Rush + stand MK (+12 on hit / +8 on block); Punish Counter gives +70% (2040) damage, Hard Knockdown (denies back-roll option on wake-up), depletes 1 bar of Drive gauge from the opponent, and builds twice as much Super gauge for the attacker; Throw Escape builds 0.5 Drive bars for the defender (randomly assigned if throws are input simultaneously)

elena.name: Drive Impact: Giraffe Neck
elena.notes: 2 hits of armor on frames 1-27; Damages opponents Drive Gauge on Block (1/2 bar) | Hit (1 bar) | Counter-Hit (1.25 bar) | Punish Counter (1.5 bar); Knocks down on hit; Pushes the opponent far back on hit or block and causes a Wall Splat if they hit the wall (Parry prevents the backwards stumble and Wall Splat, greatly reducing the pushback); Regular KDA without Wall Splat +35 KD | Wall Splat on Hit +65 KD | Wall Splat on Block +72 HKD; KDA can vary greatly depending on how high the opponent wall splats (higher KDA the higher they wall splat); Advantage after Wall Splat can vary depending on distance from the corner (farther from corner gives higher advantage); Crumples the opponent on Punish Counter or after absorbing at least 1 attack during start-up (+21 frames before the crumple state goes airborne, followed by airborne state on frames 22-46 before they are grounded); Puts airborne opponents into a long spinning free juggle state when hit as a Punish Counter or after absorbing an attack; If the armor absorbs an attack it slows the overall start-up by 1F (27F total instead of 26F) and incurs 6F hitstop for each projectile hit absorbed (making it less likely to punish the opponent after absorbing projectiles); Absorbing an attack causes the player to take 1/2 the damage in recoverable health (but will KO if this would bring the player's health below zero); Stun/Dizzy occurs when a Wall Splat connects on an opponent in Burnout; Stun gives a free combo follow-up for the next 195F after hitting the wall, followed by a HKD if the player falls to the ground untouched (the last 7F before hitting the ground has a crouch-sized hurtbox but is considered standing, allowing for unique combo setups); Incurs 20% damage scaling penalty if used as the first hit of a combo (applies to wall splat on HIT, crumple, Burnout dizzy on hit/block, or any character-specific means of comboing after a regular Drive Impact); Incurs a 20% multiplier damage scaling penalty after a Wall Splat on BLOCK - Because the blocked Drive Impact is not considered a "hit" for the combo, the next attack can incur its own separate damage scaling as a combo starter; Wall Splat puts opponent into a special juggle state where the next move freely connects and continues the juggle even if it normally wouldn't (similar to a Forced Knockdown or Drive Rush juggle properties); Does not cause Wall Splat if the Drive Impact connects as a combo or a true blockstring with no gaps (LOCK icon appears on-screen); It is possible to "combo" into Stun if the opponent has under 1.5 Drive bars - a blocked DI Wall Splat from slightly outside the corner into a second DI on hit will cause Burnout and Stun (because the blocked DI is not technically considered a combo starter); Costs 1 bar of Drive Gauge; Cinematic slowdown occurs if both players activate Drive Impact within range of each other (granting a Punish Counter to the player who activates it later); Attempting to counter with DI vs. DI with under 400 HP will result in a KO, as the second player will not have enough health to absorb it; Clashes with other Drive Impacts and refunds the Drive gauge cost if they collide on the same active frame (start at exactly the same time, or 1F apart if the first Drive Impact absorbs a strike) - The meter refund does not prevent Burnout from occurring; The scrub killer

elena.name: Drive Reversal: Boar Charge
elena.notes: Has two versions: one performed during blockstun or parry stun (20F start-up) and one performed as a wake-up reversal (18F start-up); Fully invincible on frames 1-22 (blockstun) / frames 1-20 (reversal); Armor Break (blows through all armor like Drive Impact, but not counters like JP's Amnesia); Trying to Drive Reversal after the blockstun ends results in a Drive Impact; Drive Reversal immediately removes the current blockstun you're in and starts the attack; Causes a 4F screen freeze after the 6th start-up frame, which allows the opponent to perform a simple OS (inputting their buttons during the buffer window) to prevent their next attack from coming out; Safe on block (-2) when used against an opponent in Burnout; Costs 2 bars of Drive Gauge; If the opponent tries to throw against a wake-up Drive Reversal, it causes a 12F screen freeze and refunds 1 bar of Drive gauge (but does not prevent Burnout); Guaranteed to interrupt any Drive Rush canceled normal if performed immediately out of blockstun (unless the opponent reacts with an invincible move or counter)

elena.name: 斗气招架 (Drive Parry)
elena.notes: Parries all strikes and projectiles (high and low) from frame 1; 12F parry window (can hold the parry to extend the parry window); Perfect Parry occurs on the first 2 active frames (cannot achieve Perfect Parry if you buffer into parry by holding it during Reversal windows; Perfect Parries have to be timed properly); Can still hold charge directions during Parry (allowing characters with charge specials to stand block before performing their reversal); Can block during the recovery frames of a regular parry (can still get hit during the recovery frames if you don't block correctly); Getting thrown or hit at any point during the recovery frames of a whiffed parry attempt results in a Punish Counter; Successfully parrying a move puts you into the same amount of blockstun as that move would regularly do on block (but a Perfect Parry has only 1F of recovery); Throw invincible during the recovery of a successful parry (just like during blockstun); Perfect Parrying a strike has only 1F of recovery and disables the opponent from canceling their attack (basically a guaranteed punish opportunity except for safe jump setups); Perfect Parrying a strike requires holding the correct block direction (Down+Back for low strikes, Back for high/mid strikes); Attempting a Perfect Parry with the wrong block direction results in an "imperfect parry" that builds an extra 3000 Drive Gauge and plays a distinct audio/visual cue; After a successful Perfect Parry, you suffer a 50% penalty to your Damage, Drive Gauge Generation, and Drive Gauge Damage on any of your following attacks when punishing the opponent (in addition, both you and the opponent suffer a 20% penalty to your Super Meter gain during this period); Fully invincible for 6F after a successful Perfect Parry against a strike, which carries over to any attack you perform (ensuring a 5F or faster punish will always interrupt multi-hit attacks); Perfect Parrying projectiles puts you into fixed 10 frames of recovery and applies the same 50% scaling penalties (and 20% Super Meter penalty) on your following attacks when punishing the opponent; Parrying a Strike and Projectile on the same frame will result in a regular parry for the strike attack (effectively ignoring the projectile's hitstop / blockstun); Perfect Parrying a Strike and Projectile on the same frame will give a screen freeze like you Perfect Parried a Strike, but still give you 10F recovery as if you had Perfect Parried a Projectile; Can cancel into Drive Rush during active frames 3 and onward (fastest Drive Rush method is to buffer a forward input before doing parry + forward again); Can cancel into Drive Reversal from a successful parry (just like you normally can during blockstun); Costs 1/2 bar of Drive Gauge and continues to deplete 50 Drive Gauge per frame (0.3 Drive bars per second) as you hold the Parry; You lose the parry if you go into Burnout from the initial Drive Gauge cost (Perfect Parry requires frame-perfect timing when starting from under 1/2 of a Drive bar); Rewards 1 bar of Drive Gauge (1/2 bar total after factoring in the initial parry cost) for successfully parrying a strike; Rewards 1/2 bar of Drive Gauge (0 bar total after factoring in the initial parry cost) for successfully parrying a projectile (with a few exceptions); Rewards 2 bars of Drive Gauge (1.5 bars total after factoring in the initial parry cost) for successful parrying a Super Art or Drive Impact; Successfully parrying a strike attack splits the regular block pushback between both players (while Perfect Parrying a strike removes all of its pushback); Successfully parrying a projectile or Drive Impact reduces the pushback of it by half (while Perfect Parrying a projectile or Drive Impact removes all of its pushback); Your hurtbox and throw box expand slightly towards the opponent for the entire duration of the Parry (Throw box extension starts instantly on frame 1, while the Hurtbox extension starts on frame 3, after the initial 2F Perfect Parry window); Parrying while crouching maintains a regular crouch hurtbox for the first 2 frames of the parry (during the initial Perfect Parry window)

elena.name: 斗气冲刺 (Drive Rush)
elena.notes: Dashes forward and enhances the next normal or command normal used out of the Drive Rush with +4 extra hitstun / blockstun, as well as improved juggle properties (Juggle Limit increased by +3 / Juggle Start/Increase reduced to 0); The +4 bonus frame advantage gained from a Drive Rush enhanced move also stacks with any bonus frame advantage that move may have gained from Counter-Hit, Punish Counter, or Burnout; Grounded special-cancelable normals can also be canceled into Drive Rush on hit or block, as well as from light normals on whiff; Drive Rush maintains buffers (freezes the buffer window) during its start-up and freeze frames - This allows players to do things normally not possible within the normal buffer windows, such as Drive Rushing into a charge special; The initial 10F screen freeze eats the opponent's directional inputs (except Jumps) but does not prevent attacks from being buffered immediately afterward (this can cause inputs to be combined in unintended ways, such as crouch MK + Fireball performing a raw Fireball, or a vertical jump + walk forward turning into a forward jump); Framedata shown in parentheses refers to the Drive Rush version used from a Parry; Drive Rush recovery is only 24F total (23F if done from a Parry) - but the enhanced dash itself is 46F total (45F if done from Parry) and you can cancel it as early as frame 9 (frame 11 if done from a Parry); Inputting a direction (walk/crouch/block/jump) after the Drive Rush recovery plays out 2 additional recovery frames before the transition occurs (this allows the user to perform an enhanced crouching or command normal late in the dash by inputting the direction + button simultaneously); You stop building any form of Drive Gauge on your attacks after using a Drive Rush in the MIDDLE of a combo (but you still continue to build Drive gauge as normal if you did Drive Rush at the START of a combo); Applies an extra damage scaling penalty after using a Drive Rush in the MIDDLE of a combo (no damage scaling if you use Drive Rush at the START of a combo); Costs 3 bars of Drive Gauge if canceled into from a normal attack; Costs 1/2 bar of Drive Gauge if canceled into from Parry (for a total of 1 bar of Drive Gauge when you factor in the initial 1/2 bar cost of the Parry); Normals used out of Drive Rush carry additional forward momentum (but throws and specials immediately halt all momentum, which can be a useful strategy to punish opponents for trying to interrupt your Drive Rush); Parry Drive Rush can only be initiated after frame 3 of the Parry (but can be performed immediately after recovering from a successful parry); Parry Drive Rush cannot be initiated with less than 1/2 of a Drive bar (as the initial Parry cost will put the user into Burnout) - But whiff canceling a Light normal into Drive Rush can achieve a similar effect; Cannot cancel Drive Rush into a Parry (inputting MP+MK results in a MK normal coming out instead); Drive Rush puts the user into a counter-hit state for the entire duration (this makes it impossible to tech a throw that connects during the dash)

elena.name: Taunt
elena.notes: Framedata listed is for the down+Taunt version that deals a bit of damage (300) but is very punishable on hit or block; Back Taunt can transition to a handstand walk by holding forward or backward on frames 181-370

elena.name: Lynx Song > Leopard Snap

guile.name: Knee Bazooka
guile.notes: Crushes lows on frames 7-17; Can be spaced so it hits on last active frame, but it requires extremely specific spacing; Has some juggle potential

guile.name: Rolling Sobat
guile.notes: Crushes lows on frames 7-17; Very strong tool in neutral; The forward Sobat version has +3F extra recovery frames (21F) on whiff; Has a stronger priority hitbox on the back version; Has some Juggle potential

guile.name: Reverse Spin Kick
guile.notes: Throw invincible and crushes lows on frames 4-28; Very long range poke tool that beats both lows and throws and is pretty safe on block if spaced out properly (some very fast Supers with good range can punish it spaced out); Knocks down (+29 KD) grounded opponents on Counter-Hit; Causes a crumple state against grounded opponents on Punish Counter (opponent is in an airborne state for +9 frames before being knocked down); Puts airborne opponents into a limited juggle state on Counter-Hit / Punish Counter; The brief extended leg hurtbox on frame 16 of start-up (1F before active) is strike invincible (cannot counter-poke projectiles)

guile.name: Guile High Kick
guile.notes: Whiffs on most crouching moves (can still hit some like crouch HP); Launches opponent into a spinning free juggle state on Punish Counter; Puts airborne opponents into a limited juggle state on Counter-Hit; Has a very lenient cancel window for hit confirming (23F hit confirm window) and setting up Sonic Boom loops spacing; Not a reliable anti-air by itself (extends hurtboxes and does not have a strong anti-air hitbox); The brief extended leg hurtbox on frame 9 of start-up (1F before active) is strike invincible (cannot counter-poke projectiles)

guile.name: Recoil Cannon
guile.notes: Puts opponent into a limited juggle state on hit; The start-up of the HP follow-up is kara cancelable on frames 8-9 which positions Guile further back (helps optimize his gameplan and pressure)

guile.name: Double Shot
guile.notes: Second hit puts airborne opponents into a limited juggle state; Second hit adds 10% damage scaling penalty; +12 extra KDA (KD +56) when canceled into level 2 Super

guile.name: Drake Fang
guile.notes: Second hit (f+MP) is an Overhead; Second hit (f+MP) spikes down airborne opponents; 5F gap on block (can trade with 5F normals trying to punish the crouch MK on block; Counter-hit / Punish Counter puts the opponent into a limited juggle OTG state (can be followed up with LK / MK / OD Flash Kick juggles, with LK being by far the most consistent due to range); Second hit maintains the Counter-hit / Punish Counter state from the initial crouch MK

guile.name: Phantom Cutter
guile.notes: Launches opponent into a limited juggle state; Second hit (df+HK) only combos from Drive Rush (including Drive Rush juggle scenarios) or after a Punish Counter (first hit launches on Punish Counter) - this is hit confirmable since the cancel window is VERY lenient after the first hit of crHK; First hit (2HK) incurs a 20% damage scaling penalty if used as the first hit of a combo

guile.name: Dragon Suplex
guile.notes: Pseudo-Throw Loop: Frame-perfect walk forward throw beats 6F attacks on wake-up (corner only) - Beats 4F attacks (real throw loop) against wider characters like Alex / Blanka / Honda / Marisa / Zangief; Can also just Drive Rush to get a strike/throw mix in the corner; Punish Counter gives +70% (2040) damage, Hard Knockdown (denies back-roll option on wake-up), depletes 1 bar of Drive gauge from the opponent, and builds twice as much Super gauge for the attacker; Throw Escape builds 0.5 Drive bars for the defender (randomly assigned if throws are input simultaneously)

guile.name: Judo Throw
guile.notes: Back Throw oki when cornered: Can Drive Rush for a strike/throw mix or just do a meaty Sonic Boom or strike; Punish Counter gives +70% (2040) damage, Hard Knockdown (denies back-roll option on wake-up), depletes 1 bar of Drive gauge from the opponent, and builds twice as much Super gauge for the attacker; Throw Escape builds 0.5 Drive bars for the defender (randomly assigned if throws are input simultaneously)

guile.name: Flying Mare
guile.notes: Gets oki when near the corner (can also Drive Rush to get a bit further); Knockdown advantage is slightly better the higher in the air you air throw them; Punish Counter gives +70% (2040) damage, Hard Knockdown (denies back-roll option on wake-up), depletes 1 bar of Drive gauge from the opponent, and builds twice as much Super gauge for both players

guile.name: Flying Buster Drop
guile.notes: Back Throw oki when cornered: Yes but only a Drive Rush strike (throw not in range); Punish Counter gives +70% (2040) damage, Hard Knockdown (denies back-roll option on wake-up), depletes 1 bar of Drive gauge from the opponent, and builds twice as much Super gauge for both players

guile.name: Drive Impact: Blitz Combination
guile.notes: 2 hits of armor on frames 1-27; Damages opponents Drive Gauge on Block (1/2 bar) | Hit (1 bar) | Counter-Hit (1.25 bar) | Punish Counter (1.5 bar); Knocks down on hit; Pushes the opponent far back on hit or block and causes a Wall Splat if they hit the wall (Parry prevents the backwards stumble and Wall Splat, greatly reducing the pushback); Regular KDA without Wall Splat +35 KD | Wall Splat on Hit +65 KD | Wall Splat on Block +72 HKD; KDA can vary greatly depending on how high the opponent wall splats (higher KDA the higher they wall splat); Advantage after Wall Splat can vary depending on distance from the corner (farther from corner gives higher advantage); Crumples the opponent on Punish Counter or after absorbing at least 1 attack during start-up (+21 frames before the crumple state goes airborne, followed by airborne state on frames 22-46 before they are grounded); Puts airborne opponents into a long spinning free juggle state when hit as a Punish Counter or after absorbing an attack; If the armor absorbs an attack it slows the overall start-up by 1F (27F total instead of 26F) and incurs 6F hitstop for each projectile hit absorbed (making it less likely to punish the opponent after absorbing projectiles); Absorbing an attack causes the player to take 1/2 the damage in recoverable health (but will KO if this would bring the player's health below zero); Stun/Dizzy occurs when a Wall Splat connects on an opponent in Burnout; Stun gives a free combo follow-up for the next 195F after hitting the wall, followed by a HKD if the player falls to the ground untouched (the last 7F before hitting the ground has a crouch-sized hurtbox but is considered standing, allowing for unique combo setups); Incurs 20% damage scaling penalty if used as the first hit of a combo (applies to wall splat on HIT, crumple, Burnout dizzy on hit/block, or any character-specific means of comboing after a regular Drive Impact); Incurs a 20% multiplier damage scaling penalty after a Wall Splat on BLOCK - Because the blocked Drive Impact is not considered a "hit" for the combo, the next attack can incur its own separate damage scaling as a combo starter; Wall Splat puts opponent into a special juggle state where the next move freely connects and continues the juggle even if it normally wouldn't (similar to a Forced Knockdown or Drive Rush juggle properties); Does not cause Wall Splat if the Drive Impact connects as a combo or a true blockstring with no gaps (LOCK icon appears on-screen); It is possible to "combo" into Stun if the opponent has under 1.5 Drive bars - a blocked DI Wall Splat from slightly outside the corner into a second DI on hit will cause Burnout and Stun (because the blocked DI is not technically considered a combo starter); Costs 1 bar of Drive Gauge; Cinematic slowdown occurs if both players activate Drive Impact within range of each other (granting a Punish Counter to the player who activates it later); Attempting to counter with DI vs. DI with under 400 HP will result in a KO, as the second player will not have enough health to absorb it; Clashes with other Drive Impacts and refunds the Drive gauge cost if they collide on the same active frame (start at exactly the same time, or 1F apart if the first Drive Impact absorbs a strike) - The meter refund does not prevent Burnout from occurring; The scrub killer

guile.name: Drive Reversal: Strike Eagle
guile.notes: Has two versions: one performed during blockstun or parry stun (20F start-up) and one performed as a wake-up reversal (18F start-up); Fully invincible on frames 1-22 (blockstun) / frames 1-20 (reversal); Armor Break (blows through all armor like Drive Impact, but not counters like JP's Amnesia); Trying to Drive Reversal after the blockstun ends results in a Drive Impact; Drive Reversal immediately removes the current blockstun you're in and starts the attack; Causes a 4F screen freeze after the 6th start-up frame, which allows the opponent to perform a simple OS (inputting their buttons during the buffer window) to prevent their next attack from coming out; Safe on block (-2) when used against an opponent in Burnout; Costs 2 bars of Drive Gauge; If the opponent tries to throw against a wake-up Drive Reversal, it causes a 12F screen freeze and refunds 1 bar of Drive gauge (but does not prevent Burnout); Guaranteed to interrupt any Drive Rush canceled normal if performed immediately out of blockstun (unless the opponent reacts with an invincible move or counter)

guile.name: 斗气招架 (Drive Parry)
guile.notes: Parries all strikes and projectiles (high and low) from frame 1; 12F parry window (can hold the parry to extend the parry window); Perfect Parry occurs on the first 2 active frames (cannot achieve Perfect Parry if you buffer into parry by holding it during Reversal windows; Perfect Parries have to be timed properly); Can still hold charge directions during Parry (allowing characters with charge specials to stand block before performing their reversal); Can block during the recovery frames of a regular parry (can still get hit during the recovery frames if you don't block correctly); Getting thrown or hit at any point during the recovery frames of a whiffed parry attempt results in a Punish Counter; Successfully parrying a move puts you into the same amount of blockstun as that move would regularly do on block (but a Perfect Parry has only 1F of recovery); Throw invincible during the recovery of a successful parry (just like during blockstun); Perfect Parrying a strike has only 1F of recovery and disables the opponent from canceling their attack (basically a guaranteed punish opportunity except for safe jump setups); Perfect Parrying a strike requires holding the correct block direction (Down+Back for low strikes, Back for high/mid strikes); Attempting a Perfect Parry with the wrong block direction results in an "imperfect parry" that builds an extra 3000 Drive Gauge and plays a distinct audio/visual cue; After a successful Perfect Parry, you suffer a 50% penalty to your Damage, Drive Gauge Generation, and Drive Gauge Damage on any of your following attacks when punishing the opponent (in addition, both you and the opponent suffer a 20% penalty to your Super Meter gain during this period); Fully invincible for 6F after a successful Perfect Parry against a strike, which carries over to any attack you perform (ensuring a 5F or faster punish will always interrupt multi-hit attacks); Perfect Parrying projectiles puts you into fixed 10 frames of recovery and applies the same 50% scaling penalties (and 20% Super Meter penalty) on your following attacks when punishing the opponent; Parrying a Strike and Projectile on the same frame will result in a regular parry for the strike attack (effectively ignoring the projectile's hitstop / blockstun); Perfect Parrying a Strike and Projectile on the same frame will give a screen freeze like you Perfect Parried a Strike, but still give you 10F recovery as if you had Perfect Parried a Projectile; Can cancel into Drive Rush during active frames 3 and onward (fastest Drive Rush method is to buffer a forward input before doing parry + forward again); Can cancel into Drive Reversal from a successful parry (just like you normally can during blockstun); Costs 1/2 bar of Drive Gauge and continues to deplete 50 Drive Gauge per frame (0.3 Drive bars per second) as you hold the Parry; You lose the parry if you go into Burnout from the initial Drive Gauge cost (Perfect Parry requires frame-perfect timing when starting from under 1/2 of a Drive bar); Rewards 1 bar of Drive Gauge (1/2 bar total after factoring in the initial parry cost) for successfully parrying a strike; Rewards 1/2 bar of Drive Gauge (0 bar total after factoring in the initial parry cost) for successfully parrying a projectile (with a few exceptions); Rewards 2 bars of Drive Gauge (1.5 bars total after factoring in the initial parry cost) for successful parrying a Super Art or Drive Impact; Successfully parrying a strike attack splits the regular block pushback between both players (while Perfect Parrying a strike removes all of its pushback); Successfully parrying a projectile or Drive Impact reduces the pushback of it by half (while Perfect Parrying a projectile or Drive Impact removes all of its pushback); Your hurtbox and throw box expand slightly towards the opponent for the entire duration of the Parry (Throw box extension starts instantly on frame 1, while the Hurtbox extension starts on frame 3, after the initial 2F Perfect Parry window); Parrying while crouching maintains a regular crouch hurtbox for the first 2 frames of the parry (during the initial Perfect Parry window)

guile.name: 斗气冲刺 (Drive Rush)
guile.notes: Dashes forward and enhances the next normal or command normal used out of the Drive Rush with +4 extra hitstun / blockstun, as well as improved juggle properties (Juggle Limit increased by +3 / Juggle Start/Increase reduced to 0); The +4 bonus frame advantage gained from a Drive Rush enhanced move also stacks with any bonus frame advantage that move may have gained from Counter-Hit, Punish Counter, or Burnout; Grounded special-cancelable normals can also be canceled into Drive Rush on hit or block, as well as from light normals on whiff; Drive Rush maintains buffers (freezes the buffer window) during its start-up and freeze frames - This allows players to do things normally not possible within the normal buffer windows, such as Drive Rushing into a charge special; The initial 10F screen freeze eats the opponent's directional inputs (except Jumps) but does not prevent attacks from being buffered immediately afterward (this can cause inputs to be combined in unintended ways, such as crouch MK + Fireball performing a raw Fireball, or a vertical jump + walk forward turning into a forward jump); Framedata shown in parentheses refers to the Drive Rush version used from a Parry; Drive Rush recovery is only 24F total (23F if done from a Parry) - but the enhanced dash itself is 46F total (45F if done from Parry) and you can cancel it as early as frame 9 (frame 11 if done from a Parry); Inputting a direction (walk/crouch/block/jump) after the Drive Rush recovery plays out 2 additional recovery frames before the transition occurs (this allows the user to perform an enhanced crouching or command normal late in the dash by inputting the direction + button simultaneously); You stop building any form of Drive Gauge on your attacks after using a Drive Rush in the MIDDLE of a combo (but you still continue to build Drive gauge as normal if you did Drive Rush at the START of a combo); Applies an extra damage scaling penalty after using a Drive Rush in the MIDDLE of a combo (no damage scaling if you use Drive Rush at the START of a combo); Costs 3 bars of Drive Gauge if canceled into from a normal attack; Costs 1/2 bar of Drive Gauge if canceled into from Parry (for a total of 1 bar of Drive Gauge when you factor in the initial 1/2 bar cost of the Parry); Normals used out of Drive Rush carry additional forward momentum (but throws and specials immediately halt all momentum, which can be a useful strategy to punish opponents for trying to interrupt your Drive Rush); Parry Drive Rush can only be initiated after frame 3 of the Parry (but can be performed immediately after recovering from a successful parry); Parry Drive Rush cannot be initiated with less than 1/2 of a Drive bar (as the initial Parry cost will put the user into Burnout) - But whiff canceling a Light normal into Drive Rush can achieve a similar effect; Cannot cancel Drive Rush into a Parry (inputting MP+MK results in a MK normal coming out instead); Drive Rush puts the user into a counter-hit state for the entire duration (this makes it impossible to tech a throw that connects during the dash)

guile.name: Sonic Blade > Sonic Cross
guile.notes: Can perform the follow-up Sonic Boom even without any charge on frames 35-40; Projectile speed varies depending on button strength: LP (Classic) / L (Modern): 0.035 (after 9F~) | MP (Classic) / M (Modern): 0.064 | HP (Classic) / H (Modern): 0.081; MP and HP versions deal extra Drive Damage on Block (MP: 5000 | HP: 4000) compared to LP (3500); Extended leg hurtbox on frames 2-39 (vulnerable to low attacks); Inputting the forward + button follow-up within a certain window results in a Perfect Boom which gets +200 damage on the first hit; Hit effects and damage varies greatly depending on if the initial Sonic Blade connects to the opponent before the follow-up Sonic Boom is performed; Frame advantage on Hit / Block refers to when the Sonic Blade and Sonic Boom are combined (refer to Sonic Boom's framedata for when the Sonic Blade dissipates before the follow-up Sonic Boom is performed); If both the Sonic Blade and Sonic Boom are combined, it becomes a 2-hit projectile that deals 1000 damage (1200 damage on the Perfect Boom timings) and causes a KD +44 (up close) on hit; The Sonic Boom follow-up by itself is -3 on block but if the Sonic Blade and Sonic boom is combined the projectile is only -1 on block (up close); 10F start-up listed refers to the follow-up Sonic Boom (actual start-up varies greatly depending on which version of Sonic Blade was performed); Deals 500 extra Drive Damage on block (LP is 3500) for the HP version (4000) and 1500 extra for the MP version (5000); Puts opponents into a limited juggle state on hit

guile.name: Sonic Blade > OD Sonic Cross

guile.name: Sonic Hurricane
guile.notes: Takes 45 frames to charge (holds charge for 22F); 7-hit Super projectile; Strike and Throw invincible on frames 1-8; No invincibility on the HP (Classic) / L (Modern) version; HP (Classic) / L (Modern) version can hit standing opponents if used up close; Framedata shown in the parentheses refers to the HP version where Guile aims his Super into the air; HP (Classic) / L (Modern) version deals 200 less damage (1800) but puts opponent into a limited juggle state for follow-up juggles; KDA listed refers to the LP/MP grounded versions (HP (Classic) / L (Modern) version has very variable KDA against airborne opponents, but usually a bit over +70 KDA); Armor Break; Depletes 0.5 Drive Bar on hit for the opponent; Cannot be performed while Sonic Blade (QCB special) is active on screen; First 3 active frames of the grounded version (LP/MP) has very short range on opponents not already in a combo, effectively making this Super 11F start-up when trying to use it as a Punish Tool from a distance; HP (Classic) / L (Modern) version can be followed up into the other LP/MP versions of this move for double SA1 juggles, provided that the initial HP (Classic) / L (Modern)  version hit a grounded opponent and started the juggle

ingrid.notes: Short range but fast jab option that links naturally into stand LK or on counter-hit into crouch MP; Chains into stand LP / crouch LP / crouch LK; Incurs 20% damage scaling penalty if used as the first hit of a combo

ingrid.name: 站中拳 (5MP)
ingrid.notes: A lot of active frames make this a strong meaty / oki tool (up to +5 oH / +4 oB with meaty timing); Goes into a Target Combo follow-up (MP > MK) that's used as a primary combo tool

ingrid.name: 站重拳 (5HP)
ingrid.notes: Long range whiff punish tool that leads to a full combo on Punish Counter with f+HP or Drive Rush; 1F extra recovery on whiff and block; The brief extended arm hurtbox on frame 11 of start-up (1F before active) is strike invincible (cannot counter-poke projectiles); Incurs 20% damage scaling penalty if used as the first hit of a combo

ingrid.name: 站轻脚 (5LK)
ingrid.notes: Rather short range for a stand LK, but still the furthest range of Ingrid's light normals; Incurs 20% damage scaling penalty if used as the first hit of a combo

ingrid.name: 站中脚 (5MK)
ingrid.notes: Highest damage and hitstun out of Ingrid's cancelable mediums; Forward movement allows Ingrid to maintain a consistent corner spacing when canceling into Sun Shot; Strong whiff punish tool that can cancel into HK Sun Rise on Punish Counter

ingrid.name: 站重脚 (5HK)
ingrid.notes: 2 hits (only the second hit is Super cancelable); Puts airborne opponents into a limited juggle OTG bounce state that allows a Super juggle; Active frames 1-3 hit upward but have poor hitbox priority making anti-airs inconsistent; Strong approach tool with Drive Rush (links into mediums or grants a +2 strike/throw mixup on block); Carries over Counter-Hit / Punish Counter bonus frame advantage to both hits

ingrid.name: 蹲轻拳 (2LP)
ingrid.notes: Slightly more range and lower pushback than stand LP but not as advantageous on hit (no link into stand LK or counter-hit link into crouch MP); Chains into stand LP / crouch LP / crouch LK; Topmost hurtboxes on frames 1-5 are vulnerable only to airborne attacks (this is to discourage its use as an anti-air); Incurs 20% damage scaling penalty if used as the first hit of a combo

ingrid.name: 蹲中拳 (2MP)
ingrid.notes: Solid combo and buffer tool; Can link into stand MP on crouching opponents only (otherwise only links to stand LK if not canceled); A lot of active frames make this a strong meaty / oki tool (up to +9 oH / +2 oB with meaty timing); 3F extra recovery on whiff; Topmost hurtboxes on frames 1-10 are vulnerable only to airborne attacks (this is to discourage its use as an anti-air)

ingrid.name: 蹲重拳 (2HP)
ingrid.notes: Long range cancelable poke / buffer / combo tool with a strong disjointed hitbox; Better advantage on block than most ranged cancelable pokes; When done from Drive Rush on block, sets up a +3 tick throw or an auto-shimmy against characters with standard throw range

ingrid.name: 蹲轻脚 (2LK)
ingrid.notes: Chains into stand LP / crouch LP / crouch LK; Incurs 20% damage scaling penalty if used as the first hit of a combo

ingrid.name: 蹲中脚 (2MK)
ingrid.notes: Standard fully cancelable crouch MK; Incurs 20% damage scaling penalty if used as the first hit of a combo

ingrid.name: 蹲重脚 (2HK)
ingrid.notes: Solid range and hitbox priority; Has some Juggle potential naturally without Drive Rush

ingrid.name: 跳轻拳 (j.LP)
ingrid.notes: Fastest air option (4F) with good air-to-air hitbox priority

ingrid.name: 跳中拳 (j.MP)
ingrid.notes: Puts airborne opponents into a limited juggle state; Projectile invincible on lower body (legs) on frames 8-23

ingrid.name: 跳重拳 (j.HP)
ingrid.notes: Spikes down airborne opponents on Counter-Hit / Punish Counter; Projectile invincible on lower body (legs) on frames 9-23; Visually deceptive range (hitbox and hurtbox extend further beyond Ingrid's arm); Best downward reach of Ingrid's jump-ins for vertical approaches

ingrid.name: 跳轻脚 (j.LK)
ingrid.notes: Cross-up

ingrid.name: 跳中脚 (j.MK)
ingrid.notes: Cross-up; Projectile invincible on lower body (but not the extended kicking leg) on frames 8-21

ingrid.name: 跳重脚 (j.HK)
ingrid.notes: Puts airborne opponents into a limited juggle state; Projectile invincible on lower body (but not the extended kicking leg) on frames 12-19; Has a Target Combo follow-up option (8HK > 8HK); Best horizontal range of Ingrid's jump-ins

ingrid.name: Sun Bright
ingrid.notes: Overhead; Short range but has unique juggle potential as it puts airborne opponents into an OTG limited juggle state on hit; Very high active frame count for an overhead (up to +6 on Hit / 0 on Block with meaty timing)

ingrid.name: Halo Flight
ingrid.notes: Low Crush (but not actually airborne) on frames 9-19; Huge range and a strong hitbox priority Low Crush that can lead into enormous damage conversions via Solar Burst (especially with Sun Crest stocks ready); Can easily be spaced out to be safe on block from 4F punishes (effectively safe on block when used properly); Cancelable into Solar Burst on hit or block (this cancel can be interrupted on block with 4-5F normals, or with air invincible reversals); Puts the opponent into a free juggle state on hit (limited juggle state if the opponent is already in a knockdown / juggle); 3F extra recovery on whiff

ingrid.name: Glowing Touch 1
ingrid.notes: Good hitbox priority poke tool with a built-in hit confirmable Target Combo; Ingrid pulls back her standing leg hurtbox on frames 5-11 making this a good tool against low attacks

ingrid.name: Luminous Uppercut 1
ingrid.notes: Cannot hit crouching opponents; Solid anti-air hitbox but no head or upper body invincibility (likely to trade if not timed early); Cannot hit cross-up (behind Ingrid); Puts the opponent into a free juggle state on hit and does not increase the current juggle state either; Cannot be canceled but the Target Combo follow-up (b+HP > b+HP) is fully cancelable; Ingrid shifts backward during startup unless she is fully cornered

ingrid.name: Pretty Heel Kick
ingrid.notes: Mostly a combo tool; Second hit (MK) puts airborne opponents into a limited juggle state on hit (but does not increase the juggle counter on an opponent already being juggled); Second hit (MK) counts as 2 hits of damage scaling

ingrid.name: Glowing Touch 2
ingrid.notes: Solid tool for whiff punishing and also very useful for Drive Rush juggle routes (can juggle 2HK or SA1 in some midscreen routes depending on distance and juggle height); Second hit (HP) puts grounded opponents into a limited juggle state on hit (but does not increase the juggle counter on an opponent already being juggled); 6F gap on block between hits (up to 8F if delayed)

ingrid.name: Luminous Uppercut 2
ingrid.notes: Cannot hit crouching opponents (opponent can crouch block even after stand blocking the initial b+HP); Second hit is fully cancelable; Second hit puts the opponent into a limited juggle state on hit; Reduced knockdown advantage (+37) if only the 2nd hit connects on a grounded opponent; 7F gap on block between hits (up to 11F if delayed)

ingrid.name: Satellite Leap
ingrid.notes: Air-to-air only (too slow to connect on grounded opponents even after a max-height jump HK); Both hits on the second HK put airborne opponents into a limited juggle state on hit (maintaining the current juggle counter set by the first HK hit); The first hit of the second HK pulls the opponent towards Ingrid in order to make the second hit juggle more consistently, however with extremely specific jump angles and timings, this second hit can whiff after the first hit lands, causing the opponent to fly over Ingrid as she lands, resulting in a sideswitch of which Ingrid can follow-up with various juggles after; Hatson's third favorite move in the game

ingrid.name: Strange Knuckle
ingrid.notes: No true throw loop, but can dash to become +1 in the corner in range for a 2-light confirm (or a throw that loses to reversal 4F normals); Can set up a LP Sun Shot that allows Ingrid to dash forward for great frame advantage or anti-air if the opponent jumps out of the corner; After activating SA2, can throw the opponent into the falling projectiles for a limited juggle state (incurs 20% damage scaling penalty when starting a combo); Punish Counter gives +70% (2040) damage, Hard Knockdown (denies back-roll option on wake-up), depletes 1 bar of Drive gauge from the opponent, and builds twice as much Super gauge for the attacker; Throw Escape builds 0.5 Drive bars for the defender (randomly assigned if throws are input simultaneously)

ingrid.name: Gravity Drop
ingrid.notes: No true throw oki after a corner side switch (but can threaten with ranged normals, forward dash, or Drive Rush normals); Can set up a LP Sun Shot that allows Ingrid to dash forward for great frame advantage or anti-air if the opponent jumps out of the corner; After activating SA2, can throw the opponent into the falling projectiles for a free juggle state (does not incur a damage scaling penalty since the juggle happens before the throw itself damages the opponent); Punish Counter gives +70% (2040) damage, Hard Knockdown (denies back-roll option on wake-up), depletes 1 bar of Drive gauge from the opponent, and builds twice as much Super gauge for the attacker; Throw Escape builds 0.5 Drive bars for the defender (randomly assigned if throws are input simultaneously)

ingrid.name: Drive Impact: Twinkle Kick
ingrid.notes: 2 hits of armor on frames 1-27; Damages opponents Drive Gauge on Block (1/2 bar) | Hit (1 bar) | Counter-Hit (1.25 bar) | Punish Counter (1.5 bar); Knocks down on hit; Pushes the opponent far back on hit or block and causes a Wall Splat if they hit the wall (Parry prevents the backwards stumble and Wall Splat, greatly reducing the pushback); Regular KDA without Wall Splat +35 KD | Wall Splat on Hit +65 KD | Wall Splat on Block +72 HKD; KDA can vary greatly depending on how high the opponent wall splats (higher KDA the higher they wall splat); Advantage after Wall Splat can vary depending on distance from the corner (farther from corner gives higher advantage); Crumples the opponent on Punish Counter or after absorbing at least 1 attack during start-up (+21 frames before the crumple state goes airborne, followed by airborne state on frames 22-46 before they are grounded); Puts airborne opponents into a long spinning free juggle state when hit as a Punish Counter or after absorbing an attack; If the armor absorbs an attack it slows the overall start-up by 1F (27F total instead of 26F) and incurs 6F hitstop for each projectile hit absorbed (making it less likely to punish the opponent after absorbing projectiles); Absorbing an attack causes the player to take 1/2 the damage in recoverable health (but will KO if this would bring the player's health below zero); Stun/Dizzy occurs when a Wall Splat connects on an opponent in Burnout; Stun gives a free combo follow-up for the next 195F after hitting the wall, followed by a HKD if the player falls to the ground untouched (the last 7F before hitting the ground has a crouch-sized hurtbox but is considered standing, allowing for unique combo setups); Incurs 20% damage scaling penalty if used as the first hit of a combo (applies to wall splat on HIT, crumple, Burnout dizzy on hit/block, or any character-specific means of comboing after a regular Drive Impact); Incurs a 20% multiplier damage scaling penalty after a Wall Splat on BLOCK - Because the blocked Drive Impact is not considered a "hit" for the combo, the next attack can incur its own separate damage scaling as a combo starter; Wall Splat puts opponent into a special juggle state where the next move freely connects and continues the juggle even if it normally wouldn't (similar to a Forced Knockdown or Drive Rush juggle properties); Does not cause Wall Splat if the Drive Impact connects as a combo or a true blockstring with no gaps (LOCK icon appears on-screen); It is possible to "combo" into Stun if the opponent has under 1.5 Drive bars - a blocked DI Wall Splat from slightly outside the corner into a second DI on hit will cause Burnout and Stun (because the blocked DI is not technically considered a combo starter); Costs 1 bar of Drive Gauge; Cinematic slowdown occurs if both players activate Drive Impact within range of each other (granting a Punish Counter to the player who activates it later); Attempting to counter with DI vs. DI with under 400 HP will result in a KO, as the second player will not have enough health to absorb it; Clashes with other Drive Impacts and refunds the Drive gauge cost if they collide on the same active frame (start at exactly the same time, or 1F apart if the first Drive Impact absorbs a strike) - The meter refund does not prevent Burnout from occurring; The scrub killer

ingrid.name: Drive Reversal: Odd Flight
ingrid.notes: Has two versions: one performed during blockstun or parry stun (20F start-up) and one performed as a wake-up reversal (18F start-up); Fully invincible on frames 1-22 (blockstun) / frames 1-20 (reversal); Armor Break (blows through all armor like Drive Impact, but not counters like JP's Amnesia); Trying to Drive Reversal after the blockstun ends results in a Drive Impact; Drive Reversal immediately removes the current blockstun you're in and starts the attack; Causes a 4F screen freeze after the 6th start-up frame, which allows the opponent to perform a simple OS (inputting their buttons during the buffer window) to prevent their next attack from coming out; Safe on block (-2) when used against an opponent in Burnout; Costs 2 bars of Drive Gauge; If the opponent tries to throw against a wake-up Drive Reversal, it causes a 12F screen freeze and refunds 1 bar of Drive gauge (but does not prevent Burnout); Guaranteed to interrupt any Drive Rush canceled normal if performed immediately out of blockstun (unless the opponent reacts with an invincible move or counter)

ingrid.name: 斗气招架 (Drive Parry)
ingrid.notes: Parries all strikes and projectiles (high and low) from frame 1; 12F parry window (can hold the parry to extend the parry window); Perfect Parry occurs on the first 2 active frames (cannot achieve Perfect Parry if you buffer into parry by holding it during Reversal windows; Perfect Parries have to be timed properly); Can still hold charge directions during Parry (allowing characters with charge specials to stand block before performing their reversal); Can block during the recovery frames of a regular parry (can still get hit during the recovery frames if you don't block correctly); Getting thrown or hit at any point during the recovery frames of a whiffed parry attempt results in a Punish Counter; Successfully parrying a move puts you into the same amount of blockstun as that move would regularly do on block (but a Perfect Parry has only 1F of recovery); Throw invincible during the recovery of a successful parry (just like during blockstun); Perfect Parrying a strike has only 1F of recovery and disables the opponent from canceling their attack (basically a guaranteed punish opportunity except for safe jump setups); Perfect Parrying a strike requires holding the correct block direction (Down+Back for low strikes, Back for high/mid strikes); Attempting a Perfect Parry with the wrong block direction results in an "imperfect parry" that builds an extra 3000 Drive Gauge and plays a distinct audio/visual cue; After a successful Perfect Parry, you suffer a 50% penalty to your Damage, Drive Gauge Generation, and Drive Gauge Damage on any of your following attacks when punishing the opponent (in addition, both you and the opponent suffer a 20% penalty to your Super Meter gain during this period); Fully invincible for 6F after a successful Perfect Parry against a strike, which carries over to any attack you perform (ensuring a 5F or faster punish will always interrupt multi-hit attacks); Perfect Parrying projectiles puts you into fixed 10 frames of recovery and applies the same 50% scaling penalties (and 20% Super Meter penalty) on your following attacks when punishing the opponent; Parrying a Strike and Projectile on the same frame will result in a regular parry for the strike attack (effectively ignoring the projectile's hitstop / blockstun); Perfect Parrying a Strike and Projectile on the same frame will give a screen freeze like you Perfect Parried a Strike, but still give you 10F recovery as if you had Perfect Parried a Projectile; Can cancel into Drive Rush during active frames 3 and onward (fastest Drive Rush method is to buffer a forward input before doing parry + forward again); Can cancel into Drive Reversal from a successful parry (just like you normally can during blockstun); Costs 1/2 bar of Drive Gauge and continues to deplete 50 Drive Gauge per frame (0.3 Drive bars per second) as you hold the Parry; You lose the parry if you go into Burnout from the initial Drive Gauge cost (Perfect Parry requires frame-perfect timing when starting from under 1/2 of a Drive bar); Rewards 1 bar of Drive Gauge (1/2 bar total after factoring in the initial parry cost) for successfully parrying a strike; Rewards 1/2 bar of Drive Gauge (0 bar total after factoring in the initial parry cost) for successfully parrying a projectile (with a few exceptions); Rewards 2 bars of Drive Gauge (1.5 bars total after factoring in the initial parry cost) for successful parrying a Super Art or Drive Impact; Successfully parrying a strike attack splits the regular block pushback between both players (while Perfect Parrying a strike removes all of its pushback); Successfully parrying a projectile or Drive Impact reduces the pushback of it by half (while Perfect Parrying a projectile or Drive Impact removes all of its pushback); Your hurtbox and throw box expand slightly towards the opponent for the entire duration of the Parry (Throw box extension starts instantly on frame 1, while the Hurtbox extension starts on frame 3, after the initial 2F Perfect Parry window); Parrying while crouching maintains a regular crouch hurtbox for the first 2 frames of the parry (during the initial Perfect Parry window)

ingrid.name: 斗气冲刺 (Drive Rush)
ingrid.notes: Dashes forward and enhances the next normal or command normal used out of the Drive Rush with +4 extra hitstun / blockstun, as well as improved juggle properties (Juggle Limit increased by +3 / Juggle Start/Increase reduced to 0); The +4 bonus frame advantage gained from a Drive Rush enhanced move also stacks with any bonus frame advantage that move may have gained from Counter-Hit, Punish Counter, or Burnout; Grounded special-cancelable normals can also be canceled into Drive Rush on hit or block, as well as from light normals on whiff; Drive Rush maintains buffers (freezes the buffer window) during its start-up and freeze frames - This allows players to do things normally not possible within the normal buffer windows, such as Drive Rushing into a charge special; The initial 10F screen freeze eats the opponent's directional inputs (except Jumps) but does not prevent attacks from being buffered immediately afterward (this can cause inputs to be combined in unintended ways, such as crouch MK + Fireball performing a raw Fireball, or a vertical jump + walk forward turning into a forward jump); Framedata shown in parentheses refers to the Drive Rush version used from a Parry; Drive Rush recovery is only 24F total (23F if done from a Parry) - but the enhanced dash itself is 46F total (45F if done from Parry) and you can cancel it as early as frame 9 (frame 11 if done from a Parry); Inputting a direction (walk/crouch/block/jump) after the Drive Rush recovery plays out 2 additional recovery frames before the transition occurs (this allows the user to perform an enhanced crouching or command normal late in the dash by inputting the direction + button simultaneously); You stop building any form of Drive Gauge on your attacks after using a Drive Rush in the MIDDLE of a combo (but you still continue to build Drive gauge as normal if you did Drive Rush at the START of a combo); Applies an extra damage scaling penalty after using a Drive Rush in the MIDDLE of a combo (no damage scaling if you use Drive Rush at the START of a combo); Costs 3 bars of Drive Gauge if canceled into from a normal attack; Costs 1/2 bar of Drive Gauge if canceled into from Parry (for a total of 1 bar of Drive Gauge when you factor in the initial 1/2 bar cost of the Parry); Normals used out of Drive Rush carry additional forward momentum (but throws and specials immediately halt all momentum, which can be a useful strategy to punish opponents for trying to interrupt your Drive Rush); Parry Drive Rush can only be initiated after frame 3 of the Parry (but can be performed immediately after recovering from a successful parry); Parry Drive Rush cannot be initiated with less than 1/2 of a Drive bar (as the initial Parry cost will put the user into Burnout) - But whiff canceling a Light normal into Drive Rush can achieve a similar effect; Cannot cancel Drive Rush into a Parry (inputting MP+MK results in a MK normal coming out instead); Drive Rush puts the user into a counter-hit state for the entire duration (this makes it impossible to tech a throw that connects during the dash)

ingrid.name: Taunt
ingrid.notes: Forward Taunt: if the opponent stands directly in front of Ingrid, performs an attack that deals 0 damage and fills the opponent's Super gauge on hit/block/parry; Back Taunt: summons a Monoid that can be controlled with its own moveset; Monoid has access to 6 attacks: LP/LK (low divekick) | MP/MK (overhead) | HP/HK (high strike) | HP+HK (beam) | jump L/M/H (downward aerial strike) | qcb,qcf+HP/HK (3-bar Super); Monoid cannot block and is fully controllable mid-air (can also slide forward during the startup of most attacks); Ingrid returns after standing idle for an extended period or after the 3-bar Super cinematic on hit; Upon Ingrid's return, inputting LP > LP > Back > LK > HK (Modern: L > L > 4 > M > H) before the high five starts a transformation into Dark Ingrid (fills up Health / Super gauge / Sun Crests to maximum and gains access to enhanced moves)

ingrid.name: Sun Veil
ingrid.notes: Strike and Projectile invincible on frames 6-20; Absorbing a strike results in a counter-attack that knocks down the opponent on hit (this counter can be Blocked / Perfect Parried if triggered by moves with low enough recovery); Counter-Attack properties: 12F start-up + 3F active + 21F recovery (45F total) | Strike attack | Fully invincible frames 1-14 | Armor Break | Safe on block (-3) | 1.70 Range | No collision box on frames 1-14 so certain moves can phase through Ingrid before the Counter hits them; Can absorb a 1-hit projectile regular or OD dissipates the projectile with 28F total recovery but no counter-attack; Cannot absorb multi-hit or Super projectiles; Ingrid is in a Counter-hit state on frames 1-5 and a Punish Counter state for the rest of the duration; Slight vulnerable hurtbox extension on whiff on Ingrid's extended hand on frames 21-36; The counter hitbox is much taller than Ingrid's usual standard hurtbox (can be triggered by moves that would normally whiff); BUG: If the opponent triggers the Strike Counter while on the other side of Ingrid (like a cross-up jump), the opponent cannot perform any action on their first frame of recovery except jumping or walking. This 1F input lockout bug usually doesn't occur if the Counter is triggered while in the front of Ingrid

ingrid.name: Vanishing Sun (forward)
ingrid.notes: Fully invincible on frames 13-27; Airborne on frames 21-46 (Forced Knockdown state); Teleports forward to the opponent's location (but can whiff in some juggle routes where the opponent is flying backward too quickly); Puts opponents into a limited juggle state with follow-ups possible in the corner after an airborne connect; Can be countered on reaction since Ingrid is vulnerable for 8F after reappearing from the teleport before her attack is active (can also use air invincible attacks since this is an airborne strike)

ingrid.name: Vanishing Sun (air)
ingrid.notes: Fully invincible on frames 13-27; Airborne on frames 20-48 (Forced Knockdown state); Teleports above the opponent and comes down with an Overhead strike that is plus on block; Can whiff over opponents walking forward; Puts grounded opponents into a limited juggle state with follow-ups possible in the corner; Puts airborne opponents into a limited juggle OTG bounce with follow-ups possible even midscreen; Can be countered on reaction since Ingrid is vulnerable for 15F after reappearing from the teleport before her attack is active (can also use air invincible attacks since this is an airborne strike); Counts as 2 hits of damage scaling

ingrid.name: Vanishing Sun (backward)
ingrid.notes: Fully invincible on frames 13-26; Counter-hit state if Ingrid is hit before the invincibility window; 22 vulnerable recovery frames after reappearing (Punish Counter state); Extended hurtboxes after reappearing on frames 27-48 (until the end of recovery); Distance: 1.74

ingrid.name: Shining Sun
ingrid.notes: Strike and Throw invincible on frames 1-15; Airborne on frames 16-95 (Forced Knockdown state); Armor Break; Depletes 0.5 Drive Bar on hit for the opponent; Can hold the button during the Super freeze to spend Sun Crests in exchange for higher damage and increased KD Advantage; 0 Sun Crests: 1900 Damage, HKD +12, sends opponent 1/2 screen away; 1 Sun Crest: hold button for 30F, 2300 Damage, HKD +17, sends opponent 2/3 screen away; 2 Sun Crests: hold button for 60F, 2700 Damage, HKD +20, sends opponent fullscreen; 1st hit deals 400 damage and puts the opponent into a limited juggle state if it trades with a projectile (opponent floats high for an easy hitconfirm); Slow startup for a reversal (opponents can easily pressure with light normals and recover on time to block); Large gap between active frames can cause anti-air SA1 to whiff entirely on high airborne opponents; Cannot hit cross-up (behind Ingrid)

ingrid.name: Order of the Sun
ingrid.notes: No form of invincibility whatsoever; Fires a light beacon into the air that summons downward-hitting 2-hit Super Projectiles (projectiles disappear if Ingrid is hit); Each 2-hit Super Projectile hit armor breaks; Button strength determines beacon position (Modern: hold back / neutral / forward to control position); LP appears in front of the opponent, MP appears at the opponent's current position, and HP appears behind the opponent (except at fullscreen); Can hold the button during the Super freeze to spend Sun Crests for enhanced versions: 1 Sun Crest spawns 4 projectiles (hold button 26F), 2 Sun Crests spawn 5 projectiles (hold button 73F); Total startup for the first projectile attack depends on strength (LP 103: | MP: 68 | HP: 98); Damage distribution of projectiles: 250x2*250x2*300x2*400x2*500x2 (up to 1600 0-stock / 2400 1-stock / 3400 2-stock); First, second, and fourth projectiles do not launch a grounded opponent; Third projectile hit launches a grounded opponent into the air (this hit also sets up quick air reset mixup potential for Ingrid); Fifth (final) projectile hit puts the opponent into an OTG juggle state; All five potential projectile hits put the opponent into a free juggle state and do not increase the current juggle state either; The gap on block between each set of projectiles varies in the following order: 7F / 6F / 9F / 6F gap (switching between stand/crouch block can slightly increase or decrease these gaps, but the opponent is always throwable between blocked projectiles); Ingrid can't generate any Super meter while the Super is active or for the remainder of any combo that was started during the Super

ingrid.name: Cosmic Ray
ingrid.notes: Fully invincible on frames 1-22; Projectile that targets the opponent's location from anywhere on screen (opponent can still avoid this attack if they quickly move out of it during start-up); Armor Break; Depletes 1.5 Drive Bars on hit for the opponent; Super cinematic time regenerates ~2.1 Drive Bars for Ingrid; Incurs 10% damage scaling when canceled into from specials; Extremely slow startup as a reversal (opponents can easily pressure with lights or some mediums and recovery on time to block)

ingrid.name: Cosmic Ray (Critical Art)
ingrid.notes: Fully invincible on frames 1-22; Projectile that targets the opponent's location from anywhere on screen (opponent can still avoid this attack if they quickly move out of it during start-up); Critical Art deals +500 damage over regular version; Armor Break; Depletes 2 Drive Bars on hit for the opponent; Super cinematic time regenerates ~2.3 Drive Bars for Ingrid; Incurs 10% damage scaling when canceled into from specials; Extremely slow startup as a reversal (opponents can easily pressure with lights or some mediums and recovery on time to block)

ingrid.name: Sunburst Beam
ingrid.notes: Dark Ingrid only; Tall 16-hit beam projectile that reaches fullscreen (most hits will connect even if the opponent falls into the beam near the end of active frames); Hitbox expands on active frames 1-4 before reaching its full range on active frame 5; Deals massive chip damage (2500) against Burnout (50% of its base damage instead of the usual 25%)

ingrid.name: Sunburst Blow
ingrid.notes: Dark Ingrid only; 1 hit of Armor on frames 6-33 (until end of active frames); Immediately puts the opponent into Burnout on Hit; Armor Break; Cannot be special canceled into from normals; Hits twice on hit (only one hit on block)

ingrid.name: Sun Octopus
ingrid.notes: Dark Ingrid only; Fully invincible on frames 1-7; Command grab super like Zangief's SA3; Entire start-up happens before the initial Super cinematic freeze, meaning that this move is effectively 0F start-up after the Super is activated, making it inescapable if the opponent didn't already do something to avoid the grab before the Super was activated; Can be combo'd into on grounded opponents; Depletes 1 Drive Bar on hit for the oppponent; Super cinematic time regenerates ~1.6 Drive Bars for Ingrid

ingrid.name: Monoid Low Dive
ingrid.notes: 3 hits; Can hold forward during startup to steer and increase its range; Hits low despite the divekick-like animation

ingrid.name: Monoid Overhead Hammer
ingrid.notes: Knocks down on grounded hit and resets vs. airborne opponents; Can hold forward during startup to steer and increase its range

ingrid.name: Monoid Star Thrust
ingrid.notes: Knocks down on grounded hit and resets vs. airborne opponents; Can hold forward during startup to steer and increase its range

ingrid.name: Monoid Beam
ingrid.notes: Knocks down on both grounded/airborne opponents; Cannot be steered like the other Monoid attacks; Input has no kara-cancel leniency (must input HP+HK on the exact same frame)

ingrid.name: Monoid Aerial Strike
ingrid.notes: Knocks down on grounded hit and resets vs. airborne opponents; Can hold forward during startup to steer and increase its range; Active frames 3-6 gain a second hitbox that can hit cross-up

ingrid.name: Monoid Super
ingrid.notes: Fully invincible on frames 31-57; Armor Break; Medium range strike Super that costs 3 bars of Super but only deals 3000 damage; Ingrid comes in to high five the Monoid and take its place if the Super manages to hit the opponent; Can transform into Dark Ingrid on hit by inputting LP > LP > 4 > LK > HK before the high five (but significantly more unsafe on hit); Generally not worth using unless it will kill the opponent due to it being hugely punishable (especially punishable on hit)

ingrid.name: Sun Shot
ingrid.notes: Sends a horizontal 1-hit projectile a medium distance that pauses before continuing forward; Projectile speed: 0.065 (start) / 0.11 (end); No hurtbox extension at all on frame 17 when initially throwing the fireball, and then slight projectile invincible hurtbox extension on her hand on frames 18-44; Minor hurtbox extension of the front leg on frames 18-45; Puts airborne opponents into a limited juggle state; The button can be held 17F during start-up to increase its projectile speed (0.17 instead of 0.11) once it shoots forward; Projectile disappears 1F after Ingrid is hit; Modern Controls: cannot use the held version (holding SP results in the regular M version)

variations.invincible: No hurtbox extension at all on frame 17 when initially throwing the fireball, and then slight projectile invincible hurtbox extension on her hand on frames 18-44
