jamie.name: 站轻拳 (5LP)
jamie.notes: Different stand LP from the level 1 Drink Level version; Generally better frame advantage than the Level 1 Drink stand LP, but much less range and no Target Combo or chain cancels; Incurs 20% damage scaling penalty if used as the first hit of a combo

jamie.name: 站中拳 (5MP)
jamie.notes: Core combo / frametrap / oki tool with strong frame advantage and good amount of active frames; Hit confirmable into crouch HP on Counter-Hit

jamie.name: 站重拳 (5HP)
jamie.notes: Core combo / juggle tool with naturally high juggle potential (without Drive Rush) with all 3 hits putting airborne opponents into a limited juggle state; Very fast start-up and fast 3-hit string makes this a super strong tool against Drive Impacts and other armor moves; Only cancelable on the first 2 hits; Carries over Counter-Hit / Punish Counter bonus frame advantage to all hits; Last hit has pretty good range and makes for a good whiff punish tool (the third hit is effectively 12F start-up) with +5 on Punish allowing for a follow-up combo (can be spaced so that the third strike hits meaty up to +7 on Punish Counter); Leaves Jamie up close for pressure / mixup on hit / counter-hit; Can be used in combination with Drive Rush as a fast get-in tool, but Drive Rushing with crouch LP / crouch MP / stand MP all give better pressure on block (albeit with shorter range); Hatson's favorite move in SF6

jamie.name: 站轻脚 (5LK)
jamie.notes: Chains into crouch LP / crouch LK / stand LK; Incurs 20% damage scaling penalty if used as the first hit of a combo; Can infinitely chain into itself; Moves Jamie's positioning forward a little bit so chaining from this LK into other lights grants them extra range; Has a different animation when chained into from his other light normals

jamie.name: 站中脚 (5MK)
jamie.notes: Great poke and buffer tool at close / mid-range; Jamie lifts up his front leg hurtbox on frames 4-12 making this a good tool against low attacks; +1F extra recovery frame (18F) on whiff; Jamie's only cancelable medium that combos into HP Palm on Punish Counter (very useful in mid-range footsies prior to reaching Drink Level 2)

jamie.name: 站重脚 (5HK)
jamie.notes: Core Punish / Poke / Juggle tool with huge range, fully cancelable and even hit confirmable with practice; Second active frame has increased range and reduced pushback which always positions Jamie back to that perfect distance / spacing for the second active frame; This makes for a great poke and drive gauge bully tool in neutral when properly spaced out; Causes a crumple-like free juggle state on a grounded Punish Counter (opponent is in a grounded state for +9 frames before going airborne); Puts airborne opponents into a limited juggle state; If canceled into Drink off a Punish Counter in the corner, Jamie can do a juggle follow-up with a 4F (crouch LP) before the opponent falls onto the ground (can juggle into 5F stand LK if the drink activates the Drink Level 4 install); The brief extended leg hurtbox on frame 14 of start-up (1F before active) is strike invincible (cannot counter-poke projectiles)

jamie.name: 蹲轻拳 (2LP)
jamie.notes: Chains into crouch LP / crouch LK / stand LK; Jamie's only 4F normal; Incurs 20% damage scaling penalty if used as the first hit of a combo; Deals 50 less base damage (250 at Drink Level 2) than all other crouch jabs in the game (normally deal 300 damage)

jamie.name: 蹲中拳 (2MP)
jamie.notes: Good combo and buffer tool with strong hitbox priority; +2F extra recovery frames (15F) on whiff

jamie.name: 蹲重拳 (2HP)
jamie.notes: Forces stand; Jamie's head hurtbox is invincible to airborne strikes on frames 8-32; Primary combo tool as well as a strong anti-air (but cannot hit cross-up behind Jamie); Only cancelable on the first two active frames; Maintains the current juggle state (has 0 Juggle Increase) which opens up more juggle routes

jamie.name: 蹲轻脚 (2LK)
jamie.notes: Chains into crouch LP / crouch LK / stand LK; Incurs 20% damage scaling penalty if used as the first hit of a combo

jamie.name: 蹲中脚 (2MK)
jamie.notes: Incurs 20% hit damage scaling penalty if used as the first hit of a combo; Has big pushback on block making this move relatively safe to poke with and to bait retaliations from the opponent

jamie.name: 蹲重脚 (2HK)
jamie.notes: Second hit has quite bit a further range than the first hit; Has a Target Combo follow-up (can hit confirm into this) that's a great way of raising drink level while still maintaining oki mixups in the corner; Can be spaced out to make only the second hit connect, making the move deceptively safe on block; +1F extra recovery frame (29F) on block; Second hit is not a low after the first hit is blocked; Has high natural juggle limit

jamie.name: 跳轻拳 (j.LP)
jamie.notes: Cross-up; Can be used as an instant Overhead

jamie.name: 跳中拳 (j.MP)
jamie.notes: Puts airborne opponents into a juggle state; Cancelable into his Divekick (Drink Level 1) during forward jump; Shifts the normal jumping hurtbox upward during start-up (helps with avoiding some attacks)

jamie.name: 跳重拳 (j.HP)
jamie.notes: Spikes down airborne opponents; Has some natural juggle limit (similar to jump MP); I whip my hair back and forth!

jamie.name: 跳轻脚 (j.LK)
jamie.notes: Has the furthest horizontal range of all of Jamie's jump-ins

jamie.name: 跳中脚 (j.MK)
jamie.notes: Cross-up

jamie.name: 跳重脚 (j.HK)
jamie.notes: Amazing air-to-air / anti-air tool due to the rewards it leads to on airborne hit; Both hits put airborne opponents into a limited juggle state; Shifts the normal jumping hurtbox upward during start-up (helps with avoiding some attacks)

jamie.name: Indian Step
jamie.notes: Chains into crouch LP / crouch LK / stand LK; Incurs 20% damage scaling penalty if used as the first hit of a combo; Can infinitely chain into itself; Moves Jamie's positioning forward a little bit so chaining from this LK into other lights grants them extra range; We do a little trolling

jamie.name: Tensei Kick
jamie.notes: Jamie's head and kicking leg hurtboxes are invincible to airborne strikes on frames 9-11 (during the 3 active frames); Jump cancelable on HIT only (Jamie always jumps forward no matter which up direction is pressed); Launches opponent into a limited juggle state (free juggle state if used from Drive Rush); Primary combo / juggle tool as well as a good anti-air (but cannot hit cross-up behind Jamie); Counts as 2 hits of damage scaling when used as the start of a combo (like when anti-airing)

jamie.name: Falling Star Kick
jamie.notes: Overhead; High profile (crushes lows) on frames 10-19; No target combo follow-up unless at Drink Level 2; Gains twice as much range at Drink Level 2 and higher; Can be spaced to hit on later active frames; Spiked knockdown on airborne opponents (no follow-up juggle possible)

jamie.name: Hermit's Elbow
jamie.notes: Jamie pulls back his hurtboxes on frames 5-12 before striking back with his elbow (can be used to avoid throws and attacks, and then Punish Countering them); Doesn't pull back the hurtboxes as far or have as much range as the Drink Level 3 version (but has better combo potential); No target combo follow-up unless at Drink Level 3; Cancelable into all Supers on Hit / Block

jamie.name: Senei Kick
jamie.notes: Not a low attack (despite what it looks like); Very good range (reaches about 60% screen length) going especially far when combined with Drive Rush momentum; No target combo follow-up unless at Drink Level 4; Cancelable into all Supers on Hit / Block

jamie.name: Phantom Sway
jamie.notes: Usually followed up with the Drink follow-up since it's Jamie's best way to raise his drink level while still maintaining knockdown pressure in the corner; Sometimes it can be good to not go for the Drink follow-up if you're already at Drink Level 4 and want to get better oki options for pressure

jamie.name: Phantom Sway + Drink
jamie.notes: Grants +1 Drink Level to Jamie; Restores 1/4 extra bar of Drive Gauge | 1/24th (~4%) of Burnout Gauge; Jamie's optimal way to raise the Drink Level, while also restoring some Drive Gauge / Burnout and still maintaining a strike / throw mixup in the corner

jamie.name: Back Shaver
jamie.notes: Throw Loop: Dash up for +4 mixup between throw/strike (not possible on mid-screen back-roll); Can press / hold the LP or LK button during the throw to restore 1/2 extra bar of Drive Gauge | 1/12th (~8%) of Burnout Gauge while sacrificing some oki (+7 KD instead of +23); Punish Counter gives +70% (1836) damage, Hard Knockdown (denies back-roll option on wake-up), depletes 1 bar of Drive gauge from the opponent, and builds twice as much Super gauge for the attacker; Throw Escape builds 0.5 Drive bars for the defender (randomly assigned if throws are input simultaneously)

jamie.name: Wheel Punch
jamie.notes: Back Throw Loop: Can Drive Rush into meaty strike / throw mix when performed while cornered; Can also do meaty MP / OD Palm for + frames as well as both giving follow-up combos on hit; Punish Counter gives +70% (1836) damage, Hard Knockdown (denies back-roll option on wake-up), depletes 1 bar of Drive gauge from the opponent, and builds twice as much Super gauge for the attacker; Throw Escape builds 0.5 Drive bars for the defender (randomly assigned if throws are input simultaneously)

jamie.name: Drive Impact: Vainglory Strike
jamie.notes: 2 hits of armor on frames 1-27; Damages opponents Drive Gauge on Block (1/2 bar) | Hit (1 bar) | Counter-Hit (1.25 bar) | Punish Counter (1.5 bar); Knocks down on hit; Pushes the opponent far back on hit or block and causes a Wall Splat if they hit the wall (Parry prevents the backwards stumble and Wall Splat, greatly reducing the pushback); Regular KDA without Wall Splat +35 KD | Wall Splat on Hit +65 KD | Wall Splat on Block +72 HKD; KDA can vary greatly depending on how high the opponent wall splats (higher KDA the higher they wall splat); Advantage after Wall Splat can vary depending on distance from the corner (farther from corner gives higher advantage); Crumples the opponent on Punish Counter or after absorbing at least 1 attack during start-up (+21 frames before the crumple state goes airborne, followed by airborne state on frames 22-46 before they are grounded); Puts airborne opponents into a long spinning free juggle state when hit as a Punish Counter or after absorbing an attack; If the armor absorbs an attack it slows the overall start-up by 1F (27F total instead of 26F) and incurs 6F hitstop for each projectile hit absorbed (making it less likely to punish the opponent after absorbing projectiles); Absorbing an attack causes the player to take 1/2 the damage in recoverable health (but will KO if this would bring the player's health below zero); Stun/Dizzy occurs when a Wall Splat connects on an opponent in Burnout; Stun gives a free combo follow-up for the next 195F after hitting the wall, followed by a HKD if the player falls to the ground untouched (the last 7F before hitting the ground has a crouch-sized hurtbox but is considered standing, allowing for unique combo setups); Incurs 20% damage scaling penalty if used as the first hit of a combo (applies to wall splat on HIT, crumple, Burnout dizzy on hit/block, or any character-specific means of comboing after a regular Drive Impact); Incurs a 20% multiplier damage scaling penalty after a Wall Splat on BLOCK - Because the blocked Drive Impact is not considered a "hit" for the combo, the next attack can incur its own separate damage scaling as a combo starter; Wall Splat puts opponent into a special juggle state where the next move freely connects and continues the juggle even if it normally wouldn't (similar to a Forced Knockdown or Drive Rush juggle properties); Does not cause Wall Splat if the Drive Impact connects as a combo or a true blockstring with no gaps (LOCK icon appears on-screen); It is possible to "combo" into Stun if the opponent has under 1.5 Drive bars - a blocked DI Wall Splat from slightly outside the corner into a second DI on hit will cause Burnout and Stun (because the blocked DI is not technically considered a combo starter); Costs 1 bar of Drive Gauge; Cinematic slowdown occurs if both players activate Drive Impact within range of each other (granting a Punish Counter to the player who activates it later); Attempting to counter with DI vs. DI with under 400 HP will result in a KO, as the second player will not have enough health to absorb it; Clashes with other Drive Impacts and refunds the Drive gauge cost if they collide on the same active frame (start at exactly the same time, or 1F apart if the first Drive Impact absorbs a strike) - The meter refund does not prevent Burnout from occurring; The scrub killer

jamie.name: Drive Reversal: Leg Sweep
jamie.notes: Has two versions: one performed during blockstun or parry stun (20F start-up) and one performed as a wake-up reversal (18F start-up); Fully invincible on frames 1-22 (blockstun) / frames 1-20 (reversal); Armor Break (blows through all armor like Drive Impact, but not counters like JP's Amnesia); Trying to Drive Reversal after the blockstun ends results in a Drive Impact; Drive Reversal immediately removes the current blockstun you're in and starts the attack; Causes a 4F screen freeze after the 6th start-up frame, which allows the opponent to perform a simple OS (inputting their buttons during the buffer window) to prevent their next attack from coming out; Safe on block (-2) when used against an opponent in Burnout; Costs 2 bars of Drive Gauge; If the opponent tries to throw against a wake-up Drive Reversal, it causes a 12F screen freeze and refunds 1 bar of Drive gauge (but does not prevent Burnout); Guaranteed to interrupt any Drive Rush canceled normal if performed immediately out of blockstun (unless the opponent reacts with an invincible move or counter)

jamie.name: 斗气招架 (Drive Parry)
jamie.notes: Parries all strikes and projectiles (high and low) from frame 1; 12F parry window (can hold the parry to extend the parry window); Perfect Parry occurs on the first 2 active frames (cannot achieve Perfect Parry if you buffer into parry by holding it during Reversal windows; Perfect Parries have to be timed properly); Can still hold charge directions during Parry (allowing characters with charge specials to stand block before performing their reversal); Can block during the recovery frames of a regular parry (can still get hit during the recovery frames if you don't block correctly); Getting thrown or hit at any point during the recovery frames of a whiffed parry attempt results in a Punish Counter; Successfully parrying a move puts you into the same amount of blockstun as that move would regularly do on block (but a Perfect Parry has only 1F of recovery); Throw invincible during the recovery of a successful parry (just like during blockstun); Perfect Parrying a strike has only 1F of recovery and disables the opponent from canceling their attack (basically a guaranteed punish opportunity except for safe jump setups); Perfect Parrying a strike requires holding the correct block direction (Down+Back for low strikes, Back for high/mid strikes); Attempting a Perfect Parry with the wrong block direction results in an "imperfect parry" that builds an extra 3000 Drive Gauge and plays a distinct audio/visual cue; After a successful Perfect Parry, you suffer a 50% penalty to your Damage, Drive Gauge Generation, and Drive Gauge Damage on any of your following attacks when punishing the opponent (in addition, both you and the opponent suffer a 20% penalty to your Super Meter gain during this period); Fully invincible for 6F after a successful Perfect Parry against a strike, which carries over to any attack you perform (ensuring a 5F or faster punish will always interrupt multi-hit attacks); Perfect Parrying projectiles puts you into fixed 10 frames of recovery and applies the same 50% scaling penalties (and 20% Super Meter penalty) on your following attacks when punishing the opponent; Parrying a Strike and Projectile on the same frame will result in a regular parry for the strike attack (effectively ignoring the projectile's hitstop / blockstun); Perfect Parrying a Strike and Projectile on the same frame will give a screen freeze like you Perfect Parried a Strike, but still give you 10F recovery as if you had Perfect Parried a Projectile; Can cancel into Drive Rush during active frames 3 and onward (fastest Drive Rush method is to buffer a forward input before doing parry + forward again); Can cancel into Drive Reversal from a successful parry (just like you normally can during blockstun); Costs 1/2 bar of Drive Gauge and continues to deplete 50 Drive Gauge per frame (0.3 Drive bars per second) as you hold the Parry; You lose the parry if you go into Burnout from the initial Drive Gauge cost (Perfect Parry requires frame-perfect timing when starting from under 1/2 of a Drive bar); Rewards 1 bar of Drive Gauge (1/2 bar total after factoring in the initial parry cost) for successfully parrying a strike; Rewards 1/2 bar of Drive Gauge (0 bar total after factoring in the initial parry cost) for successfully parrying a projectile (with a few exceptions); Rewards 2 bars of Drive Gauge (1.5 bars total after factoring in the initial parry cost) for successful parrying a Super Art or Drive Impact; Successfully parrying a strike attack splits the regular block pushback between both players (while Perfect Parrying a strike removes all of its pushback); Successfully parrying a projectile or Drive Impact reduces the pushback of it by half (while Perfect Parrying a projectile or Drive Impact removes all of its pushback); Your hurtbox and throw box expand slightly towards the opponent for the entire duration of the Parry (Throw box extension starts instantly on frame 1, while the Hurtbox extension starts on frame 3, after the initial 2F Perfect Parry window); Parrying while crouching maintains a regular crouch hurtbox for the first 2 frames of the parry (during the initial Perfect Parry window)

jamie.name: 斗气冲刺 (Drive Rush)
jamie.notes: Dashes forward and enhances the next normal or command normal used out of the Drive Rush with +4 extra hitstun / blockstun, as well as improved juggle properties (Juggle Limit increased by +3 / Juggle Start/Increase reduced to 0); The +4 bonus frame advantage gained from a Drive Rush enhanced move also stacks with any bonus frame advantage that move may have gained from Counter-Hit, Punish Counter, or Burnout; Grounded special-cancelable normals can also be canceled into Drive Rush on hit or block, as well as from light normals on whiff; Drive Rush maintains buffers (freezes the buffer window) during its start-up and freeze frames - This allows players to do things normally not possible within the normal buffer windows, such as Drive Rushing into a charge special; The initial 10F screen freeze eats the opponent's directional inputs (except Jumps) but does not prevent attacks from being buffered immediately afterward (this can cause inputs to be combined in unintended ways, such as crouch MK + Fireball performing a raw Fireball, or a vertical jump + walk forward turning into a forward jump); Framedata shown in parentheses refers to the Drive Rush version used from a Parry; Drive Rush recovery is only 24F total (23F if done from a Parry) - but the enhanced dash itself is 46F total (45F if done from Parry) and you can cancel it as early as frame 9 (frame 11 if done from a Parry); Inputting a direction (walk/crouch/block/jump) after the Drive Rush recovery plays out 2 additional recovery frames before the transition occurs (this allows the user to perform an enhanced crouching or command normal late in the dash by inputting the direction + button simultaneously); You stop building any form of Drive Gauge on your attacks after using a Drive Rush in the MIDDLE of a combo (but you still continue to build Drive gauge as normal if you did Drive Rush at the START of a combo); Applies an extra damage scaling penalty after using a Drive Rush in the MIDDLE of a combo (no damage scaling if you use Drive Rush at the START of a combo); Costs 3 bars of Drive Gauge if canceled into from a normal attack; Costs 1/2 bar of Drive Gauge if canceled into from Parry (for a total of 1 bar of Drive Gauge when you factor in the initial 1/2 bar cost of the Parry); Normals used out of Drive Rush carry additional forward momentum (but throws and specials immediately halt all momentum, which can be a useful strategy to punish opponents for trying to interrupt your Drive Rush); Parry Drive Rush can only be initiated after frame 3 of the Parry (but can be performed immediately after recovering from a successful parry); Parry Drive Rush cannot be initiated with less than 1/2 of a Drive bar (as the initial Parry cost will put the user into Burnout) - But whiff canceling a Light normal into Drive Rush can achieve a similar effect; Cannot cancel Drive Rush into a Parry (inputting MP+MK results in a MK normal coming out instead); Drive Rush puts the user into a counter-hit state for the entire duration (this makes it impossible to tech a throw that connects during the dash)

jamie.name: Taunt
jamie.notes: His taunts change depending on drink level; Jamie's neutral taunt where he leans down momentarily can avoid a lot of attacks (his hurtbox lies down); Jamie's forward taunt during level 4 puts him to sleep for several seconds, making avoid most attacks unless they hit low (his hurtbox lies down for a while)

jamie.name: The Devil Inside
jamie.notes: Jamie's Drink Level affects his damage / move list / framedata / movement and various other properties; Drink Level 0 damage output: 90%; Drink Level 1 damage output: 95%; Drink Level 2 damage output: 100%; Drink Level 3 damage output: 105%; Drink Level 4 Damage Output: 110%; Increases Drink Level by 1; Restores 1/4th bar of Drive Gauge | 1/24th (~4%) of Burnout Gauge while in Drink Levels 0-3; Restores 1/2 bar of Drive Gauge | 1/12th (~8%) of Burnout Gauge while in Drink Level 4; Hold punch to gain further Drink Levels and Drive Gauge (refer to the framedata for the multiple drink versions); The start-up frames refer to when Jamie actually acquires the +1 to his Drink Level followed by a few recovery frames afterwards; 1F less total duration (49F) if Jamie reaches Drink Level 4; If Jamie is already at Drink Level 4 then he can hold the button to keep drinking indefinitely to recover his Drive Gauge

jamie.name: The Devil Inside (2 drinks)
jamie.notes: Increases Drink Level by 2; Restores 1/2 bar of Drive Gauge | 1/12th (~8%) of Burnout Gauge while in Drink Levels 0-3; Restores 1 bar of Drive Gauge | 1/6th (~17%) of Burnout Gauge while in Drink Level 4; The start-up frames refer to when Jamie actually acquires the +2 to his Drink Level followed by a few recovery frames afterwards; 2F less total duration (95F) if Jamie reaches Drink Level 4

jamie.name: The Devil Inside (3 drinks)
jamie.notes: Increases Drink Level by 3; Restores 3/4th bar of Drive Gauge | 1/8th (12.5%) of Burnout Gauge while in Drink Levels 03; Restores 1.5 bars of Drive Gauge | 1/4th (25%) of Burnout Gauge while in Drink Level 4; The start-up frames refer to when Jamie actually acquires the +3 to his Drink Level followed by a few recovery frames afterwards; 2F less total duration (144F) if Jamie reaches Drink Level 4

jamie.name: The Devil Inside (4 drinks)
jamie.notes: Increases Drink Level by 4; Restores 1 bar of Drive Gauge | 1/6th (~17%) of Burnout Gauge while in Drink Levels 0-3; Restores 2 bars of Drive Gauge | 1/3rd (~33%) of Burnout Gauge while in Drink Level 4; The start-up frames refer to when Jamie actually acquires the +4 to his Drink Level followed by a few recovery frames afterwards

jamie.name: The Devil Inside (DR4 activation)
jamie.notes: This move happens automatically when Jamie reaches drink level 4; This automatic activation cuts the recovery frames a bit short on all the moves that reach Drink Level 4, potentially granting far better oki scenarios upon activation

jamie.name: Breakin'
jamie.notes: Strike and Throw invincible on frames 1-12; Armor Break; Depletes 0.5 Drive Bar on hit for the opponent; Can hold down during the move to get +1 Drink Level as well as restoring 1/2 extra bar of Drive Gauge | 1/12th (~8%) of Burnout Gauge, in exchange for sacrificing some damage (-315 damage) and some oki (+4 KDA instead of +12); Moves Jamie quite far forward during its initial active frames, with impressive reach on its hitboxes; Jamie's fastest startup invincible Super Art makes this the ideal Reversal option while in Burnout; KDA is usually higher juggled into which can lead into stronger oki (Example: +3 extra KDA when juggled into after OD Palm)

jamie.name: The Devil's Song
jamie.notes: Duration of 900 frames (15 seconds) - The remaining timer freezes during any hitstop; Temporarily grants Jamie access to Drink Level 4 as well as restoring 1 bar of Drive Gauge | 1/6th (~17%) of Burnout Gauge; Jamie still only deals 105% damage during this super if it's activated during Drink Levels 0-3 as opposed to the 110% damage Jamie normally deals at Drink Level 4; Jamie does not build any Super meter while this super buff is active (however if he's already at Drink Level 4 when he activates this Super, then there's no buff timer so he can continue building Super meter); When used already at Drink Level 4: Instantly restores 3 bars of Jamie's Drive Gauge | 1/2 (50%) of Burnout Gauge; Jamie retains all the Drink Levels he previously had after the Super's duration expires

jamie.name: Getsuga Saiho
jamie.notes: Fully invincible on frames 1-12; Launches the opponent into a free juggle state on the regular version; Only goes into cinematic on first hit (only get a regular +14 knockdown for 450 damage on second hit); Armor Break; Depletes 1.5 Drive Bars on hit for the opponent; Super cinematic time regenerates ~1.8 Drive Bars for Jamie; Incurs 10% damage scaling when canceled into from specials; Puts the opponent into a free juggle state (and resets the current Juggle Counter to 0) allowing for free-form follow-up juggles

jamie.name: Getsuga Saiho (Critical Art)
jamie.notes: Fully invincible on frames 1-12; Only goes into cinematic on first hit (only get a regular +14 knockdown for 450 damage on second hit); Armor Break; Depletes 2 Drive Bars on hit for the opponent; Super cinematic time regenerates ~2.2 Drive Bars for Jamie; Incurs 10% damage scaling when canceled into from specials

jp.name: 站轻拳 (5LP)
jp.notes: Chains into stand LP / crouch LP / crouch LK; Incurs 20% damage scaling penalty if used as the first hit of a combo

jp.name: 站中拳 (5MP)

jp.name: 站重拳 (5HP)
jp.notes: JP's main combo / juggle / punish tool, as well as being fully cancelable with solid range for checking the opponent; Very strong punish tool granting full combo conversions with Drive Rush; Puts airborne opponents into a limited juggle state; Has some juggle potential naturally without Drive Rush; Large but brief hurtbox extension 1F before active frames which is strike invincible (cannot counter-poke projectiles); Has slightly extended hurtboxes for the entire recovery frames; Counts as 2 hits of damage scaling when used as the start of a combo

jp.name: 站轻脚 (5LK)
jp.notes: Incurs 20% damage scaling penalty if used as the first hit of a combo

jp.name: 站中脚 (5MK)
jp.notes: Solid range combo tool that's fully cancelable; Lifts up the hurtbox of his extended foot on frames 2-10 making this a strong poke against low attacks

jp.name: 站重脚 (5HK)
jp.notes: Head hurtbox is invincible to airborne strikes on frames 9-15; Extended kicking leg is invincible to airborne strikes on frames 12-17; Jack-of-all-trades tool for JP that does a bit of everything (combo / pressure / oki / target-combo mixups / anti-air all in one button); Whiffs on crouching from further away; Can be canceled into Departure: Shadow / Window while a portal is active

jp.name: 蹲轻拳 (2LP)
jp.notes: JP's only 4F normal option; Chains into stand LP / crouch LP / crouch LK; Incurs 20% damage scaling penalty if used as the first hit of a combo; Topmost hurtboxes on frames 1-5 are vulnerable only to airborne attacks (this is to discourage its use as an anti-air)

jp.name: 蹲中拳 (2MP)
jp.notes: Solid combo / poke / buffer tool; Topmost hurtboxes on frames 1-10 are vulnerable only to airborne attacks (this is to discourage its use as an anti-air)

jp.name: 蹲重拳 (2HP)
jp.notes: Extended arm is invincible to airborne strikes on frames 10-14 (after first active frame); Strong vertical anti-air; Cannot hit cross-up (behind JP); Extremely short horizontal range (mostly for anti-airing); Has naturally high juggle limit without Drive Rush

jp.name: 蹲轻脚 (2LK)
jp.notes: Chains into stand LP / crouch LP / crouch LK; Incurs 20% damage scaling penalty if used as the first hit of a combo; Can be canceled into Departure: Shadow / Window while a portal is active (does not combo)

jp.name: 蹲中脚 (2MK)
jp.notes: Extremely far range low poke tool that shifts JP's positioning forward; Can hit confirm into crouch MP on Punish Counter when in range; Incurs 20% damage scaling penalty if used as the first hit of a combo; Can be canceled into Departure: Shadow / Window while a portal is active

jp.name: 蹲重脚 (2HK)
jp.notes: Very short range sweep but has solid hitbox priority; Has some Juggle potential naturally without Drive Rush

jp.name: 跳中拳 (j.MP)
jp.notes: Very far horizontal reach (furthest of JP's air normals); Huge hurtbox extension 2F before active makes this move susceptible to being counterpoked out of the air; Projectile invincible on lower body (legs) on frames 12-22

jp.name: 跳重拳 (j.HP)
jp.notes: Spikes down airborne opponents on Counter-Hit / Punish Counter; Solid vertical hitbox priority (below JP); Projectile invincible on lower body (legs) on frames 9-23

jp.name: 跳轻脚 (j.LK)
jp.notes: Cross-up; Can be used as a fuzzy instant Overhead after a deep jump-in Heavy (or jump-in Mediums in Burnout as well)

jp.name: 跳中脚 (j.MK)
jp.notes: Puts airborne opponents into a limited juggle state on hit; Good juggle / air-to-air tool; Projectile invincible on lower body (legs) on frames 7-20

jp.name: 跳重脚 (j.HK)
jp.notes: Very far horizontal reach (furthest of JP's air normals); Huge hurtbox extension 2F before active makes this move susceptible to being counterpoked out of the air

jp.name: Guillotinna
jp.notes: Overhead; Good frame advantage on hit (can combo when meaty or on Counter-Hit / Punish)

jp.name: Malice
jp.notes: Very far range sweep (albeit a bit slow start-up) that can be very hard to punish on block for some characters when spaced out properly; JP ducks slightly during start-up losing his head hurtbox on frames 13-34 (but not low enough to get under Sagat's MP/HP Tiger Shot) and is considered in a Standing state for the entire duration; Has naturally high juggle limit without Drive Rush

jp.name: Bylina
jp.notes: Head and extended kicking leg hurtboxes are invincible to airborne strikes on frames 8-16; Solid horizontal anti-air (albeit a bit slow start-up) that launches opponents on hit into a limited juggle state; Core combo / juggle tool; Cannot hit cross-up (behind JP); First hit forces stand on hit; Second hit cannot hit crouching opponents, resulting in 3F worse frame advantage on block (-8); Both hits are cancelable (the cancel window executes after the second hits active frames)

jp.name: Grom Strelka First
jp.notes: Fully cancelable combo tool that also has a Target Combo extension

jp.name: Grom Strelka
jp.notes: Fully cancelable combo tool; 1F gap on block between hits; Counts as 2 hits of damage scaling

jp.name: Zilant

jp.name: Zilant Mid
jp.notes: Overhead

jp.name: Zilant Low

jp.name: Ravina
jp.notes: Throw Loop: Dash forward +1 for a weak corner strike/throw mixup (throw loses to 4F lights) or Drive Rush and manually time a mixup; Throws the opponent almost full-screen away; Incurs 40% damage scaling penalty when juggling into SA2 / Amnesia bombs; Punish Counter gives +70% (2040) damage, Hard Knockdown (denies back-roll option on wake-up), depletes 1 bar of Drive gauge from the opponent, and builds twice as much Super gauge for the attacker; Throw Escape builds 0.5 Drive bars for the defender (randomly assigned if throws are input simultaneously)

jp.name: Uragan
jp.notes: Back Throw oki when cornered: Can Drive Rush into Strike / Throw mix or just lock down with Torbalan (QCF Ghosts) or meaty Triglav (d,d+P); Throws the opponent almost full-screen away; Does not deal its damage until the opponent hits the ground, and thus does not incur any damage scaling penalty when juggled into SA2; Punish Counter gives +70% (2040) damage, Hard Knockdown (denies back-roll option on wake-up), depletes 1 bar of Drive gauge from the opponent, and builds twice as much Super gauge for the attacker; Throw Escape builds 0.5 Drive bars for the defender (randomly assigned if throws are input simultaneously)

jp.name: Tornado
jp.notes: Switches sides with opponent; Air Throw oki when cornered: Yes (+10 KD in their face after a forward dash); Punish Counter gives +70% (2040) damage, Hard Knockdown (denies back-roll option on wake-up), depletes 1 bar of Drive gauge from the opponent, and builds twice as much Super gauge for both players

jp.name: Drive Impact: Espada
jp.notes: 2 hits of armor on frames 1-27; Damages opponents Drive Gauge on Block (1/2 bar) | Hit (1 bar) | Counter-Hit (1.25 bar) | Punish Counter (1.5 bar); Knocks down on hit; Pushes the opponent far back on hit or block and causes a Wall Splat if they hit the wall (Parry prevents the backwards stumble and Wall Splat, greatly reducing the pushback); Regular KDA without Wall Splat +35 KD | Wall Splat on Hit +65 KD | Wall Splat on Block +72 HKD; KDA can vary greatly depending on how high the opponent wall splats (higher KDA the higher they wall splat); Advantage after Wall Splat can vary depending on distance from the corner (farther from corner gives higher advantage); Crumples the opponent on Punish Counter or after absorbing at least 1 attack during start-up (+21 frames before the crumple state goes airborne, followed by airborne state on frames 22-46 before they are grounded); Puts airborne opponents into a long spinning free juggle state when hit as a Punish Counter or after absorbing an attack; If the armor absorbs an attack it slows the overall start-up by 1F (27F total instead of 26F) and incurs 6F hitstop for each projectile hit absorbed (making it less likely to punish the opponent after absorbing projectiles); Absorbing an attack causes the player to take 1/2 the damage in recoverable health (but will KO if this would bring the player's health below zero); Stun/Dizzy occurs when a Wall Splat connects on an opponent in Burnout; Stun gives a free combo follow-up for the next 195F after hitting the wall, followed by a HKD if the player falls to the ground untouched (the last 7F before hitting the ground has a crouch-sized hurtbox but is considered standing, allowing for unique combo setups); Incurs 20% damage scaling penalty if used as the first hit of a combo (applies to wall splat on HIT, crumple, Burnout dizzy on hit/block, or any character-specific means of comboing after a regular Drive Impact); Incurs a 20% multiplier damage scaling penalty after a Wall Splat on BLOCK - Because the blocked Drive Impact is not considered a "hit" for the combo, the next attack can incur its own separate damage scaling as a combo starter; Wall Splat puts opponent into a special juggle state where the next move freely connects and continues the juggle even if it normally wouldn't (similar to a Forced Knockdown or Drive Rush juggle properties); Does not cause Wall Splat if the Drive Impact connects as a combo or a true blockstring with no gaps (LOCK icon appears on-screen); It is possible to "combo" into Stun if the opponent has under 1.5 Drive bars - a blocked DI Wall Splat from slightly outside the corner into a second DI on hit will cause Burnout and Stun (because the blocked DI is not technically considered a combo starter); Costs 1 bar of Drive Gauge; Cinematic slowdown occurs if both players activate Drive Impact within range of each other (granting a Punish Counter to the player who activates it later); Attempting to counter with DI vs. DI with under 400 HP will result in a KO, as the second player will not have enough health to absorb it; Clashes with other Drive Impacts and refunds the Drive gauge cost if they collide on the same active frame (start at exactly the same time, or 1F apart if the first Drive Impact absorbs a strike) - The meter refund does not prevent Burnout from occurring; The scrub killer

jp.name: Drive Reversal: Exilio
jp.notes: Has two versions: one performed during blockstun or parry stun (20F start-up) and one performed as a wake-up reversal (18F start-up); Fully invincible on frames 1-22 (blockstun) / frames 1-20 (reversal); Armor Break (blows through all armor like Drive Impact, but not counters like JP's Amnesia); Trying to Drive Reversal after the blockstun ends results in a Drive Impact; Drive Reversal immediately removes the current blockstun you're in and starts the attack; Causes a 4F screen freeze after the 6th start-up frame, which allows the opponent to perform a simple OS (inputting their buttons during the buffer window) to prevent their next attack from coming out; Safe on block (-2) when used against an opponent in Burnout; Costs 2 bars of Drive Gauge; If the opponent tries to throw against a wake-up Drive Reversal, it causes a 12F screen freeze and refunds 1 bar of Drive gauge (but does not prevent Burnout); Guaranteed to interrupt any Drive Rush canceled normal if performed immediately out of blockstun (unless the opponent reacts with an invincible move or counter)

jp.name: 斗气招架 (Drive Parry)
jp.notes: Parries all strikes and projectiles (high and low) from frame 1; 12F parry window (can hold the parry to extend the parry window); Perfect Parry occurs on the first 2 active frames (cannot achieve Perfect Parry if you buffer into parry by holding it during Reversal windows; Perfect Parries have to be timed properly); Can still hold charge directions during Parry (allowing characters with charge specials to stand block before performing their reversal); Can block during the recovery frames of a regular parry (can still get hit during the recovery frames if you don't block correctly); Getting thrown or hit at any point during the recovery frames of a whiffed parry attempt results in a Punish Counter; Successfully parrying a move puts you into the same amount of blockstun as that move would regularly do on block (but a Perfect Parry has only 1F of recovery); Throw invincible during the recovery of a successful parry (just like during blockstun); Perfect Parrying a strike has only 1F of recovery and disables the opponent from canceling their attack (basically a guaranteed punish opportunity except for safe jump setups); Perfect Parrying a strike requires holding the correct block direction (Down+Back for low strikes, Back for high/mid strikes); Attempting a Perfect Parry with the wrong block direction results in an "imperfect parry" that builds an extra 3000 Drive Gauge and plays a distinct audio/visual cue; After a successful Perfect Parry, you suffer a 50% penalty to your Damage, Drive Gauge Generation, and Drive Gauge Damage on any of your following attacks when punishing the opponent (in addition, both you and the opponent suffer a 20% penalty to your Super Meter gain during this period); Fully invincible for 6F after a successful Perfect Parry against a strike, which carries over to any attack you perform (ensuring a 5F or faster punish will always interrupt multi-hit attacks); Perfect Parrying projectiles puts you into fixed 10 frames of recovery and applies the same 50% scaling penalties (and 20% Super Meter penalty) on your following attacks when punishing the opponent; Parrying a Strike and Projectile on the same frame will result in a regular parry for the strike attack (effectively ignoring the projectile's hitstop / blockstun); Perfect Parrying a Strike and Projectile on the same frame will give a screen freeze like you Perfect Parried a Strike, but still give you 10F recovery as if you had Perfect Parried a Projectile; Can cancel into Drive Rush during active frames 3 and onward (fastest Drive Rush method is to buffer a forward input before doing parry + forward again); Can cancel into Drive Reversal from a successful parry (just like you normally can during blockstun); Costs 1/2 bar of Drive Gauge and continues to deplete 50 Drive Gauge per frame (0.3 Drive bars per second) as you hold the Parry; You lose the parry if you go into Burnout from the initial Drive Gauge cost (Perfect Parry requires frame-perfect timing when starting from under 1/2 of a Drive bar); Rewards 1 bar of Drive Gauge (1/2 bar total after factoring in the initial parry cost) for successfully parrying a strike; Rewards 1/2 bar of Drive Gauge (0 bar total after factoring in the initial parry cost) for successfully parrying a projectile (with a few exceptions); Rewards 2 bars of Drive Gauge (1.5 bars total after factoring in the initial parry cost) for successful parrying a Super Art or Drive Impact; Successfully parrying a strike attack splits the regular block pushback between both players (while Perfect Parrying a strike removes all of its pushback); Successfully parrying a projectile or Drive Impact reduces the pushback of it by half (while Perfect Parrying a projectile or Drive Impact removes all of its pushback); Your hurtbox and throw box expand slightly towards the opponent for the entire duration of the Parry (Throw box extension starts instantly on frame 1, while the Hurtbox extension starts on frame 3, after the initial 2F Perfect Parry window); Parrying while crouching maintains a regular crouch hurtbox for the first 2 frames of the parry (during the initial Perfect Parry window)

jp.name: 斗气冲刺 (Drive Rush)
jp.notes: Dashes forward and enhances the next normal or command normal used out of the Drive Rush with +4 extra hitstun / blockstun, as well as improved juggle properties (Juggle Limit increased by +3 / Juggle Start/Increase reduced to 0); The +4 bonus frame advantage gained from a Drive Rush enhanced move also stacks with any bonus frame advantage that move may have gained from Counter-Hit, Punish Counter, or Burnout; Grounded special-cancelable normals can also be canceled into Drive Rush on hit or block, as well as from light normals on whiff; Drive Rush maintains buffers (freezes the buffer window) during its start-up and freeze frames - This allows players to do things normally not possible within the normal buffer windows, such as Drive Rushing into a charge special; The initial 10F screen freeze eats the opponent's directional inputs (except Jumps) but does not prevent attacks from being buffered immediately afterward (this can cause inputs to be combined in unintended ways, such as crouch MK + Fireball performing a raw Fireball, or a vertical jump + walk forward turning into a forward jump); Framedata shown in parentheses refers to the Drive Rush version used from a Parry; Drive Rush recovery is only 24F total (23F if done from a Parry) - but the enhanced dash itself is 46F total (45F if done from Parry) and you can cancel it as early as frame 9 (frame 11 if done from a Parry); Inputting a direction (walk/crouch/block/jump) after the Drive Rush recovery plays out 2 additional recovery frames before the transition occurs (this allows the user to perform an enhanced crouching or command normal late in the dash by inputting the direction + button simultaneously); You stop building any form of Drive Gauge on your attacks after using a Drive Rush in the MIDDLE of a combo (but you still continue to build Drive gauge as normal if you did Drive Rush at the START of a combo); Applies an extra damage scaling penalty after using a Drive Rush in the MIDDLE of a combo (no damage scaling if you use Drive Rush at the START of a combo); Costs 3 bars of Drive Gauge if canceled into from a normal attack; Costs 1/2 bar of Drive Gauge if canceled into from Parry (for a total of 1 bar of Drive Gauge when you factor in the initial 1/2 bar cost of the Parry); Normals used out of Drive Rush carry additional forward momentum (but throws and specials immediately halt all momentum, which can be a useful strategy to punish opponents for trying to interrupt your Drive Rush); Parry Drive Rush can only be initiated after frame 3 of the Parry (but can be performed immediately after recovering from a successful parry); Parry Drive Rush cannot be initiated with less than 1/2 of a Drive bar (as the initial Parry cost will put the user into Burnout) - But whiff canceling a Light normal into Drive Rush can achieve a similar effect; Cannot cancel Drive Rush into a Parry (inputting MP+MK results in a MK normal coming out instead); Drive Rush puts the user into a counter-hit state for the entire duration (this makes it impossible to tech a throw that connects during the dash)

jp.name: Triglav
jp.notes: 1-hit projectile hitbox; Button strength determines the distance at which the spike spawns (LP (Classic) / L (Modern): 30% screen length | MP (Classic) / M (Modern): 60% screen length | HP (Classic) / H (Modern): 90% screen length); Modern Controls: When using the SP (Special) button function, the distance of the spike can be chosen depending on which direction is held within 10 frames of start-up (Back: Light version 30% screen length | Neutral: Medium version 60% screen length | Forward: Heavy version for 90% screen length); The spike appears from the ground travelling upwards (takes 3F to reach max height); Multifunctional tool that's good for zoning / juggling / pressure / chip damage, as well a good oki tool with its plentiful active frames and strong frame advantage on block when meaty; Launches opponent into a limited juggle state on hit; All versions behave the same when used in the corner

jp.name: Departure
jp.notes: Spawns a portal in the air according to button strength used (LP: Close | MP: Mid | HP: Far); After 150 frames; The portal automatically spawns a 1-hit projectile hitbox into the direction of the opponent; The spike appears from the portal travelling downwards towards the opponent; It takes the spike 1F to reach tall standing characters | 2F to reach medium size standing characters | 3F to reach crouching characters; Portal goes away if JP is hit or thrown; Portal opens up and then goes away if JP teleports to it via Departure: Window (qcb+LP/MP); Spike can be activated prematurely with Departure: Shadow (qcb+HP); Spike launches opponents into a free juggle state on hit when initating a juggle; Juggle Increase value becomes +1 when connecting mid-combo on an opponent in a Free Juggle state (but otherwise maintains the Juggle Count (+0 Juggle Increase) when hitting an opponent already in a limited juggle state (Juggle Count > 0)); Spike causes 31F of blockstun on block (true block advantage is very variable depending on what JP is doing); All versions of the Portal are placed at the edge of the screen when used in the corner; Counts as 2 hits of damage scaling when used as the start of a combo

jp.name: Departure: Window
jp.notes: Fully invincible on frames 6-25 (while JP is off-screen); Airborne on frames 26-41 (Forced Knockdown + Punish Counter state) followed by 3F landing recovery; Teleports JP to its location and allows for follow-up aerial attacks on frames 31-41; Teleport location with OD portals active depends on button strength (LP: closer portal | MP: farther portal); JP always faces towards the opponent after teleporting to a portal (can make for very ambigous cross-ups); If JP does any move in the air then he has 3 landing recovery frames where he is punishable; If JP doesn't do any move in the air then he has only 1 landing recovery frame where he is punishable (but can block and cancel into anything he wants on the later 2 landing recovery frames); The landing recovery frames follow the same rule as regular jumps do (they can never be canceled into any movement related options such as walking, dashing or another jump); Can be canceled into from crouch LK / crouch MK / stand MP / stand HK despite not normally being special cancelable

jp.name: Departure: Shadow
jp.notes: Spawns a 1-hit projectile hitbox into the direction of the opponent from the active portal; Multifunctional tool that's good for zoning / juggling / pressure / chip damage, as well a good oki tool with its plentiful active frames and very strong frame advantage on block; Spike launches opponents into a free juggle state on hit when initating a juggle; Juggle Increase value becomes +1 when connecting mid-combo on an opponent in a Free Juggle state (but otherwise maintains the Juggle Count (+0 Juggle Increase) when hitting an opponent already in a limited juggle state (Juggle Count > 0)); First active frame doesn't reach grounded opponents (effectively 20F start-up against standing opponents); First 2 active frames don't reach regular size crouching opponents (effectively 21F start-up against crouching opponents); Counts as 2 hits of damage scaling when used as the start of a combo; Can be canceled into from crouch LK / crouch MK / stand MP / stand HK despite not normally being special cancelable

jp.name: Torbalan (Feint)
jp.notes: Great tool for mixing up your zoning / pressure and baiting the opponent

jp.name: Embrace
jp.notes: 1-hit ranged Command Grab projectile; Command Grab which can be combo'd into; Projectile speed: 0.13 which then decelerates by 0.01 per frame when the ghost gets into proximity of the opponent; Cannot be performed if a portal (Departure special or Super Art 2) is on screen; Deals +15% extra damage (2070) on Punish Counter

jp.name: Amnesia
jp.notes: Counters Strikes (but not projectiles) frames 3-20; Rewards 1 bar of Drive Gauge on a successful counter; On successful Counter, JP steps back with 18~20F recovery (Normals & most Specials: 18F recovery | some Specials: 20F) recovery that's fully invincible and places a bomb near the opponent that continues to track them and explodes soon after (projectile hitbox explosion); Before the bomb explodes, it has a 1-hit projectile hitbox durability which can absorb any OD or non-OD projectiles (but loses to Super projectiles); Bomb causes proximity guard; The bomb incurs 60% damage scaling when combo'd into or when used as the first hit of a combo (applies the 60% scaling onto the third hit of the combo); The bomb detonates early if SA3 is used to immediately punish the opponent after a succesful parry (this is to avoid JP being able to avoid the damage scalings by going straight into SA3); A successful counter disables the opponent from canceling their attack (just like a Perfect Parry does); Due to JP's recovery on a successful parry, the opponent can potentially recover before JP and continue the pressure as his fully invincible recovery finishes; This move cannot be performed again after a successful counter until the prior bombs have detonated; Counter-hit state on frames 1-2; Punish Counter state on frames 3-55

jp.name: Amnesia: Bomb
jp.notes: This move refers to the projectile bomb that spawns after Amnesia is successfully triggered; 1-hit projectile hitbox; Before the bomb explodes, it has a 1-hit Super projectile hitbox durability which can absorb any OD or non-OD projectiles (but loses to Super projectiles); Bomb causes proximity guard; The bomb incurs 60% damage scaling when combo'd into or when used as the first hit of a combo (applies the 60% scaling onto the third hit of the combo); The bomb detonates early if SA3 is used to immediately punish the opponent after a succesful parry (this is to avoid JP being able to avoid the damage scalings by going straight into SA3); Launches the opponent into a free juggle state on hit (and doesn't increase the current juggle state)

jp.name: Chornobog
jp.notes: Strike and Throw invincible on frames 1-10; Projectile hitbox on frames 8-21 that nullifies 1 hit of any projectile (Super projectile priority), followed by a 1-hit Super projectile on frames 22 and onward (flies full-screen); Armor Break; Depletes 0.5 Drive Bar on hit for the opponent; Knockdown increases the higher up it hits or the later active frames it lands; Despite being a projectile hitbox, this move can be Perfect Parried as if it was a Strike hitbox (screen freeze and only 1F recovery)

jp.name: Lovushka
jp.notes: No invincibility whatsoever; Spawns 4 separate 1-hit Super projectiles around the opponent that fly towards the middle in this order; High > Overhead > Low > Overhead; Each hit armor breaks; Each hit depletes 0.25 Drive Bar on hit for the opponent (1 Drive Bar in total); Incurs 25% damage scaling when combo'd into or when used as the first hit of a combo (applies the 25% scaling onto the third hit of the combo); Overall start-up of each projectile: 34F > 71F > 108F > 145F; Each projectile causes 20F of blockstun on block (17F gap between each projectile on block)

jp.name: Interdiction
jp.notes: Teleports next to the opponent during startup (attack can whiff if opponent is too high in the air); Fully invincible on frames 1-23; Armor Break; Depletes 1.5 Drive Bars on hit for the opponent; Super cinematic time regenerates ~1.8 Drive Bars for JP

jp.name: Interdiction (Critical Art)

juri.name: Drive Impact: Sekkan Kick
juri.notes: 2 hits of armor on frames 1-27; Damages opponents Drive Gauge on Block (1/2 bar) | Hit (1 bar) | Counter-Hit (1.25 bar) | Punish Counter (1.5 bar); Knocks down on hit; Pushes the opponent far back on hit or block and causes a Wall Splat if they hit the wall (Parry prevents the backwards stumble and Wall Splat, greatly reducing the pushback); Regular KDA without Wall Splat +35 KD | Wall Splat on Hit +65 KD | Wall Splat on Block +72 HKD; KDA can vary greatly depending on how high the opponent wall splats (higher KDA the higher they wall splat); Advantage after Wall Splat can vary depending on distance from the corner (farther from corner gives higher advantage); Crumples the opponent on Punish Counter or after absorbing at least 1 attack during start-up (+21 frames before the crumple state goes airborne, followed by airborne state on frames 22-46 before they are grounded); Puts airborne opponents into a long spinning free juggle state when hit as a Punish Counter or after absorbing an attack; If the armor absorbs an attack it slows the overall start-up by 1F (27F total instead of 26F) and incurs 6F hitstop for each projectile hit absorbed (making it less likely to punish the opponent after absorbing projectiles); Absorbing an attack causes the player to take 1/2 the damage in recoverable health (but will KO if this would bring the player's health below zero); Stun/Dizzy occurs when a Wall Splat connects on an opponent in Burnout; Stun gives a free combo follow-up for the next 195F after hitting the wall, followed by a HKD if the player falls to the ground untouched (the last 7F before hitting the ground has a crouch-sized hurtbox but is considered standing, allowing for unique combo setups); Incurs 20% damage scaling penalty if used as the first hit of a combo (applies to wall splat on HIT, crumple, Burnout dizzy on hit/block, or any character-specific means of comboing after a regular Drive Impact); Incurs a 20% multiplier damage scaling penalty after a Wall Splat on BLOCK - Because the blocked Drive Impact is not considered a "hit" for the combo, the next attack can incur its own separate damage scaling as a combo starter; Wall Splat puts opponent into a special juggle state where the next move freely connects and continues the juggle even if it normally wouldn't (similar to a Forced Knockdown or Drive Rush juggle properties); Does not cause Wall Splat if the Drive Impact connects as a combo or a true blockstring with no gaps (LOCK icon appears on-screen); It is possible to "combo" into Stun if the opponent has under 1.5 Drive bars - a blocked DI Wall Splat from slightly outside the corner into a second DI on hit will cause Burnout and Stun (because the blocked DI is not technically considered a combo starter); Costs 1 bar of Drive Gauge; Cinematic slowdown occurs if both players activate Drive Impact within range of each other (granting a Punish Counter to the player who activates it later); Attempting to counter with DI vs. DI with under 400 HP will result in a KO, as the second player will not have enough health to absorb it; Clashes with other Drive Impacts and refunds the Drive gauge cost if they collide on the same active frame (start at exactly the same time, or 1F apart if the first Drive Impact absorbs a strike) - The meter refund does not prevent Burnout from occurring; The scrub killer

juri.name: Drive Reversal: Kaita Raid
juri.notes: Has two versions: one performed during blockstun or parry stun (20F start-up) and one performed as a wake-up reversal (18F start-up); Fully invincible on frames 1-22 (blockstun) / frames 1-20 (reversal); Armor Break (blows through all armor like Drive Impact, but not counters like JP's Amnesia); Trying to Drive Reversal after the blockstun ends results in a Drive Impact; Drive Reversal immediately removes the current blockstun you're in and starts the attack; Causes a 4F screen freeze after the 6th start-up frame, which allows the opponent to perform a simple OS (inputting their buttons during the buffer window) to prevent their next attack from coming out; Safe on block (-2) when used against an opponent in Burnout; Costs 2 bars of Drive Gauge; If the opponent tries to throw against a wake-up Drive Reversal, it causes a 12F screen freeze and refunds 1 bar of Drive gauge (but does not prevent Burnout); Guaranteed to interrupt any Drive Rush canceled normal if performed immediately out of blockstun (unless the opponent reacts with an invincible move or counter)

juri.name: 斗气招架 (Drive Parry)
juri.notes: Parries all strikes and projectiles (high and low) from frame 1; 12F parry window (can hold the parry to extend the parry window); Perfect Parry occurs on the first 2 active frames (cannot achieve Perfect Parry if you buffer into parry by holding it during Reversal windows; Perfect Parries have to be timed properly); Can still hold charge directions during Parry (allowing characters with charge specials to stand block before performing their reversal); Can block during the recovery frames of a regular parry (can still get hit during the recovery frames if you don't block correctly); Getting thrown or hit at any point during the recovery frames of a whiffed parry attempt results in a Punish Counter; Successfully parrying a move puts you into the same amount of blockstun as that move would regularly do on block (but a Perfect Parry has only 1F of recovery); Throw invincible during the recovery of a successful parry (just like during blockstun); Perfect Parrying a strike has only 1F of recovery and disables the opponent from canceling their attack (basically a guaranteed punish opportunity except for safe jump setups); Perfect Parrying a strike requires holding the correct block direction (Down+Back for low strikes, Back for high/mid strikes); Attempting a Perfect Parry with the wrong block direction results in an "imperfect parry" that builds an extra 3000 Drive Gauge and plays a distinct audio/visual cue; After a successful Perfect Parry, you suffer a 50% penalty to your Damage, Drive Gauge Generation, and Drive Gauge Damage on any of your following attacks when punishing the opponent (in addition, both you and the opponent suffer a 20% penalty to your Super Meter gain during this period); Fully invincible for 6F after a successful Perfect Parry against a strike, which carries over to any attack you perform (ensuring a 5F or faster punish will always interrupt multi-hit attacks); Perfect Parrying projectiles puts you into fixed 10 frames of recovery and applies the same 50% scaling penalties (and 20% Super Meter penalty) on your following attacks when punishing the opponent; Parrying a Strike and Projectile on the same frame will result in a regular parry for the strike attack (effectively ignoring the projectile's hitstop / blockstun); Perfect Parrying a Strike and Projectile on the same frame will give a screen freeze like you Perfect Parried a Strike, but still give you 10F recovery as if you had Perfect Parried a Projectile; Can cancel into Drive Rush during active frames 3 and onward (fastest Drive Rush method is to buffer a forward input before doing parry + forward again); Can cancel into Drive Reversal from a successful parry (just like you normally can during blockstun); Costs 1/2 bar of Drive Gauge and continues to deplete 50 Drive Gauge per frame (0.3 Drive bars per second) as you hold the Parry; You lose the parry if you go into Burnout from the initial Drive Gauge cost (Perfect Parry requires frame-perfect timing when starting from under 1/2 of a Drive bar); Rewards 1 bar of Drive Gauge (1/2 bar total after factoring in the initial parry cost) for successfully parrying a strike; Rewards 1/2 bar of Drive Gauge (0 bar total after factoring in the initial parry cost) for successfully parrying a projectile (with a few exceptions); Rewards 2 bars of Drive Gauge (1.5 bars total after factoring in the initial parry cost) for successful parrying a Super Art or Drive Impact; Successfully parrying a strike attack splits the regular block pushback between both players (while Perfect Parrying a strike removes all of its pushback); Successfully parrying a projectile or Drive Impact reduces the pushback of it by half (while Perfect Parrying a projectile or Drive Impact removes all of its pushback); Your hurtbox and throw box expand slightly towards the opponent for the entire duration of the Parry (Throw box extension starts instantly on frame 1, while the Hurtbox extension starts on frame 3, after the initial 2F Perfect Parry window); Parrying while crouching maintains a regular crouch hurtbox for the first 2 frames of the parry (during the initial Perfect Parry window)

juri.name: 斗气冲刺 (Drive Rush)
juri.notes: Dashes forward and enhances the next normal or command normal used out of the Drive Rush with +4 extra hitstun / blockstun, as well as improved juggle properties (Juggle Limit increased by +3 / Juggle Start/Increase reduced to 0); The +4 bonus frame advantage gained from a Drive Rush enhanced move also stacks with any bonus frame advantage that move may have gained from Counter-Hit, Punish Counter, or Burnout; Grounded special-cancelable normals can also be canceled into Drive Rush on hit or block, as well as from light normals on whiff; Drive Rush maintains buffers (freezes the buffer window) during its start-up and freeze frames - This allows players to do things normally not possible within the normal buffer windows, such as Drive Rushing into a charge special; The initial 10F screen freeze eats the opponent's directional inputs (except Jumps) but does not prevent attacks from being buffered immediately afterward (this can cause inputs to be combined in unintended ways, such as crouch MK + Fireball performing a raw Fireball, or a vertical jump + walk forward turning into a forward jump); Framedata shown in parentheses refers to the Drive Rush version used from a Parry; Drive Rush recovery is only 24F total (23F if done from a Parry) - but the enhanced dash itself is 46F total (45F if done from Parry) and you can cancel it as early as frame 9 (frame 11 if done from a Parry); Inputting a direction (walk/crouch/block/jump) after the Drive Rush recovery plays out 2 additional recovery frames before the transition occurs (this allows the user to perform an enhanced crouching or command normal late in the dash by inputting the direction + button simultaneously); You stop building any form of Drive Gauge on your attacks after using a Drive Rush in the MIDDLE of a combo (but you still continue to build Drive gauge as normal if you did Drive Rush at the START of a combo); Applies an extra damage scaling penalty after using a Drive Rush in the MIDDLE of a combo (no damage scaling if you use Drive Rush at the START of a combo); Costs 3 bars of Drive Gauge if canceled into from a normal attack; Costs 1/2 bar of Drive Gauge if canceled into from Parry (for a total of 1 bar of Drive Gauge when you factor in the initial 1/2 bar cost of the Parry); Normals used out of Drive Rush carry additional forward momentum (but throws and specials immediately halt all momentum, which can be a useful strategy to punish opponents for trying to interrupt your Drive Rush); Parry Drive Rush can only be initiated after frame 3 of the Parry (but can be performed immediately after recovering from a successful parry); Parry Drive Rush cannot be initiated with less than 1/2 of a Drive bar (as the initial Parry cost will put the user into Burnout) - But whiff canceling a Light normal into Drive Rush can achieve a similar effect; Cannot cancel Drive Rush into a Parry (inputting MP+MK results in a MK normal coming out instead); Drive Rush puts the user into a counter-hit state for the entire duration (this makes it impossible to tech a throw that connects during the dash)

ken.notes: 2 hits of armor on frames 1-27; Damages opponents Drive Gauge on Block (1/2 bar) | Hit (1 bar) | Counter-Hit (1.25 bar) | Punish Counter (1.5 bar); Knocks down on hit; Pushes the opponent far back on hit or block and causes a Wall Splat if they hit the wall (Parry prevents the backwards stumble and Wall Splat, greatly reducing the pushback); The scrub killer

After a successful Perfect Parry, you suffer a 50% penalty to your Damage, Drive Gauge Generation, and Drive Gauge Damage on any of your following attacks when punishing the opponent (in addition, both you and the opponent suffer a 20% penalty to your Super Meter gain during this period); Fully invincible for 6F after a successful Perfect Parry against a strike, which carries over to any attack you perform (ensuring a 5F or faster punish will always interrupt multi-hit attacks); Perfect Parrying projectiles puts you into fixed 10 frames of recovery and applies the same 50% scaling penalties (and 20% Super Meter penalty) on your following attacks when punishing the opponent; Parrying a Strike and Projectile on the same frame will result in a regular parry for the strike attack (effectively ignoring the projectile's hitstop / blockstun); Perfect Parrying a Strike and Projectile on the same frame will give a screen freeze like you Perfect Parried a Strike, but still give you 10F recovery as if you had Perfect Parried a Projectile; Can cancel into Drive Rush during active frames 3 and onward (fastest Drive Rush method is to buffer a forward input before doing parry + forward again); Can cancel into Drive Reversal from a successful parry (just like you normally can during blockstun); Costs 1/2 bar of Drive Gauge and continues to deplete 50 Drive Gauge per frame (0.3 Drive bars per second) as you hold the Parry; You lose the parry if you go into Burnout from the initial Drive Gauge cost (Perfect Parry requires frame-perfect timing when starting from under 1/2 of a Drive bar); Rewards 1 bar of Drive Gauge (1/2 bar total after factoring in the initial parry cost) for successfully parrying a strike; Rewards 1/2 bar of Drive Gauge (0 bar total after factoring in the initial parry cost) for successfully parrying a projectile (with a few exceptions); Rewards 2 bars of Drive Gauge (1.5 bars total after factoring in the initial parry cost) for successful parrying a Super Art or Drive Impact; Successfully parrying a strike attack splits the regular block pushback between both players (while Perfect Parrying a strike removes all of its pushback); Successfully parrying a projectile or Drive Impact reduces the pushback of it by half (while Perfect Parrying a projectile or Drive Impact removes all of its pushback); Your hurtbox and throw box expand slightly towards the opponent for the entire duration of the Parry (Throw box extension starts instantly on frame 1, while the Hurtbox extension starts on frame 3, after the initial 2F Perfect Parry window); Parrying while crouching maintains a regular crouch hurtbox for the first 2 frames of the parry (during the initial Perfect Parry window)

ken.name: 斗气冲刺 (Drive Rush)
ken.notes: Dashes forward and enhances the next normal or command normal used out of the Drive Rush with +4 extra hitstun / blockstun, as well as improved juggle properties (Juggle Limit increased by +3 / Juggle Start/Increase reduced to 0); The +4 bonus frame advantage gained from a Drive Rush enhanced move also stacks with any bonus frame advantage that move may have gained from Counter-Hit, Punish Counter, or Burnout; Grounded special-cancelable normals can also be canceled into Drive Rush on hit or block, as well as from light normals on whiff; Drive Rush maintains buffers (freezes the buffer window) during its start-up and freeze frames - This allows players to do things normally not possible within the normal buffer windows, such as Drive Rushing into a charge special; The initial 10F screen freeze eats the opponent's directional inputs (except Jumps) but does not prevent attacks from being buffered immediately afterward (this can cause inputs to be combined in unintended ways, such as crouch MK + Fireball performing a raw Fireball, or a vertical jump + walk forward turning into a forward jump); Framedata shown in parentheses refers to the Drive Rush version used from a Parry; Drive Rush recovery is only 24F total (23F if done from a Parry) - but the enhanced dash itself is 46F total (45F if done from Parry) and you can cancel it as early as frame 9 (frame 11 if done from a Parry); Inputting a direction (walk/crouch/block/jump) after the Drive Rush recovery plays out 2 additional recovery frames before the transition occurs (this allows the user to perform an enhanced crouching or command normal late in the dash by inputting the direction + button simultaneously); You stop building any form of Drive Gauge on your attacks after using a Drive Rush in the MIDDLE of a combo (but you still continue to build Drive gauge as normal if you did Drive Rush at the START of a combo); Applies an extra damage scaling penalty after using a Drive Rush in the MIDDLE of a combo (no damage scaling if you use Drive Rush at the START of a combo); Costs 3 bars of Drive Gauge if canceled into from a normal attack; Costs 1/2 bar of Drive Gauge if canceled into from Parry (for a total of 1 bar of Drive Gauge when you factor in the initial 1/2 bar cost of the Parry); Normals used out of Drive Rush carry additional forward momentum (but throws and specials immediately halt all momentum, which can be a useful strategy to punish opponents for trying to interrupt your Drive Rush); Parry Drive Rush can only be initiated after frame 3 of the Parry (but can be performed immediately after recovering from a successful parry); Parry Drive Rush cannot be initiated with less than 1/2 of a Drive bar (as the initial Parry cost will put the user into Burnout) - But whiff canceling a Light normal into Drive Rush can achieve a similar effect; Cannot cancel Drive Rush into a Parry (inputting MP+MK results in a MK normal coming out instead); Drive Rush puts the user into a counter-hit state for the entire duration (this makes it impossible to tech a throw that connects during the dash)
