bison.name: Devil Reverse (bomb)
bison.notes: Hits Overhead; Can be steered left / right; Puts opponent into a limited juggle state on hit (more combo follow-ups possible in the corner); Grants massive frame advantage on block, allowing for easy follow-up pressure and lots of Drive Gauge chip; KD and block advantage varies depending on how high/low to the ground Dictator connects (better knockdown and block advantage the lower to the ground Dictator connects); Does not trigger Psycho Mine detonation if Perfect Parried; Dictator is in a crouching state during landing recovery; Forced Knockdown state while airborne

variations.notes: Hits Overhead; Can be steered left / right; Puts opponent into a limited juggle state on hit (more combo follow-ups possible in the corner); Grants massive frame advantage on block, allowing for easy follow-up pressure and lots of Drive Gauge chip; KD and block advantage varies depending on how high/low to the ground Dictator connects (better knockdown and block advantage the lower to the ground Dictator connects); Does not trigger Psycho Mine detonation if Perfect Parried; Dictator is in a crouching state during landing recovery; Forced Knockdown state while airborne

mai.name: 站轻拳 (5LP)
mai.notes: Chains into stand LP / crouch LP / crouch LK; Shorter range than crouch LP but +1F extra hitstun meaning move combo potential (naturally combos into things like LP/MP Ryuuenbu (QCB special); Incurs 20% damage scaling penalty if used as the first hit of a combo

mai.name: 站中拳 (5MP)
mai.notes: Decent range with strong hitbox priority and fully cancelable makes this a solid neutral tool; +2F extra recovery (17F) on whiff; Extends a very wide arm hurtbox until frame 15 of whiff recovery and a full-body hurtbox until the end of recovery making it relatively easy to whiff punish

mai.name: 站重拳 (5HP)
mai.notes: Core combo / pressure / whiff punish tool that leads into Mai's highest damage routes and most suffocating block pressure; Last active frame has quite a bit more range, granting even better whiff punish links when spaced out (crouch MK can link when spaced out)

mai.name: 站轻脚 (5LK)
mai.notes: Very short range but goes into the LK Target Combo follow-ups; Incurs 20% damage scaling penalty if used as the first hit of a combo; BUG?: Has 1F extra hitstop compared to the universal rule of light attacks

mai.name: 站中脚 (5MK)
mai.notes: Good combo / poke / whiff punish tool; Mai lifts up her front leg hurtbox on frames 4-17 making this a good tool against low attacks; Good hitbox priority; Can easily be hit confirmed into SA2 on Punish Counter (also works on Counter-Hit at closer ranges)

mai.name: 站重脚 (5HK)
mai.notes: Good whiff punish tool; Causes a crumple-like free juggle state on a grounded Punish Counter (opponent is airborne for any follow-up hits); Mai lifts up her standing leg hurtbox on frames 10-16 making this a decent tool against low attacks; Puts airborne opponents into a limited juggle state on Punish Counter; The brief extended leg hurtbox on frame 13 of start-up (1F before active) is strike invincible (cannot counter-poke projectiles); +3F extra recovery frames (22F) on whiff

mai.name: 蹲轻拳 (2LP)
mai.notes: Chains into stand LP / crouch LP / crouch LK; Furthest range of Mai's light buttons (but less combo potential than 5LP due to 1F less hitstun); Incurs 20% damage scaling penalty if used as the first hit of a combo; Topmost hurtboxes on frames 1-6 are vulnerable only to airborne attacks (this is to discourage its use as an anti-air)

mai.name: 蹲中拳 (2MP)
mai.notes: Decent combo / buffer tool; Solid range for a crouch MP and shifts Mai's positioning forward, making this also a pretty good whiff punish tool (can link into stand HP or Sweep on Punish Counter); +2F extra recovery (17F) on whiff

mai.name: 蹲重拳 (2HP)
mai.notes: Mostly a combo tool (like from Drive Rush) but the first hit does have strong hitbox priority for counter-poking; First hit pulls in the opponent on hit or block; Second hit leaves you close enough on hit to link into combos; Second hit has high pushback on block to keep Mai out of throw range even when used out of Drive Rush (must walk back to escape a reversal throw against Marisa / Zangief)

mai.name: 蹲轻脚 (2LK)
mai.notes: Chains into stand LP / crouch LP / crouch LK; Incurs 20% damage scaling penalty if used as the first hit of a combo

mai.name: 蹲中脚 (2MK)
mai.notes: Your average SF6 crouch MK; Incurs a 20% damage scaling penalty if used as the first hit of a combo

mai.name: 蹲重脚 (2HK)
mai.notes: Has good hitbox priority against low attacks (the extended kick hurtbox can effectively low crush some low attacks); +1F extra recovery frame (23F) on block; +3F extra recovery frames (25F) on whiff

mai.name: 跳轻拳 (j.LP)
mai.notes: Fast air-to-air option; Best horizontal hitbox priority of Mai's jumping attacks

mai.name: 跳中拳 (j.MP)
mai.notes: Puts airborne opponents into a limited juggle state; Important juggle tool after OD Hissatsu Shinobi Bachi (allows midscreen juggles into Level 1 Super); Good air-to-air hitboxes

mai.name: 跳重拳 (j.HP)
mai.notes: Good hitbox for vertical air approaches

mai.name: 跳轻脚 (j.LK)
mai.notes: Cross-up; Can be used as an instant Overhead

mai.name: 跳中脚 (j.MK)
mai.notes: Cross-up

mai.name: 跳重脚 (j.HK)
mai.notes: Furthest horizontal range of Mai's jump-in attacks

mai.name: Senkotsu Uchi
mai.notes: Fast Overhead with decent frame advantage (can meaty on last active frame to get jab combo follow-ups); Causes a spiked knockdown on airborne opponents

mai.name: Handstand Kick
mai.notes: Legs and lower body (keep in mind Mai is upside down) are invincible to airborne strikes on frames 8-12 making this a fantastic anti-air; Forced stand on hit (important for some combo routes); Cannot hit cross-up (behind Mai); Very easily hit confirmable into its Target Combo follow-up; Decent oki tool with lots of active frames that can be up to +7 on hit / +3 on block

mai.name: Hien Ren Kyaku 1
mai.notes: Forces stand on hit; This 2-hit version can be useful for some combo extensions while the latter hits of Kachousen (fan) are falling down onto the opponent

mai.name: Hien Ren Kyaku 2
mai.notes: Mai leaps off the opponent and can be followed up with a Musasabi no Mai (Divekick) or SA2 before landing (Divekick can be delayed quite a bit for potentially better angle and + frames on Flame Stock version); Airborne on frames 10-35 (Forced Knockdown state) followed by 4F landing recovery; True blockstring and mostly safe on block midscreen due to the distance it creates; Some Supers reach far enough to punish Mai, but in many cases she can respond with Divekick or Air Level 2 Super on reaction to avoid the punish; Divekick follow-up won't combo if the Divekick is delayed too much (59F hit confirm window for the Divekick to still combo); Divekick follow-up leads into +42 safe jump oki if the initial LK hits slightly spaced out

mai.name: Hoshi Kujaku
mai.notes: Extremely easy to hit confirm (28F window); Puts opponents into a limited juggle state (juggle follow-ups depend on if the opponent was grounded or airborne like after a Drive Rush juggle extension); Mai becomes fully invincible after the HK follow-up lands on hit; +8 extra recovery frames on whiff

mai.name: Shiranui Gourin
mai.notes: Throw Loop: Dash up for +3 mixup between strike / throw (corner only, cannot walk back to bait throw tech); Can walk up for a throw loop with 2F timing on Zangief and 1F timing on Blanka/E. Honda; Punish Counter gives +70% (2040) damage, Hard Knockdown (denies back-roll option on wake-up), depletes 1 bar of Drive gauge from the opponent, and builds twice as much Super gauge for the attacker; Throw Escape builds 0.5 Drive bars for the defender (randomly assigned if throws are input simultaneously)

mai.name: Fuusha Kuzushi
mai.notes: Back Throw oki: Can do meaty attacks or Drive Rush into strike / throw (corner only); Punish Counter gives +70% (2040) damage, Hard Knockdown (denies back-roll option on wake-up), depletes 1 bar of Drive gauge from the opponent, and builds twice as much Super gauge for the attacker; Throw Escape builds 0.5 Drive bars for the defender (randomly assigned if throws are input simultaneously)

mai.name: Yume Zakura
mai.notes: Corner Air Throw: Dash up for +2 mixup between strike / throw (corner only); Punish Counter gives +70% (2040) damage, Hard Knockdown (denies back-roll option on wake-up), depletes 1 bar of Drive gauge from the opponent, and builds twice as much Super gauge for both players

mai.name: Drive Impact: Botan Ichige
mai.notes: 2 hits of armor on frames 1-27; Damages opponents Drive Gauge on Block (1/2 bar) | Hit (1 bar) | Counter-Hit (1.25 bar) | Punish Counter (1.5 bar); Knocks down on hit; Pushes the opponent far back on hit or block and causes a Wall Splat if they hit the wall (Parry prevents the backwards stumble and Wall Splat, greatly reducing the pushback); Regular KDA without Wall Splat +35 KD | Wall Splat on Hit +65 KD | Wall Splat on Block +72 HKD; KDA can vary greatly depending on how high the opponent wall splats (higher KDA the higher they wall splat); Advantage after Wall Splat can vary depending on distance from the corner (farther from corner gives higher advantage); Crumples the opponent on Punish Counter or after absorbing at least 1 attack during start-up (+21 frames before the crumple state goes airborne, followed by airborne state on frames 22-46 before they are grounded); Puts airborne opponents into a long spinning free juggle state when hit as a Punish Counter or after absorbing an attack; If the armor absorbs an attack it slows the overall start-up by 1F (27F total instead of 26F) and incurs 6F hitstop for each projectile hit absorbed (making it less likely to punish the opponent after absorbing projectiles); Absorbing an attack causes the player to take 1/2 the damage in recoverable health (but will KO if this would bring the player's health below zero); Stun/Dizzy occurs when a Wall Splat connects on an opponent in Burnout; Stun gives a free combo follow-up for the next 195F after hitting the wall, followed by a HKD if the player falls to the ground untouched (the last 7F before hitting the ground has a crouch-sized hurtbox but is considered standing, allowing for unique combo setups); Incurs 20% damage scaling penalty if used as the first hit of a combo (applies to wall splat on HIT, crumple, Burnout dizzy on hit/block, or any character-specific means of comboing after a regular Drive Impact); Incurs a 20% multiplier damage scaling penalty after a Wall Splat on BLOCK - Because the blocked Drive Impact is not considered a "hit" for the combo, the next attack can incur its own separate damage scaling as a combo starter; Wall Splat puts opponent into a special juggle state where the next move freely connects and continues the juggle even if it normally wouldn't (similar to a Forced Knockdown or Drive Rush juggle properties); Does not cause Wall Splat if the Drive Impact connects as a combo or a true blockstring with no gaps (LOCK icon appears on-screen); It is possible to "combo" into Stun if the opponent has under 1.5 Drive bars - a blocked DI Wall Splat from slightly outside the corner into a second DI on hit will cause Burnout and Stun (because the blocked DI is not technically considered a combo starter); Costs 1 bar of Drive Gauge; Cinematic slowdown occurs if both players activate Drive Impact within range of each other (granting a Punish Counter to the player who activates it later); Attempting to counter with DI vs. DI with under 400 HP will result in a KO, as the second player will not have enough health to absorb it; Clashes with other Drive Impacts and refunds the Drive gauge cost if they collide on the same active frame (start at exactly the same time, or 1F apart if the first Drive Impact absorbs a strike) - The meter refund does not prevent Burnout from occurring; The scrub killer

mai.name: Drive Reversal: Yusura Ume
mai.notes: Has two versions: one performed during blockstun or parry stun (20F start-up) and one performed as a wake-up reversal (18F start-up); Fully invincible on frames 1-22 (blockstun) / frames 1-20 (reversal); Armor Break (blows through all armor like Drive Impact, but not counters like JP's Amnesia); Trying to Drive Reversal after the blockstun ends results in a Drive Impact; Drive Reversal immediately removes the current blockstun you're in and starts the attack; Causes a 4F screen freeze after the 6th start-up frame, which allows the opponent to perform a simple OS (inputting their buttons during the buffer window) to prevent their next attack from coming out; Safe on block (-2) when used against an opponent in Burnout; Costs 2 bars of Drive Gauge; If the opponent tries to throw against a wake-up Drive Reversal, it causes a 12F screen freeze and refunds 1 bar of Drive gauge (but does not prevent Burnout); Guaranteed to interrupt any Drive Rush canceled normal if performed immediately out of blockstun (unless the opponent reacts with an invincible move or counter)

mai.name: 斗气招架 (Drive Parry)
mai.notes: Parries all strikes and projectiles (high and low) from frame 1; 12F parry window (can hold the parry to extend the parry window); Perfect Parry occurs on the first 2 active frames (cannot achieve Perfect Parry if you buffer into parry by holding it during Reversal windows; Perfect Parries have to be timed properly); Can still hold charge directions during Parry (allowing characters with charge specials to stand block before performing their reversal); Can block during the recovery frames of a regular parry (can still get hit during the recovery frames if you don't block correctly); Getting thrown or hit at any point during the recovery frames of a whiffed parry attempt results in a Punish Counter; Successfully parrying a move puts you into the same amount of blockstun as that move would regularly do on block (but a Perfect Parry has only 1F of recovery); Throw invincible during the recovery of a successful parry (just like during blockstun); Perfect Parrying a strike has only 1F of recovery and disables the opponent from canceling their attack (basically a guaranteed punish opportunity except for safe jump setups); Perfect Parrying a strike requires holding the correct block direction (Down+Back for low strikes, Back for high/mid strikes); Attempting a Perfect Parry with the wrong block direction results in an "imperfect parry" that builds an extra 3000 Drive Gauge and plays a distinct audio/visual cue; After a successful Perfect Parry, you suffer a 50% penalty to your Damage, Drive Gauge Generation, and Drive Gauge Damage on any of your following attacks when punishing the opponent (in addition, both you and the opponent suffer a 20% penalty to your Super Meter gain during this period); Fully invincible for 6F after a successful Perfect Parry against a strike, which carries over to any attack you perform (ensuring a 5F or faster punish will always interrupt multi-hit attacks); Perfect Parrying projectiles puts you into fixed 10 frames of recovery and applies the same 50% scaling penalties (and 20% Super Meter penalty) on your following attacks when punishing the opponent; Parrying a Strike and Projectile on the same frame will result in a regular parry for the strike attack (effectively ignoring the projectile's hitstop / blockstun); Perfect Parrying a Strike and Projectile on the same frame will give a screen freeze like you Perfect Parried a Strike, but still give you 10F recovery as if you had Perfect Parried a Projectile; Can cancel into Drive Rush during active frames 3 and onward (fastest Drive Rush method is to buffer a forward input before doing parry + forward again); Can cancel into Drive Reversal from a successful parry (just like you normally can during blockstun); Costs 1/2 bar of Drive Gauge and continues to deplete 50 Drive Gauge per frame (0.3 Drive bars per second) as you hold the Parry; You lose the parry if you go into Burnout from the initial Drive Gauge cost (Perfect Parry requires frame-perfect timing when starting from under 1/2 of a Drive bar); Rewards 1 bar of Drive Gauge (1/2 bar total after factoring in the initial parry cost) for successfully parrying a strike; Rewards 1/2 bar of Drive Gauge (0 bar total after factoring in the initial parry cost) for successfully parrying a projectile (with a few exceptions); Rewards 2 bars of Drive Gauge (1.5 bars total after factoring in the initial parry cost) for successful parrying a Super Art or Drive Impact; Successfully parrying a strike attack splits the regular block pushback between both players (while Perfect Parrying a strike removes all of its pushback); Successfully parrying a projectile or Drive Impact reduces the pushback of it by half (while Perfect Parrying a projectile or Drive Impact removes all of its pushback); Your hurtbox and throw box expand slightly towards the opponent for the entire duration of the Parry (Throw box extension starts instantly on frame 1, while the Hurtbox extension starts on frame 3, after the initial 2F Perfect Parry window); Parrying while crouching maintains a regular crouch hurtbox for the first 2 frames of the parry (during the initial Perfect Parry window)

mai.name: 斗气冲刺 (Drive Rush)
mai.notes: Dashes forward and enhances the next normal or command normal used out of the Drive Rush with +4 extra hitstun / blockstun, as well as improved juggle properties (Juggle Limit increased by +3 / Juggle Start/Increase reduced to 0); The +4 bonus frame advantage gained from a Drive Rush enhanced move also stacks with any bonus frame advantage that move may have gained from Counter-Hit, Punish Counter, or Burnout; Grounded special-cancelable normals can also be canceled into Drive Rush on hit or block, as well as from light normals on whiff; Drive Rush maintains buffers (freezes the buffer window) during its start-up and freeze frames - This allows players to do things normally not possible within the normal buffer windows, such as Drive Rushing into a charge special; The initial 10F screen freeze eats the opponent's directional inputs (except Jumps) but does not prevent attacks from being buffered immediately afterward (this can cause inputs to be combined in unintended ways, such as crouch MK + Fireball performing a raw Fireball, or a vertical jump + walk forward turning into a forward jump); Framedata shown in parentheses refers to the Drive Rush version used from a Parry; Drive Rush recovery is only 24F total (23F if done from a Parry) - but the enhanced dash itself is 46F total (45F if done from Parry) and you can cancel it as early as frame 9 (frame 11 if done from a Parry); Inputting a direction (walk/crouch/block/jump) after the Drive Rush recovery plays out 2 additional recovery frames before the transition occurs (this allows the user to perform an enhanced crouching or command normal late in the dash by inputting the direction + button simultaneously); You stop building any form of Drive Gauge on your attacks after using a Drive Rush in the MIDDLE of a combo (but you still continue to build Drive gauge as normal if you did Drive Rush at the START of a combo); Applies an extra damage scaling penalty after using a Drive Rush in the MIDDLE of a combo (no damage scaling if you use Drive Rush at the START of a combo); Costs 3 bars of Drive Gauge if canceled into from a normal attack; Costs 1/2 bar of Drive Gauge if canceled into from Parry (for a total of 1 bar of Drive Gauge when you factor in the initial 1/2 bar cost of the Parry); Normals used out of Drive Rush carry additional forward momentum (but throws and specials immediately halt all momentum, which can be a useful strategy to punish opponents for trying to interrupt your Drive Rush); Parry Drive Rush can only be initiated after frame 3 of the Parry (but can be performed immediately after recovering from a successful parry); Parry Drive Rush cannot be initiated with less than 1/2 of a Drive bar (as the initial Parry cost will put the user into Burnout) - But whiff canceling a Light normal into Drive Rush can achieve a similar effect; Cannot cancel Drive Rush into a Parry (inputting MP+MK results in a MK normal coming out instead); Drive Rush puts the user into a counter-hit state for the entire duration (this makes it impossible to tech a throw that connects during the dash)

mai.name: Taunt
mai.notes: Back Taunt is 430F start-up that spawns 8-hit Super projectile hitboxes on both sides of Mai; Projectile hitbox low to the ground that hits for 800 damage total (1500 damage if doing the held version) but is also hugely punishable even on hit; Deals no chip damage

mai.name: Kachousen (hold)
mai.notes: 1-hit projectile; This fan cannot be swatted away by the opponent (behaves like a normal projectile would); The fan bounces upwards before falling back down (Projectile hitbox) after connecting with the opponent on hit or block (this gives Mai time to get in some follow-up hits or pressure); Projectile Speed and how far up the fan bounces upon hit / block varies depending on button strength; LP (Classic) / L (Modern): 0.04 speed and low fan bounce; MP (Classic) / M (Modern): 0.05 speed and medium fan bounce; HP (Classic) / H (Modern): 0.07 speed and high fan bounce; LP fan bounce gaps on hit / block vs Standing: 1F on hit / 5F on block | vs Crouch: 7F on hit / 11F on block; MP fan bounce gaps on hit / block vs Standing: 18F on hit / 22F on block | vs Crouch: 24F on hit / 28F on block; HP fan bounce gaps on hit / block vs Standing: 30F on hit / 34F on block | vs Crouch: 36F on hit / 40F on block; The frame gaps in fan bounces are slightly smaller on taller characters (1F smaller vs Dee Jay | 2F smaller vs Zangief, Sagat, Marisa and JP, meaning that a fully held LP fan bounce combos naturally on hit against those 3 characters when they're standing); These tall characters also cannot punish a fully held LP fan bounce with a throw, making them more susceptible to corner fan pressure; Leg (3-62F), body (19-31F), and arm (32-48F) hurtbox extensions are projectile invincible; Puts airborne opponents into a limited juggle state; Frame advantage listed on hit / block refers to the initial hit before the bounce (the bouncing fan deals 30F hitstun / 26F blockstun by itself, granting Mai potentially huge frame advantage); Any follow-up attack that Mai does overwrites the hitstun / blockstun of the bouncing fan

mai.name: Kachousen (stock + hold)
mai.notes: Enhanced: 1 extra hit and +100 damage (600 damage) before the bounce; 2-hit projectile; This fan cannot be swatted away by the opponent (behaves like a normal projectile would); Carries over Counter-Hit / Punish Counter bonus frame advantage to the first 2 hits before the bounce; The fan bounces upwards before falling back down (Projectile hitbox) after connecting with the opponent on hit or block (this gives Mai time to get in some follow-up hits or pressure); Projectile Speed and how far up the fan bounces upon hit / block varies depending on button strength; LP (Classic) / L (Modern): 0.04 speed and low fan bounce; MP (Classic) / M (Modern): 0.05 speed and medium fan bounce; HP (Classic) / H (Modern): 0.07 speed and high fan bounce; LP fan bounce gaps on hit / block vs Standing: 9F on hit / 11F on block | vs Crouch: 15F on hit / 17F on block; MP fan bounce gaps on hit / block vs Standing: 26F on hit / 28F on block | vs Crouch: 32F on hit / 34F on block; HP fan bounce gaps on hit / block vs Standing: 38F on hit / 40F on block | vs Crouch: 44F on hit / 46F on block; The frame gaps in fan bounces are slightly smaller on taller characters (1F smaller vs Dee Jay | 2F smaller vs Zangief, Sagat, Marisa and JP); Leg (32-62F) and arm (32-48F) hurtbox extensions are projectile invincible; Puts airborne opponents into a limited juggle state; The bouncing fan does not trigger proximity guard (opponent can walk back during it) and counts as an air attack (anti-air invulnerable moves can pass through it)

mai.name: Midare Kachousen
mai.notes: Two separate 1-hit OD projectiles (Four separate OD projectiles in total if you factor in the prior OD Kachousen); Projectile Speed: 0.072; These fans cannot be swatted away by the opponent (behaves like normal OD projectiles would); Bounces upwards before falling back down after connecting with the opponent on hit or block (this gives Mai time to get in some follow-up hits or pressure); There are brief gaps on block before the follow-up fans connect (close range only), as well as before both the bouncing fans connect (the window of these gaps varies greatly depending on if the opponent is standing / crouching, as well as being few frames smaller for taller characters like Dee Jay, JP, Marisa, Sagat, Zangief); Arm/head hurtbox extensions on frames 28-79 are projectile invincible; Puts the opponent into a limited juggle state on hit

mai.name: Midare Kachousen (stock)
mai.notes: Enhanced: Deals +200 extra damage on a regular hit (1400 damage total) with both the initial OD fans as well as the follow-up fans all bounce, resulting in 8 projectiles total (4 hitting directly, and 4 bouncing) which gives Mai huge frame advantage on block; Two separate 1-hit OD projectiles (Four separate OD projectiles in total if you factor in the prior OD Kachousen); Projectile Speed: 0.072; These fans cannot be swatted away by the opponent (behaves like normal OD projectiles would); Bounces upwards before falling back down after connecting with the opponent on hit or block (this gives Mai time to get in some follow-up hits or pressure); The frame advantage on block as well as the bouncing gap on block is far lower on taller characters (Dee Jay, JP, Marisa, Sagat, Zangief); Bounce gap on block for the final fan vs normal size characters Standing / Crouching: 9F vs Standing / 7F vs Crouching; Bounce gap on block for the final fan vs taller characters Standing / Crouching: 26F vs Standing / 7F vs Crouching; Frame advantage on block vs normal size characters Standing / Crouching: +33 on block vs Standing / +40 on block vs Crouching; Frame advantage on block vs taller characters Standing / Crouching: +15 on block vs Standing / +39 on block vs Crouching; Arm/head hurtbox extensions on frames 28-79 are projectile invincible; Puts the opponent into a limited juggle state on hit

mai.name: Musasabi no Mai
mai.notes: Can only be performed during a forward jump; Puts the opponent into a limited juggle state on hit; Forced Knockdown state while airborne; Solid hitbox for a divekick but rather slow start-up and long landing recovery frames; +10F extra recovery frames (28F) on whiff when landing behind the opponent; Crouching state on the final landing recovery frame

mai.name: Musasabi no Mai (stock)
mai.notes: Enhanced: +100 damage (1100 damage total) and better frame advantage on hit / block; Can only be performed during a forward jump; Puts the opponent into a limited juggle state on hit (same juggle potential as the regular OD version); Forced Knockdown state while airborne; Solid hitbox for a divekick but rather slow start-up and long landing recovery frames; +10F extra recovery frames (28F) on whiff when landing behind the opponent; Crouching state on the final landing recovery frame; Incurs 30% damage scaling penalty if used as the first hit of a combo

mai.name: Kagerou no Mai
mai.notes: Invincible only to airborne strikes on frames 1-39; Armor Break; Depletes 0.5 Drive Bar on hit for the opponent; Grants Mai 5 Flame Stocks on the final recovery frame which enhances all her Specials as well as SA1 and SA2; Core tool in Mai's gameplay to get her Flame Stocks; Very fast start-up for a Level 1 Super, although short range; Fantastic anti-air tool that hits on both sides of Mai; Projectile hitbox with 8 hits of Super projectile durability; Perfect Parry incurs only 1 recovery frame (unlike most projectiles) allowing opponents to interrupt between hits; Knockdown Advantage listed refers to when used on grounded opponents (KDA is higher and varies greatly on airborne opponents)

mai.name: Kagerou no Mai (stock)
mai.notes: Enhanced: +300 damage (2300 total), better oki (KD +40 instead of +28) and increased horizontal range; Invincible only to airborne strikes on frames 1-77; Armor Break; Depletes 0.5 Drive Bar on hit for the opponent; Grants Mai 5 Flame Stocks on the final recovery frame which enhances all her Specials as well as SA1 and SA2; Very fast start-up for a Level 1 Super, although short range; Fantastic anti-air tool that hits on both sides of Mai; Projectile hitbox with 12 hits of Super projectile durability; Perfect Parry incurs only 1 recovery frame (unlike most projectiles) allowing opponents to interrupt between hits; Knockdown Advantage listed refers to when used on grounded opponents (KDA is higher and varies greatly on airborne opponents)

mai.name: Chou Hissatsu Shinobi Bachi
mai.notes: Fully invincible on frames 1-8; Armor Break; Depletes 1 Drive Bar on hit for the opponent; Very good range but lacks the Projectile invincibility to more easily counter projectiles, which the enhanced stock version has; Can counter projectile on reaction if close enough (can punish projectiles from much further away if you do the faster air version (Tiger Knee the QCF input)); Deals less damage at further ranges due the first few hits hitting earlier; +11F extra recovery frames (37F) on block

mai.name: Chou Hissatsu Shinobi Bachi (stock)
mai.notes: Enhanced: Gains Projectile invincibility extension and +200 damage (3000 total), making this a very strong tool against other projectile users; Fully invincible on frames 1-8 and then Projectile invincible on frames 9-12; Armor Break; Depletes 1 Drive Bar on hit for the opponent; Very good range and can easily counter Projectiles on reaction (airborne version is even better at this); Deals less damage at further ranges due to first few hits hitting earlier in the active frames; Mai gets +20% damage from Counter-Hit / Punish to all hits of this Super (can be a lot of damage by itself when used properly as a whiff punish tool); +6F extra recovery frames (37F) on block

mai.name: Air Chou Hissatsu Shinobi Bachi
mai.notes: No form of invincibility whatsoever; Only 3F start-up when used in air as opposed to the 7F grounded version; Armor Break; Depletes 1 Drive Bar on hit for the opponent (if all hits land); Very fast and great range makes this a good air-to-air / combo tool, and can also be used to punish long-range fireball attempts (requires good timing since projectiles can clip your hurtbox if you do it too close to the ground); Deals slightly less damage at further ranges due to the first few hits hitting earlier in the active frames; Mai gets +20% damage (3360) from Counter-Hit / Punish to all hits of this Super (can be a lot of damage by itself when used properly as a whiff punish tool); Frame advantage and damage output varies drastically depending on distance (at least -50 on block, up to -70 or more if blocked and Mai flies over the opponent); If blocked, Mai is very likely to fly over the opponent if they're not cornered, resulting in Mai being even more punishable on block (but potentially far away); Cannot hit cross-up (behind Mai)

mai.name: Air Chou Hissatsu Shinobi Bachi (stock)

Enhanced: +100 extra damage on second hit (900 damage total); Can be followed-up with airborne normals / specials on frames 54-74 (air follow-ups are not possible on block); Mai does not leap into the air if the initial cartweel is blocked; Airborne on frames 31-74 (Forced Knockdown state) followed by 3F landing recovery if no follow-up is performed in the air; Second hit (elbow) cannot hit grounded opponents beyond the first active frame; Only second hit is cancelable into SA2/SA3 (usually better to delay the SA2 cancel here for the airborne version)

mai.name: Musasabi no Mai
mai.notes: Can only be performed during a forward jump; Puts the opponent into a limited juggle state on hit (more juggle potential than the non-OD version); Forced Knockdown state while airborne; Solid hitbox for a divekick but rather slow start-up and long landing recovery frames; +10F extra recovery frames (28F) on whiff when landing behind the opponent; Crouching state on the final landing recovery frame; Incurs 30% damage scaling penalty if used as the first hit of a combo

variations.notes: Can only be performed during a forward jump; Puts the opponent into a limited juggle state on hit (more juggle potential than the non-OD version); Forced Knockdown state while airborne; Solid hitbox for a divekick but rather slow start-up and long landing recovery frames; +10F extra recovery frames (28F) on whiff when landing behind the opponent; Crouching state on the final landing recovery frame; Incurs 30% damage scaling penalty if used as the first hit of a combo

mai.name: Musasabi no Mai (stock)
mai.notes: Enhanced: +100 damage (1300 damage total), better frame advantage on hit / block, and better juggle potential (even causes OTG ground bounce on airborne hits); Can only be performed during a forward jump; Puts the opponent into a limited juggle state on hit (better oki and more juggle potential than the regular OD version); Causes an OTG ground bounce on airborne hits; Forced Knockdown state while airborne; Solid hitbox for a divekick but rather slow start-up and long landing recovery frames; +10F extra recovery frames (28F) on whiff when landing behind the opponent; Crouching state on the final landing recovery frame; Incurs 30% damage scaling penalty if used as the first hit of a combo

variations.notes: Enhanced: +100 damage (1300 damage total), better frame advantage on hit / block, and better juggle potential (even causes OTG ground bounce on airborne hits); Can only be performed during a forward jump; Puts the opponent into a limited juggle state on hit (better oki and more juggle potential than the regular OD version); Causes an OTG ground bounce on airborne hits; Forced Knockdown state while airborne; Solid hitbox for a divekick but rather slow start-up and long landing recovery frames; +10F extra recovery frames (28F) on whiff when landing behind the opponent; Crouching state on the final landing recovery frame; Incurs 30% damage scaling penalty if used as the first hit of a combo

manon.name: 站轻拳 (5LP)
manon.notes: Chains into stand LP / crouch LP / crouch LK; Manon's main light combo tool since it combos naturally into QCB+LK/MK enders; Incurs 20% damage scaling penalty if used as the first hit of a combo

manon.name: 站中拳 (5MP)
manon.notes: Forward moving fully cancelable medium that also goes into Manon's MP>MK target combo to get her main mixup game going; Good oki tool due to its many active frames; Punish Counter changes the properties of her target combo follow-ups (turns it into a Hard Knockdown); Effective as a Drive Rush check with its forward movement and counter-hit combo into LP Hitgrab for a medal

manon.name: 站重拳 (5HP)
manon.notes: Basically just a slower but better version of her stand MP with better damage, range, hitboxes, and target combo follow-up; Cancelable into all Super Arts; Puts airborne opponents into a limited juggle state on hit (HP follow-up pulls the opponent in with an air reset); Punish Counter changes the properties of her target combo follow-ups (turns it into a Knockdown); Manon steps all the way back to her original starting position if nothing is input for up to 7 frames after the Recovery frames finish (Manon otherwise shifts forward ~0.45 distance if she doesn't let these post-recovery frames play out)

manon.name: 站轻脚 (5LK)
manon.notes: Pretty decent range light button; Incurs 20% damage scaling penalty if used as the first hit of a combo

manon.name: 站中脚 (5MK)
manon.notes: Not a low attack but is fully cancelable; Manon lifts up her front leg hurtbox on frames 9-12 (mostly during active frames) along with great hitbox priority making this a great tool against low attacks; Combos into LP Hitgrab on counter-hit making it an effective buffer tool for building medals

manon.name: 站重脚 (5HK)
manon.notes: Very far range poke and punish tool (about 40% screen range) that combos into her LK/MK Dégagé (qcb+LK/MK) on Punish Counter even from max range; 3F less recovery (23F) on HIT only; Puts airborne opponents into a free juggle state on Punish Counter; The brief extended leg hurtbox on frame 14 of start-up (1F before active) is strike invincible (cannot counter-poke projectiles)

manon.name: 蹲轻拳 (2LP)
manon.notes: Chains into stand LP / crouch LP / crouch LK; True blockstring when chained into crouch LP or stand LP; Incurs 20% damage scaling penalty if used as the first hit of a combo; Topmost hurtboxes on frames 1-5 are vulnerable only to airborne attacks (this is to discourage its use as an anti-air)

manon.name: 蹲中拳 (2MP)
manon.notes: +4F extra recovery frames (15F) on whiff only; Manon's main combo starter along with back HP

manon.name: 蹲重拳 (2HP)
manon.notes: Manon's extended arm and head hurtbox are invincible to airborne strikes on frames 7-34; Great anti-air tool with a built-in target combo follow-up for a KD that leaves the opponent up next to Manon for some oki

manon.name: 蹲轻脚 (2LK)
manon.notes: Chains into stand LP / crouch LP / crouch LK; Incurs 20% damage scaling penalty if used as the first hit of a combo; Less pushback on hit/block compared to other light normals

manon.name: 蹲中脚 (2MK)
manon.notes: A good range low poke with a ton of pushback on hit and block (can combo into crouch LP point blank); Incurs 20% damage scaling penalty if used as the first hit of a combo; Most useful when used out of Drive Rush (links into b+HP on hit)

manon.name: 蹲重脚 (2HK)
manon.notes: Standard sweep with huge range and good hitbox priority; Manon shifts forward a lot during start-up, which can push her hurtbox into a counter-poke

manon.name: 跳轻拳 (j.LP)
manon.notes: Manon's fastest air option with decent air-to-air hitboxes

manon.name: 跳中拳 (j.MP)
manon.notes: Fantastic air-to-air hitboxes; Puts airborne opponents into a limited juggle state; Projectile invincible on her lower body on frames 8-22 (can help Manon avoid projectiles below)

manon.name: 跳重拳 (j.HP)
manon.notes: Spikes down airborne opponents on hit

manon.name: 跳轻脚 (j.LK)
manon.notes: Cross-up; Can be used as a fuzzy instant Overhead after a deep jump-in Heavy (or jump-in Mediums in Burnout as well)

manon.name: 跳中脚 (j.MK)
manon.notes: Cross-up; Projectile invincible on her lower body on frames 7-20 (can help Manon avoid projectiles below)

manon.name: 跳重脚 (j.HK)
manon.notes: Very strong jump-in hitboxes (Manon's best jump-in button)

manon.name: Révérence
manon.notes: Manon's main combo tool; Very strong tool for pressure and oki; Puts airborne opponents into a limited juggle state

manon.name: Tomoe Derrière
manon.notes: Not a low attack (despite looking like a slide); Manon's kicking leg is invincible to airborne strikes on frames 9-19; Strong vertical anti-air and juggle tool; Can hit cross-up (behind Manon); Manon kicks airborne opponents back over her to the other side (air reset); Knocks down grounded opponents on hit; Punish Counter: Manon kicks the opponent back over her and scores a tumbling Hard Knockdown that can juggle into crouch HK / SA1 / SA2 (only SA1 is consistent if the opponent is airborne); Only first active frame hits grounded opponents (mostly used against airborne opponents)

manon.name: Back MK
manon.notes: Fantastic anti-air tool against horizontal and vertical approaches (but cannot hit cross-up behind Manon); Puts airborne opponents into a limited juggle state; Cancelable into an Overhead target combo follow-up (MK) on frames 17-25 (does not combo naturally if the cancel is delayed at all)

manon.name: En Haut
manon.notes: Overhead string that's also fully cancelable (very rare in Street Fighter); Forces crouch on hit; Carries over Counter-Hit / Punish Counter bonus frame advantage and Drive damage to both hits of this Target Combo (allows stronger cancel routes); Puts airborne opponents into a limited OTG juggle state; Combos naturally if this Overhead follow-up is not delayed at all; 2F gap on block that can be made bigger by manually delaying this overhead follow-up (various frametrap scenarios)

manon.name: À Terre
manon.notes: Pulls the opponent up close to Manon for a +2 mixup situation on hit; The initial stand MP can be canceled into this MK follow-up on frames 12-14 (15F hit confirm window if you factor in the 12F hitstop of stand MP); Grants a Hard Knockdown (+32) after Punish Counter stand MP that grants strong oki anywhere on the screen

manon.name: Temps Lié
manon.notes: Pulls the opponent up close to Manon for a +3 mixup situation on hit (much easier to hit confirm this one than the MP>MK target combo); First HP hit puts airborne opponents into a limited juggle state on hit (then the HP follow-up pulls the opponent in with an air reset); The initial stand HP can be canceled into this HP follow-up on frames 18-25 (28F hit confirm window if you factor in the 13F hitstop of stand HP); Puts opponent into a limited juggle state when landed after Punish Counter stand HP (KD +48); This juggled hit counts as 2 hits for damage scaling; +2F extra recovery frames (19F) on block only

manon.name: Allongé
manon.notes: Spikes down airborne opponents into a +17~19 Knockdown state (higher KDA the higher in the air the opponent is when pulled down)

manon.name: Ouchi Gari
manon.notes: Throw Loop: Manually time throw on their wake-up (not possible on mid-screen back-roll); Punish Counter gives +70% (2040) damage, Hard Knockdown (denies back-roll option on wake-up), depletes 1 bar of Drive gauge from the opponent, and builds twice as much Super gauge for the attacker; Throw Escape builds 0.5 Drive bars for the defender (randomly assigned if throws are input simultaneously)

manon.name: Uchi Mata
manon.notes: Throw Loop: after corner side switch, Drive Rush into a manually timed throw (3F timing window) or microwalk into a LP command throw; Punish Counter gives +70% (2040) damage, Hard Knockdown (denies back-roll option on wake-up), depletes 1 bar of Drive gauge from the opponent, and builds twice as much Super gauge for the attacker; Throw Escape builds 0.5 Drive bars for the defender (randomly assigned if throws are input simultaneously)

manon.name: Drive Impact: Glissade
manon.notes: 2 hits of armor on frames 1-27; Damages opponents Drive Gauge on Block (1/2 bar) | Hit (1 bar) | Counter-Hit (1.25 bar) | Punish Counter (1.5 bar); Knocks down on hit; Pushes the opponent far back on hit or block and causes a Wall Splat if they hit the wall (Parry prevents the backwards stumble and Wall Splat, greatly reducing the pushback); Regular KDA without Wall Splat +35 KD | Wall Splat on Hit +65 KD | Wall Splat on Block +72 HKD; KDA can vary greatly depending on how high the opponent wall splats (higher KDA the higher they wall splat); Advantage after Wall Splat can vary depending on distance from the corner (farther from corner gives higher advantage); Crumples the opponent on Punish Counter or after absorbing at least 1 attack during start-up (+21 frames before the crumple state goes airborne, followed by airborne state on frames 22-46 before they are grounded); Puts airborne opponents into a long spinning free juggle state when hit as a Punish Counter or after absorbing an attack; If the armor absorbs an attack it slows the overall start-up by 1F (27F total instead of 26F) and incurs 6F hitstop for each projectile hit absorbed (making it less likely to punish the opponent after absorbing projectiles); Absorbing an attack causes the player to take 1/2 the damage in recoverable health (but will KO if this would bring the player's health below zero); Stun/Dizzy occurs when a Wall Splat connects on an opponent in Burnout; Stun gives a free combo follow-up for the next 195F after hitting the wall, followed by a HKD if the player falls to the ground untouched (the last 7F before hitting the ground has a crouch-sized hurtbox but is considered standing, allowing for unique combo setups); Incurs 20% damage scaling penalty if used as the first hit of a combo (applies to wall splat on HIT, crumple, Burnout dizzy on hit/block, or any character-specific means of comboing after a regular Drive Impact); Incurs a 20% multiplier damage scaling penalty after a Wall Splat on BLOCK - Because the blocked Drive Impact is not considered a "hit" for the combo, the next attack can incur its own separate damage scaling as a combo starter; Wall Splat puts opponent into a special juggle state where the next move freely connects and continues the juggle even if it normally wouldn't (similar to a Forced Knockdown or Drive Rush juggle properties); Does not cause Wall Splat if the Drive Impact connects as a combo or a true blockstring with no gaps (LOCK icon appears on-screen); It is possible to "combo" into Stun if the opponent has under 1.5 Drive bars - a blocked DI Wall Splat from slightly outside the corner into a second DI on hit will cause Burnout and Stun (because the blocked DI is not technically considered a combo starter); Costs 1 bar of Drive Gauge; Cinematic slowdown occurs if both players activate Drive Impact within range of each other (granting a Punish Counter to the player who activates it later); Attempting to counter with DI vs. DI with under 400 HP will result in a KO, as the second player will not have enough health to absorb it; Clashes with other Drive Impacts and refunds the Drive gauge cost if they collide on the same active frame (start at exactly the same time, or 1F apart if the first Drive Impact absorbs a strike) - The meter refund does not prevent Burnout from occurring; The scrub killer

manon.name: Drive Reversal: Écarté
manon.notes: Has two versions: one performed during blockstun or parry stun (20F start-up) and one performed as a wake-up reversal (18F start-up); Fully invincible on frames 1-22 (blockstun) / frames 1-20 (reversal); Armor Break (blows through all armor like Drive Impact, but not counters like JP's Amnesia); Trying to Drive Reversal after the blockstun ends results in a Drive Impact; Drive Reversal immediately removes the current blockstun you're in and starts the attack; Causes a 4F screen freeze after the 6th start-up frame, which allows the opponent to perform a simple OS (inputting their buttons during the buffer window) to prevent their next attack from coming out; Safe on block (-2) when used against an opponent in Burnout; Costs 2 bars of Drive Gauge; If the opponent tries to throw against a wake-up Drive Reversal, it causes a 12F screen freeze and refunds 1 bar of Drive gauge (but does not prevent Burnout); Guaranteed to interrupt any Drive Rush canceled normal if performed immediately out of blockstun (unless the opponent reacts with an invincible move or counter)

manon.name: 斗气招架 (Drive Parry)
manon.notes: Parries all strikes and projectiles (high and low) from frame 1; 12F parry window (can hold the parry to extend the parry window); Perfect Parry occurs on the first 2 active frames (cannot achieve Perfect Parry if you buffer into parry by holding it during Reversal windows; Perfect Parries have to be timed properly); Can still hold charge directions during Parry (allowing characters with charge specials to stand block before performing their reversal); Can block during the recovery frames of a regular parry (can still get hit during the recovery frames if you don't block correctly); Getting thrown or hit at any point during the recovery frames of a whiffed parry attempt results in a Punish Counter; Successfully parrying a move puts you into the same amount of blockstun as that move would regularly do on block (but a Perfect Parry has only 1F of recovery); Throw invincible during the recovery of a successful parry (just like during blockstun); Perfect Parrying a strike has only 1F of recovery and disables the opponent from canceling their attack (basically a guaranteed punish opportunity except for safe jump setups); Perfect Parrying a strike requires holding the correct block direction (Down+Back for low strikes, Back for high/mid strikes); Attempting a Perfect Parry with the wrong block direction results in an "imperfect parry" that builds an extra 3000 Drive Gauge and plays a distinct audio/visual cue; After a successful Perfect Parry, you suffer a 50% penalty to your Damage, Drive Gauge Generation, and Drive Gauge Damage on any of your following attacks when punishing the opponent (in addition, both you and the opponent suffer a 20% penalty to your Super Meter gain during this period); Fully invincible for 6F after a successful Perfect Parry against a strike, which carries over to any attack you perform (ensuring a 5F or faster punish will always interrupt multi-hit attacks); Perfect Parrying projectiles puts you into fixed 10 frames of recovery and applies the same 50% scaling penalties (and 20% Super Meter penalty) on your following attacks when punishing the opponent; Parrying a Strike and Projectile on the same frame will result in a regular parry for the strike attack (effectively ignoring the projectile's hitstop / blockstun); Perfect Parrying a Strike and Projectile on the same frame will give a screen freeze like you Perfect Parried a Strike, but still give you 10F recovery as if you had Perfect Parried a Projectile; Can cancel into Drive Rush during active frames 3 and onward (fastest Drive Rush method is to buffer a forward input before doing parry + forward again); Can cancel into Drive Reversal from a successful parry (just like you normally can during blockstun); Costs 1/2 bar of Drive Gauge and continues to deplete 50 Drive Gauge per frame (0.3 Drive bars per second) as you hold the Parry; You lose the parry if you go into Burnout from the initial Drive Gauge cost (Perfect Parry requires frame-perfect timing when starting from under 1/2 of a Drive bar); Rewards 1 bar of Drive Gauge (1/2 bar total after factoring in the initial parry cost) for successfully parrying a strike; Rewards 1/2 bar of Drive Gauge (0 bar total after factoring in the initial parry cost) for successfully parrying a projectile (with a few exceptions); Rewards 2 bars of Drive Gauge (1.5 bars total after factoring in the initial parry cost) for successful parrying a Super Art or Drive Impact; Successfully parrying a strike attack splits the regular block pushback between both players (while Perfect Parrying a strike removes all of its pushback); Successfully parrying a projectile or Drive Impact reduces the pushback of it by half (while Perfect Parrying a projectile or Drive Impact removes all of its pushback); Your hurtbox and throw box expand slightly towards the opponent for the entire duration of the Parry (Throw box extension starts instantly on frame 1, while the Hurtbox extension starts on frame 3, after the initial 2F Perfect Parry window); Parrying while crouching maintains a regular crouch hurtbox for the first 2 frames of the parry (during the initial Perfect Parry window)

manon.name: 斗气冲刺 (Drive Rush)
manon.notes: Dashes forward and enhances the next normal or command normal used out of the Drive Rush with +4 extra hitstun / blockstun, as well as improved juggle properties (Juggle Limit increased by +3 / Juggle Start/Increase reduced to 0); The +4 bonus frame advantage gained from a Drive Rush enhanced move also stacks with any bonus frame advantage that move may have gained from Counter-Hit, Punish Counter, or Burnout; Grounded special-cancelable normals can also be canceled into Drive Rush on hit or block, as well as from light normals on whiff; Drive Rush maintains buffers (freezes the buffer window) during its start-up and freeze frames - This allows players to do things normally not possible within the normal buffer windows, such as Drive Rushing into a charge special; The initial 10F screen freeze eats the opponent's directional inputs (except Jumps) but does not prevent attacks from being buffered immediately afterward (this can cause inputs to be combined in unintended ways, such as crouch MK + Fireball performing a raw Fireball, or a vertical jump + walk forward turning into a forward jump); Framedata shown in parentheses refers to the Drive Rush version used from a Parry; Drive Rush recovery is only 24F total (23F if done from a Parry) - but the enhanced dash itself is 46F total (45F if done from Parry) and you can cancel it as early as frame 9 (frame 11 if done from a Parry); Inputting a direction (walk/crouch/block/jump) after the Drive Rush recovery plays out 2 additional recovery frames before the transition occurs (this allows the user to perform an enhanced crouching or command normal late in the dash by inputting the direction + button simultaneously); You stop building any form of Drive Gauge on your attacks after using a Drive Rush in the MIDDLE of a combo (but you still continue to build Drive gauge as normal if you did Drive Rush at the START of a combo); Applies an extra damage scaling penalty after using a Drive Rush in the MIDDLE of a combo (no damage scaling if you use Drive Rush at the START of a combo); Costs 3 bars of Drive Gauge if canceled into from a normal attack; Costs 1/2 bar of Drive Gauge if canceled into from Parry (for a total of 1 bar of Drive Gauge when you factor in the initial 1/2 bar cost of the Parry); Normals used out of Drive Rush carry additional forward momentum (but throws and specials immediately halt all momentum, which can be a useful strategy to punish opponents for trying to interrupt your Drive Rush); Parry Drive Rush can only be initiated after frame 3 of the Parry (but can be performed immediately after recovering from a successful parry); Parry Drive Rush cannot be initiated with less than 1/2 of a Drive bar (as the initial Parry cost will put the user into Burnout) - But whiff canceling a Light normal into Drive Rush can achieve a similar effect; Cannot cancel Drive Rush into a Parry (inputting MP+MK results in a MK normal coming out instead); Drive Rush puts the user into a counter-hit state for the entire duration (this makes it impossible to tech a throw that connects during the dash)

manon.name: Grand Fouetté
manon.notes: The start-up frames the spin is cancelable into the kick follow-up from depends on the spin version (LP: frames 16-20 | MP: frames 17-21 | HP: frames 18-22); Projectile invincible during the spin on frames 3-16 (up to frame 22 if the Kick follow-up is delayed on HP Spin); Launches opponent into a limited juggle state (free juggle state and +4 extra KDA on Punish Counter); Due to huge range this move can be spaced out to hit on later active frames for better frame advantage on hit/block/punish/parry; Incurs 10% damage scaling onto itself when combo'd into, as well as 20% damage scaling if used as the first hit of a combo

manon.name: Renversé Feint
manon.notes: Distance traveled, Projectile invincibility window, and overall duration of feint depends on the strength of button used; LP Feint: Projectile invincible on frames 3-15 | 31F total | 0.85 distance; MP Feint: Projectile invincible on frames 3-16 | 32F total | 1.10 distance; HP Feint: Projectile invincible on frames 3-17 | 33F total | 1.14 distance

manon.name: Arabesque
manon.notes: Strike and Throw invincible on frames 1-13; Armor Break; Low attack; Depletes 0.5 Drive Bar on hit for the opponent; Can switch sides with the opponent on hit

manon.name: Étoile
manon.notes: Fully invincible on frames 1-9; Armor Break; Airborne on frames 21-36 and again on frames 68-118 (Forced Knockdown state while airborne); Depletes 1 Drive Bar on hit for the opponent; The final leaping kick whiffs on crouch blocking opponents

manon.name: Pas de Deux
manon.notes: Fully invincible on frames 1-8; Range: 1.46~1.49; Command Grab which can be combo'd into with 5% additional damage scaling (15% damage scaling if combo'd into from QCF+HK); Depletes 1.5 Drive Bars on hit for the opponent; Super cinematic time regenerates ~2.2 Drive Bars for Manon; Damage increases with each Medal level; Medal Level 1: 4000 damage; Medal Level 2: 4100 damage; Medal Level 3: 4200 damage; Medal Level 4: 4400 damage; Medal Level 5: 4600 damage

manon.name: Pas de Deux (Critical Art)
manon.notes: Fully invincible on frames 1-8; Range: 1.46~1.49; Command Grab which can be combo'd into with 5% additional damage scaling (15% damage scaling if combo'd into from QCF+HK); Critical Art does +500 extra damage over regular version; Depletes 2 Drive Bars on hit for the opponent; Super cinematic time regenerates ~2.4 Drive Bars for Manon; Damage increases with each Medal level; Medal Level 1: 4500 damage; Medal Level 2: 4600 damage; Medal Level 3: 4700 damage; Medal Level 4: 4900 damage; Medal Level 5: 5100 damage

manon.name: Manège Doré
manon.notes: Range: 1.37; Medium range (and medium start-up) of her command grabs; Cannot be special canceled into; Increases Manon's Medal Level by +1 on hit; Damage and Super Gain increases with each Medal Level; Medal Level 1: 2000 damage / 3000 Super Gain; Medal Level 2: 2300 damage / 3000 Super Gain; Medal Level 3: 2700 damage / 4000 Super Gain; Medal Level 4: 3000 damage / 4000 Super Gain; Medal Level 5: 3700 damage / 5000 Super Gain

manon.name: Rond-point
manon.notes: Invincible to airborne strikes on upper body and extended leg on frames 7-19; Very strong anti-air tool; Cannot hit cross-up (behind Manon); Launches the opponent into a limited juggle state on hit; Only first hit is cancelable; SA3 cancel only combos if this attack is absorbed by an armor

manon.name: Dégagé
manon.notes: Airborne on frames 15-39 (Forced Knockdown state); Very far range combo / punish tool that sets up Manon's mixup game in the corner

marisa.name: 蹲重拳 (2HP)
marisa.notes: Can be held; Head hurtbox is invincible to airborne strikes on frames 10-13; Decent anti-air (albeit a bit slow) that extends a much wider hitbox on active frame 3; Cannot hit cross-up (behind Marisa); Only the first two active frames can hit grounded opponents (rest only hits airborne); Puts opponent into a limited juggle state on hit; Launches much higher on Punish Counter; Has some Juggle potential naturally without Drive Rush

marisa.name: Crouch HP (hold)
marisa.notes: Button must be held for 17 frames (results in uncharged version if released early); Uncharged version comes out in only 4 frames if HP is released between start-up frames 5-16; Head hurtbox is invincible to airborne strikes on frames 20-31; Mostly a combo / juggle tool (too slow to really anti-air); Cannot hit cross-up (behind Marisa); Only the first two active frames can hit grounded opponents (rest only hits airborne); Launches opponent into a limited juggle state on hit; Launches much higher on Punish Counter (can lead to multiple charged heavy normals for huge meterless damage); Has some Juggle potential naturally without Drive Rush; Marisa's throw hurtbox does not extend before the active frame, allowing her to use this as a high-reward shimmy tool; Cancelable into Super on active frames 1-2 only (can always combo into fully charged Level 1 Super for great damage)

marisa.name: Knee (hold)

marisa.name: Falx Crusher

marisa.name: Light Two Hitter

marisa.name: Medium Two Hitter

marisa.name: Heavy Two Hitter
marisa.notes: Gains +2F extra blockstun and extra range when canceled from fully charged stand HP (+4 on Block); 5F gap on block (trades with 6F) when canceled from uncharged stand HP; True blockstring when canceled from fully charged stand HP and deals massive Drive damage on block; Grants a safe jump (KD +42) near the corner

marisa.name: Mounted Grace
marisa.notes: Throw Loop: Can Drive Rush into a meaty throw in the corner only; Punish Counter gives +70% (2040) damage, Hard Knockdown (denies back-roll option on wake-up), depletes 1 bar of Drive gauge from the opponent, and builds twice as much Super gauge for the attacker; Throw Escape builds 0.5 Drive bars for the defender (randomly assigned if throws are input simultaneously)

marisa.name: Ponte Milvio
marisa.notes: Throw Loop when used while cornered: Dash forward for a meaty ranged strike or Drive Rush for a meaty strike/throw mix; Punish Counter gives +70% (2040) damage, Hard Knockdown (denies back-roll option on wake-up), depletes 1 bar of Drive gauge from the opponent, and builds twice as much Super gauge for the attacker; Throw Escape builds 0.5 Drive bars for the defender (randomly assigned if throws are input simultaneously)

marisa.name: Drive Impact: Secutor
marisa.notes: 2 hits of armor on frames 1-27; Damages opponents Drive Gauge on Block (1/2 bar) | Hit (1 bar) | Counter-Hit (1.25 bar) | Punish Counter (1.5 bar); Knocks down on hit; Pushes the opponent far back on hit or block and causes a Wall Splat if they hit the wall (Parry prevents the backwards stumble and Wall Splat, greatly reducing the pushback); Regular KDA without Wall Splat +35 KD | Wall Splat on Hit +65 KD | Wall Splat on Block +72 HKD; KDA can vary greatly depending on how high the opponent wall splats (higher KDA the higher they wall splat); Advantage after Wall Splat can vary depending on distance from the corner (farther from corner gives higher advantage); Crumples the opponent on Punish Counter or after absorbing at least 1 attack during start-up (+21 frames before the crumple state goes airborne, followed by airborne state on frames 22-46 before they are grounded); Puts airborne opponents into a long spinning free juggle state when hit as a Punish Counter or after absorbing an attack; If the armor absorbs an attack it slows the overall start-up by 1F (27F total instead of 26F) and incurs 6F hitstop for each projectile hit absorbed (making it less likely to punish the opponent after absorbing projectiles); Absorbing an attack causes the player to take 1/2 the damage in recoverable health (but will KO if this would bring the player's health below zero); Stun/Dizzy occurs when a Wall Splat connects on an opponent in Burnout; Stun gives a free combo follow-up for the next 195F after hitting the wall, followed by a HKD if the player falls to the ground untouched (the last 7F before hitting the ground has a crouch-sized hurtbox but is considered standing, allowing for unique combo setups); Incurs 20% damage scaling penalty if used as the first hit of a combo (applies to wall splat on HIT, crumple, Burnout dizzy on hit/block, or any character-specific means of comboing after a regular Drive Impact); Incurs a 20% multiplier damage scaling penalty after a Wall Splat on BLOCK - Because the blocked Drive Impact is not considered a "hit" for the combo, the next attack can incur its own separate damage scaling as a combo starter; Wall Splat puts opponent into a special juggle state where the next move freely connects and continues the juggle even if it normally wouldn't (similar to a Forced Knockdown or Drive Rush juggle properties); Does not cause Wall Splat if the Drive Impact connects as a combo or a true blockstring with no gaps (LOCK icon appears on-screen); It is possible to "combo" into Stun if the opponent has under 1.5 Drive bars - a blocked DI Wall Splat from slightly outside the corner into a second DI on hit will cause Burnout and Stun (because the blocked DI is not technically considered a combo starter); Costs 1 bar of Drive Gauge; Cinematic slowdown occurs if both players activate Drive Impact within range of each other (granting a Punish Counter to the player who activates it later); Attempting to counter with DI vs. DI with under 400 HP will result in a KO, as the second player will not have enough health to absorb it; Clashes with other Drive Impacts and refunds the Drive gauge cost if they collide on the same active frame (start at exactly the same time, or 1F apart if the first Drive Impact absorbs a strike) - The meter refund does not prevent Burnout from occurring; The scrub killer

marisa.name: Drive Reversal: Love Tap
marisa.notes: Has two versions: one performed during blockstun or parry stun (20F start-up) and one performed as a wake-up reversal (18F start-up); Fully invincible on frames 1-22 (blockstun) / frames 1-20 (reversal); Armor Break (blows through all armor like Drive Impact, but not counters like JP's Amnesia); Trying to Drive Reversal after the blockstun ends results in a Drive Impact; Drive Reversal immediately removes the current blockstun you're in and starts the attack; Causes a 4F screen freeze after the 6th start-up frame, which allows the opponent to perform a simple OS (inputting their buttons during the buffer window) to prevent their next attack from coming out; Safe on block (-2) when used against an opponent in Burnout; Costs 2 bars of Drive Gauge; If the opponent tries to throw against a wake-up Drive Reversal, it causes a 12F screen freeze and refunds 1 bar of Drive gauge (but does not prevent Burnout); Guaranteed to interrupt any Drive Rush canceled normal if performed immediately out of blockstun (unless the opponent reacts with an invincible move or counter); Inflicts 4F less hitstop (16F) on block compared to most characters which affects the timing of the opponent's punish

marisa.name: 斗气招架 (Drive Parry)
marisa.notes: Parries all strikes and projectiles (high and low) from frame 1; 12F parry window (can hold the parry to extend the parry window); Perfect Parry occurs on the first 2 active frames (cannot achieve Perfect Parry if you buffer into parry by holding it during Reversal windows; Perfect Parries have to be timed properly); Can still hold charge directions during Parry (allowing characters with charge specials to stand block before performing their reversal); Can block during the recovery frames of a regular parry (can still get hit during the recovery frames if you don't block correctly); Getting thrown or hit at any point during the recovery frames of a whiffed parry attempt results in a Punish Counter; Successfully parrying a move puts you into the same amount of blockstun as that move would regularly do on block (but a Perfect Parry has only 1F of recovery); Throw invincible during the recovery of a successful parry (just like during blockstun); Perfect Parrying a strike has only 1F of recovery and disables the opponent from canceling their attack (basically a guaranteed punish opportunity except for safe jump setups); Perfect Parrying a strike requires holding the correct block direction (Down+Back for low strikes, Back for high/mid strikes); Attempting a Perfect Parry with the wrong block direction results in an "imperfect parry" that builds an extra 3000 Drive Gauge and plays a distinct audio/visual cue; After a successful Perfect Parry, you suffer a 50% penalty to your Damage, Drive Gauge Generation, and Drive Gauge Damage on any of your following attacks when punishing the opponent (in addition, both you and the opponent suffer a 20% penalty to your Super Meter gain during this period); Fully invincible for 6F after a successful Perfect Parry against a strike, which carries over to any attack you perform (ensuring a 5F or faster punish will always interrupt multi-hit attacks); Perfect Parrying projectiles puts you into fixed 10 frames of recovery and applies the same 50% scaling penalties (and 20% Super Meter penalty) on your following attacks when punishing the opponent; Parrying a Strike and Projectile on the same frame will result in a regular parry for the strike attack (effectively ignoring the projectile's hitstop / blockstun); Perfect Parrying a Strike and Projectile on the same frame will give a screen freeze like you Perfect Parried a Strike, but still give you 10F recovery as if you had Perfect Parried a Projectile; Can cancel into Drive Rush during active frames 3 and onward (fastest Drive Rush method is to buffer a forward input before doing parry + forward again); Can cancel into Drive Reversal from a successful parry (just like you normally can during blockstun); Costs 1/2 bar of Drive Gauge and continues to deplete 50 Drive Gauge per frame (0.3 Drive bars per second) as you hold the Parry; You lose the parry if you go into Burnout from the initial Drive Gauge cost (Perfect Parry requires frame-perfect timing when starting from under 1/2 of a Drive bar); Rewards 1 bar of Drive Gauge (1/2 bar total after factoring in the initial parry cost) for successfully parrying a strike; Rewards 1/2 bar of Drive Gauge (0 bar total after factoring in the initial parry cost) for successfully parrying a projectile (with a few exceptions); Rewards 2 bars of Drive Gauge (1.5 bars total after factoring in the initial parry cost) for successful parrying a Super Art or Drive Impact; Successfully parrying a strike attack splits the regular block pushback between both players (while Perfect Parrying a strike removes all of its pushback); Successfully parrying a projectile or Drive Impact reduces the pushback of it by half (while Perfect Parrying a projectile or Drive Impact removes all of its pushback); Your hurtbox and throw box expand slightly towards the opponent for the entire duration of the Parry (Throw box extension starts instantly on frame 1, while the Hurtbox extension starts on frame 3, after the initial 2F Perfect Parry window); Parrying while crouching maintains a regular crouch hurtbox for the first 2 frames of the parry (during the initial Perfect Parry window)

marisa.name: 斗气冲刺 (Drive Rush)
marisa.notes: Dashes forward and enhances the next normal or command normal used out of the Drive Rush with +4 extra hitstun / blockstun, as well as improved juggle properties (Juggle Limit increased by +3 / Juggle Start/Increase reduced to 0); The +4 bonus frame advantage gained from a Drive Rush enhanced move also stacks with any bonus frame advantage that move may have gained from Counter-Hit, Punish Counter, or Burnout; Grounded special-cancelable normals can also be canceled into Drive Rush on hit or block, as well as from light normals on whiff; Drive Rush maintains buffers (freezes the buffer window) during its start-up and freeze frames - This allows players to do things normally not possible within the normal buffer windows, such as Drive Rushing into a charge special; The initial 10F screen freeze eats the opponent's directional inputs (except Jumps) but does not prevent attacks from being buffered immediately afterward (this can cause inputs to be combined in unintended ways, such as crouch MK + Fireball performing a raw Fireball, or a vertical jump + walk forward turning into a forward jump); Framedata shown in parentheses refers to the Drive Rush version used from a Parry; Drive Rush recovery is only 24F total (23F if done from a Parry) - but the enhanced dash itself is 46F total (45F if done from Parry) and you can cancel it as early as frame 9 (frame 11 if done from a Parry); Inputting a direction (walk/crouch/block/jump) after the Drive Rush recovery plays out 2 additional recovery frames before the transition occurs (this allows the user to perform an enhanced crouching or command normal late in the dash by inputting the direction + button simultaneously); You stop building any form of Drive Gauge on your attacks after using a Drive Rush in the MIDDLE of a combo (but you still continue to build Drive gauge as normal if you did Drive Rush at the START of a combo); Applies an extra damage scaling penalty after using a Drive Rush in the MIDDLE of a combo (no damage scaling if you use Drive Rush at the START of a combo); Costs 3 bars of Drive Gauge if canceled into from a normal attack; Costs 1/2 bar of Drive Gauge if canceled into from Parry (for a total of 1 bar of Drive Gauge when you factor in the initial 1/2 bar cost of the Parry); Normals used out of Drive Rush carry additional forward momentum (but throws and specials immediately halt all momentum, which can be a useful strategy to punish opponents for trying to interrupt your Drive Rush); Parry Drive Rush can only be initiated after frame 3 of the Parry (but can be performed immediately after recovering from a successful parry); Parry Drive Rush cannot be initiated with less than 1/2 of a Drive bar (as the initial Parry cost will put the user into Burnout) - But whiff canceling a Light normal into Drive Rush can achieve a similar effect; Cannot cancel Drive Rush into a Parry (inputting MP+MK results in a MK normal coming out instead); Drive Rush puts the user into a counter-hit state for the entire duration (this makes it impossible to tech a throw that connects during the dash)
