rashid.name: 站中脚 (5MK)
rashid.notes: Mostly a combo tool (links into stand MP); Decent poke that combos into itself on Counter-Hit; +2F extra recovery frames (19F) on whiff

rashid.name: 站重脚 (5HK)
rashid.notes: Combo / Juggle tool with surprisingly far range; Launches airborne opponents into a limited juggle state (launches grounded opponents as well on Punish Counter and pulls the opponent towards Rashid for easier follow-ups); Cannot hit cross-up (behind Rashid); Can be used as an oki / meaty tool, but has a lot of pushback on hit and block; Forces stand on hit; The brief extended leg hurtbox extension on frame 12 (1F before active) is strike invincible (cannot counter-poke projectiles); Last 2 active frames whiff on crouch

rashid.name: 蹲轻拳 (2LP)
rashid.notes: Chains into stand LP / crouch LP / crouch LK; Incurs 20% damage scaling penalty if used as the first hit of a combo; Topmost hurtboxes on frames 1-7 are vulnerable only to airborne attacks (this is to discourage its use as an anti-air)

rashid.name: 蹲中拳 (2MP)
rashid.notes: Rashid's main frametrap / oki / combo tool as well as being a decent anti-air on frames 7-9; Cannot hit cross-up (behind Rashid); Whiffs on crouching from further away

rashid.name: 蹲重拳 (2HP)
rashid.notes: Decent poke / punish tool that's cancelable into all Super Arts and combos into stand HP on Punish Counter (if close enough to the opponent); A lot of pushback on hit and block (only punishable on block if used point blank against long-reaching 4F lights); Incurs 20% hit damage scaling penalty if used as the first hit of a combo; +2F extra recovery frames (23F) on whiff; Topmost hurtboxes on frames 8-14 are projectile invincible (avoids Sagat's MP/HP Tiger Shot)

rashid.name: 蹲轻脚 (2LK)
rashid.notes: Chains into stand LP / crouch LP / crouch LK; Incurs 20% damage scaling penalty if used as the first hit of a combo

rashid.name: 蹲中脚 (2MK)
rashid.notes: Standard crouch MK with a bit short range; Incurs 20% damage scaling penalty if used as the first hit of a combo

rashid.name: 蹲重脚 (2HK)
rashid.notes: Has some Juggle potential naturally without Drive Rush; Has fixed framedata on block (always -11 on block even with meaty timing) with +4F extra recovery frames (28F)

rashid.name: 跳中拳 (j.MP)
rashid.notes: Puts airborne opponents into a limited juggle state; Cancelable into Arabian Skyhigh (QCB+K) during forward jump; Shifts the normal jumping hurtbox upward during start-up (helps with avoiding some attacks)

rashid.name: 跳重拳 (j.HP)
rashid.notes: First hit puts airborne opponents into a limited juggle state; Second hit spikes down airborne opponents; If the first hit is blocked, the second hit is no longer an Overhead

rashid.name: 跳轻脚 (j.LK)
rashid.notes: Furthest horizontal range of Rashid's jump attacks

rashid.name: 跳中脚 (j.MK)
rashid.notes: Cross-up; Shifts the normal jumping hurtbox upward during start-up (helps with avoiding some attacks)

rashid.name: Blitz Strike
rashid.notes: Rashid bounces forward off the opponent on hit and block giving him access to all his airborne moves again (except for another Blitz Strike / d+HP) on frames 12-23; Rashid is in a forced knockdown state after he bounces off the opponent on hit or block; Spikes down airborne opponents into an OTG state; Can only be performed during a forward jump or after Arabian Skyhigh (double jump special); Rashid may land immediately if this hits an airborne opponent just before Rashid lands (1F timing window making this a very difficult juggle to get consistently); Incurs a 15% damage scaling penalty if used as the first hit of a combo

rashid.name: Aerial Shot
rashid.notes: Good air-to-air tool; Puts airborne opponents into a limited juggle state; Shifts the normal jumping hurtbox upward during start-up (helps with avoiding some attacks)

rashid.name: Run
rashid.notes: Rashid starts running forward if he holds forward after inputting his forward dash; Cancelable into a Low/High follow-ups on frames 18-72 (first 18F being the regular forward dash); If Rashid does not input any follow-up between frames 18-72 then his Run comes to a stop with 18F recovery frames at the (90F total duration); Rashid can stop his Run at any point by releasing his forward input (5F recovery on the stop); Rashid can jump forward out of this Run without having to play out the 5F recovery on regular stop (neutral jumping or jumping backwards still requires Rashid to first stop for 5F); Rashid is in a Counter-Hit state during his entire Run, including the Stop recovery frames; Wind enhancement: Increased running speed

rashid.name: Backup
rashid.notes: Upper body Projectile invincible on frames 1-19; Crouching state for the entire duration; Rashid does a follow-up strike on HIT only, side switching with his opponent and becomes fully Projectile invincible for the rest of the move's duration; Usually creates a big distance between Rashid and the opponent, but if the opponent was already cornered before the side switch, then they're close enough for a follow-up combo; Carries over Counter-Hit / Punish Counter bonus frame advantage to both hits; Wind enhancement on frames 1-17: Increased range; Puts airborne opponents into a limited juggle state; Second hit is super cancelable on HIT only; Incurs 20% hit damage scaling penalty if used as the first hit of a combo

rashid.name: Tempest Moon
rashid.notes: Not an Overhead; Airborne on frames 6-21 (Forced Knockdown state); Carries over Counter-Hit / Punish Counter bonus frame advantage to both hits; Incurs 15% damage scaling penalty if used as the first hit of a combo; Can be enhanced by air currents (wind) on frames 1-3; Second hit is Super cancelable on hit or block

rashid.name: Tempest Moon (wind)
rashid.notes: Not an Overhead; Airborne on frames 21-36 (Forced Knockdown state); Puts the opponent into a limited juggle OTG state (regular +22 Knockdown if the first hit doesn't connect); Counts as 2 hits of damage scaling

rashid.name: Flapping Spin
rashid.notes: Only first his is fully cancelable; First hit puts airborne opponents into a limited juggle state (second hit air resets); Carries over Counter-Hit / Punish Counter bonus frame advantage to both hits; One of Rashid's main combo / juggle tools; Decent range and combos on Punish Counter makes this a decent whiff punish tool; Wind enhancement on frames 3-10: Full-screen range

rashid.name: Beak Assault
rashid.notes: Overhead with very far range; Not actually airborne; Can be spaced out to hit on later active frames for a combo conversion on hit; Wind enhancement on frames 4-25: Almost full-screen range

rashid.name: Crescent Kick
rashid.notes: Low crushes on frames 7-19 (but not actually airborne); Great tool against low attacks as it combos into crouch MK or stand/crouch MP on Punish Counter; Great option to use out of Drive Rush with huge range, plus frames, as well as low crushing low attack checks on the way; +3F extra recovery frames (23F) on whiff; Incurs 20% hit damage scaling penalty if used as the first hit of a combo; Can be spaced out to hit on later active frames (up to +6 oH / +0 oB); Wind Enhancement on frames 6-19: Full-screen range

rashid.name: Rising Kick
rashid.notes: Launches the opponent into a limited juggle state on hit; Fully cancelable on hit and block; Counts as 2 hits of damage scaling

rashid.name: Side Flip
rashid.notes: Rashid flips forward with no collision boxes on frames 8-23 allowing him to flip through opponents; Rashid can follow-up the flip with 3 different jump trajectories on frames 19-25; Wind enhancement on frames 2-20: Almost full-screen range flip

rashid.name: Front Flip
rashid.notes: Trajectory of the jump depends on which direction is held while inputting KK; Back: Short jump trajectory; Neutral: Far jump trajectory (bit further than regular forward jump); Forward: Extra far jump trajectory (goes past the opponent mid-screen); Can use any air attack on frames 22-40; 8F landing recovery frames if no air attack in input; Wind enhancement on frames 1-36: All flips go full-screen forward

rashid.name: Wall Jump
rashid.notes: Forced Knockdown and Counter-Hit state for the entire duration of the jump; Can be performed after any jump direction as long as the wall is in range; Cannot be peformed after Blitz Strike (d+HP in air) or Arabian Skyhigh (QCB+K in air)

rashid.name: Riding Glider
rashid.notes: Throw Loop: hold Run briefly, then stop for a manually timed strike/throw mixup (does not work on mid-screen back rolls); Throw Loop has a 3F timing window (4F on Blanka / E. Honda / Zangief); Punish Counter gives +70% (2040) damage, Hard Knockdown (denies back-roll option on wake-up), depletes 1 bar of Drive gauge from the opponent, and builds twice as much Super gauge for the attacker; Throw Escape builds 0.5 Drive bars for the defender (randomly assigned if throws are input simultaneously)

rashid.name: Sunset Drop
rashid.notes: Throw Oki: Can Drive Rush into a meaty strike; Punish Counter gives +70% (2040) damage, Hard Knockdown (denies back-roll option on wake-up), depletes 1 bar of Drive gauge from the opponent, and builds twice as much Super gauge for the attacker; Throw Escape builds 0.5 Drive bars for the defender (randomly assigned if throws are input simultaneously)

rashid.name: Desert Slider
rashid.notes: Throw Oki (corner only): Drive Rush oki; Punish Counter gives +70% (2040) damage, Hard Knockdown (denies back-roll option on wake-up), depletes 1 bar of Drive gauge from the opponent, and builds twice as much Super gauge for both players

rashid.name: Drive Impact: Eagle Edge
rashid.notes: 2 hits of armor on frames 1-27; Damages opponents Drive Gauge on Block (1/2 bar) | Hit (1 bar) | Counter-Hit (1.25 bar) | Punish Counter (1.5 bar); Knocks down on hit; Pushes the opponent far back on hit or block and causes a Wall Splat if they hit the wall (Parry prevents the backwards stumble and Wall Splat, greatly reducing the pushback); Regular KDA without Wall Splat +35 KD | Wall Splat on Hit +65 KD | Wall Splat on Block +72 HKD; KDA can vary greatly depending on how high the opponent wall splats (higher KDA the higher they wall splat); Advantage after Wall Splat can vary depending on distance from the corner (farther from corner gives higher advantage); Crumples the opponent on Punish Counter or after absorbing at least 1 attack during start-up (+21 frames before the crumple state goes airborne, followed by airborne state on frames 22-46 before they are grounded); Puts airborne opponents into a long spinning free juggle state when hit as a Punish Counter or after absorbing an attack; If the armor absorbs an attack it slows the overall start-up by 1F (27F total instead of 26F) and incurs 6F hitstop for each projectile hit absorbed (making it less likely to punish the opponent after absorbing projectiles); Absorbing an attack causes the player to take 1/2 the damage in recoverable health (but will KO if this would bring the player's health below zero); Stun/Dizzy occurs when a Wall Splat connects on an opponent in Burnout; Stun gives a free combo follow-up for the next 195F after hitting the wall, followed by a HKD if the player falls to the ground untouched (the last 7F before hitting the ground has a crouch-sized hurtbox but is considered standing, allowing for unique combo setups); Incurs 20% damage scaling penalty if used as the first hit of a combo (applies to wall splat on HIT, crumple, Burnout dizzy on hit/block, or any character-specific means of comboing after a regular Drive Impact); Incurs a 20% multiplier damage scaling penalty after a Wall Splat on BLOCK - Because the blocked Drive Impact is not considered a "hit" for the combo, the next attack can incur its own separate damage scaling as a combo starter; Wall Splat puts opponent into a special juggle state where the next move freely connects and continues the juggle even if it normally wouldn't (similar to a Forced Knockdown or Drive Rush juggle properties); Does not cause Wall Splat if the Drive Impact connects as a combo or a true blockstring with no gaps (LOCK icon appears on-screen); It is possible to "combo" into Stun if the opponent has under 1.5 Drive bars - a blocked DI Wall Splat from slightly outside the corner into a second DI on hit will cause Burnout and Stun (because the blocked DI is not technically considered a combo starter); Costs 1 bar of Drive Gauge; Cinematic slowdown occurs if both players activate Drive Impact within range of each other (granting a Punish Counter to the player who activates it later); Attempting to counter with DI vs. DI with under 400 HP will result in a KO, as the second player will not have enough health to absorb it; Clashes with other Drive Impacts and refunds the Drive gauge cost if they collide on the same active frame (start at exactly the same time, or 1F apart if the first Drive Impact absorbs a strike) - The meter refund does not prevent Burnout from occurring; The scrub killer

rashid.name: Drive Reversal: Eagle Slash
rashid.notes: Has two versions: one performed during blockstun or parry stun (20F start-up) and one performed as a wake-up reversal (18F start-up); Fully invincible on frames 1-22 (blockstun) / frames 1-20 (reversal); Armor Break (blows through all armor like Drive Impact, but not counters like JP's Amnesia); Trying to Drive Reversal after the blockstun ends results in a Drive Impact; Drive Reversal immediately removes the current blockstun you're in and starts the attack; Causes a 4F screen freeze after the 6th start-up frame, which allows the opponent to perform a simple OS (inputting their buttons during the buffer window) to prevent their next attack from coming out; Safe on block (-2) when used against an opponent in Burnout; Costs 2 bars of Drive Gauge; If the opponent tries to throw against a wake-up Drive Reversal, it causes a 12F screen freeze and refunds 1 bar of Drive gauge (but does not prevent Burnout); Guaranteed to interrupt any Drive Rush canceled normal if performed immediately out of blockstun (unless the opponent reacts with an invincible move or counter)

rashid.name: 斗气招架 (Drive Parry)
rashid.notes: Parries all strikes and projectiles (high and low) from frame 1; 12F parry window (can hold the parry to extend the parry window); Perfect Parry occurs on the first 2 active frames (cannot achieve Perfect Parry if you buffer into parry by holding it during Reversal windows; Perfect Parries have to be timed properly); Can still hold charge directions during Parry (allowing characters with charge specials to stand block before performing their reversal); Can block during the recovery frames of a regular parry (can still get hit during the recovery frames if you don't block correctly); Getting thrown or hit at any point during the recovery frames of a whiffed parry attempt results in a Punish Counter; Successfully parrying a move puts you into the same amount of blockstun as that move would regularly do on block (but a Perfect Parry has only 1F of recovery); Throw invincible during the recovery of a successful parry (just like during blockstun); Perfect Parrying a strike has only 1F of recovery and disables the opponent from canceling their attack (basically a guaranteed punish opportunity except for safe jump setups); Perfect Parrying a strike requires holding the correct block direction (Down+Back for low strikes, Back for high/mid strikes); Attempting a Perfect Parry with the wrong block direction results in an "imperfect parry" that builds an extra 3000 Drive Gauge and plays a distinct audio/visual cue; After a successful Perfect Parry, you suffer a 50% penalty to your Damage, Drive Gauge Generation, and Drive Gauge Damage on any of your following attacks when punishing the opponent (in addition, both you and the opponent suffer a 20% penalty to your Super Meter gain during this period); Fully invincible for 6F after a successful Perfect Parry against a strike, which carries over to any attack you perform (ensuring a 5F or faster punish will always interrupt multi-hit attacks); Perfect Parrying projectiles puts you into fixed 10 frames of recovery and applies the same 50% scaling penalties (and 20% Super Meter penalty) on your following attacks when punishing the opponent; Parrying a Strike and Projectile on the same frame will result in a regular parry for the strike attack (effectively ignoring the projectile's hitstop / blockstun); Perfect Parrying a Strike and Projectile on the same frame will give a screen freeze like you Perfect Parried a Strike, but still give you 10F recovery as if you had Perfect Parried a Projectile; Can cancel into Drive Rush during active frames 3 and onward (fastest Drive Rush method is to buffer a forward input before doing parry + forward again); Can cancel into Drive Reversal from a successful parry (just like you normally can during blockstun); Costs 1/2 bar of Drive Gauge and continues to deplete 50 Drive Gauge per frame (0.3 Drive bars per second) as you hold the Parry; You lose the parry if you go into Burnout from the initial Drive Gauge cost (Perfect Parry requires frame-perfect timing when starting from under 1/2 of a Drive bar); Rewards 1 bar of Drive Gauge (1/2 bar total after factoring in the initial parry cost) for successfully parrying a strike; Rewards 1/2 bar of Drive Gauge (0 bar total after factoring in the initial parry cost) for successfully parrying a projectile (with a few exceptions); Rewards 2 bars of Drive Gauge (1.5 bars total after factoring in the initial parry cost) for successful parrying a Super Art or Drive Impact; Successfully parrying a strike attack splits the regular block pushback between both players (while Perfect Parrying a strike removes all of its pushback); Successfully parrying a projectile or Drive Impact reduces the pushback of it by half (while Perfect Parrying a projectile or Drive Impact removes all of its pushback); Your hurtbox and throw box expand slightly towards the opponent for the entire duration of the Parry (Throw box extension starts instantly on frame 1, while the Hurtbox extension starts on frame 3, after the initial 2F Perfect Parry window); Parrying while crouching maintains a regular crouch hurtbox for the first 2 frames of the parry (during the initial Perfect Parry window)

rashid.name: 斗气冲刺 (Drive Rush)
rashid.notes: Dashes forward and enhances the next normal or command normal used out of the Drive Rush with +4 extra hitstun / blockstun, as well as improved juggle properties (Juggle Limit increased by +3 / Juggle Start/Increase reduced to 0); The +4 bonus frame advantage gained from a Drive Rush enhanced move also stacks with any bonus frame advantage that move may have gained from Counter-Hit, Punish Counter, or Burnout; Grounded special-cancelable normals can also be canceled into Drive Rush on hit or block, as well as from light normals on whiff; Drive Rush maintains buffers (freezes the buffer window) during its start-up and freeze frames - This allows players to do things normally not possible within the normal buffer windows, such as Drive Rushing into a charge special; The initial 10F screen freeze eats the opponent's directional inputs (except Jumps) but does not prevent attacks from being buffered immediately afterward (this can cause inputs to be combined in unintended ways, such as crouch MK + Fireball performing a raw Fireball, or a vertical jump + walk forward turning into a forward jump); Framedata shown in parentheses refers to the Drive Rush version used from a Parry; Drive Rush recovery is only 24F total (23F if done from a Parry) - but the enhanced dash itself is 46F total (45F if done from Parry) and you can cancel it as early as frame 9 (frame 11 if done from a Parry); Inputting a direction (walk/crouch/block/jump) after the Drive Rush recovery plays out 2 additional recovery frames before the transition occurs (this allows the user to perform an enhanced crouching or command normal late in the dash by inputting the direction + button simultaneously); You stop building any form of Drive Gauge on your attacks after using a Drive Rush in the MIDDLE of a combo (but you still continue to build Drive gauge as normal if you did Drive Rush at the START of a combo); Applies an extra damage scaling penalty after using a Drive Rush in the MIDDLE of a combo (no damage scaling if you use Drive Rush at the START of a combo); Costs 3 bars of Drive Gauge if canceled into from a normal attack; Costs 1/2 bar of Drive Gauge if canceled into from Parry (for a total of 1 bar of Drive Gauge when you factor in the initial 1/2 bar cost of the Parry); Normals used out of Drive Rush carry additional forward momentum (but throws and specials immediately halt all momentum, which can be a useful strategy to punish opponents for trying to interrupt your Drive Rush); Parry Drive Rush can only be initiated after frame 3 of the Parry (but can be performed immediately after recovering from a successful parry); Parry Drive Rush cannot be initiated with less than 1/2 of a Drive bar (as the initial Parry cost will put the user into Burnout) - But whiff canceling a Light normal into Drive Rush can achieve a similar effect; Cannot cancel Drive Rush into a Parry (inputting MP+MK results in a MK normal coming out instead); Drive Rush puts the user into a counter-hit state for the entire duration (this makes it impossible to tech a throw that connects during the dash)

rashid.name: Whirlwind Shot
rashid.notes: 1-hit projectile; Can hold the kick button to charge up the projectile; Trajectory and speed of the projectile depends on button strength used; LK version: Furthest horizontal range (Projectile speed: 0.03 on frames 1-2 accelerating up to 0.1 on frames 3 and onward); MK version: Mid-range (Projectile speed: 0.03 on frames 1-2 accelerating up to 0.07 on frames 3 and onward); HK version: Short horizontal range, mostly used for vertical purposes (Projectile speed: 0.03 on frames 1-3 accelerating up to 0.04 on frames 4 and onward); Comes out in 6 frames if the kick button is released between frames 11-27; Cannot be performed while Super Art 2 (Ysaar) is active on screen

rashid.name: Whirlwind Shot (lvl 2)
rashid.notes: 2-hit projectile; Carries over Counter-Hit / Punish Counter bonus frame advantage to both hits; Trajectory of the projectile depends on button strength used; LK version: Furthest horizontal range (Projectile speed: 0.03 on frames 1-2 accelerating up to 0.1 on frames 3 and onward); MK version: Mid-range (Projectile speed: 0.03 on frames 1-2 accelerating up to 0.07 on frames 3 and onward); HK version: Short horizontal range, mostly used for vertical purposes (Projectile speed: 0.03 on frames 1-3 accelerating up to 0.04 on frames 4 and onward); Need to hold the kick button for at least 28 frames for this half-way charged version of the move; Minimum start-up is 34F if the kick button is released at exactly frame 28 of start-up (up to 53F start-up if you delay the kick release to frame 47); Comes out in 6 frames if the kick button is released between frames 28-47; Cannot be performed while Super Art 2 (Ysaar) is active on screen

rashid.name: Whirlwind Shot (lvl 3)
rashid.notes: 3-hit projectile; Carries over Counter-Hit / Punish Counter bonus frame advantage to all hits; Trajectory of the projectile depends on button strength used; LK version: Furthest horizontal range (Projectile speed: 0.03 on frames 1-2 accelerating up to 0.1 on frames 3 and onward); MK version: Mid-range (Projectile speed: 0.03 on frames 1-2 accelerating up to 0.07 on frames 3 and onward); HK version: Short horizontal range, mostly used for vertical purposes (Projectile speed: 0.03 on frames 1-3 accelerating up to 0.04 on frames 4 and onward); Need to hold the kick button for at least 48 frames for this fully charged version of the move; Summons a non-hitting Tornado on frame 51 next to Rashid that lasts for 60 frames and enhances any of Rashid's movement / command normals / specials used within the wind area; Cannot be performed while Super Art 2 (Ysaar) is active on screen

rashid.name: Wing Stroke
rashid.notes: Airborne on frames 22-61 (Forced Knockdown state); Cancelable into air normals / specials on frames 32-51; 6F landing recovery frames on whiff; Can be enhanced by air currents (wind) on frames 32-47; Can also be used after a fully charged OD Whirlwind Shot

rashid.name: Super Rashid Kick
rashid.notes: Strike and Throw invincible on frames 1-15; Airborne on frames 9-35; Armor Break; Depletes 0.5 Drive Bar on hit for the opponent; Great combo / juggle / anti-air tool; Deals 300 less damage (1800) if it doesn't hit on the first active frame; Variable KD Advantage (+7~14) against airborne opponents; Rashid switches sides with the opponent on a grounded hit (cinematic version)

rashid.name: Ysaar
rashid.notes: No form of invincibility whatsoever; 5-hit Super projectile; Projectile speed: 0.01 which starts moving forward on frame 7 (accelerates up to 0.115 speed if Rashid kicks the tornado with Arabian Cyclone (QCB+K)); Armor Break; Depletes 1 Drive Bar on hit for the opponent; Prevents any super meter build while active; Travels full-screen by itself; The wind enhances all of Rashid's movement / command normals / specials just by touching the tornado; Rashid can kick the tornado forward at great speed (0.115 projectile speed) by hitting it with his Arabian Cyclone special (QCB+P); The air current from the tornado dissipates 120F (2 seconds) after all the hits are depleted or after the active frames run out; Cannot perform any form of Whirlwind Shots (QCF+K) while this Super Art is active; Incurs 20% damage scaling penalty if used in the middle of a combo; Rashid can't generate any Super meter until the active frames of the whirlwind are over

rashid.name: Altair

rashid.name: Arabian Skyhigh
rashid.notes: Lower leg is projectile invincible on frames 1-26; 3F landing recovery; First active frame can only hit juggled opponets; Only possible to perform during a forward jump or front flip (Side Flip > Front Flip); Has a minimum height limit (cannot cancel into this from Blitz Strike (d+HP in air) if it connects too low to the ground); Rashid performs a flip kick attack in the air before leaping forward into another jump arc; This MK version of the Double Jump has a similar jump arc to Rashid's regular forward jump; KDA (Knockdown advantage) varies greatly; Launches opponent into a limited juggle state on hit; Wind enhancement on frames 1-18: Shifts Rashid forward in the air before he performs the double jump

ryu.name: 站轻拳 (5LP)
ryu.notes: Chains into stand LP / crouch LP / crouch LK; Incurs 20% damage scaling penalty if used as the first hit of a combo

ryu.name: 站中拳 (5MP)
ryu.notes: Combo / oki frametrap tool; +2F extra recovery frames (13F) on whiff

ryu.name: 站重拳 (5HP)
ryu.notes: Fantastic combo / poke tool that's hit confirmable with a lot of active frames; Forces stand (vital for the HP > HK target combo follow-up); Shoto stand HP privilege

ryu.name: 站轻脚 (5LK)
ryu.notes: Good range for a light normal; Incurs 20% damage scaling penalty if used as the first hit of a combo

ryu.name: 站中脚 (5MK)
ryu.notes: Good poke tool with good hitbox priority (disjoint); Ryu lifts up his front leg hurtbox on frames 4-11 making this a good tool against low attacks

ryu.name: 站重脚 (5HK)
ryu.notes: Whiffs on most crouching moves (can still hit some like crouch HP); Good horizontal anti-air; Puts airborne opponents into a juggle state; Crumples on Punish Counter (+11 frames before the crumple state goes airborne); The brief extended leg hurtbox on frame 11 of start-up (1F before active) is strike invincible (cannot counter-poke projectiles)

ryu.name: 蹲轻拳 (2LP)
ryu.notes: Chains into stand LP / crouch LP / crouch LK; Incurs 20% damage scaling penalty if used as the first hit of a combo; Topmost hurtboxes on frames 1-5 are vulnerable only to airborne attacks (this is to discourage its use as an anti-air)

ryu.name: 蹲中拳 (2MP)
ryu.notes: Great combo / poke / buffer / pressure tool; 4 active frames and solid frame advantage makes this an ideal oki tool as well; +2F extra recovery frames (15F) on whiff; Topmost hurtboxes on frames 1-9 are vulnerable only to airborne attacks (this is to discourage its use as an anti-air)

ryu.name: 蹲重拳 (2HP)
ryu.notes: Extended fist hurtbox is invincible to airborne strikes on frame 9; Head hurtbox is invincible to airborne strikes on frames 10-14; Forces stand on hit; Solid anti-air; Cannot hit cross-up (behind Ryu); Only cancelable on the first active frame; Deals 5F less hitstun after the first active frame resulting in worse frame advantage on hit beyond the first active frame (can't get any meaty combos on oki)

ryu.name: 蹲轻脚 (2LK)
ryu.notes: Chains into stand LP / crouch LP / crouch LK; Incurs 20% damage scaling penalty if used as the first hit of a combo

ryu.name: 蹲中脚 (2MK)
ryu.notes: Standard shoto crouch MK; If blocked, Ryu can safely cancel into Hadoken while recovering in time to counter Drive Impact; Incurs a 20% damage scaling penalty if used as the first hit of a combo; Footsies!

ryu.name: 蹲重脚 (2HK)
ryu.notes: Has very good range and hitbox priority; Has some Juggle potential naturally without Drive Rush; Has fixed framedata on block (always -12 on block even with meaty timing) with +6F extra recovery frames (29F)

ryu.name: 跳轻拳 (j.LP)
ryu.notes: Can be used as a fuzzy instant Overhead after a deep jump-in Medium / Heavy

ryu.name: 跳中拳 (j.MP)
ryu.notes: Both hits put airborne opponents into a limited juggle state; Both hits are cancelable into Air Tatsus; Great air-to-air hitbox priority; Shifts the normal jumping hurtbox upward during start-up (helps with avoiding some attacks)

ryu.name: 跳重拳 (j.HP)
ryu.notes: Spikes down airborne opponents on Counter-Hit or Punish Counter

ryu.name: 跳轻脚 (j.LK)
ryu.notes: Cross-up

ryu.name: 跳中脚 (j.MK)
ryu.notes: Cross-up; Shifts the normal jumping hurtbox upward during start-up (helps with avoiding some attacks)

ryu.name: 跳重脚 (j.HK)
ryu.notes: Pretty standard jump-in attack

ryu.name: Collarbone Breaker
ryu.notes: Great overhead with good start-up and frame advantage on hit, decent range, as well as hitting two times to blow through some armored moves; Can hit meaty on last active frame for +5/-1 frame advantage; Carries over Counter-Hit / Punish Counter bonus frame advantage to both hits; Second hit is not an Overhead if the first hit connects

ryu.name: Short Uppercut
ryu.notes: Very short range combo tool; Forces stand on hit; Only cancelable on the first active frame; OK anti-air option; Deals 8F less hitstun after the first active frame (don't try to use this as a meaty tool on oki, it's actually punishable on HIT then); Last 2 active frames whiff on crouching opponents

ryu.name: Solar Plexus Strike
ryu.notes: Forward moving and + on Hit and Block makes this a very good combo / pressure tool; Second hit can whiff when whiff punishing, resulting in +8 on Punish; Carries over Counter-Hit / Punish Counter bonus frame advantage to both hits; First hit puts airborne opponents into a free juggle state (to prevent the second hit from whiffing, so that Ryu doesn't get punishes on airborne juggles); Leaves opponent in throw range on block at close range (opponent can walk back to avoid throw, but is in range for crouch LK > stand LP punish)

ryu.name: Axe Kick
ryu.notes: First hit forces stand on hit; First hit puts airborne opponents into a limited juggle state; Second hit puts airborne opponents into a limited OTG juggle state (usually +14 KD); Carries over Counter-Hit / Punish Counter bonus frame advantage to both hits

ryu.name: Whirlwind Kick
ryu.notes: Low crushes on frames 13-20; Cancelable into regular/OD Air Tatsu on Hit or Block; Puts airborne opponents into a limited juggle state on hit; Very useful for juggling after midscreen OD High Blade Kick (the cancel into Air Tatsu gives Ryu solid damage, corner carry, and oki); Extends a proximity guard box on frame 2 that reaches the attack's maximum range (prevents opponents from walking back out of its startup)

ryu.name: Fuwa Triple Strike 2
ryu.notes: Last hit (HK) can be canceled into Denjin Charge (down+Punch on Classic / down+attack on Modern) on HIT only for a +7 Knockdown (can even maintain pressure in corner); Hits consistently even at max range of MP where his other combo routes drop

ryu.name: High Double Strike
ryu.notes: Second hit (HK) can be canceled into Denjin Charge (down+Punch on Classic / down+attack on Modern) on HIT only for a +10 Knockdown (can even maintain pressure in corner); Second hit (HK) whiffs on crouching (-18 on block on crouching when it whiffs); Puts the opponent into a limited juggle state on hit (but the second hit maintains current juggle state, so Drive Rush HP>HK can result in free juggle state after Crumples or Wall splats); Can juggle into MP / OD Shoryuken or SA3 in the corner if not canceled into Denjin Charge

ryu.name: 前普通投
ryu.notes: Throw Loop: Manually time throw again or use LP to framekill into meaty throw (not possible on mid-screen back-roll); Punish Counter gives +70% (2040) damage, Hard Knockdown (denies back-roll option on wake-up), depletes 1 bar of Drive gauge from the opponent, and builds twice as much Super gauge for the attacker; Throw Escape builds 0.5 Drive bars for the defender (randomly assigned if throws are input simultaneously)

ryu.name: 后普通投
ryu.notes: Back Throw oki: Nope (+11 at mid-range - OD Fireball does cover most options); Punish Counter gives +70% (2040) damage, Hard Knockdown (denies back-roll option on wake-up), depletes 1 bar of Drive gauge from the opponent, and builds twice as much Super gauge for the attacker; Throw Escape builds 0.5 Drive bars for the defender (randomly assigned if throws are input simultaneously)

ryu.name: Drive Impact: Shingeki
ryu.notes: 2 hits of armor on frames 1-27; Damages opponents Drive Gauge on Block (1/2 bar) | Hit (1 bar) | Counter-Hit (1.25 bar) | Punish Counter (1.5 bar); Knocks down on hit; Pushes the opponent far back on hit or block and causes a Wall Splat if they hit the wall (Parry prevents the backwards stumble and Wall Splat, greatly reducing the pushback); Regular KDA without Wall Splat +35 KD | Wall Splat on Hit +65 KD | Wall Splat on Block +72 HKD; KDA can vary greatly depending on how high the opponent wall splats (higher KDA the higher they wall splat); Advantage after Wall Splat can vary depending on distance from the corner (farther from corner gives higher advantage); Crumples the opponent on Punish Counter or after absorbing at least 1 attack during start-up (+21 frames before the crumple state goes airborne, followed by airborne state on frames 22-46 before they are grounded); Puts airborne opponents into a long spinning free juggle state when hit as a Punish Counter or after absorbing an attack; If the armor absorbs an attack it slows the overall start-up by 1F (27F total instead of 26F) and incurs 6F hitstop for each projectile hit absorbed (making it less likely to punish the opponent after absorbing projectiles); Absorbing an attack causes the player to take 1/2 the damage in recoverable health (but will KO if this would bring the player's health below zero); Stun/Dizzy occurs when a Wall Splat connects on an opponent in Burnout; Stun gives a free combo follow-up for the next 195F after hitting the wall, followed by a HKD if the player falls to the ground untouched (the last 7F before hitting the ground has a crouch-sized hurtbox but is considered standing, allowing for unique combo setups); Incurs 20% damage scaling penalty if used as the first hit of a combo (applies to wall splat on HIT, crumple, Burnout dizzy on hit/block, or any character-specific means of comboing after a regular Drive Impact); Incurs a 20% multiplier damage scaling penalty after a Wall Splat on BLOCK - Because the blocked Drive Impact is not considered a "hit" for the combo, the next attack can incur its own separate damage scaling as a combo starter; Wall Splat puts opponent into a special juggle state where the next move freely connects and continues the juggle even if it normally wouldn't (similar to a Forced Knockdown or Drive Rush juggle properties); Does not cause Wall Splat if the Drive Impact connects as a combo or a true blockstring with no gaps (LOCK icon appears on-screen); It is possible to "combo" into Stun if the opponent has under 1.5 Drive bars - a blocked DI Wall Splat from slightly outside the corner into a second DI on hit will cause Burnout and Stun (because the blocked DI is not technically considered a combo starter); Costs 1 bar of Drive Gauge; Cinematic slowdown occurs if both players activate Drive Impact within range of each other (granting a Punish Counter to the player who activates it later); Attempting to counter with DI vs. DI with under 400 HP will result in a KO, as the second player will not have enough health to absorb it; Clashes with other Drive Impacts and refunds the Drive gauge cost if they collide on the same active frame (start at exactly the same time, or 1F apart if the first Drive Impact absorbs a strike) - The meter refund does not prevent Burnout from occurring; The scrub killer

ryu.name: Drive Reversal: Chest Strike
ryu.notes: Has two versions: one performed during blockstun or parry stun (20F start-up) and one performed as a wake-up reversal (18F start-up); Fully invincible on frames 1-22 (blockstun) / frames 1-20 (reversal); Armor Break (blows through all armor like Drive Impact, but not counters like JP's Amnesia); Trying to Drive Reversal after the blockstun ends results in a Drive Impact; Drive Reversal immediately removes the current blockstun you're in and starts the attack; Causes a 4F screen freeze after the 6th start-up frame, which allows the opponent to perform a simple OS (inputting their buttons during the buffer window) to prevent their next attack from coming out; Safe on block (-2) when used against an opponent in Burnout; Costs 2 bars of Drive Gauge; If the opponent tries to throw against a wake-up Drive Reversal, it causes a 12F screen freeze and refunds 1 bar of Drive gauge (but does not prevent Burnout); Guaranteed to interrupt any Drive Rush canceled normal if performed immediately out of blockstun (unless the opponent reacts with an invincible move or counter)

ryu.name: 斗气招架 (Drive Parry)
ryu.notes: Parries all strikes and projectiles (high and low) from frame 1; 12F parry window (can hold the parry to extend the parry window); Perfect Parry occurs on the first 2 active frames (cannot achieve Perfect Parry if you buffer into parry by holding it during Reversal windows; Perfect Parries have to be timed properly); Can still hold charge directions during Parry (allowing characters with charge specials to stand block before performing their reversal); Can block during the recovery frames of a regular parry (can still get hit during the recovery frames if you don't block correctly); Getting thrown or hit at any point during the recovery frames of a whiffed parry attempt results in a Punish Counter; Successfully parrying a move puts you into the same amount of blockstun as that move would regularly do on block (but a Perfect Parry has only 1F of recovery); Throw invincible during the recovery of a successful parry (just like during blockstun); Perfect Parrying a strike has only 1F of recovery and disables the opponent from canceling their attack (basically a guaranteed punish opportunity except for safe jump setups); Perfect Parrying a strike requires holding the correct block direction (Down+Back for low strikes, Back for high/mid strikes); Attempting a Perfect Parry with the wrong block direction results in an "imperfect parry" that builds an extra 3000 Drive Gauge and plays a distinct audio/visual cue; After a successful Perfect Parry, you suffer a 50% penalty to your Damage, Drive Gauge Generation, and Drive Gauge Damage on any of your following attacks when punishing the opponent (in addition, both you and the opponent suffer a 20% penalty to your Super Meter gain during this period); Fully invincible for 6F after a successful Perfect Parry against a strike, which carries over to any attack you perform (ensuring a 5F or faster punish will always interrupt multi-hit attacks); Perfect Parrying projectiles puts you into fixed 10 frames of recovery and applies the same 50% scaling penalties (and 20% Super Meter penalty) on your following attacks when punishing the opponent; Parrying a Strike and Projectile on the same frame will result in a regular parry for the strike attack (effectively ignoring the projectile's hitstop / blockstun); Perfect Parrying a Strike and Projectile on the same frame will give a screen freeze like you Perfect Parried a Strike, but still give you 10F recovery as if you had Perfect Parried a Projectile; Can cancel into Drive Rush during active frames 3 and onward (fastest Drive Rush method is to buffer a forward input before doing parry + forward again); Can cancel into Drive Reversal from a successful parry (just like you normally can during blockstun); Costs 1/2 bar of Drive Gauge and continues to deplete 50 Drive Gauge per frame (0.3 Drive bars per second) as you hold the Parry; You lose the parry if you go into Burnout from the initial Drive Gauge cost (Perfect Parry requires frame-perfect timing when starting from under 1/2 of a Drive bar); Rewards 1 bar of Drive Gauge (1/2 bar total after factoring in the initial parry cost) for successfully parrying a strike; Rewards 1/2 bar of Drive Gauge (0 bar total after factoring in the initial parry cost) for successfully parrying a projectile (with a few exceptions); Rewards 2 bars of Drive Gauge (1.5 bars total after factoring in the initial parry cost) for successful parrying a Super Art or Drive Impact; Successfully parrying a strike attack splits the regular block pushback between both players (while Perfect Parrying a strike removes all of its pushback); Successfully parrying a projectile or Drive Impact reduces the pushback of it by half (while Perfect Parrying a projectile or Drive Impact removes all of its pushback); Your hurtbox and throw box expand slightly towards the opponent for the entire duration of the Parry (Throw box extension starts instantly on frame 1, while the Hurtbox extension starts on frame 3, after the initial 2F Perfect Parry window); Parrying while crouching maintains a regular crouch hurtbox for the first 2 frames of the parry (during the initial Perfect Parry window)

ryu.name: 斗气冲刺 (Drive Rush)
ryu.notes: Dashes forward and enhances the next normal or command normal used out of the Drive Rush with +4 extra hitstun / blockstun, as well as improved juggle properties (Juggle Limit increased by +3 / Juggle Start/Increase reduced to 0); The +4 bonus frame advantage gained from a Drive Rush enhanced move also stacks with any bonus frame advantage that move may have gained from Counter-Hit, Punish Counter, or Burnout; Grounded special-cancelable normals can also be canceled into Drive Rush on hit or block, as well as from light normals on whiff; Drive Rush maintains buffers (freezes the buffer window) during its start-up and freeze frames - This allows players to do things normally not possible within the normal buffer windows, such as Drive Rushing into a charge special; The initial 10F screen freeze eats the opponent's directional inputs (except Jumps) but does not prevent attacks from being buffered immediately afterward (this can cause inputs to be combined in unintended ways, such as crouch MK + Fireball performing a raw Fireball, or a vertical jump + walk forward turning into a forward jump); Framedata shown in parentheses refers to the Drive Rush version used from a Parry; Drive Rush recovery is only 24F total (23F if done from a Parry) - but the enhanced dash itself is 46F total (45F if done from Parry) and you can cancel it as early as frame 9 (frame 11 if done from a Parry); Inputting a direction (walk/crouch/block/jump) after the Drive Rush recovery plays out 2 additional recovery frames before the transition occurs (this allows the user to perform an enhanced crouching or command normal late in the dash by inputting the direction + button simultaneously); You stop building any form of Drive Gauge on your attacks after using a Drive Rush in the MIDDLE of a combo (but you still continue to build Drive gauge as normal if you did Drive Rush at the START of a combo); Applies an extra damage scaling penalty after using a Drive Rush in the MIDDLE of a combo (no damage scaling if you use Drive Rush at the START of a combo); Costs 3 bars of Drive Gauge if canceled into from a normal attack; Costs 1/2 bar of Drive Gauge if canceled into from Parry (for a total of 1 bar of Drive Gauge when you factor in the initial 1/2 bar cost of the Parry); Normals used out of Drive Rush carry additional forward momentum (but throws and specials immediately halt all momentum, which can be a useful strategy to punish opponents for trying to interrupt your Drive Rush); Parry Drive Rush can only be initiated after frame 3 of the Parry (but can be performed immediately after recovering from a successful parry); Parry Drive Rush cannot be initiated with less than 1/2 of a Drive bar (as the initial Parry cost will put the user into Burnout) - But whiff canceling a Light normal into Drive Rush can achieve a similar effect; Cannot cancel Drive Rush into a Parry (inputting MP+MK results in a MK normal coming out instead); Drive Rush puts the user into a counter-hit state for the entire duration (this makes it impossible to tech a throw that connects during the dash)

ryu.name: 电刃炼气
ryu.notes: Gives access to a more powerful one-time Denjin version of Ryu's HP/OD FIreball, HP/OD Hashogeki, and Shinku Hadoken (SA1); Ryu charges up on frame 50 even though total recovery is 52 frames; Ryu is in a Counter-Hit state for the entire duration

ryu.name: Denjin Charge Hadoken
ryu.notes: 2-hit projectile; Projectile Speed: 0.12; Puts opponent into a limited juggle state on hit; Projectile speed is not affected by button strength; Incurs a 20% damage scaling penalty if used as the first hit of a combo

ryu.name: Air Tatsumaki Senpukyaku
ryu.notes: Can hit cross-up (behind Ryu); Not an Overhead; Only possible during forward jump; Launches opponent into a limited juggle state on hit; Frame advantage on block varies depending on how low to the ground the Air Tatsu connects; 4F less blockstun on cross-up (ranges from -6 to -1 on cross-up block); 16F landing recovery frames of which the majority (13F) is in a crouching state; Forced knockdown state while airborne; The version of Air Tatsu canceled from f+HK is -16 on block and KD +38 on hit (higher KD advantage vs. airborne, but slightly worse positioning for midscreen oki)

ryu.name: Denjin Charge Hashogeki
ryu.notes: Strike hitbox for has 2 hit of projectile durability against non-OD projectiles (OD projectiles still break through it); +3 on block makes this good for keeping up pressure; Launches opponent into a spinning limited juggle state on hit; BUG: Does not consume the Denjin Charge if a prior Hadoken is still on-screen

ryu.name: SA1: 真空波动拳
ryu.notes: Strike and Throw invincible on frames 1-7; 5-hit Super projectile; Projectile Speed: 0.15; Projectile speed is not affected by button strength; Armor Break; Depletes 0.5 Drive Bar on hit for the opponent; Can be used at the same time as OD Hadoken is on screen

ryu.name: Denjin Hadoken
ryu.notes: Strike and Throw invincible on frames 1-7; 8-hit Super projectile; Projectile Speed: 0.24; Projectile speed is not affected by button strength; Armor Break; Depletes 0.5 Drive Bar on hit for the opponent

ryu.name: SA2: 真·波掌击
ryu.notes: Fully invincible on frames 1-13 (extended to 1-18 if you hold the button up to 5F after Super freeze ends); Only invincible on frames 1-9 if you charge for a higher level version (as low as 1-7F if you release the button on the fastest possible level 2 SA2 charge); Strike hitbox; Fully held version puts opponent into a tumbling OTG limited juggle state (+78 KD); Start-up frames in parentheses refers to the minimum start-up of the held versions (18F for level 2 (2900 damage) / 50F for level 3 (3000 damage)); Armor Break; Depletes 1 Drive Bar on hit for the opponent; Fully held version has an extreme amount of pushback on block, making this hard to punish unless parried into Drive Rush or some other long range punish

ryu.name: Denjin Hashogeki
ryu.notes: Fully invincible on frames 1-13 (extended to 1-18 if you hold the button up to 5F after Super freeze ends); Only invincible on frames 1-9 if you charge for a higher level version (as low as 1-7F if you release the button on the fastest possible level 2 SA2 charge); Strike hitbox; The level 2 and 3 charged versions put opponent into a tumbling OTG limited juggle state (+78 KD); The level 2 versions counts as 2 hits for damage scaling when combo'd into; Start-up frames in parentheses refers to the minimum start-up of the held versions (18F for level 2 (3300 damage) / 50F for level 3 (3400 damage)); Denjin charged version does +400 extra damage; Armor Break; Depletes 1 Drive Bar on hit for the opponent; Fully held version has an extreme amount of pushback on block, making this hard to punish unless parried into Drive Rush or some other long range punish

ryu.name: SA3: 真·升龙拳
ryu.notes: Fully invincible on frames 1-16; Airborne on frames 7-48 (Forced Knockdown state); Armor Break; Depletes 1.5 Drive Bars on hit for the opponent; Super cinematic time regenerates ~2,2 Drive Bars for Ryu; Only goes into the cinematic version if it hits on the first 2 active frames; Deals less damage if it doesn't go into the cinematic version (3000~3600 damage depending on how it hits); Incurs 10% damage scaling when canceled into from specials (40% scaling when canceled into from a DP combo starter); Only 2F start-up when canceled into from HP Shoryuken; Deals 100 less chip damage (1000) against crouch blocking opponents; Deals 50 less chip damage (1050) against normal size stand blocking characters (only deals 1100 chip damage against tall standing characters like Dee Jay / JP / Marisa / Sagat / Zangief)

ryu.name: CA: 真·升龙拳

sagat.name: Drive Impact: Tiger Punishment
sagat.notes: 2 hits of armor on frames 1-27; Damages opponents Drive Gauge on Block (1/2 bar) | Hit (1 bar) | Counter-Hit (1.25 bar) | Punish Counter (1.5 bar); Knocks down on hit; Pushes the opponent far back on hit or block and causes a Wall Splat if they hit the wall (Parry prevents the backwards stumble and Wall Splat, greatly reducing the pushback); Regular KDA without Wall Splat +35 KD | Wall Splat on Hit +65 KD | Wall Splat on Block +72 HKD; KDA can vary greatly depending on how high the opponent wall splats (higher KDA the higher they wall splat); Advantage after Wall Splat can vary depending on distance from the corner (farther from corner gives higher advantage); Crumples the opponent on Punish Counter or after absorbing at least 1 attack during start-up (+21 frames before the crumple state goes airborne, followed by airborne state on frames 22-46 before they are grounded); Puts airborne opponents into a long spinning free juggle state when hit as a Punish Counter or after absorbing an attack; If the armor absorbs an attack it slows the overall start-up by 1F (27F total instead of 26F) and incurs 6F hitstop for each projectile hit absorbed (making it less likely to punish the opponent after absorbing projectiles); Absorbing an attack causes the player to take 1/2 the damage in recoverable health (but will KO if this would bring the player's health below zero); Stun/Dizzy occurs when a Wall Splat connects on an opponent in Burnout; Stun gives a free combo follow-up for the next 195F after hitting the wall, followed by a HKD if the player falls to the ground untouched (the last 7F before hitting the ground has a crouch-sized hurtbox but is considered standing, allowing for unique combo setups); Incurs 20% damage scaling penalty if used as the first hit of a combo (applies to wall splat on HIT, crumple, Burnout dizzy on hit/block, or any character-specific means of comboing after a regular Drive Impact); Incurs a 20% multiplier damage scaling penalty after a Wall Splat on BLOCK - Because the blocked Drive Impact is not considered a "hit" for the combo, the next attack can incur its own separate damage scaling as a combo starter; Wall Splat puts opponent into a special juggle state where the next move freely connects and continues the juggle even if it normally wouldn't (similar to a Forced Knockdown or Drive Rush juggle properties); Does not cause Wall Splat if the Drive Impact connects as a combo or a true blockstring with no gaps (LOCK icon appears on-screen); It is possible to "combo" into Stun if the opponent has under 1.5 Drive bars - a blocked DI Wall Splat from slightly outside the corner into a second DI on hit will cause Burnout and Stun (because the blocked DI is not technically considered a combo starter); Costs 1 bar of Drive Gauge; Cinematic slowdown occurs if both players activate Drive Impact within range of each other (granting a Punish Counter to the player who activates it later); Attempting to counter with DI vs. DI with under 400 HP will result in a KO, as the second player will not have enough health to absorb it; Clashes with other Drive Impacts and refunds the Drive gauge cost if they collide on the same active frame (start at exactly the same time, or 1F apart if the first Drive Impact absorbs a strike) - The meter refund does not prevent Burnout from occurring; The scrub killer

sagat.name: Drive Reversal: Tiger Twin Babel
sagat.notes: Has two versions: one performed during blockstun or parry stun (20F start-up) and one performed as a wake-up reversal (18F start-up); Fully invincible on frames 1-22 (blockstun) / frames 1-20 (reversal); Armor Break (blows through all armor like Drive Impact, but not counters like JP's Amnesia); Trying to Drive Reversal after the blockstun ends results in a Drive Impact; Drive Reversal immediately removes the current blockstun you're in and starts the attack; Causes a 4F screen freeze after the 6th start-up frame, which allows the opponent to perform a simple OS (inputting their buttons during the buffer window) to prevent their next attack from coming out; Safe on block (-2) when used against an opponent in Burnout; Costs 2 bars of Drive Gauge; If the opponent tries to throw against a wake-up Drive Reversal, it causes a 12F screen freeze and refunds 1 bar of Drive gauge (but does not prevent Burnout); Guaranteed to interrupt any Drive Rush canceled normal if performed immediately out of blockstun (unless the opponent reacts with an invincible move or counter)

sagat.name: 斗气招架 (Drive Parry)
sagat.notes: Parries all strikes and projectiles (high and low) from frame 1; 12F parry window (can hold the parry to extend the parry window); Perfect Parry occurs on the first 2 active frames (cannot achieve Perfect Parry if you buffer into parry by holding it during Reversal windows; Perfect Parries have to be timed properly); Can still hold charge directions during Parry (allowing characters with charge specials to stand block before performing their reversal); Can block during the recovery frames of a regular parry (can still get hit during the recovery frames if you don't block correctly); Getting thrown or hit at any point during the recovery frames of a whiffed parry attempt results in a Punish Counter; Successfully parrying a move puts you into the same amount of blockstun as that move would regularly do on block (but a Perfect Parry has only 1F of recovery); Throw invincible during the recovery of a successful parry (just like during blockstun); Perfect Parrying a strike has only 1F of recovery and disables the opponent from canceling their attack (basically a guaranteed punish opportunity except for safe jump setups); Perfect Parrying a strike requires holding the correct block direction (Down+Back for low strikes, Back for high/mid strikes); Attempting a Perfect Parry with the wrong block direction results in an "imperfect parry" that builds an extra 3000 Drive Gauge and plays a distinct audio/visual cue; After a successful Perfect Parry, you suffer a 50% penalty to your Damage, Drive Gauge Generation, and Drive Gauge Damage on any of your following attacks when punishing the opponent (in addition, both you and the opponent suffer a 20% penalty to your Super Meter gain during this period); Fully invincible for 6F after a successful Perfect Parry against a strike, which carries over to any attack you perform (ensuring a 5F or faster punish will always interrupt multi-hit attacks); Perfect Parrying projectiles puts you into fixed 10 frames of recovery and applies the same 50% scaling penalties (and 20% Super Meter penalty) on your following attacks when punishing the opponent; Parrying a Strike and Projectile on the same frame will result in a regular parry for the strike attack (effectively ignoring the projectile's hitstop / blockstun); Perfect Parrying a Strike and Projectile on the same frame will give a screen freeze like you Perfect Parried a Strike, but still give you 10F recovery as if you had Perfect Parried a Projectile; Can cancel into Drive Rush during active frames 3 and onward (fastest Drive Rush method is to buffer a forward input before doing parry + forward again); Can cancel into Drive Reversal from a successful parry (just like you normally can during blockstun); Costs 1/2 bar of Drive Gauge and continues to deplete 50 Drive Gauge per frame (0.3 Drive bars per second) as you hold the Parry; You lose the parry if you go into Burnout from the initial Drive Gauge cost (Perfect Parry requires frame-perfect timing when starting from under 1/2 of a Drive bar); Rewards 1 bar of Drive Gauge (1/2 bar total after factoring in the initial parry cost) for successfully parrying a strike; Rewards 1/2 bar of Drive Gauge (0 bar total after factoring in the initial parry cost) for successfully parrying a projectile (with a few exceptions); Rewards 2 bars of Drive Gauge (1.5 bars total after factoring in the initial parry cost) for successful parrying a Super Art or Drive Impact; Successfully parrying a strike attack splits the regular block pushback between both players (while Perfect Parrying a strike removes all of its pushback); Successfully parrying a projectile or Drive Impact reduces the pushback of it by half (while Perfect Parrying a projectile or Drive Impact removes all of its pushback); Your hurtbox and throw box expand slightly towards the opponent for the entire duration of the Parry (Throw box extension starts instantly on frame 1, while the Hurtbox extension starts on frame 3, after the initial 2F Perfect Parry window); Parrying while crouching maintains a regular crouch hurtbox for the first 2 frames of the parry (during the initial Perfect Parry window)

sagat.name: 斗气冲刺 (Drive Rush)
sagat.notes: Dashes forward and enhances the next normal or command normal used out of the Drive Rush with +4 extra hitstun / blockstun, as well as improved juggle properties (Juggle Limit increased by +3 / Juggle Start/Increase reduced to 0); The +4 bonus frame advantage gained from a Drive Rush enhanced move also stacks with any bonus frame advantage that move may have gained from Counter-Hit, Punish Counter, or Burnout; Grounded special-cancelable normals can also be canceled into Drive Rush on hit or block, as well as from light normals on whiff; Drive Rush maintains buffers (freezes the buffer window) during its start-up and freeze frames - This allows players to do things normally not possible within the normal buffer windows, such as Drive Rushing into a charge special; The initial 10F screen freeze eats the opponent's directional inputs (except Jumps) but does not prevent attacks from being buffered immediately afterward (this can cause inputs to be combined in unintended ways, such as crouch MK + Fireball performing a raw Fireball, or a vertical jump + walk forward turning into a forward jump); Framedata shown in parentheses refers to the Drive Rush version used from a Parry; Drive Rush recovery is only 24F total (23F if done from a Parry) - but the enhanced dash itself is 46F total (45F if done from Parry) and you can cancel it as early as frame 9 (frame 11 if done from a Parry); Inputting a direction (walk/crouch/block/jump) after the Drive Rush recovery plays out 2 additional recovery frames before the transition occurs (this allows the user to perform an enhanced crouching or command normal late in the dash by inputting the direction + button simultaneously); You stop building any form of Drive Gauge on your attacks after using a Drive Rush in the MIDDLE of a combo (but you still continue to build Drive gauge as normal if you did Drive Rush at the START of a combo); Applies an extra damage scaling penalty after using a Drive Rush in the MIDDLE of a combo (no damage scaling if you use Drive Rush at the START of a combo); Costs 3 bars of Drive Gauge if canceled into from a normal attack; Costs 1/2 bar of Drive Gauge if canceled into from Parry (for a total of 1 bar of Drive Gauge when you factor in the initial 1/2 bar cost of the Parry); Normals used out of Drive Rush carry additional forward momentum (but throws and specials immediately halt all momentum, which can be a useful strategy to punish opponents for trying to interrupt your Drive Rush); Parry Drive Rush can only be initiated after frame 3 of the Parry (but can be performed immediately after recovering from a successful parry); Parry Drive Rush cannot be initiated with less than 1/2 of a Drive bar (as the initial Parry cost will put the user into Burnout) - But whiff canceling a Light normal into Drive Rush can achieve a similar effect; Cannot cancel Drive Rush into a Parry (inputting MP+MK results in a MK normal coming out instead); Drive Rush puts the user into a counter-hit state for the entire duration (this makes it impossible to tech a throw that connects during the dash)

sagat.name: Mighty Tiger
sagat.notes: Overhead; Frametraps the opponent trying to interrupt the other two follow-ups on block (2F gap, 3F trades from LK/MK Nexus and 0F gap, 1F trades from HK Nexus); Puts airborne opponents into an OTG limited juggle state; Safe on block if the opponent is in Burnout (can only frametrap by delaying the f+LK input after LK/MK Nexus); Drive Impact punishes the overhead after LK/MK Nexus on block (safe after HK Nexus unless the f+LK input is delayed); On a close range hit, opponent is left close enough for a throw or Crouch LK confirm; Incurs 20% damage scaling penalty if used as the first hit of a combo

sagat.name: Greedy Tiger
sagat.notes: Plus on block follow-up that whiffs on crouching opponents (resulting in -19 on hit / -26 on block from LK/MK version and -17 on hit / -24 on block from HK version); +2F extra recovery frames (19F) on whiff only; 4F gap on block (5F trades) after LK/MK Tiger Nexus, so can be interrupted by standing/crouching 4F jabs; 2F gap on block (3F trades) after HK Tiger Nexus for a frametrap against standing 4F lights (but still loses to crouching attacks); Counts as 2 hits of damage scaling when combo'd into; Puts the opponent into a limited juggle state (can follow up with LP/OD Tiger Uppercut in the corner); Safe to reversal Drive Impact after Tiger Nexus on block

sagat.name: Nova Tiger
sagat.notes: Launcher that's advantageous on block and hits both Standing and Crouching; Despite its obvious strengths, this move has gaps on block and is unsafe to things like Drive Impact / Perfect Parry / invincible reversals; Only combos naturally from HK Tiger Nexus (requires juggle state from LK / MK versions); Frametraps when used from HK Tiger Nexus against a burned out opponent; Leaves opponent close enough for a throw / Crouch LK mixup on block (but Sagat cannot shimmy immediate throw tech); Counts as 2 hits of damage scaling when combo'd into; Puts the opponent into a limited juggle state

sagat.name: SA1: 猛虎加册
sagat.notes: Strike and Throw invincible on frames 1-13; 8-hit Super projectile; Projectile Speed: 0.23; Projectile speed is not affected by button strength; Armor Break; Depletes 0.5 Drive Bars on hit for the opponent; Can be used while OD High/Low Tiger Shot is on the screen (but not meterless Tiger Shot)

sagat.name: Savage Tiger

sagat.name: Savage Tiger Raid
sagat.notes: This follow-up is used for just straight up damage or as a combo ender; Good corner carry (over half screen) but no oki afterward; Depletes 1 Drive Bar on hit for the opponent

sagat.name: Savage Tiger Zenith
sagat.notes: This follow-up launches them into a juggle scenario with follow-up combos / corner carry; Depletes 1 Drive Bar on hit for the opponent; Follow-up juggle routes generally deal a bit less damage than Tiger Raid in exchange for oki, corner carry, and rebuilding some Super meter; Most flexible option in terms of options possible afterwards?; Incurs 50% damage scaling penalty if used as the first hit of a combo and counts as 4 hits of damage scaling when combo'd into

sagat.name: Savage Tiger Pendulum
sagat.notes: This follow-up is used to swap sides with the opponent at the cost of oki and 300 damage; Useful when cornered and low on resources (Burnout); Depletes 1 Drive Bar on hit for the opponent

sagat.name: Savage Tiger Stomp
sagat.notes: This follow-up gives a Hard Knockdown (HKD; opponent can't back-roll) and leaves Sagat right next to the opponent for some pressure at the cost of 300 damage; Depletes 1 Drive Bar on hit for the opponent
