terry.name: 站中拳 (5MP)
terry.notes: Core combo / buffer tool that leads into various Target Combos; Can be a good poke / bully tool in close range, especially in Burnout due to its small pushback on block

terry.name: 站重拳 (5HP)
terry.notes: 2-hit combo / buffer / pressure tool that's very easily hit confirmed if both hits connect; Cancelable on both hits; Carries over Counter-Hit / Punish Counter bonus frame advantage to both hits; First hit has increased hitstun for combo potential (second hit won't combo naturally into things like HK Power Charge); Solid hitbox priority can make this a good counter-poke tool in neutral; First hit has less range than the second (only the second hit will connect outside of close range); 2F less recovery (16F) on block; Hitstop for the second hit is +3 extra (13F) if the first hit whiffs; Leaves Terry slightly outside throw range when blocked out of Drive Rush (but he can microwalk to throw while beating 4F normals)

terry.name: 站轻脚 (5LK)
terry.notes: Incurs 20% damage scaling penalty if used as the first hit of a combo; Terry's main way of comboing into the spaced out LK Power Charge for combo extensions

terry.name: 站中脚 (5MK)
terry.notes: Core combo and poke tool; Terry lifts up his front leg hurtbox on frames 3-20 making this a good tool against low attacks; Can easily hit confirm this on Counter-Hit into SA1 (Buster Wolf) or on Punish Counter into Fire Kick (2MK > 2HK) if in range of 2MK

terry.name: 站重脚 (5HK)
terry.notes: Solid bully tool with decent range and hitbox priority as well as doing good Drive Gauge chip on block; Decent anti-air on frames 14-15 (think Chun-Li stand HK but worse); Causes a crumple-like free juggle state on a grounded Punish Counter (+18 frames to connect a follow-up combo before the opponent is knocked down); Puts airborne opponents into a limited juggle state on Punish Counter; The brief extended leg hurtbox on frame 11 of start-up (1F before active) is strike invincible (cannot counter-poke projectiles)

terry.name: 蹲轻拳 (2LP)
terry.notes: Chains into stand LP / crouch LP / crouch LK; Incurs 20% damage scaling penalty if used as the first hit of a combo; Terry's only way to naturally combo into MP Burn Knuckle from LP/2LK starters; Shortest range of Terry's light attacks; Topmost hurtboxes on frames 1-6 are vulnerable only to airborne attacks (this is to discourage its use as an anti-air)

terry.name: 蹲中拳 (2MP)
terry.notes: Fantastic combo / poke / buffer / oki tool; +2F extra recovery frames (15F) on whiff; +1F extra recovery frame (14F) on block; Topmost hurtboxes on frames 1-9 are vulnerable only to airborne attacks (this is to discourage its use as an anti-air)

terry.name: 蹲重拳 (2HP)
terry.notes: Forces stand on hit; Solid anti-air on frames 10-13 (but has no air invincibility frames); Cannot hit cross-up (behind Terry); Only cancelable on the first two active frames; Cancel window can be delayed manually when canceling into OD Power Wave to adjust positioning during combos and create more combo routes; Short horizontal range (can only be combo'd into from up close); +4F extra total animation (35F) on whiff or when active frames 3-6 connect on hit or block (framedata listed in parentheses, shorter overall duration if active frames 1-2 connect on hit or block)

terry.name: 蹲轻脚 (2LK)
terry.notes: Chains into stand LP / crouch LP / crouch LK; Incurs 20% damage scaling penalty if used as the first hit of a combo; Very small pushback, strong hitbox priority, good range, and a +3 on hit low attack, makes this Terry's ideal light combo / blockstring starter

terry.name: 蹲中脚 (2MK)
terry.notes: Fantastic range for a crouch MK; Cancelable into a HK Target Combo that launches the opponent into a limited juggle state on hit; Incurs a 20% damage scaling penalty if used as the first hit of a combo

terry.name: 蹲重脚 (2HK)
terry.notes: Has strong hitbox priority for counter-poking purposes; Situational anti-air from further away jumps; Has some Juggle potential naturally without Drive Rush

terry.name: 跳轻拳 (j.LP)
terry.notes: Fast air-to-air option

terry.name: 跳中拳 (j.MP)
terry.notes: Puts airborne opponents into a limited juggle state; Big air-to-air hitboxes; Can only just barely connect on standing grounded opponents on the last active frame

terry.name: 跳重拳 (j.HP)
terry.notes: Spikes down airborne opponents on Counter-Hit or Punish Counter; Strong hitbox priority for vertical approaches

terry.name: 跳轻脚 (j.LK)
terry.notes: Another quick air-to-air option

terry.name: 跳中脚 (j.MK)
terry.notes: Cross-up that also has great hitbox priority on the front

terry.name: 跳重脚 (j.HK)
terry.notes: Terry's strongest jump-in; Furthest horizontal reach and also has fantastic hitbox priority for both horizontal and vertical approaches

terry.name: Hammer Punch
terry.notes: Just a pretty standard Overhead (can meaty last active frame to do jab combo follow-ups); BUG: Drive gauge / Super meter values are all out of wack on this move (this was likely scripted as a Medium command normal at some point and Capcom forgot to adjust all its values properly)

terry.name: Power Drive
terry.notes: Knocks down opponent on hit; 2F gap on block (frametrap); Relatively safe on block if spaced out (many stand LK can punish if not spaced out properly); Can be hit confirmed (but this is very hard at 16F hit confirm window); Second hit incurs 30% immediate damage scaling when combo'd into from stand MP

terry.name: Power Shoot
terry.notes: Launches opponent into a limited juggle state; Counts as 2 hits of damage scaling when both hits land; Not a natural combo (requires at least a Counter-Hit, Drive Rush, juggle state, or meaty stand MP); 4F gap on block (5F attacks trade)

terry.name: Power Dunk
terry.notes: Only possible to perform on hit; Great combo extension tool that gives decent corner carry and oki; Last hit (Power Dunk!) can be manually delayed to hit a 3-frame Just Frame window to deal 140 extra damage (2350 total) and get increased drive / super gain (this Just Frame version is indicated by an increased screen shake and hitstop upon impact); Power Dunk follow-up is on a 6F cancel window and the Just Frame input is on frames 2-4 on that window, while frames 1 and 5-6 result in a regular Power Dunk; Try using visual cues to help with the Just Frame timing, for example pressing the button when Terry's kicking leg touches the ground; KDA (Knockdown Advantage) varies depending on how delayed the Power Dunk is performed (less KDA the more it is delayed); The Just Frame version always has a consistent KDA of +24

terry.name: Fire Kick
terry.notes: Low target combo that's fully cancelable and launches opponent into a limited juggle state on hit

terry.name: Passing Sway
terry.notes: Useful mixup / reset / sideswap tool; Terry steps into the background after second hit (MK) on HIT only on frames 20-40 (Terry is fully invincible and has no collision boxes during this period); 1F gap between hits on block (up to 2F if manually delayed); Cancelable into two different follow-ups (MP or MK) on HIT only; The cancel window for the follow-ups is on frames 30-36 (delaying the follow-ups can make the opponent's invincible Reversals whiff entirely); While the follow-ups can be countered with a strike / air invincible Reversals and Perfect Parry, if Terry delays the follow-ups then on paper he can beat everything in the game except for Lily's SA2 (the only way for the opponent to otherwise counter the delayed follow-ups is to also delay their own moves, and thus the mind games begin)

terry.name: Passing Sway > Jumping Lariat
terry.notes: Fully invincible and has no collision during entire start-up and active frames (this can be utilized to avoid every Reversal attempt in the game except for Lily's SA2); Hold forward to increase the distance Terry moves forward before swinging (can hold forward to go behind the opponent and intentionally whiff the MP follow-up, resulting in -23~29 on whiff); Cannot hit cross-up (MK follow-up is designed for that); Doesn't combo on hit from MP > MK; 3-9 frames gap on hit depending on how much the follow-up is delayed (although this gap is not that relevant since Terry is still fully invincible during it); A cornered opponent can hold forward to make this follow-up whiff no matter whether Terry holds forward or back (works mid-screen as well if Terry delays the Jumping Lariat follow-up)

terry.name: Passing Sway > Jumping Knee
terry.notes: Fully invincible and has no collision during entire start-up and active frames (this can be utilized to avoid every Reversal attempt in the game except for Lily's SA2); Hold forward to increase the distance Terry moves forward before swinging (not holding forward makes Terry whiff the knee and stay in front of the opponent, resulting in -25~31 on whiff); Cannot hit in the front (can only hit cross-up behind the opponent); Doesn't combo on hit from MP > MK; 3-9 frames gap on hit depending on how much the follow-up is delayed (although this gap is not that relevant since Terry is still fully invincible during it); An opponent with 0.043 forward walk speed or faster can hold forward to block this follow-up behind them even if Terry holds back during the Jumping Knee follow-up (all characters can do this if Terry delays the Jumping Knee follow-up)

terry.name: Grasping Upper
terry.notes: Throw loop (corner or midscreen neutral rise only): Dash forward for +3 strike/throw mix (cannot walk back to shimmy); Can walk forward for a frame perfect throw loop (4F timing on Zangief, 3F timing on Blanka / E. Honda, 2F timing on Alex / Marisa / Sagat); Punish Counter gives +70% (2040) damage, Hard Knockdown (denies back-roll option on wake-up), depletes 1 bar of Drive gauge from the opponent, and builds twice as much Super gauge for the attacker; Throw Escape builds 0.5 Drive bars for the defender (randomly assigned if throws are input simultaneously)

terry.name: Buster Throw
terry.notes: Throw oki (corner / quick rise only): Drive Rush strike / throw mix; Punish Counter gives +70% (2040) damage, Hard Knockdown (denies back-roll option on wake-up), depletes 1 bar of Drive gauge from the opponent, and builds twice as much Super gauge for the attacker; Throw Escape builds 0.5 Drive bars for the defender (randomly assigned if throws are input simultaneously)

terry.name: Drive Impact: Back Spin Kick
terry.notes: 2 hits of armor on frames 1-27; Damages opponents Drive Gauge on Block (1/2 bar) | Hit (1 bar) | Counter-Hit (1.25 bar) | Punish Counter (1.5 bar); Knocks down on hit; Pushes the opponent far back on hit or block and causes a Wall Splat if they hit the wall (Parry prevents the backwards stumble and Wall Splat, greatly reducing the pushback); Regular KDA without Wall Splat +35 KD | Wall Splat on Hit +65 KD | Wall Splat on Block +72 HKD; KDA can vary greatly depending on how high the opponent wall splats (higher KDA the higher they wall splat); Advantage after Wall Splat can vary depending on distance from the corner (farther from corner gives higher advantage); Crumples the opponent on Punish Counter or after absorbing at least 1 attack during start-up (+21 frames before the crumple state goes airborne, followed by airborne state on frames 22-46 before they are grounded); Puts airborne opponents into a long spinning free juggle state when hit as a Punish Counter or after absorbing an attack; If the armor absorbs an attack it slows the overall start-up by 1F (27F total instead of 26F) and incurs 6F hitstop for each projectile hit absorbed (making it less likely to punish the opponent after absorbing projectiles); Absorbing an attack causes the player to take 1/2 the damage in recoverable health (but will KO if this would bring the player's health below zero); Stun/Dizzy occurs when a Wall Splat connects on an opponent in Burnout; Stun gives a free combo follow-up for the next 195F after hitting the wall, followed by a HKD if the player falls to the ground untouched (the last 7F before hitting the ground has a crouch-sized hurtbox but is considered standing, allowing for unique combo setups); Incurs 20% damage scaling penalty if used as the first hit of a combo (applies to wall splat on HIT, crumple, Burnout dizzy on hit/block, or any character-specific means of comboing after a regular Drive Impact); Incurs a 20% multiplier damage scaling penalty after a Wall Splat on BLOCK - Because the blocked Drive Impact is not considered a "hit" for the combo, the next attack can incur its own separate damage scaling as a combo starter; Wall Splat puts opponent into a special juggle state where the next move freely connects and continues the juggle even if it normally wouldn't (similar to a Forced Knockdown or Drive Rush juggle properties); Does not cause Wall Splat if the Drive Impact connects as a combo or a true blockstring with no gaps (LOCK icon appears on-screen); It is possible to "combo" into Stun if the opponent has under 1.5 Drive bars - a blocked DI Wall Splat from slightly outside the corner into a second DI on hit will cause Burnout and Stun (because the blocked DI is not technically considered a combo starter); Costs 1 bar of Drive Gauge; Cinematic slowdown occurs if both players activate Drive Impact within range of each other (granting a Punish Counter to the player who activates it later); Attempting to counter with DI vs. DI with under 400 HP will result in a KO, as the second player will not have enough health to absorb it; Clashes with other Drive Impacts and refunds the Drive gauge cost if they collide on the same active frame (start at exactly the same time, or 1F apart if the first Drive Impact absorbs a strike) - The meter refund does not prevent Burnout from occurring; The scrub killer

terry.name: Drive Reversal: Back Knuckle
terry.notes: Has two versions: one performed during blockstun or parry stun (20F start-up) and one performed as a wake-up reversal (18F start-up); Fully invincible on frames 1-22 (blockstun) / frames 1-20 (reversal); Armor Break (blows through all armor like Drive Impact, but not counters like JP's Amnesia); Trying to Drive Reversal after the blockstun ends results in a Drive Impact; Drive Reversal immediately removes the current blockstun you're in and starts the attack; Causes a 4F screen freeze after the 6th start-up frame, which allows the opponent to perform a simple OS (inputting their buttons during the buffer window) to prevent their next attack from coming out; Safe on block (-2) when used against an opponent in Burnout; Costs 2 bars of Drive Gauge; If the opponent tries to throw against a wake-up Drive Reversal, it causes a 12F screen freeze and refunds 1 bar of Drive gauge (but does not prevent Burnout); Guaranteed to interrupt any Drive Rush canceled normal if performed immediately out of blockstun (unless the opponent reacts with an invincible move or counter)

terry.name: 斗气招架 (Drive Parry)
terry.notes: Parries all strikes and projectiles (high and low) from frame 1; 12F parry window (can hold the parry to extend the parry window); Perfect Parry occurs on the first 2 active frames (cannot achieve Perfect Parry if you buffer into parry by holding it during Reversal windows; Perfect Parries have to be timed properly); Can still hold charge directions during Parry (allowing characters with charge specials to stand block before performing their reversal); Can block during the recovery frames of a regular parry (can still get hit during the recovery frames if you don't block correctly); Getting thrown or hit at any point during the recovery frames of a whiffed parry attempt results in a Punish Counter; Successfully parrying a move puts you into the same amount of blockstun as that move would regularly do on block (but a Perfect Parry has only 1F of recovery); Throw invincible during the recovery of a successful parry (just like during blockstun); Perfect Parrying a strike has only 1F of recovery and disables the opponent from canceling their attack (basically a guaranteed punish opportunity except for safe jump setups); Perfect Parrying a strike requires holding the correct block direction (Down+Back for low strikes, Back for high/mid strikes); Attempting a Perfect Parry with the wrong block direction results in an "imperfect parry" that builds an extra 3000 Drive Gauge and plays a distinct audio/visual cue; After a successful Perfect Parry, you suffer a 50% penalty to your Damage, Drive Gauge Generation, and Drive Gauge Damage on any of your following attacks when punishing the opponent (in addition, both you and the opponent suffer a 20% penalty to your Super Meter gain during this period); Fully invincible for 6F after a successful Perfect Parry against a strike, which carries over to any attack you perform (ensuring a 5F or faster punish will always interrupt multi-hit attacks); Perfect Parrying projectiles puts you into fixed 10 frames of recovery and applies the same 50% scaling penalties (and 20% Super Meter penalty) on your following attacks when punishing the opponent; Parrying a Strike and Projectile on the same frame will result in a regular parry for the strike attack (effectively ignoring the projectile's hitstop / blockstun); Perfect Parrying a Strike and Projectile on the same frame will give a screen freeze like you Perfect Parried a Strike, but still give you 10F recovery as if you had Perfect Parried a Projectile; Can cancel into Drive Rush during active frames 3 and onward (fastest Drive Rush method is to buffer a forward input before doing parry + forward again); Can cancel into Drive Reversal from a successful parry (just like you normally can during blockstun); Costs 1/2 bar of Drive Gauge and continues to deplete 50 Drive Gauge per frame (0.3 Drive bars per second) as you hold the Parry; You lose the parry if you go into Burnout from the initial Drive Gauge cost (Perfect Parry requires frame-perfect timing when starting from under 1/2 of a Drive bar); Rewards 1 bar of Drive Gauge (1/2 bar total after factoring in the initial parry cost) for successfully parrying a strike; Rewards 1/2 bar of Drive Gauge (0 bar total after factoring in the initial parry cost) for successfully parrying a projectile (with a few exceptions); Rewards 2 bars of Drive Gauge (1.5 bars total after factoring in the initial parry cost) for successful parrying a Super Art or Drive Impact; Successfully parrying a strike attack splits the regular block pushback between both players (while Perfect Parrying a strike removes all of its pushback); Successfully parrying a projectile or Drive Impact reduces the pushback of it by half (while Perfect Parrying a projectile or Drive Impact removes all of its pushback); Your hurtbox and throw box expand slightly towards the opponent for the entire duration of the Parry (Throw box extension starts instantly on frame 1, while the Hurtbox extension starts on frame 3, after the initial 2F Perfect Parry window); Parrying while crouching maintains a regular crouch hurtbox for the first 2 frames of the parry (during the initial Perfect Parry window)

terry.name: 斗气冲刺 (Drive Rush)
terry.notes: Dashes forward and enhances the next normal or command normal used out of the Drive Rush with +4 extra hitstun / blockstun, as well as improved juggle properties (Juggle Limit increased by +3 / Juggle Start/Increase reduced to 0); The +4 bonus frame advantage gained from a Drive Rush enhanced move also stacks with any bonus frame advantage that move may have gained from Counter-Hit, Punish Counter, or Burnout; Grounded special-cancelable normals can also be canceled into Drive Rush on hit or block, as well as from light normals on whiff; Drive Rush maintains buffers (freezes the buffer window) during its start-up and freeze frames - This allows players to do things normally not possible within the normal buffer windows, such as Drive Rushing into a charge special; The initial 10F screen freeze eats the opponent's directional inputs (except Jumps) but does not prevent attacks from being buffered immediately afterward (this can cause inputs to be combined in unintended ways, such as crouch MK + Fireball performing a raw Fireball, or a vertical jump + walk forward turning into a forward jump); Framedata shown in parentheses refers to the Drive Rush version used from a Parry; Drive Rush recovery is only 24F total (23F if done from a Parry) - but the enhanced dash itself is 46F total (45F if done from Parry) and you can cancel it as early as frame 9 (frame 11 if done from a Parry); Inputting a direction (walk/crouch/block/jump) after the Drive Rush recovery plays out 2 additional recovery frames before the transition occurs (this allows the user to perform an enhanced crouching or command normal late in the dash by inputting the direction + button simultaneously); You stop building any form of Drive Gauge on your attacks after using a Drive Rush in the MIDDLE of a combo (but you still continue to build Drive gauge as normal if you did Drive Rush at the START of a combo); Applies an extra damage scaling penalty after using a Drive Rush in the MIDDLE of a combo (no damage scaling if you use Drive Rush at the START of a combo); Costs 3 bars of Drive Gauge if canceled into from a normal attack; Costs 1/2 bar of Drive Gauge if canceled into from Parry (for a total of 1 bar of Drive Gauge when you factor in the initial 1/2 bar cost of the Parry); Normals used out of Drive Rush carry additional forward momentum (but throws and specials immediately halt all momentum, which can be a useful strategy to punish opponents for trying to interrupt your Drive Rush); Parry Drive Rush can only be initiated after frame 3 of the Parry (but can be performed immediately after recovering from a successful parry); Parry Drive Rush cannot be initiated with less than 1/2 of a Drive bar (as the initial Parry cost will put the user into Burnout) - But whiff canceling a Light normal into Drive Rush can achieve a similar effect; Cannot cancel Drive Rush into a Parry (inputting MP+MK results in a MK normal coming out instead); Drive Rush puts the user into a counter-hit state for the entire duration (this makes it impossible to tech a throw that connects during the dash)

terry.name: Buster Wolf
terry.notes: Strike and Throw invincible on frames 1-8; Armor Break; Depletes 0.5 Drive Bar on hit for the opponent; Great Reversal and Combo tool with fast start-up and great range (travels ~80% screen length); Puts opponent into a limited juggle state on hit (can juggle into another Buster Wolf if it juggles on later active frames); 15F less recovery frames (45F) on block than on whiff

terry.name: Power Geyser
terry.notes: Fully invincible on frames 1-17; Invincible to airborne strikes on frames 18-25 (until active frames run out); Armor Break; Depletes 1 Drive Bar on hit for the opponent; 1-hit Super projectile hitbox; Great for combos and juggles as well as a situational anti-air tool; Can be followed up on HIT only with Twin Geyser (costs 3 bars of Drive Gauge), and then again with Triple Geyser (costs another bar of Super meter), resulting in big damage overall; Can also be input with a 21416+P motion for a different visual effect (this version has no actual affect on the properties)

terry.name: Twin Geyser
terry.notes: No form of invincibility on this first follow-up hit; This follow-up hit does not deplete any extra Drive Bar on hit for the opponent; Costs 3 extra bars of Drive Gauge to use and can be followed up on HIT only with Triple Geyser (costs another bar of Super Meter); This follow-up can be delayed quite a bit to adjust for the following juggle scenarios; Launches the opponent into a limited juggle state (can be followed up with combo extensions)

terry.name: Triple Geyser
terry.notes: Fully invincible for the entire duration of this final third hit; Depletes 0,2 extra Drive Bar on hit for the opponent (total of 1,2 Drive Bars); Costs another bar of Super meter to use (total cost being 3 bars of Super); Deals slightly higher base damage by itself than a raw SA3; If Terry attempts to perform this follow-up without having enough Super meter, he will instead perform a feint which leaves him at -3 KD (this wastes his potential juggle follow-ups after Twin Geyser)

terry.name: Rising Fang
terry.notes: Fully invincible on frames 1-16; Armor Break; Depletes 1.5 Drive Bars on hit for the opponent; Super cinematic time regenerates 2.1 Drive Bars for Terry; Only goes into the cinematic version if it hits on the first 3 active frames; Deals less damage and doesn't cause a HKD if it doesn't go into cinematic version (2650-3000 damage depending on how it hits); Only 2F start-up when canceled into from Rising Tackle / Quick Burn / Burning Knuckle; Last hit whiffs on crouch block resulting in slightly worse block advantage (-53) a bit less chip and drive gauge damage; Incurs 10% damage scaling when canceled into from specials (30% when canceled into from a Rising Tackle combo starter)

terry.name: Rising Fang (Critical Art)
terry.notes: Fully invincible on frames 1-16; Armor Break; Depletes 1.5 Drive Bars on hit for the opponent; Super cinematic time regenerates 2.1 Drive Bars for Terry; Only goes into the cinematic version if it hits on the first 3 active frames; Deals less damage and doesn't cause a HKD if it doesn't go into cinematic version (3150-3500 damage depending on how it hits); Only 2F start-up when canceled into from Rising Tackle / Quick Burn / Burning Knuckle; Last hit whiffs on crouch block resulting in slightly worse block advantage (-53) a bit less chip and drive gauge damage; Incurs 10% damage scaling when canceled into from specials (30% when canceled into from a Rising Tackle combo starter); Critical Art does +500 extra damage over regular version

terry.name: Power Wave
terry.notes: 1-hit projectile; Projectile Speed: 0.02~0.21 (starts slow and then speeds up a lot as it goes forward); Travels ~60% screen length very fast, but dissipates quickly; Does not go underneath fireballs (clashes with regular fireballs); Extended arm hurtbox on frames 21-39 is Projectile invincible; No head hurtbox on frames 11-41 while Terry is leaning over; Causes a knockdown on Counter-Hit / Punish Counter; Puts airborne opponents into a limited juggle state

variations.invincible: Extended arm hurtbox on frames 14-37 is Projectile invincible
variations.notes: 1-hit projectile; Projectile Speed: 0.06; Travels full-screen; Goes underneath most traditional fireballs (clashes with Juri's Fireball); Extended arm hurtbox on frames 14-37 is Projectile invincible; No head hurtbox on frames 11-41 while Terry is leaning over; Puts airborne opponents into a limited juggle state

variations.invincible: Extended arm hurtbox on frames 21-39 is Projectile invincible
variations.notes: 1-hit projectile; Projectile Speed: 0.02~0.21 (starts slow and then speeds up a lot as it goes forward); Travels ~60% screen length very fast, but dissipates quickly; Does not go underneath fireballs (clashes with regular fireballs); Extended arm hurtbox on frames 21-39 is Projectile invincible; No head hurtbox on frames 11-41 while Terry is leaning over; Causes a knockdown on Counter-Hit / Punish Counter; Puts airborne opponents into a limited juggle state

variations.invincible: Extended arm hurtbox on frames 21-25 is Projectile invincible
variations.notes: 2-hit OD projectile; Projectile Speed: 0.055; Travels full-screen; Does not go underneath fireballs (clashes with regular fireballs); Extended arm hurtbox on frames 21-25 is Projectile invincible; No head hurtbox on frames 13-36 while Terry is leaning over; Carries over Counter-Hit / Punish Counter bonus frame advantage to both hits; Puts airborne opponents into a limited juggle state (can pop them up twice in certain juggle combos)

terry.name: Round Wave
terry.notes: 1-hit stationary projectile hitbox that still counts as a Strike for the purpose of being Perfect Parried, but otherwise functions as a projectile attack; Close-up combo / pressure / oki tool that's very plus on block; Extended arm hurtbox on frames 38-46 is NOT projectile invincible (after the active frames are finished); No head hurtbox on frames 24-48 while Terry is leaning over; Puts airborne opponents into a limited juggle state

variations.invincible: Extended arm hurtbox on frames 38-46 is NOT projectile invincible (after the active frames are finished)
variations.notes: 1-hit stationary projectile hitbox that still counts as a Strike for the purpose of being Perfect Parried, but otherwise functions as a projectile attack; Close-up combo / pressure / oki tool that's very plus on block; Extended arm hurtbox on frames 38-46 is NOT projectile invincible (after the active frames are finished); No head hurtbox on frames 24-48 while Terry is leaning over; Puts airborne opponents into a limited juggle state

terry.name: Quick Burn
terry.notes: Second hit is an Overhead (effectively 22 frame start-up if the first hit whiffs) with decent range that can also be spaced out to be +4 on hit, and then combo'd into stand LP in the corner; Fast but short range special that's useful for light confirms and maintaining grounded pressure after a light confirm; Leaves Terry in throw range on hit with a +3 strike / throw / shimmy mixup (can also backdash to be at least +10 if the opponent techs a throw for a sweep / SA1 punish); Cancels into SA3 on the second hit only

variations.notes: Second hit is an Overhead (effectively 22 frame start-up if the first hit whiffs) with decent range that can also be spaced out to be +4 on hit, and then combo'd into stand LP in the corner; Fast but short range special that's useful for light confirms and maintaining grounded pressure after a light confirm; Leaves Terry in throw range on hit with a +3 strike / throw / shimmy mixup (can also backdash to be at least +10 if the opponent techs a throw for a sweep / SA1 punish); Cancels into SA3 on the second hit only

Second hit is an Overhead (effectively 22 frame start-up if the first hit whiffs); Third hit puts opponent into a limited juggle state; Third hit only comes out on HIT; Only SA2/SA3 cancelable on the first 2 hits; Framedata listed refers to the version that plays out on block or whiff (Terry performs an extra knockdown attack on HIT only); Gives solid damage and oki from Terry's light normal hitconfirms

terry.name: Burning Knuckle
terry.notes: Faster but shorter range and less active frames compared to the slower HP version (Terry does not lift his arms up at the start for this MP version); Can be plus on block if spaced properly / hitting meaty on later active frame (this gives a screen shake effect to indicate that Terry has the frame advantage); Great tool to close the distance for pressure during the opponents Burnout (the screen does not shake if you are +1~4 on an opponent in Burnout); Grants additional Knockdown advantage on last 2 active frames (even a +42 KD safe jump if last active frame connects on hit); Only cancelable into SA3 (Rising Fang) on the first active frame, cannot be performed from far away

yasmine.name: 站轻拳 (5LP)

yasmine.name: 站重拳 (5HP)
yasmine.notes: 3 hits (only cancelable on the 2nd hit); Can be hitconfirmed but has reduced hit or block advantage on a delayed cancel (as low as +6 / -2 on DRC); Carries over Counter-Hit / Punish Counter bonus frame advantage to all hits; Core combo tool with huge juggle potential and also pretty good range for whiff punishing; Generally too much pushback on hit to convert on Counter-Hit, but converts into bigger combos on Punish Counter or Drive Rush

yasmine.name: 站轻脚 (5LK)

yasmine.name: 站中脚 (5MK)

yasmine.name: 站重脚 (5HK)

yasmine.name: 蹲轻拳 (2LP)

yasmine.name: 蹲中拳 (2MP)

yasmine.name: 蹲重拳 (2HP)

yasmine.name: 蹲轻脚 (2LK)

yasmine.name: 蹲重脚 (2HK)

yasmine.name: 跳轻拳 (j.LP)

yasmine.name: 跳中拳 (j.MP)

yasmine.name: Walis na Pabagsak

yasmine.name: Kidlat na Hiwa

yasmine.name: Sunod-sunod na Sipa 1

yasmine.name: Sunod-sunod na Sipa 2

yasmine.name: Kumbinasyong Pampabagsak

yasmine.name: Pigil-Ulo

yasmine.name: Hila-Kamay
yasmine.notes: Oki after corner side switch: ?; Punish Counter gives +70% (2040) damage, Hard Knockdown (denies back-roll option on wake-up), depletes 1 bar of Drive gauge from the opponent, and builds twice as much Super gauge for the attacker; Throw Escape builds 0.5 Drive bars for the defender (randomly assigned if throws are input simultaneously)

yasmine.name: Drive Impact: Dagok sa Katawan
yasmine.notes: 2 hits of armor on frames 1-27; Damages opponents Drive Gauge on Block (1/2 bar) | Hit (1 bar) | Counter-Hit (1.25 bar) | Punish Counter (1.5 bar); Knocks down on hit; Pushes the opponent far back on hit or block and causes a Wall Splat if they hit the wall (Parry prevents the backwards stumble and Wall Splat, greatly reducing the pushback); Regular KDA without Wall Splat +35 KD | Wall Splat on Hit +65 KD | Wall Splat on Block +72 HKD; KDA can vary greatly depending on how high the opponent wall splats (higher KDA the higher they wall splat); Advantage after Wall Splat can vary depending on distance from the corner (farther from corner gives higher advantage); Crumples the opponent on Punish Counter or after absorbing at least 1 attack during start-up (+21 frames before the crumple state goes airborne, followed by airborne state on frames 22-46 before they are grounded); Puts airborne opponents into a long spinning free juggle state when hit as a Punish Counter or after absorbing an attack; If the armor absorbs an attack it slows the overall start-up by 1F (27F total instead of 26F) and incurs 6F hitstop for each projectile hit absorbed (making it less likely to punish the opponent after absorbing projectiles); Absorbing an attack causes the player to take 1/2 the damage in recoverable health (but will KO if this would bring the player's health below zero); Stun/Dizzy occurs when a Wall Splat connects on an opponent in Burnout; Stun gives a free combo follow-up for the next 195F after hitting the wall, followed by a HKD if the player falls to the ground untouched (the last 7F before hitting the ground has a crouch-sized hurtbox but is considered standing, allowing for unique combo setups); Incurs 20% damage scaling penalty if used as the first hit of a combo (applies to wall splat on HIT, crumple, Burnout dizzy on hit/block, or any character-specific means of comboing after a regular Drive Impact); Incurs a 20% multiplier damage scaling penalty after a Wall Splat on BLOCK - Because the blocked Drive Impact is not considered a "hit" for the combo, the next attack can incur its own separate damage scaling as a combo starter; Wall Splat puts opponent into a special juggle state where the next move freely connects and continues the juggle even if it normally wouldn't (similar to a Forced Knockdown or Drive Rush juggle properties); Does not cause Wall Splat if the Drive Impact connects as a combo or a true blockstring with no gaps (LOCK icon appears on-screen); It is possible to "combo" into Stun if the opponent has under 1.5 Drive bars - a blocked DI Wall Splat from slightly outside the corner into a second DI on hit will cause Burnout and Stun (because the blocked DI is not technically considered a combo starter); Costs 1 bar of Drive Gauge; Cinematic slowdown occurs if both players activate Drive Impact within range of each other (granting a Punish Counter to the player who activates it later); Attempting to counter with DI vs. DI with under 400 HP will result in a KO, as the second player will not have enough health to absorb it; Clashes with other Drive Impacts and refunds the Drive gauge cost if they collide on the same active frame (start at exactly the same time, or 1F apart if the first Drive Impact absorbs a strike) - The meter refund does not prevent Burnout from occurring; The scrub killer

yasmine.name: Drive Reversal: Dobleng Palo Gamit ang Palad
yasmine.notes: Has two versions: one performed during blockstun or parry stun (20F start-up) and one performed as a wake-up reversal (18F start-up); Fully invincible on frames 1-22 (blockstun) / frames 1-20 (reversal); Armor Break (blows through all armor like Drive Impact, but not counters like JP's Amnesia); Trying to Drive Reversal after the blockstun ends results in a Drive Impact; Drive Reversal immediately removes the current blockstun you're in and starts the attack; Causes a 4F screen freeze after the 6th start-up frame, which allows the opponent to perform a simple OS (inputting their buttons during the buffer window) to prevent their next attack from coming out; Safe on block (-2) when used against an opponent in Burnout; Costs 2 bars of Drive Gauge; If the opponent tries to throw against a wake-up Drive Reversal, it causes a 12F screen freeze and refunds 1 bar of Drive gauge (but does not prevent Burnout); Guaranteed to interrupt any Drive Rush canceled normal if performed immediately out of blockstun (unless the opponent reacts with an invincible move or counter)

yasmine.name: 斗气招架 (Drive Parry)
yasmine.notes: Parries all strikes and projectiles (high and low) from frame 1; 12F parry window (can hold the parry to extend the parry window); Perfect Parry occurs on the first 2 active frames (cannot achieve Perfect Parry if you buffer into parry by holding it during Reversal windows; Perfect Parries have to be timed properly); Can still hold charge directions during Parry (allowing characters with charge specials to stand block before performing their reversal); Can block during the recovery frames of a regular parry (can still get hit during the recovery frames if you don't block correctly); Getting thrown or hit at any point during the recovery frames of a whiffed parry attempt results in a Punish Counter; Successfully parrying a move puts you into the same amount of blockstun as that move would regularly do on block (but a Perfect Parry has only 1F of recovery); Throw invincible during the recovery of a successful parry (just like during blockstun); Perfect Parrying a strike has only 1F of recovery and disables the opponent from canceling their attack (basically a guaranteed punish opportunity except for safe jump setups); Perfect Parrying a strike requires holding the correct block direction (Down+Back for low strikes, Back for high/mid strikes); Attempting a Perfect Parry with the wrong block direction results in an "imperfect parry" that builds an extra 3000 Drive Gauge and plays a distinct audio/visual cue; After a successful Perfect Parry, you suffer a 50% penalty to your Damage, Drive Gauge Generation, and Drive Gauge Damage on any of your following attacks when punishing the opponent (in addition, both you and the opponent suffer a 20% penalty to your Super Meter gain during this period); Fully invincible for 6F after a successful Perfect Parry against a strike, which carries over to any attack you perform (ensuring a 5F or faster punish will always interrupt multi-hit attacks); Perfect Parrying projectiles puts you into fixed 10 frames of recovery and applies the same 50% scaling penalties (and 20% Super Meter penalty) on your following attacks when punishing the opponent; Parrying a Strike and Projectile on the same frame will result in a regular parry for the strike attack (effectively ignoring the projectile's hitstop / blockstun); Perfect Parrying a Strike and Projectile on the same frame will give a screen freeze like you Perfect Parried a Strike, but still give you 10F recovery as if you had Perfect Parried a Projectile; Can cancel into Drive Rush during active frames 3 and onward (fastest Drive Rush method is to buffer a forward input before doing parry + forward again); Can cancel into Drive Reversal from a successful parry (just like you normally can during blockstun); Costs 1/2 bar of Drive Gauge and continues to deplete 50 Drive Gauge per frame (0.3 Drive bars per second) as you hold the Parry; You lose the parry if you go into Burnout from the initial Drive Gauge cost (Perfect Parry requires frame-perfect timing when starting from under 1/2 of a Drive bar); Rewards 1 bar of Drive Gauge (1/2 bar total after factoring in the initial parry cost) for successfully parrying a strike; Rewards 1/2 bar of Drive Gauge (0 bar total after factoring in the initial parry cost) for successfully parrying a projectile (with a few exceptions); Rewards 2 bars of Drive Gauge (1.5 bars total after factoring in the initial parry cost) for successful parrying a Super Art or Drive Impact; Successfully parrying a strike attack splits the regular block pushback between both players (while Perfect Parrying a strike removes all of its pushback); Successfully parrying a projectile or Drive Impact reduces the pushback of it by half (while Perfect Parrying a projectile or Drive Impact removes all of its pushback); Your hurtbox and throw box expand slightly towards the opponent for the entire duration of the Parry (Throw box extension starts instantly on frame 1, while the Hurtbox extension starts on frame 3, after the initial 2F Perfect Parry window); Parrying while crouching maintains a regular crouch hurtbox for the first 2 frames of the parry (during the initial Perfect Parry window)

yasmine.name: 斗气冲刺 (Drive Rush)
yasmine.notes: Dashes forward and enhances the next normal or command normal used out of the Drive Rush with +4 extra hitstun / blockstun, as well as improved juggle properties (Juggle Limit increased by +3 / Juggle Start/Increase reduced to 0); The +4 bonus frame advantage gained from a Drive Rush enhanced move also stacks with any bonus frame advantage that move may have gained from Counter-Hit, Punish Counter, or Burnout; Grounded special-cancelable normals can also be canceled into Drive Rush on hit or block, as well as from light normals on whiff; Drive Rush maintains buffers (freezes the buffer window) during its start-up and freeze frames - This allows players to do things normally not possible within the normal buffer windows, such as Drive Rushing into a charge special; The initial 10F screen freeze eats the opponent's directional inputs (except Jumps) but does not prevent attacks from being buffered immediately afterward (this can cause inputs to be combined in unintended ways, such as crouch MK + Fireball performing a raw Fireball, or a vertical jump + walk forward turning into a forward jump); Framedata shown in parentheses refers to the Drive Rush version used from a Parry; Drive Rush recovery is only 24F total (23F if done from a Parry) - but the enhanced dash itself is 46F total (45F if done from Parry) and you can cancel it as early as frame 9 (frame 11 if done from a Parry); Inputting a direction (walk/crouch/block/jump) after the Drive Rush recovery plays out 2 additional recovery frames before the transition occurs (this allows the user to perform an enhanced crouching or command normal late in the dash by inputting the direction + button simultaneously); You stop building any form of Drive Gauge on your attacks after using a Drive Rush in the MIDDLE of a combo (but you still continue to build Drive gauge as normal if you did Drive Rush at the START of a combo); Applies an extra damage scaling penalty after using a Drive Rush in the MIDDLE of a combo (no damage scaling if you use Drive Rush at the START of a combo); Costs 3 bars of Drive Gauge if canceled into from a normal attack; Costs 1/2 bar of Drive Gauge if canceled into from Parry (for a total of 1 bar of Drive Gauge when you factor in the initial 1/2 bar cost of the Parry); Normals used out of Drive Rush carry additional forward momentum (but throws and specials immediately halt all momentum, which can be a useful strategy to punish opponents for trying to interrupt your Drive Rush); Parry Drive Rush can only be initiated after frame 3 of the Parry (but can be performed immediately after recovering from a successful parry); Parry Drive Rush cannot be initiated with less than 1/2 of a Drive bar (as the initial Parry cost will put the user into Burnout) - But whiff canceling a Light normal into Drive Rush can achieve a similar effect; Cannot cancel Drive Rush into a Parry (inputting MP+MK results in a MK normal coming out instead); Drive Rush puts the user into a counter-hit state for the entire duration (this makes it impossible to tech a throw that connects during the dash)

yasmine.name: Neutral Taunt
yasmine.notes: Neutral taunt performs a 400 damage knockdown strike on frame 574 when catching the knife (gives a shorter knockdown on Punish Counter for some reason); Obviously not actually useful in any way since it's massively punishable even on hit

yasmine.name: Forward Taunt (Hadoken!)
yasmine.notes: Forward taunt performs a short range stationary 1-hit projectile attack (Hadoken!) if any button is held on frame 275 of startup (total startup 450F); Obviously not actually useful in any way since it's massively punishable even on hit

yasmine.name: Mukha ng Langit
yasmine.notes: Airborne on frames 14-48; Button strength determines flip trajectory (LK short / MK mid / HK far); Modern Controls: trajectory changes when holding Down+Back / Down / Down+Forward; Standing state and hurtbox size during the 11 landing recovery frames; Follow-ups can be input on frames 24-44; Can input OD follow-ups with PP or KK input

yasmine.name: Mukha ng Langit > Kulog

yasmine.name: Mukha ng Langit > Ulan
yasmine.notes: Hits cross-up (cannot hit in front); Can look visually deceptive and look like it's hitting on the front, and then land behind (when this happens, it's not actually a cross-up and can be blocked both ways thanks to SF6's built-in cross-up protection); Button strength determines downward trajectory; LP (Classic) / L (Modern): Close range trajectory; MP (Classic) / M (Modern): Medium range trajectory; HP (Classic) / H (Modern): Far range trajectory; Incurs 30% damage scaling penalty if used as the first hit of a combo

yasmine.name: Pangil sa Likuran
yasmine.notes: 2-hit Projectile (but can only hit once on the initial upwards trajectory, and then applies the remaining hits on the return back); Button strength determines the boomerang's angle / trajectory as well as the overall travel time (the active projectile hitbox); LP (Classic) / L (Modern): Short distance and 50 active frames; MP (Classic) / M (Modern): Medium distance and 60 active frames; HP (Classic) / H (Modern): Far distance and 74 active frames; Can only have one boomerang projectile on-screen at a time (disappears if Yasmine is hit); Only the first 3 active frames are Super cancelable; When spaced out during combos this can give enough frame advantage for further combo extensions, this is easier to do against standing opponents since most of the boomerang trajectories whiff on crouching opponents if not used point-blank (crouch HP forces stand and combos naturally into this special so it's the ideal normal to use for boomerang combos); The first hit on the initial upwards trajectory doesn't knockdown grounded opponents, but the last hit on the return back does put the opponent into a limited juggle state on hit; Incurs 20% damage scaling penalty if used as the first hit of a combo, and counts as 2 hits of damage scaling when used during a combo; Framedata listed refers to when used point-blank (the frame advantage is obviously a lot better when the boomerang is returning and Yasmine has already fully recovered)

yasmine.name: Hiwa ng Kalangitan

yasmine.name: Nakatagong Lakas
yasmine.notes: Duration of 1500 frames (25 seconds) and consumes 375 frames (25%) of the install timer when using any version of her Alon special (qcf+P follow-ups); Grants access to a new special move (Linya ng Liwanag / Rapid Slash) and changes the properties of OD Alon (qcf+PP follow-up), using this move also consumes 375 frames (25%) of the install timer; Yasmine remains in Bayani Mode even after using enhanced specials while the install timer is active; Cannot build additional Super gauge while the install timer is active; Install timer freezes during any hitstop

yasmine.name: Pamumukadkad ng Sampaguita
yasmine.notes: Fully invincible on frames 1-12; Armor Break; Depletes 1.5 Drive Bars on hit for the opponent; Super cinematic time regenerates ~2.2 Drive Bars for Yasmine; Incurs 10% damage scaling when canceled into from specials; 2F start-up when canceled into from Specials; Leaves Yasmine fullscreen even if the opponent was cornered (can get some oki with Drive Rush into a delayed button, but no true strike/throw oki); Can be used as a projectile counter from about round start distance if it reaches an opponent's extended hurtbox; Tall hitbox can anti-air at longer ranges but whiffs under a close or mid range jump-in

yasmine.name: Pamumukadkad ng Sampaguita (Critical Art)
yasmine.notes: Fully invincible on frames 1-12; Critical Art does +500 extra damage over regular version; Armor Break; Depletes 2 Drive Bars on hit for the opponent; Super cinematic time regenerates ~2.3 Drive Bars for Yasmine; Incurs 10% damage scaling when canceled into from specials; 2F start-up when canceled into from Specials; Yasmine can forward dash for +1 oki, leaving her near the edge of throw range (both Throw and Light chains can lose to back walk); Gets much stronger oki with Drive Rush and can bait 6F reversals with immediate Drive Rush > crouch LP; Can be used as a projectile counter from about round start distance if it reaches an opponent's extended hurtbox; Tall hitbox can anti-air at longer ranges but whiffs under a close or mid range jump-in

yasmine.name: Linya ng Liwanag
yasmine.notes: Only accessible during Level 2 Super install; Each use depletes the SA2 install timer by 375F (25%); Can be canceled into from Yasmine's stand MK or crouch MK Target Combos (these Target Combos are otherwise not cancelable in any way); Puts opponent into a limited juggle state on hit; Switches sides on hit and will pass behind an opponent if the first hit does not connect (like on a knocked down or jumping opponent); When the 1st hit is blocked or parried, Yasmine stops her forward momentum and does not perform the 2nd hit (2F active + 24F recovery); Startup time for the cross-up hit is functionally 30F; Startup time can be up to 3F faster (19F) if Yasmine crosses behind an airborne or teleporting opponent with no collision box; The gap between active frames is increased to 2(11)5 when the first hit connects; Whiff recovery is 1F faster (19F) if Yasmine passes far behind the opponent before whiffing the 2nd hit; Reaches fullscreen and extends a huge proximity box forward starting on frame 15; Incurs 20% damage scaling penalty if used as the first hit of a combo, and counts as 2 hits of damage scaling when used during a combo

yasmine.name: Daloy ng Tubig

zangief.name: 站轻拳 (5LP)

zangief.name: 站中拳 (5MP)

zangief.name: Stand HP (hold)
zangief.notes: 1-hit of armor on upper-body on frames 4-34 (attacks that hit low enough can go past the armor); The armor for partially held HP is lost immediately upon releasing HP (followed up with un-armored 10F start-up HP attack); The 10F start-up shown in the parentheses refers to when the HP button is released after holding HP for at least 6 frames; Fully held HP version deals a ton of damage, drive gauge chip as well as give good frame advantage on block makes this a very powerful tool if the opponent doesn't stop it; Fully held version deals 400 extra damage (1400); +2F extra recovery frames (24F) on whiff; Causes a +40 Hard Knockdown on Counter-Hit (and a ground slide on Punish Counter for +54 Hard Knockdown)

zangief.name: 站轻脚 (5LK)

zangief.name: 站中脚 (5MK)
zangief.notes: Very good poke button with decent range, strong hitbox priority and very good damage for a MK poke

zangief.name: 站重脚 (5HK)
zangief.notes: Cannot hit crouching; Zangief's kicking leg is invincible to airborne strikes on frames 13-22; Good horizontal anti-air (albeit a bit slow start-up); The brief extended leg hurtbox on frame 12 of start-up (1F before active) is strike invincible (cannot counter-poke projectiles); Launches opponent into a free juggle state (KD +51) on Punish Counter; Puts airborne opponents into a limited juggle state on hit

zangief.name: 蹲轻拳 (2LP)
zangief.notes: Plus frames on blocked jab (this is unique to Zangief) and a true blockstring when chained into crouch LP or crouch LK, allowing Zangief to pressure better with his light chains than the rest of the roster; Chains into stand LP / crouch LP / crouch LK; Only 3F start-up when chained into; Incurs 20% damage scaling penalty if used as the first hit of a combo; Topmost hurtboxes on frames 1-7 are vulnerable only to airborne attacks (this is to discourage its use as an anti-air)

zangief.name: 蹲中拳 (2MP)
zangief.notes: Mostly a combo / buffer tool; Topmost hurtboxes on frames 1-7 are vulnerable only to airborne attacks (this is to discourage its use as an anti-air) and Projectile invincible on frames 1-15 (avoids Sagat's MP/HP Tiger Shot)

zangief.name: 蹲重拳 (2HP)
zangief.notes: Zangief's head hurtbox is invincible to airborne strikes on frames 10-19 (helps with anti-airing); Good vertical anti-air (but pretty slow start-up); Only the first 3 active frames can hit grounded (the rest only hits airborne aiming above Zangief); Active frames 4-8 (frames 15-19 overall) can hit cross-up (behind Zangief); Launches the opponent into a limited juggle state on hit (Punish Counter launches them higher and into an OTG free juggle state, which Zangief can follow-up with a combo)

zangief.name: 蹲轻脚 (2LK)

zangief.name: 蹲中脚 (2MK)

zangief.name: 蹲重脚 (2HK)

zangief.name: 跳轻拳 (j.LP)

zangief.name: 跳中拳 (j.MP)

zangief.name: 跳重拳 (j.HP)
zangief.notes: Spikes down airborne opponents on hit.

zangief.name: 跳轻脚 (j.LK)

zangief.name: 跳中脚 (j.MK)

zangief.name: 跳重脚 (j.HK)

zangief.name: Jump HK (hold)

zangief.name: Flying Headbutt

zangief.name: Hellstab

zangief.name: Knee Hammer
