zangief.name: Headbutt
zangief.notes: Tons of frame advantage and active frames, as well as heavy damage and fully cancelable makes this a core tool for damage, pressure and oki; +2F extra recovery frames (17F) on whiff; Puts airborne opponents into a limited juggle state; Incurs 25% damage scaling penalty if used as the first hit of a combo; Counts as 2 hits of damage scaling when combo'd into

zangief.name: Cyclone Wheel Kick
zangief.notes: Overhead; Low crushes on frames 13-28; Not actually airborne; First 2 active frames can only hit airborne (making this effectively 24F start-up against standing opponents and 26F start-up against crouching opponents); +2 extra KDA (KD +30) against crouching opponents; Can be spaced out to hit on later active frames for increased KDA and better safety on block (the spacing and pushback on block can even make this safe on block at further ranges); Puts airborne opponents into a limited juggle state; Puts opponent into an OTG juggle state on Punish Counter; Has some juggle potential naturally without Drive Rush

zangief.name: Smetana Dropkick
zangief.notes: Throw invincible and low crushes on frames 5-26; Not actually airborne; Very strong hitbox priority (could be used for potential counterpoking); Sends the opponent tumbling on a Punish Counter which can lead into a wall splat (HKD +128); The wall splat Punish Counter is Juggle Start 0 against grounded opponents but Juggle Start 1 against airborne opponents; The opponent is in a grounded state after the low wall splat so they can be Thrown or Command Grabbed (but strike attacks still put the opponent into a juggle state even if they're technically grounded)

zangief.name: Machine Gun Chops 1
zangief.notes: Very lenient cancel window makes this second hit very easy to Counter-Hit / Punish confirm into (28F hit confirm window); Only combos from Standing Medium Punch on Counter Hit, Punish Counter, when it hits meaty on active frames 3-4, or when used after Drive Rush; Can be performed on whiff; Second hit will whiff if the initial MP connects from too far away; 6F blockstring gap between hits

zangief.name: Machine Gun Chops 2
zangief.notes: Last hit combos naturally from the prior MP (second hit); Can be performed on whiff; 7F blockstring gap between hits

zangief.name: Stomp
zangief.notes: Lifts up most of his leg hurtboxes on frames 5-9 making this a strong tool against low attacks (a Low attack that also crushes other Lows); 2F blockstring gap between each stomp; Cannot perform the 2nd stomp follow-up if the 1st hit whiffs; 2nd hit of the TC can whiff at farther ranges; Incurs 20% damage scaling penalty if used as the first hit of a combo; Has strong synergy with held Stand HP which is primarily countered by low pokes

zangief.name: Power Stomps 1
zangief.notes: This second MK combos naturally, but requires Counter-Hit to combo into the third MK hit; 2F blockstring gap between each stomp; Cannot be performed if the 1st stomp whiffs, but can continue into the 3rd stomp if this hit whiffs (this leaves a 14F gap on hit / 21F gap on block)

zangief.name: Power Stomps 2
zangief.notes: Only combos from the second hit of the target combo on Counter Hit; Can be performed on whiff; 2F blockstring gap between each stomp (can frametrap opponents trying to take back their turn)

zangief.name: Bodyslam
zangief.notes: LP+LK Input can be held for an additonal hit (+600 additional damage); Data in parentheses refers to the held version; Throw Loop: Manually timed walk forward into Throw (not possible on mid-screen back roll); Punish Counter gives +70% damage (2040 unheld | 2640 held), Hard Knockdown (denies back-roll option on wake-up), depletes 1 bar of Drive gauge from the opponent, and builds twice as much Super gauge for the attacker; Throw Escape builds 0.5 Drive bars for the defender (randomly assigned if throws are input simultaneously)

zangief.name: German Suplex
zangief.notes: Deals 300 extra damage (1500) over normal throw (1200) but sacrifices all oki; Punish Counter gives +70% (2550) damage, Hard Knockdown (denies back-roll option on wake-up), depletes 1 bar of Drive gauge from the opponent, and builds twice as much Super gauge for the attacker; Throw Escape builds 0.5 Drive bars for the defender (randomly assigned if throws are input simultaneously); Builds more Super meter than a standard throw

zangief.name: Capture Suplex
zangief.notes: Throw Loop (corner only): Meaty strike or command grab; Deals 200 extra damage (1400) over normal throw damage (1200); Punish Counter gives +70% (2380) damage, Hard Knockdown (denies back-roll option on wake-up), depletes 1 bar of Drive gauge from the opponent, and builds twice as much Super gauge for the attacker; Throw Escape builds 0.5 Drive bars for the defender (randomly assigned if throws are input simultaneously)

zangief.name: Brain Buster
zangief.notes: Deals 300 extra damage (1500) over normal throw (1200) but sacrifices throw loop oki (but can still oki with meaty strikes); Punish Counter gives +70% (2550) damage, Hard Knockdown (denies back-roll option on wake-up), depletes 1 bar of Drive gauge from the opponent, and builds twice as much Super gauge for the attacker; Throw Escape builds 0.5 Drive bars for the defender (randomly assigned if throws are input simultaneously); Builds more Super meter than a standard throw-

zangief.name: Spinebuster
zangief.notes: Zangief's best throw option for oki; Leads to a throw loop in the corner or a very strict Drive Rush throw loop midscreen; Punish Counter gives +70% (2040) damage, Hard Knockdown (denies back-roll option on wake-up), depletes 1 bar of Drive gauge from the opponent, and builds twice as much Super gauge for the attacker; Throw Escape builds 0.5 Drive bars for the defender (randomly assigned if throws are input simultaneously)

zangief.name: Russian Drop
zangief.notes: Deals 300 extra damage (1500) over normal throw (1200) but sacrifices all oki; Punish Counter gives +70% (2550) damage, Hard Knockdown (denies back-roll option on wake-up), depletes 1 bar of Drive gauge from the opponent, and builds twice as much Super gauge for the attacker; Throw Escape builds 0.5 Drive bars for the defender (randomly assigned if throws are input simultaneously); Builds more Super meter than a standard throw

zangief.name: Drive Impact: Double Russian Chop
zangief.notes: 2 hits of armor on frames 1-27; Damages opponents Drive Gauge on Block (1/2 bar) | Hit (1 bar) | Counter-Hit (1.25 bar) | Punish Counter (1.5 bar); Knocks down on hit; Pushes the opponent far back on hit or block and causes a Wall Splat if they hit the wall (Parry prevents the backwards stumble and Wall Splat, greatly reducing the pushback); Regular KDA without Wall Splat +35 KD | Wall Splat on Hit +65 KD | Wall Splat on Block +72 HKD; KDA can vary greatly depending on how high the opponent wall splats (higher KDA the higher they wall splat); Advantage after Wall Splat can vary depending on distance from the corner (farther from corner gives higher advantage); Crumples the opponent on Punish Counter or after absorbing at least 1 attack during start-up (+21 frames before the crumple state goes airborne, followed by airborne state on frames 22-46 before they are grounded); Puts airborne opponents into a long spinning free juggle state when hit as a Punish Counter or after absorbing an attack; If the armor absorbs an attack it slows the overall start-up by 1F (27F total instead of 26F) and incurs 6F hitstop for each projectile hit absorbed (making it less likely to punish the opponent after absorbing projectiles); Absorbing an attack causes the player to take 1/2 the damage in recoverable health (but will KO if this would bring the player's health below zero); Stun/Dizzy occurs when a Wall Splat connects on an opponent in Burnout; Stun gives a free combo follow-up for the next 195F after hitting the wall, followed by a HKD if the player falls to the ground untouched (the last 7F before hitting the ground has a crouch-sized hurtbox but is considered standing, allowing for unique combo setups); Incurs 20% damage scaling penalty if used as the first hit of a combo (applies to wall splat on HIT, crumple, Burnout dizzy on hit/block, or any character-specific means of comboing after a regular Drive Impact); Incurs a 20% multiplier damage scaling penalty after a Wall Splat on BLOCK - Because the blocked Drive Impact is not considered a "hit" for the combo, the next attack can incur its own separate damage scaling as a combo starter; Wall Splat puts opponent into a special juggle state where the next move freely connects and continues the juggle even if it normally wouldn't (similar to a Forced Knockdown or Drive Rush juggle properties); Does not cause Wall Splat if the Drive Impact connects as a combo or a true blockstring with no gaps (LOCK icon appears on-screen); It is possible to "combo" into Stun if the opponent has under 1.5 Drive bars - a blocked DI Wall Splat from slightly outside the corner into a second DI on hit will cause Burnout and Stun (because the blocked DI is not technically considered a combo starter); Costs 1 bar of Drive Gauge; Cinematic slowdown occurs if both players activate Drive Impact within range of each other (granting a Punish Counter to the player who activates it later); Attempting to counter with DI vs. DI with under 400 HP will result in a KO, as the second player will not have enough health to absorb it; Clashes with other Drive Impacts and refunds the Drive gauge cost if they collide on the same active frame (start at exactly the same time, or 1F apart if the first Drive Impact absorbs a strike) - The meter refund does not prevent Burnout from occurring; The scrub killer

zangief.name: Drive Reversal: Reverse Russian Kick
zangief.notes: Has two versions: one performed during blockstun or parry stun (20F start-up) and one performed as a wake-up reversal (18F start-up); Fully invincible on frames 1-22 (blockstun) / frames 1-20 (reversal); Armor Break (blows through all armor like Drive Impact, but not counters like JP's Amnesia); Trying to Drive Reversal after the blockstun ends results in a Drive Impact; Drive Reversal immediately removes the current blockstun you're in and starts the attack; Causes a 4F screen freeze after the 6th start-up frame, which allows the opponent to perform a simple OS (inputting their buttons during the buffer window) to prevent their next attack from coming out; Safe on block (-2) when used against an opponent in Burnout; Costs 2 bars of Drive Gauge; If the opponent tries to throw against a wake-up Drive Reversal, it causes a 12F screen freeze and refunds 1 bar of Drive gauge (but does not prevent Burnout); Guaranteed to interrupt any Drive Rush canceled normal if performed immediately out of blockstun (unless the opponent reacts with an invincible move or counter)

zangief.name: 斗气招架 (Drive Parry)
zangief.notes: Parries all strikes and projectiles (high and low) from frame 1; 12F parry window (can hold the parry to extend the parry window); Perfect Parry occurs on the first 2 active frames (cannot achieve Perfect Parry if you buffer into parry by holding it during Reversal windows; Perfect Parries have to be timed properly); Can still hold charge directions during Parry (allowing characters with charge specials to stand block before performing their reversal); Can block during the recovery frames of a regular parry (can still get hit during the recovery frames if you don't block correctly); Getting thrown or hit at any point during the recovery frames of a whiffed parry attempt results in a Punish Counter; Successfully parrying a move puts you into the same amount of blockstun as that move would regularly do on block (but a Perfect Parry has only 1F of recovery); Throw invincible during the recovery of a successful parry (just like during blockstun); Perfect Parrying a strike has only 1F of recovery and disables the opponent from canceling their attack (basically a guaranteed punish opportunity except for safe jump setups); Perfect Parrying a strike requires holding the correct block direction (Down+Back for low strikes, Back for high/mid strikes); Attempting a Perfect Parry with the wrong block direction results in an "imperfect parry" that builds an extra 3000 Drive Gauge and plays a distinct audio/visual cue; After a successful Perfect Parry, you suffer a 50% penalty to your Damage, Drive Gauge Generation, and Drive Gauge Damage on any of your following attacks when punishing the opponent (in addition, both you and the opponent suffer a 20% penalty to your Super Meter gain during this period); Fully invincible for 6F after a successful Perfect Parry against a strike, which carries over to any attack you perform (ensuring a 5F or faster punish will always interrupt multi-hit attacks); Perfect Parrying projectiles puts you into fixed 10 frames of recovery and applies the same 50% scaling penalties (and 20% Super Meter penalty) on your following attacks when punishing the opponent; Parrying a Strike and Projectile on the same frame will result in a regular parry for the strike attack (effectively ignoring the projectile's hitstop / blockstun); Perfect Parrying a Strike and Projectile on the same frame will give a screen freeze like you Perfect Parried a Strike, but still give you 10F recovery as if you had Perfect Parried a Projectile; Can cancel into Drive Rush during active frames 3 and onward (fastest Drive Rush method is to buffer a forward input before doing parry + forward again); Can cancel into Drive Reversal from a successful parry (just like you normally can during blockstun); Costs 1/2 bar of Drive Gauge and continues to deplete 50 Drive Gauge per frame (0.3 Drive bars per second) as you hold the Parry; You lose the parry if you go into Burnout from the initial Drive Gauge cost (Perfect Parry requires frame-perfect timing when starting from under 1/2 of a Drive bar); Rewards 1 bar of Drive Gauge (1/2 bar total after factoring in the initial parry cost) for successfully parrying a strike; Rewards 1/2 bar of Drive Gauge (0 bar total after factoring in the initial parry cost) for successfully parrying a projectile (with a few exceptions); Rewards 2 bars of Drive Gauge (1.5 bars total after factoring in the initial parry cost) for successful parrying a Super Art or Drive Impact; Successfully parrying a strike attack splits the regular block pushback between both players (while Perfect Parrying a strike removes all of its pushback); Successfully parrying a projectile or Drive Impact reduces the pushback of it by half (while Perfect Parrying a projectile or Drive Impact removes all of its pushback); Your hurtbox and throw box expand slightly towards the opponent for the entire duration of the Parry (Throw box extension starts instantly on frame 1, while the Hurtbox extension starts on frame 3, after the initial 2F Perfect Parry window); Parrying while crouching maintains a regular crouch hurtbox for the first 2 frames of the parry (during the initial Perfect Parry window)

zangief.name: 斗气冲刺 (Drive Rush)
zangief.notes: Dashes forward and enhances the next normal or command normal used out of the Drive Rush with +4 extra hitstun / blockstun, as well as improved juggle properties (Juggle Limit increased by +3 / Juggle Start/Increase reduced to 0); The +4 bonus frame advantage gained from a Drive Rush enhanced move also stacks with any bonus frame advantage that move may have gained from Counter-Hit, Punish Counter, or Burnout; Grounded special-cancelable normals can also be canceled into Drive Rush on hit or block, as well as from light normals on whiff; Drive Rush maintains buffers (freezes the buffer window) during its start-up and freeze frames - This allows players to do things normally not possible within the normal buffer windows, such as Drive Rushing into a charge special; The initial 10F screen freeze eats the opponent's directional inputs (except Jumps) but does not prevent attacks from being buffered immediately afterward (this can cause inputs to be combined in unintended ways, such as crouch MK + Fireball performing a raw Fireball, or a vertical jump + walk forward turning into a forward jump); Framedata shown in parentheses refers to the Drive Rush version used from a Parry; Drive Rush recovery is only 24F total (23F if done from a Parry) - but the enhanced dash itself is 46F total (45F if done from Parry) and you can cancel it as early as frame 9 (frame 11 if done from a Parry); Inputting a direction (walk/crouch/block/jump) after the Drive Rush recovery plays out 2 additional recovery frames before the transition occurs (this allows the user to perform an enhanced crouching or command normal late in the dash by inputting the direction + button simultaneously); You stop building any form of Drive Gauge on your attacks after using a Drive Rush in the MIDDLE of a combo (but you still continue to build Drive gauge as normal if you did Drive Rush at the START of a combo); Applies an extra damage scaling penalty after using a Drive Rush in the MIDDLE of a combo (no damage scaling if you use Drive Rush at the START of a combo); Costs 3 bars of Drive Gauge if canceled into from a normal attack; Costs 1/2 bar of Drive Gauge if canceled into from Parry (for a total of 1 bar of Drive Gauge when you factor in the initial 1/2 bar cost of the Parry); Normals used out of Drive Rush carry additional forward momentum (but throws and specials immediately halt all momentum, which can be a useful strategy to punish opponents for trying to interrupt your Drive Rush); Parry Drive Rush can only be initiated after frame 3 of the Parry (but can be performed immediately after recovering from a successful parry); Parry Drive Rush cannot be initiated with less than 1/2 of a Drive bar (as the initial Parry cost will put the user into Burnout) - But whiff canceling a Light normal into Drive Rush can achieve a similar effect; Cannot cancel Drive Rush into a Parry (inputting MP+MK results in a MK normal coming out instead); Drive Rush puts the user into a counter-hit state for the entire duration (this makes it impossible to tech a throw that connects during the dash)

zangief.name: 双重旋转金臂勾
zangief.notes: Invincible to airborne strikes on frames 6-16 (great anti-air tool on the first hit, although slow in start-up); Projectile invincible on frames 6-45; No head hurtbox on frames 1-5 and further shrinks his hurtboxes on frames 6-16; Can hold forward or back to move around slightly during the Lariat.; Connects only once on hit, but four times on block, though all hits but the first whiff vs crouching opponents.; Cannot hit cross-up (behind Zangief); Launches opponent into a free juggle state on hit if only the last hit connects (requires specific combo / punish setups); Canceling into Lariat from a normal expands the lower hitbox and increases Zangief's forward movement for consistency in combos and whiff punishes

zangief.name: LP Screw Piledriver
zangief.notes: Range: 1.62; Furthest range and highest KDA of his SPDs but least amount of damage; Deals +15% extra damage (2875) on Punish Counter; Incurs 10% damage scaling onto itself when combo'd into

zangief.name: MP Screw Piledriver
zangief.notes: Range: 1.47; Medium range and damage of his SPDs; Deals +15% extra damage (3335) on Punish Counter; Incurs 10% damage scaling onto itself when combo'd into

zangief.name: HP Screw Piledriver
zangief.notes: Range: 1.22; Shortest range of his SPDs but most amount of damage; Deals +15% extra damage (3795) on Punish Counter; Incurs 10% damage scaling onto itself when combo'd into

zangief.name: OD Screw Piledriver
zangief.notes: Range: 1.58; Slightly less range than the LP version but even more damage than the HP version; Deals +15% extra damage (3910) on Punish Counter

zangief.name: Borscht Dynamite
zangief.notes: Range: 1.46; Can be performed instantly after leaving the ground (first airborne frame of the jump); Combos after some of Zangief's launchers / juggle; 16F landing recovery frames on whiff (minimum / maximum recovery frames overall: 21+16 / 36+16); Zangief is in a crouching state for the entire landing recovery frames on whiff; Forced Knockdown state while airborne; Deals +15% extra damage (3260) on Punish Counter; Incurs 20% damage scaling onto itself when combo'd into

zangief.name: OD Borscht Dynamite
zangief.notes: Range: 1.64; Can be performed instantly after leaving the ground (first airborne frame of the jump); Combos after some of Zangief's launchers / juggles; 16F landing recovery frames on whiff (minimum / maximum recovery frames overall: 21+16 / 36+16); Zangief is in a crouching state for the entire landing recovery frames on whiff; Forced Knockdown state while airborne; Deals +15% extra damage (3375) on Punish Counter; Incurs 10% damage scaling onto itself when combo'd into

zangief.name: Russian Suplex (close)
zangief.notes: Range: 1.14; This is the up close version that plays out in close proximity (has the fastest start-up and more damage, but slightly less KDA and switches sides with the opponent); Can be input with the HK button at any range (deals 300 less damage but allows it to connect at some ranges where Siberian Express would come out instead); HK version can function as a shorter range and slower startup Command Grab up close, but instead gives stronger oki options (as well as swapping sides) than his regular SPD (Screw Piledriver); Deals +15% extra damage (LK/MK: 3335 / HK: 2990) on Punish Counter; Incurs 10% damage scaling onto itself when combo'd into

zangief.name: OD Russian Suplex (close)
zangief.notes: Range: 1.14; This is the up close version that only plays out in close proximity (has the fastest start-up and more damage, but slightly less KDA and switches sides with the opponent); Can function as a shorter range and slower startup OD Command Grab up close, but instead gives stronger oki options (as well as swapping sides) than his OD SPD (Screw Piledriver); Deals +15% extra damage (3680) on Punish Counter

zangief.name: Siberian Express (near)
zangief.notes: Run Speed: 0.086; This is the near version of Siberian Express that plays out if Zangief is further away than point-blank range but still within half-screen range; Zangief will run towards the opponent and grab them (28F start-up); Siberian Express does less damage than the close version (Russian Suplex) but has slightly higher KDA and doesn't switch sides with the opponent; Deals +15% extra damage (3105) on Punish Counter

zangief.name: OD Siberian Express (near)
zangief.notes: Run Speed: 0.086; This is the near version of Siberian Express that plays out if Zangief is further away than point-blank range but still within half-screen range; Zangief will run towards the opponent and grab them (23F start-up); Siberian Express does less damage than the close version (Russian Suplex) but has slightly higher KDA and doesn't switch sides with the opponent; Deals +15% extra damage (3450) on Punish Counter

zangief.name: Siberian Express (far)
zangief.notes: Run Speed: 0.090~0.099; This is the Far version of Siberian Express that plays out if Zangief is at least half-screen away from the opponent; This far version has one hit of armor on frame 11 and onwards as Zangief runs forward; Zangief will raise his arms up at the beginning of the animation before he runs forward; Zangief starts the Throw animation immediately if the opponent strikes the armor (this can cause Zangief to run across the screen incredibly fast if the armor is triggered from far away, such as a Dhalsim limb); Slower start-up the further away Zangief has to run to the opponent (up to 81F start-up from full-screen away); Deals +15% extra damage (3105) on Punish Counter

zangief.name: OD Siberian Express (far)
zangief.notes: Run Speed: 0.045~0.099; This is the Far version of Siberian Express that plays out if Zangief is at least half-screen away from the opponent; This far version has one hit of armor on frame 3 and onwards as Zangief runs forward; Zangief will raise his arms up at the beginning of the animation before he runs forward; Zangief starts the Throw animation immediately if the opponent strikes the armor (this can cause Zangief to run across the screen incredibly fast if the armor is triggered from far away, such as a Dhalsim limb); Slower start-up the further away Zangief has to run to the opponent (up to 81F start-up from full-screen away); Deals +15% extra damage (3450) on Punish Counter

zangief.name: Tundra Storm
zangief.notes: Counter is active on frames 6-55; Parries any incoming kick-based normals, specials, or Drive moves that hit between Zangief's open arms while in the parry stance; Cannot counter kicks from a crouching or airborne opponent, or when the opponent is behind Zangief; A successful counter results in a throw hitbox, which can make this attack whiff on airborne or throw invincible opponents)

zangief.name: Aerial Russian Slam
zangief.notes: Fully invincible on frames 1-17; Airborne on frames 2-30 (Forced Knockdown state); Depletes 0.5 Drive Bar on hit for the opponent; Can only hit airborne opponents; Cannot hit cross-up (behind Zangief); Can be quite unreliable to land in some anti-air / juggle scenarios; Suffers 20% damage scaling when combo'd into from other moves

zangief.name: Cyclone Lariat
zangief.notes: Fully invincible on frames 1-18; Projectile invincible on frames 19-119; Armor Break; Depletes 1 Drive Bar on hit for the opponent; Suctions in the opponent up to half-screen away on frames 18-108; Too slow to be effectively used as a reversal against fast buttons; The follow-up grab on hit has 3 variations depending on what direction is input during the grab animation: Neutral (Jackhammer!) | Forward (Zangief throws the opponent forward instead of behind him) | Backward (Zangief throws the opponent slightly further behind him than the neutral Jackhammer version); Both forward and backward versions deal 100 less damage than the neutral Jackhammer version; Forward version has 4F less KDA (HKD +1); Can hold the attack button to extend the duration and knock the opponent upwards (see the (hold) entry for more details on that version); If juggled into it transitions into the fully held version (since the throw follow-ups do not work on airborne opponents)

zangief.name: Cyclone Lariat (hold)
zangief.notes: Fully invincible on frames 1-18; Projectile invincible on frames 19-122; Armor Break; Depletes 1 Drive Bar on hit for the opponent; Suctions in the opponent up to half-screen away on frames 18-111; Too slow to be effectively used as a reversal against fast buttons; This entry is for the held version (or when juggled into) of Cyclone Lariat; Recovery on hit is much shorter than on whiff/block (25F); Launches the opponent into a free juggle state (limited juggle state if used in the middle of a juggle); KDA (Knockdown advantage) listed refers to the grounded version (KDA is variable when hitting airborne opponents)

zangief.name: Bolshoi Storm Buster
zangief.notes: Fully invincible on frames 1-7; Command Grab Super (Can be combo'd into off OD Lariat cancel, crumples or 3HK Punish Counter wall splat with 10% additional damage scaling); Depletes 1.5 Drive Bars on hit for the oppponent; Super cinematic time regenerates ~2.2 Drive Bars for Zangief; Entire start-up happens before the initial Super cinematic freeze, meaning that this move is effectively 0F start-up after the Super is activated, making it inescapable if the opponent didn't already do something to avoid the grab before the Super was activated

zangief.name: Bolshoi Storm Buster (Critical Art)
zangief.notes: Fully invincible on frames 1-7; Command Grab Super (Can be combo'd into off OD Lariat cancel, crumples or 3HK Punish Counter wall splat with 10% additional damage scaling); Critical Art does +500 extra damage over regular version; Depletes 2 Drive Bars on hit for the oppponent; Super cinematic time regenerates ~2.7 Drive Bars for Zangief; Entire start-up happens before the initial Super cinematic freeze, meaning that this move is effectively 0F start-up after the Super is activated, making it inescapable if the opponent didn't already do something to avoid the grab before the Super was activated

zangief.name: 双重旋转金臂勾
zangief.notes: Invincible to airborne strikes on frames 6-13 (great anti-air tool on the first hit); Projectile invincible on frames 1-36; No head hurtbox on frames 1-5 and further shrinks his hurtboxes on frames 6-13; Can hold forward or back to move around slightly during the Lariat.; First hit keeps the opponent grounded and can be canceled into SA3 for a combo; Connects only twice on hit, five times on stand block, and three times on crouch block with a 1F gap before the final hit; Zangief's most effective chip-out tool in Burnout (675 total damage on crouch block) with increased pushback on the final hit making it relatively safe (-8) if spaced out; Cannot hit cross-up (behind Zangief); If the second hit juggle is staggered, Zangief can go for more powerful follow-ups such as OD Air SPD or SA1; Only the first hit is cancelable into Level 2 Super Art; The first active frame of the second hit can only hit grounded opponents

variations.notes: Invincible to airborne strikes on frames 6-13 (great anti-air tool on the first hit); Projectile invincible on frames 1-36; No head hurtbox on frames 1-5 and further shrinks his hurtboxes on frames 6-13; Can hold forward or back to move around slightly during the Lariat.; First hit keeps the opponent grounded and can be canceled into SA3 for a combo; Connects only twice on hit, five times on stand block, and three times on crouch block with a 1F gap before the final hit; Zangief's most effective chip-out tool in Burnout (675 total damage on crouch block) with increased pushback on the final hit making it relatively safe (-8) if spaced out; Cannot hit cross-up (behind Zangief); If the second hit juggle is staggered, Zangief can go for more powerful follow-ups such as OD Air SPD or SA1; Only the first hit is cancelable into Level 2 Super Art; The first active frame of the second hit can only hit grounded opponents
